title: Jerry Jones thinks it is "unlikely" Cowboys add help in a trade
summary: The trade deadline is a couple of weeks away, but things started heating up on Tuesday with the Colts making a pair of trades that could spur other teams to start making moves as well.
full_text: The trade deadline is a couple of weeks away, but things started heating up on Tuesday with the Colts making a pair of trades that could spur other teams to start making moves as well. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has never been shy when it comes to talking about his willingness to make deals in hopes of improving his roster and he's been particularly vocal about his desire to bolster the defense in Dallas this year. That desire wasn't satiated by their early move to add cornerback Joey Porter Jr., but Jones said on 105.3 The Fan on Tuesday that he doesn't think anything else is going to come together for the Cowboys. "If we could do it where we sit right now , I would add to it," Jones said, via the team's website. "But the adding to it is a big statement. It's unlikely we'll get the opportunity from outside coming in. But if it's there, I'll do it." There's enough time left before November 10 for something to develop, but Jones thinks the Cowboys are going to have to play out the rest of the schedule with what's already on hand.
author: Josh Alper

title: Chad Kelly becomes the first million-dollar player of CFL salary-cap era
summary: Quarterback Chad Kelly said earlier this year that he'd still like to return to the NFL.
full_text: Quarterback Chad Kelly said earlier this year that he’d still like to return to the NFL . For now, he'll continue to play in the CFL. And he'll be paid more than any player in the Canadian league's salary-cap era. Via Justin Dunk of 3DownNation.com, Kelly's new five-year, $5.55 million contract with the Toronto Argonauts makes him the first million-dollar player since the CFL implemented a team-by-team spending limit. Kelly, now 32, was due to become a free agent after the current season. Nathan Rourke was the CFL's highest-paid player in 2026, at a salary of $684,700. Kelly ranked second, at $625,000. Kelly was the last pick of the 2017 draft. After his NFL career fizzled out, in 2020, he landed in the CFL in 2022 and has flourished there. To date, he has had no opportunities to follow in the footsteps of Warren Moon, Doug Flutie, Jeff Garcia, Joe Theismann, and Joe Kapp as quarterbacks who parlayed CFL success into NFL careers. At some point, why wouldn't a team in the quarterback-needy NFL give Kelly a look?
author: Mike Florio

title: Robert Griffin III wants to be the next Baylor coach
summary: From time to time, former NFL quarterback Robert Griffin III expresses interest in continuing his career.
full_text: '' From time to time, former NFL quarterback Robert Griffin III expresses interest in continuing his career. He's now inteested in embarking on a new path entirely. Earlier this week, Griffin said he'd like to become the next head coach at Baylor. " Yes, 100 percent ," Griffin told Dan Patrick on Monday, via ESPN. "If Baylor wants to get back to winning and have a university that isn't just respectable on the football field, but the fans can be proud of, they need people who know what it looks like to win at Baylor. So yeah, I would 100 percent be interested." Griffin won the Heisman Trophy at Baylor in 2011. In 2012, he became the second overall pick in the NFL draft. The NFL's Offensive Rookie of the Year, a knee injury derailed his career in Washington. By his fourth year, he was benched for Kirk Cousins. In 2016, he played for the Browns. Out of football in 2017, he spent his final three seasons with the Ravens. He last played in 2020. Baylor fired Dave Aranda on Sunday, after going 40-40 in six-plus seasons. More than a few former players have become college football coaches in recent years. Typically, their careers start at a lower-level program. Especially when, like Griffin, they have no coaching experience. Earlier this week, former NFL quarterback Philip Rivers, who has been a high-school football coach in Alabama since 2021, was named as a potential candidate at NC State, where he played before becoming the fourth overall pick in the 2004 draft. Since his playing career ended, Griffin has worked for ESPN and Fox.
author: Mike Florio

title: Texas left tackle and likely first-round pick Trevor Goosby out for season
summary: Texas left tackle Trevor Goosby, a likely first-round draft pick and the protector of Arch Manning's blind side, will miss the rest of this season with a knee injury.
full_text: Texas left tackle Trevor Goosby, a likely first-round draft pick and the protector of Arch Manning's blind side, will miss the rest of this season with a knee injury. Goosby suffered the injury on Saturday against Ole Miss. The exact nature of the injury has not been revealed, but Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said Goosby's knee doesn't look good, and Pete Thamel of ESPN reported that he won't play again this season. The 6-foot-7, 325-pound Goosby currently ranks 15th in the betting odds to be the first overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft. First overall now seems extremely unlikely, but unless the injury is very severe, he still looks like a safe bet to be a first-round pick. Goosby could also, however, decide to keep playing college football in 2027. He still has a year of NCAA eligibility left, and he is believed to be making more than $1 million in NIL this year. The combination of an even more lucrative NIL deal next year and the chance to bolster his draft stock with an even better season in 2027 may entice him to return to college and wait until 2028 to enter the NFL draft. Manning, who has had an up-and-down season at Texas this year, may struggle without Goosby protecting him, and that will also make an impact on Manning's status. Manning entered this season as the favorite to go first overall in the 2027 NFL draft, but his play this year has not justified that hype, and there's now talk that Manning could stay in college in 2027 and focus on the 2028 draft.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Malik Beasley agrees to plead guilty to gambling charges
summary: Veteran NBA guard Malik Beasley, who was indicted earlier this year for federal gambling crimes, will be revising his not-guilty plea.
full_text: Veteran NBA guard Malik Beasley, who was indicted earlier this year for federal gambling crimes, will be revising his not-guilty plea. Per Mike Vorkunov of The Athletic, Beasley will be pleading guilty . The formal charges were filed in June. Beasley was accused of participating in a scheme based on manipulation of prop bets based on his statistics. Beasley is scheduled to officially plead guilty on December 9. The nine-year veteran allegedly manipulated his play in four games with the Milwaukee Bucks during the 2023-24 season. He allegedly agreed to do so as a way to pay off a loan after falling into debt. Beasley, 29, spent nine seasons in the NBA. He earned roughly $60 million. Per Vorkunov, Beasley nearly signed a new $42 million deal after finishing second in the Sixth Man of the Year voting for the 2024-25 season. The offer was withdrawn after the gambling situation came to light. The Beasley situation is just one of several NBA gambling scandals since sports betting became legalized on a widespread basis. The NFL has avoided, to date, a major gambling scandal since the Supreme Court opened the floodgates in 2018 to state-by-state wagering on sports.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jahmyr Gibbs closing in on 6,000 scrimmage yards and 60 touchdowns in four NFL seasons
summary: Gibbs is set to become the third player in NFL history to reach those milestones within his first four years in the league.
full_text: On Sunday against the Vikings, Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs could join an elite club in NFL history. Gibbs has 5,919 scrimmage yards and 58 scrimmage touchdowns since the Lions drafted him in 2023, so as soon as Sunday he could reach 6,000 yards and 60 touchdowns in his career. If he does, he'll be just the third player in NFL history to reach those benchmarks within his first three NFL seasons. The others were Broncos Hall of Famer Terrell Davis, who had 7,594 scrimmage yards and 61 touchdowns in his first four NFL seasons, and Chargers Hall of Famer LaDainian Tomlinson, who had 7,921 scrimmage yards and 60 touchdowns in his first four NFL seasons. Gibbs has 890 yards from scrimmage this season, which puts him on pace for 2,522 yards in 17 games. That would break the all-time NFL record of 2,509 scrimmage yards in a season, set by Chris Johnson in 2009.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Packers-Lions does 24.67 million in Sunday's late window
summary: The NFL's late-afternoon window on Sundays continues to rack up big audiences.
full_text: The NFL's late-afternoon window on Sundays continues to rack up big audiences. For Week 7, Packers-Lions on Fox averaged 24.67 million viewers. While not as big as the Sunday night audience for Chiefs-Seahawks (26.3 million), it's a big number. The bi-weekly Fox slot at 4:25 p.m. ET is averaging 24.749 million viewers through the first seven weeks of the 2026 NFL season. This week, CBS has the late-afternoon broadcast, featuring a Denver rematch of the Week 1 game between the Chiefs and Broncos. Given that the Chiefs are 5-1 and the Broncos are 5-2, it should do very well. The early window should do well, too. It features the 5-2 Browns at the 5-2 Steelers, the 4-3 Ravens at the 5-1 Bills, and the 6-0 Vikings at the 4-2 Lions.
author: Mike Florio

title: Joey Porter Jr. on his critics: They'll be quiet soon
summary: Upset about not getting a contract extension before the season, cornerback Joey Porter Jr. didn't play in four games with the Steelers.
full_text: Upset about not getting a contract extension before the season, cornerback Joey Porter Jr. didn't play in four games with the Steelers. He was inactive with his on-again, off-again back issue, which wasn't an issue after the Cowboys traded for him. Porter played for the Cowboys three days after the trade, but he was inactive the following week after an unexpected illness knocked him out. It prompted questions about whether he was all-in with the Cowboys, who made clear they aren't giving him a new deal this season. Richard Sherman said on Amazon Prime Video, "I think maybe if [the Cowboys] had given him a new contract, he’d have been a little healthier today." Porter heard the speculation, but he is unbothered. “Me personally, I know the real ,” Porter told Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram . “I know the truth. I don’t really pay too much attention online to what they have to say. I just got to keep doing my job on Sundays. Once they see the tape, they’ll know. They’ll be quiet soon.” Porter has allowed only one catch for 5 yards on nine targets in three games. He has been the lockdown corner the Cowboys expected when they sent a 2027 sixth-round draft pick and a 2028 second-round draft pick to the Steelers. “It’s nothing new for me,” Porter told Harris. “I think I’ve always been capable of such. I feel like the tape from the last couple of years showed the same thing. I just keep the main thing the main thing.”
author: Charean Williams

title: Steelers-Saints in Paris generates 7.7 million on Sunday morning
summary: Sunday morning football doesn't do the same numbers as Sunday afternoon or evening (or Monday night or Thursday) football, but it does better than anything else on TV at that time of day.
full_text: Sunday morning football doesn't do the same numbers as Sunday afternoon or evening (or Monday night or Thursday) football, but it does better than anything else on TV at that time of day. The Week 7 game between the Steelers and Saints averaged 7.7 million viewers , per ESPN. The fourth straight Sunday morning game drew the third-highest audience for any international game on NFL Network. The four European games played in October (three in London, one in France) averaged 7.1 million viewers on NFLN. The only problem with early-morning football (which will proliferate if/when the NFL secures the ability to stage 16 international games per year) is that it renders the Sunday morning pregame shows irrelevant. As more and more games are played at 9:30 a.m. ET, the networks may reconsider whether they even want to have pregame shows. That said, the networks televising Sunday afternoon games need a studio presence for updates and halftimes. But the noon ET to 1:00 p.m. ET pregame shows will get smaller and smaller audiences as more and more games are played on Sunday morning.
author: Mike Florio

title: Alabama dismisses CB Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. after arrest for doxxing, harassing police officer
summary: Alabama cornerback Dre Kirkpatrick Jr., the son of former NFL cornerback Dre Kirkpatrick, has been dismissed from the team.
full_text: Alabama cornerback Dre Kirkpatrick Jr., the son of former NFL cornerback Dre Kirkpatrick, has been dismissed from the team. Coach Kalen DeBoer announced the move on Tuesday , via Alex Scarborough of ESPN. Kirkpatrick Jr. was arrested on Friday for doxxing and making harassing communications with a police officer. He had been suspended before Saturday's game against Texas A&M. The officer had been involved in a 2025 arrest of Kirkpatrick Jr. for reckless endangerment, attempting to elude police and speeding. Alabama suspended him in October 2025. He did not play again last season. More recently, Kirkpatrick Jr. allegedly texted the officer, among other things, "text me back don't be no bitch!" Kirkpatrick Jr. also allegedly posted a photo of the officer and his family on Facebook. "After gathering more information on the situation, Dre Kirkpatrick Jr. will no longer be a part of our program," DeBoer said in a statement. "He did not live up to the standards and expectations that I have set for this team and our players." Separately, Kirkpatrick Jr. is facing a misdemeanor charge from June 2026 of leaving the scene of an accident. Dre Kirkpatrick Sr. was a first-round pick of the Bengals in 2012. He spent 10 seasons in the NFL with Cincinnati, Arizona, and San Francisco. Kirkpatrick Jr., who was a second-string defensive back, joined Alabama in 2024.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jared Goff backs Dan Campbell's decision to go for it deep in Lions' own end
summary: The Lions went for it on fourth-and-1 in a tie game with 4:53 left, and Jahmyr Gibbs was stopped for a 2-yard loss.
full_text: The Lions went for it on fourth-and-1 in a tie game with 4:53 left, and Jahmyr Gibbs was stopped for a 2-yard loss. Lions coach Dan Campbell has faced questions about his unconventional decision. Campbell explained that the Lions had more confidence in their ability to gain 1 yard than risk Jordan Love executing a 4-minute, game-winning touchdown drive. Campbell added that, even if Detroit's fourth-down gamble failed, the Packers would not be able to run the clock out, leaving the Lions time to respond. It worked out as D.J. Wonnum blocked the chip-shot field goal of Packers rookie kicker Trey Smack, and the Lions won on a last-play field goal. Quarterback Jared Goff said he didn't "even think twice" when he heard the Lions were going for it deep in their own end. "I think it’s so -- I don't know the right word — exposing of people who think it’s not the right decision just because it’s in our territory," Goff said Tuesday on 97.1 The Ticket. "It’s guaranteeing us a chance to win the game no matter what. Whereas, if we punt it, they can do exactly what we did to them on the final drive, and I’m sure they wish they had another chance to touch the ball. "So it’s funny. I think back to a few years ago where we went for that fourth down against Green Bay in a similar situation, fourth-and-1, and we got it with David Montgomery. There was backlash on that, and we converted. I guess no matter what, there will be backlash, so who really cares at this point, right?" In 2024, the Lions went for it on fourth-and-1 at the Green Bay 21 with 43 seconds left. David Montgomery ran for 7 yards, and Jake Bates kicked a 35-yard field goal on the final play for a 34-31 win. "I think when we’re in those situations, we’re so much more comfortable in them than the other teams because we do them more often," Goff said, "and it is an advantage for us. It’s something that we practice and something that we spend a lot of time on, and we feel very comfortable in those situations." The Lions lead the NFL in fourth-down conversions (89) over the past five seasons and rank second in attempts (154), according to 97.1 The Ticket. Their conversion rate of 57.8 percent over that stretch ranks seventh. The Lions have converted 61.5 percent of their 13 fourth-down attempts this season. "Again, unfortunately we didn’t convert this one," said Goff. "We want to get the first down and keep the game moving and finish the game on that drive, but Dan knew that if we were not to get it, OK, they’ll either kick a field goal or they’ll score a touchdown, and then we’ll get the ball back. Now, thankfully, they missed the field goal, and everything was great, but by every measure of everything, it’s the right decision."
author: Charean Williams

title: Chiefs-Seahawks attracts 26.3 million viewers on Sunday night
summary: Even though the game itself was far from compelling, the matchup of a pair of former AFC West rivals delivered big numbers on Sunday night.
full_text: Even though the game itself was far from compelling, the matchup of a pair of former AFC West rivals delivered big numbers on Sunday night. NBC has announced that the Week 7 Chiefs-Seahawks game attracted 26.3 million viewers, on average. It's the biggest Week 7 Sunday night audience since 2013. The game between the previously-unbeaten Chiefs and the defending Super Bowl champions peaked at 29.0 million viewers from 9:30 to 9:45 p.m. ET. In 2013, Peyton Manning's return to Indianapolis racked up 27.0 million viewers on Sunday Night Football. Beyond being the biggest Week 7 Sunday night audience in 13 years, the Chiefs-Seahawks game generated the biggest viewership of any NBC game in 2026. It goes without saying (but, what the hell, I'll say it anyway) that the Week 7 number likely won't be threatened by Sunday night's game between the 2-5 Eagles and the 1-4-1 Commanders.
author: Mike Florio

title: Micah Parsons moves closer to a return
summary: The Packers' defense could be getting a major boost.
full_text: ' The Packers' defense could be getting a major boost. Linebacker Micah Parsons, who suffered a torn ACL in December 2025, seems to be moving closer to a return. Parsons remains on the reserve/Physically Unable to Perform list. The Packers can open a three-week practice window at any time. At the end of the three weeks, he must either move to the 53-man roster or return to the PUP list and not play this season. On Tuesday, coach Matt LaFleur was asked whether Parsons will return to practice next week. “ I sure hope so ,” LaFleur said, via Rob Demovsky of ESPN. As Demovsky notes, LaFleur's previous responses to that question "had been a hard no." Parsons tore his ACL on December 14, the same day Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes suffered the same injury. But it's very different for a quarterback and a front-seven defender. Parsons will be constantly navigating plenty of bodies and limbs, which inevitably will be hitting his legs and knees. He needs to be sure that he'll have the confidence in the repaired ACL before he takes the field again. Green Bay could use the boost defensively. At 4-3, they host the Panthers on Thursday night. After that, they face the Patriots and Vikings before the Week 11 bye. Given the three-week practice window, a return next week could mean that Parsons will return in Week 12, when the Packers visit the Rams in the NFL's first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cardinals sign WR Zay Jones
summary: Zay Jones was one of four wide receivers who tried out for the Cardinals on Tuesday.
full_text: Zay Jones was one of four wide receivers who tried out for the Cardinals on Tuesday. He joined Ronnie Bell, James Proche and Xavier Guillory on the practice field. The Cardinals are signing Jones, according to multiple reports. It is unclear whether Jones is joining the practice squad or the active roster, but the team announced it placed wide receiver Jalen Brooks on season-ending injured reserve on Tuesday. The Cardinals were already thin at the position after the trade of Marvin Harrison Jr. on Oct. 11. Jones, 31, has played nine NFL seasons, including a previous stint with the Cardinals. He appeared in 11 games for the Cardinals in 2024 and eight last season, missing time for a suspension in 2024 and for a torn Achilles in 2025. He has 20 receptions for 267 yards with the team. Jones became a free agent in August when the Texans cut him out of the preseason.
author: Charean Williams

title: Packers LB Zaire Franklin won't play Thursday night
summary: Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin will miss another game.
full_text: ' Packers linebacker Zaire Franklin will miss another game. It's not a surprise given the Packers play on Thursday night. Coach Matt LaFleur announced Tuesday that Franklin will not play against the Panthers. Franklin missed last week's game after getting accidentally kicked in Thursday's practice. He was diagnosed with a hairline fracture in his leg. The Packers did not place him on injured reserve, believing he can return after missing fewer than four games. Franklin ranks third on the team in tackles (41) and has two quarterback hits, a forced fumble and a pass breakup. Ty’Ron Hopper took Franklin's spot in the lineup on Sunday, and Isaiah McDuffie wore the green dot in Franklin's stead.
author: Charean Williams

title: Montez Sweat on suspension: What happened, happened and I'm moving forward
summary: Defensive end Montez Sweat's two-game suspension ended after last Thursday's win over the Patriots and he addressed his absence from the team's facility on Tuesday.
full_text: '' Defensive end Montez Sweat's two-game suspension ended after last Thursday's win over the Patriots and he addressed his absence from the team's facility on Tuesday. Sweat said "it was a surprise" to learn that he was being suspended for violating the performance-enhancing drug policy, but did not delve into the details of what happened beyond taking "full responsibility" for his actions. "It's definitely something I got to live with for my career," Sweat said, via Courtney Cronin of ESPN.com. "I never want to cheat the game, and I would never do it intentionally, but what happened, happened and I'm moving forward." Sweat said he was "devastated" to miss time and that it was tough to look head coach Ben Johnson "in the eye after you've done something detrimental like that to the team," but reiterated his desire to move forward from the ban. He had two sacks in the first five games and adding to that total will make it easier for everyone in Chicago to move past his absence.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cowboys waive RB Emari Demercado
summary: The Cowboys waived running back Emari Demercado on Tuesday, the team announced.
full_text: The Cowboys waived running back Emari Demercado on Tuesday, the team announced. Outside linebacker Marist Liufau and safety P.J. Locke are nearing a return from injured reserve. Dallas claimed Demercado off waivers from the Chiefs on Aug. 31. He played for Cowboys offensive coordinator Klayton Adams with the Cardinals in 2023-24. The Cowboys waived Demercado for the first time on Oct. 8. Demercado ran five times for 15 yards in two appearances for Dallas. He had 131 carries for 834 yards and three touchdowns in 40 games for the Cardinals over the past three seasons. He also caught 50 passes for 324 yards and a touchdown. The Cowboys also cut tight end D.J. Rogers from injured reserve.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jets stand to benefit from Colts' fire sale
summary: The Seahawks and 49ers hope to benefit in the near term from the trades they made with the Colts on Tuesday, but another team could wind up as a long-term winner.
full_text: The Seahawks and 49ers hope to benefit in the near term from the trades they made with the Colts on Tuesday, but another team could wind up as a long-term winner. When the Colts were in a better position a little less than a year ago, then-General Manager Chris Ballard dealt Indy's 2026 and 2027 first-round picks as well as wide receiver Adonai Mitchell to the Jets for cornerback Sauce Gardner. The Colts' collapse after that deal led to the Jets landing tight end Kenyon Sadiq with the 16th overall pick this year and the other first-round pick looks like it will come much earlier in the 2027 draft. Moving guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the 49ers will hurt the Colts' chances of winning their next 10 games and their first-round pick would be No. 7 overall if the season ended today. Should the Colts move others like running back Jonathan Taylor ahead of the deadline, the prospects for that pick would look even better. Given the dim prospects for the Jets' own pick — No. 10 at the moment — and their ownership of the higher pick between the Cowboys' and Packers' first-rounders through the Quinnen Williams trade, that's a lot of capital for the team to use in their attempt to end what will likely continue to be the league's longest postseason drought.
author: Josh Alper

title: With two trades in one day, Colts are clearly open for business
summary: The Sunday Splash!
full_text: The Sunday Splash! report regarding a potential fire sale in Indy was conditioned on the C olts’ performance in their three remaining games before the trade deadline. After only one game, they tapped the "Everything Must Go" sign in the front yard. Guard Quenton Nelson, as expected, has been traded to the Seahawks. Defensive tackle DeForest Buckner has been traded back to the 49ers, as expected. So who's next? Running back Jonathan Taylor has been the focal point of speculation, with ESPN linking him to the Packers, Seahawks, Broncos, and Vikings. The Vikings got the ultimate opportunity to scout Taylor on Sunday, when he accounted for 110 of the team's 218 total offensive yards in a 16-10 Minnesota win. Taylor averaged 5.3 yards per carry and went 38 yards for the Colts' only touchdown of the day. There's an obvious incentive to maximize 2027 draft picks, especially with the Colts' first-rounder committed to the Jets as the back end of the Sauce Gardner trade. But Taylor is under contract for two more years; they may want to keep him until the offseason, giving the next G.M. the opportunity to decide whether to retain Taylor or trade him in March. Of course, Taylor would have more value now to a team that hopes to augment its roster for a playoff push. Although the Vikings were burned 37 years ago this month by the Herschel Walker trade, it would take much less than the ridiculous haul of picks and players (which became more picks after the Cowboys cut them) to get Taylor. Taylor could make a huge difference for a team premised on a stout defense. While Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason have proven to be capable options at tailback, Taylor is among the best in the league. He has the power and speed to move the chains and, when given an opening, go the distance. Whatever happens with Taylor, it's clear the Colts aren't waiting to see what happens over the next two weekends. In a deadline-driven business, the timeline for the Colts isn't being driven by the deadline. It's being determined by getting deals done now and moving on.
author: Mike Florio

title: 49ers agree to acquire DeForest Buckner from Colts
summary: Buckner is headed back to the team that drafted him at No. 7 overall in 2016.
full_text: DeForest Buckner is headed back to the Bay. The 49ers — who traded Buckner to Indianapolis back in 2020 — have agreed to acquire Buckner from the Colts, according to multiple reports. Indianapolis will receive a 2027 fourth-round pick to complete the deal. While Buckner is in his 11th season, he’s still plenty productive from the interior of the defensive line. He’s recorded 4.0 sacks with four tackles for loss and eight QB hits so far in 2026. He’s also tallied three passes defensed and a fumble recovery. The No. 7 overall pick of the 2016 draft out of Oregon, Buckner was a key piece of San Francisco’s defense in his first four seasons, helping the club advance to Super Bowl LIV to cap the 2019 season. He registered 12.0 sacks for the 49ers in 2018 and 7.5 sacks for the club in 2019. He was traded to the Colts after his fourth season, with Indianapolis signing him to a long-term second contract. In Buckner’s 158 career games, he’s picked up 75.5 sacks, 101 tackles for loss, and 196 QB hits. Buckner has been palpably frustrated by the Colts losses in recent weeks. With an expiring contract, it's no surprise that he's been moved. It's the second high-profile trade of the day from the Colts, who earlier dealt guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Cardinals place WR Jalen Brooks on season-ending IR
summary: The Cardinals placed wide receiver Jalen Brooks on season-ending injured reserve, the team announced Tuesday.
full_text: The Cardinals placed wide receiver Jalen Brooks on season-ending injured reserve, the team announced Tuesday. Brooks announced on social media that he underwent emergency surgery on his wrist after dislocating it in Sunday's game. He played the final three quarters with the dislocation. "He didn’t say anything to anybody and just looking back at it and seeing it on tape, you could see every once in a while, he's kind of messing with it a little bit," coach Mike LaFleur said Monday, via Darren Urban of the team website. "I can't say enough about how tough that dude is." Brooks, 26, played 64 percent of the team’s offensive snaps on Sunday and made one catch for 35 yards. He finishes his season with five catches for 81 yards. The Cardinals did not announce a corresponding move. They did announce the re-signing of offensive lineman Austin Deculus and safety Wydett Williams Jr. to the practice squad. Safety Jerrick Reed II was released from the practice squad.
author: Charean Williams

title: Report: Lamar Jackson is expected to return Sunday
summary: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has not played since Oct. 4, missing the past three games with a high ankle sprain.
full_text: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has not played since Oct. 4, missing the past three games with a high ankle sprain. Ravens coach Jesse Minter on Monday expressed optimism about Jackson's availability for Sunday, and Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that Jackson is expected to return this week. Then again, Jackson was trending toward playing last week. He was limited in all three practices and initially questionable to play. Jackson was inactive for Sunday's game, a 35-13 loss to the Bengals. Minter would not confirm a CBS pregame report that Jackson woke up Saturday with increased swelling in his injured left ankle. The Ravens are 1-2 without Jackson, having averaged 17.7 points and 328.3 yards per game. "Lamar's 1-of-1, right? Two-time MVP , obviously a high-caliber player, but I just don't like the built-in excuse of why things are going a certain way," Minter said Monday, via Jamison Hensley of ESPN. "So while we know the caliber of player Lamar is and the numbers when he's out there versus when he's not, we understand all that. That's why he's who he is and why he's won the awards that he's won, but we can still operate better in those times where we don't have him for sure."
author: Charean Williams

title: Dave Canales knows opposing offenses are excited to game plan vs. Panthers' run defense
summary: The Panthers have the worst run defense in the NFL, and head coach Dave Canales knows what that means for opposing teams game planning against them.
full_text: ''' The Panthers have the worst run defense in the NFL , and head coach Dave Canales knows what that means for opposing teams game planning against them. Up next for the Panthers is a game on Thursday night against the Packers, who have the most pass-heavy offense in the NFL. Canales said today that after giving up 258 rushing yards on Sunday against the Buccaneers, he knows that the Packers will be excited by the opportunity to play against them. That means both trying to run the ball with Josh Jacobs, and trying to have Jordan Love beat them deep if the Panthers overcompensate for their run defense struggles by stacking the box. "Collectively, as a group, we have to be locked in to what they're going to try to do and how they're going to attack us," Canales said. "I'm sure they're watching the game and they're seeing 250 yards on the ground, and that's got to be appealing. For me, as an offensive-minded coach, I think about that and say, 'We can set some things up down the field by making sure we have a run game going.' That would be my approach, so I do expect them to run the ball, and we do expect Jordan to heave the ball down the field just like he does, and challenge the back half of our defense as well." The Packers, who have only had Jacobs for one game this season, have not run the ball well. Having the Panthers' defense come to town could be just the thing to fix that.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Deion Sanders says offer of $50,000 to critics was "a joke"
summary: Colorado coach Deion Sanders has addressed the comments made recently by Christopher "Uncle" Neely regarding a supposed willingness to pay critics $50,000 to not mention his name.
full_text: Colorado coach Deion Sanders has addressed the comments made recently by Christopher "Uncle" Neely regarding a supposed willingness to pay critics $50,000 to not mention his name. At a press conference on Tuesday, Sanders said it was " a joke ." "I think you misinterpreted that," Sanders said. "I said . . . I would love to give you money and not mention my name, and I want to see how far that goes. That was a joke, That's what we were saying. Like some people live on your name.” Before Sanders answered, someone off camera (presumably Neely) can be heard explaining the question. The person refers to a show from the spring in which that statement was made. Sanders did indeed previously make a comment along those lines. And it does indeed sound like a hypothetical, not an actual offer. Separately, Deion posted the following on Twitter this afternoon: " This is a lie but God bless u all. Y’all know me and have known me for years. When has it appeared that I’ve EVER cared what a man or woman has said about me? My son does my Videos and Neely is a friend." While it does appear that Sanders was not making a real offer when he talked about it previously, that's not how Neely's recent comments came off: "For the most part, the people that attack him wouldn’t be making the money they were making if he wasn’t here to attack. Which is why he told some of them , ‘Hey man, let’s just do this. I give you $50,000 to not mention my name for a year.’ And ain’t nobody took the deal yet. . . . And you love talking about this man so much, and you make so much talking of this man that you turned the deal down.” To answer the question Deion posed on Twitter ("When has it appeared that I’ve EVER cared what a man or woman has said about me?"), there is at least one tangible example of sensitivity to criticism. In 2024, for example, he refused to answer a question at a press conference from a reporter at the local CBS affiliate because of a problem he had with CBS generally. “ I’m not doing anything with CBS ,” Sanders said at the time. “Next question. . . . It ain’t got nothing to do with you. It’s above that. It ain’t got nothing to do with you. I’ve got love for you. I appreciate and respect you. It ain’t got nothing to do with you. They know what they did.” “I’m here in Denver not national,” the reporter responded. “You are who you are,” Deion replied. “CBS is CBS, all right? . . . I’m looking you in the eye as a man. I respect you. I’ve got love for you. But what they did was foul.” Regardless, Neely stated the offer — and the failure of any reporters to accept it — as if it were a real offer. Sanders has now given his side of the story that Neely created with the content and tone of his recent remarks.
author: Mike Florio

title: Packers list Matthew Golden as out of practice Tuesday
summary: The Packers turned in their second estimated injury report of the week on Tuesday and it showed no change in status for wide receiver Matthew Golden.
full_text: ' The Packers turned in their second estimated injury report of the week on Tuesday and it showed no change in status for wide receiver Matthew Golden. Golden was listed as out of practice for the second straight day. He is dealing with shoulder and foot injuries as the Packers move toward Thursday night's game against the Panthers. Golden leads the Packers with 36 catches and is second on the team with 540 receiving yards. Linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin), offensive lineman Travis Glover (knee), and center Sean Rhyan (ankle) were also listed as out of practice for the second straight day. Defensive tackles Anthony Campbell (ankle) and Devonte Wyatt (ankle) were bumped up to limited participation. Defensive end Brenton Cox (quad) and guard Aaron Banks (knee, toe) were also listed as limited while cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring) was listed as a full participant.
author: Josh Alper

title: Raiders activate WR Dont'e Thornton off of IR
summary: The Raiders have one of their offensive contributors back.
full_text: The Raiders have one of their offensive contributors back. Las Vegas announced on Tuesday that receiver Dont’e Thornton has been activated to the 53-man roster off injured reserve. Thornton has been sidelined by a hamstring injury suffered during training camp. A fourth-round pick in the 2025 draft, Thornton caught 10 passes for 135 yards in 15 games as a rookie. Las Vegas waived defensive tackle Jonah Laulu from its active roster to make room for Thornton. Laulu’s roster move was reported earlier on Tuesday. Additionally, the Raiders have released receiver Jamari Thrash from its practice squad.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Colts place CB Cam Taylor-Britt on IR, sign CB Kenneth Harris from practice squad
summary: The Colts signed cornerback Kenneth Harris to the 53-player roster from the practice squad, the team announced.
full_text: The Colts signed cornerback Kenneth Harris to the 53-player roster from the practice squad, the team announced. The Colts also placed cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt on injured reserve and signed cornerbacks Shemar Bartholomew and Natrone Brooks to the practice squad. Harris, 24, was twice elevated from the practice squad to the game-day roster. He has played in two games, seeing action on 21 defensive snaps and seven on special teams. Harris has recorded three tackles and a pass defensed this season. Taylor-Britt has a groin injury that will keep him out at least the next four games. He has totaled seven tackles, a tackle for loss, a sack, two passes defensed and six special teams stops.
author: Charean Williams

title: Seahawks announce Quenton Nelson trade, waive G Christian Haynes
summary: Guard Quenton Nelson will need to pass a physical to finalize his move to the Seahawks, but the team has already made room for him on their 53-man roster.
full_text: Guard Quenton Nelson will need to pass a physical to finalize his move to the Seahawks, but the team has already made room for him on their 53-man roster. The Seahawks confirmed that they have agreed to trade for Nelson on Tuesday afternoon. They will send a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder to the Colts in exchange for Nelson. With Nelson coming to Seattle, the Seahawks announced that they have waived guard Christian Haynes. The 2024 third-round pick has played in 31 games for the Seahawks and he made five starts this season while Anthony Bradford was out of the lineup. Haynes could return to the practice squad if he goes unclaimed. The Seahawks opened a spot by cutting tight end Josiah Deguara on Tuesday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Giants to sign RB Gregory Desrosiers off Chargers practice squad
summary: The Giants will be without Tyrone Tracy for at least the next four games because of a hamstring injury and they'll pluck a player from another team to fill the opening on their active roster.
full_text: The Giants will be without Tyrone Tracy for at least the next four games because of a hamstring injury and they'll pluck a player from another team to fill the opening on their active roster. General Manager Joe Schoen announced that the Giants will sign running back Gregory Desrosiers off of the Chargers' practice squad. Desrosiers signed with the Chargers after going undrafted this year. He played at Louisville, UMass and Memphis over the last six seasons. Cam Skattebo and Devin Singletary will be the top backs on the Giants' depth chart with Tracy out of action. Phil Mafah and Grant Finley are on their practice squad.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: Raiders waiving DT Jonah Laulu
summary: The Raiders are moving on from one of their young defensive linemen.
full_text: The Raiders are moving on from one of their young defensive linemen. Per Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report, Las Vegas is waiving Jonah Laulu. Laulu, 26, joined the Raiders when he was claimed off waivers in 2024. He was a Colts seventh-round pick that year who did not make the initial 53-man roster. He appeared in all 17 games for Las Vegas as a rookie and all 17 games for the team last season, starting 15 of them. But this season, he had been on the field for just 32 percent of the team’s defensive snaps in five games. He was then a healthy scratch for Sunday’s loss to the Rams. Laulu has registered 5.5 career sacks with 11 tackles for loss and 12 QB hits. He had 4.0 sacks last season.
author: Myles Simmons

title: One year later, regrading the 10 biggest deals from the 2025 NFL trade deadline
summary: From the Colts' disastrous gamble on Sauce Gardner to the Eagles' productive Jaelan Phillips rental, here is how last year's biggest deals have aged
full_text:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline has a tough act to follow. Last year saw 27 players traded in-season, which was the most in a single year in a quarter of a century. This is shaping up to be an active push to Nov. 10, but will it rival the mayhem of 2025? That remains to be determined. It is the quality of the transactions that matters more than the volume. Last year can be both a blueprint for how to pull off beneficial midseason moves and for what to avoid, because the high number of trades included multiple examples of both good deals and bad.
No deal withstood the test of time worse than the Sauce Gardner trade. It has since been panned as one of the most one-sided transactions in recent NFL history and should be a reminder that just because a player carries All-Pro bona fides, he might not be worth mortgaging the future to acquire.
The most beneficial trades are often the ones made on the margins, where teams secure mid- or late-round draft capital for players on expiring contracts. These tend to be mutually beneficial, as one team lands an instant-impact rental while the other secures future assets in exchange for someone who was destined to walk away for free. Last year's trade deadline featured a plethora of such deals.
After the 2025 deadline, we ranked every major trade . And now with the benefit of hindsight, let's re-grade the top 10.
The Gardner trade aged so poorly for Colts general manager Chris Ballard that it became a primary reason why the franchise fired him in the middle of the season. Nobody could have foreseen the stark regression the two-time All-Pro cornerback experienced upon his arrival in Indianapolis, but it is very real, and it looks awful in the context of what Ballard gave up to acquire him. Gardner has played the worst football of his career in his 17 games with the Colts, while the Jets constructed an exciting young offensive core with the assets they received in return -- plus they still have another first-round pick to add to it.
Since the Colts are trending downward this year and may emerge as sellers at the deadline as they barrel toward a potential rebuild, this is the exact situation in which they would prefer to own a 2027 first-rounder. Instead, with every loss they add to their tally, they watch the Jets lick their lips and prepare to cash in.
The Dallas defense is still a disaster, even with Williams offering solid run-stopping ability in the middle of the line. His six tackles for loss through the first six games of the year were the most by a Cowboys defensive tackle since 2013 and were tied for the most of any defensive tackle in the league this year. On an individual level, he is delivering what the Cowboys paid for when they parted with all those draft picks and signed him to a three-year, $105.9 million extension, even if it is short of the All-Pro caliber of production he logged at his peak in New York. The problem is that it has not translated to improvement on the defensive side of the ball at large.
On the Jets' side, they released Smith and have gotten practically nothing out of Ponds in the first five games of his career. He could still develop into a good cornerback, but he has only seen 59 snaps of action and allowed three catches and a touchdown on five targets in that small sample size. If he does not pan out, it will come down to the 2027 first-rounder to save this trade. That player needs to turn into a Pro Bowler to at least match what New York gave up in Williams.
The idea behind trading for Flacco was to keep the offense afloat last season until Joe Burrow returned from turf toe. It worked to an extent, as the veteran delivered a string of entertaining passing performances, including a 470-yard outburst and three consecutive games of at least 33 points. The defense was the real issue and the main reason Flacco went just 1-5 as the starter. At face value, the trade did not move the needle because of the poor record. But the offense was better with Flacco than Jake Browning , at least. Plus, the pick swap gave the Bengals another interesting young wide receiver.
Flacco was never going to be long for Cleveland as it churned through quarterbacks, so to package him in a trade swap that saw the Browns move up a round was a win for a non-contending team. A small win, but one nonetheless.
The Dugger deal was effectively a salary dump for the Patriots and one that benefited the Steelers immensely. The safety had fallen out of favor in New England to the point where the franchise bought out the remainder of a four-year extension they signed in 2024 in order to move him. It was an admission that the deal had failed and cost the Patriots $5.4 million in cash, plus roster bonuses.
Dugger was a winner from the trade because he reached unrestricted free agency two years early. The Steelers also came away on top because they got a productive version of Dugger for half a season at essentially no cost. He filled a hole in the lineup following DeShon Elliott's injury and delivered an impact with two interceptions (one of them a pick six), five passes defended, a sack, two tackles for loss and a safety. Not bad for a nine-game rental.
A third-rounder is a steep price to pay for eight games of Phillips, but when all is said and done, this trade should end up as a good one for the Eagles. Phillips was a pleasant addition to the defense, playing some of the best football of his career on a per-game basis to help Philadelphia secure a playoff spot. The Eagles elected not to re-sign him at the high price tag of four years and $120 million (which the Panthers awarded him in free agency), but they will not come away empty-handed, as his departure should net them a third-round compensatory pick in the 2027 draft. They will effectively get back what they put in.
Meanwhile, the Dolphins were unlikely to sign Phillips to an extension, too. They manifested a third-round pick instead of getting nothing in return for what would have been an exit in free agency. Everyone won here with the compensatory pick, essentially creating an invisible third piece in the trade.
Last year's Chargers offensive line was a MASH unit, and the 2026 group is only slightly healthier. Penning arrived midway through last season as an emergency fill-in and was called into action early this year, too, before he suffered a concussion of his own and landed on injured reserve on Oct. 10. That Los Angeles re-signed him at the end of his rookie contract salvaged some value from the trade, but this still is a bust of a former first-round pick whose main contribution is depth. His PFF pass-blocking grade in 2026 is the worst among all 74 qualified guards.
It was a shame that Penning did not catch on in New Orleans, considering the Saints used the No. 19 overall pick on him in 2022. At least he did not walk away for nothing.
Mike Macdonald said Monday that "early returns are positive" on Rashid Shaheed's knee after he suffered an injury in Sunday night's win over the Chiefs . His availability for the rest of the year would go a long way in cementing this trade as a fruitful one for the Seahawks, but regardless of his health, Seattle seems pleased with where it stands. Shaheed was never supposed to be more than a secondary receiving option behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and, in fact, is more of a gadget offensive weapon and special teams threat than a downfield target. He returned two kickoffs for touchdowns last season, including one in the playoffs en route to a Super Bowl ring, and earned himself a three-year, $51 million extension at the end of his 12-game run in Seattle in 2025.
Shaheed was similarly a boom-or-bust asset in New Orleans and one who would have been phased out eventually had he re-signed as the Saints identified Chris Olave , Devaughn Vele and (once healthy) Jordyn Tyson as the future of their receiving corps. Turning his expiring contract into a pair of high-end Day 3 picks should be viewed as a success since the Saints are no worse off at…
author: Carter Bahns

title: Prisco's Week 8 NFL picks: Packers over Panthers, Lions hand Vikings their first loss
summary: Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 8 picks, including the Bills to top the Ravens in a high-scoring game
full_text:
Going to the dogs last week turned out to be dog doodoo. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night.
I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1.
So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use.
One game at a time. One week at a time.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going.
Pick: Packers 31, Panthers 24
Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it.
The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk.
Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10
The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week.
Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21
The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it.
Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13
Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it.
This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it.
Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20
This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it.
The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London.
Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16
The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close.
Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20
The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush.
Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14
The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it.
Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14
This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it.
Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16
The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it.
Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17
author: Pete Prisco

title: DeForest Buckner trade grades: 49ers get reunion with three-time Pro Bowler, Colts work toward rebuild
summary: The trade makes sense for both sides
full_text:
On Tuesday, the Indianapolis Colts made two major moves towards a rebuild with the trades of offensive guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner . Nelson's trade came first, with Indy sending him to the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks for a third-round pick and a future fifth-round pick.
Their second big news of the day was Indianapolis trading Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick , according to ESPN . Buckner will now have a second stint with the team that drafted him at No. 7 overall in 2016.
These Colts trades come just about a week after firing general manager Chris Ballard. Sitting at 2-4 at the time of the firing, and 2-5 now, Indy is clearly beginning their much-needed rebuild and making those big changes along with it.
The Niners are the opposite of a rebuild, with sights set on the playoffs and beyond. They now added a reliable defensive big man who can help get them there.
Both sides can take many positives from the deal, with the edge going to the Niners.
The Colts situation, sitting at 2-5, firing their GM and needing to rebuild, certainly doesn't earn a B+, but this trade does. Freeing up cap space and getting the most value for their players while they can is a smart move on their part.
If the Colts kept Buckner and he signed with another team this offseason, the highest compensatory draft pick they could've received for him was a fifth-rounder. The 11-year veteran was likely going elsewhere at the end of the year anyway, emphasizing recently that at this stage in his career he wants to play winning football.
After their loss to the Tennessee Titans , who went into the contest without a win, in Week 6, Buckner said he was "frustrated" and added , "I'm sick and tired of the same song and dance every year."
He now gets to play meaningful football, and the Colts get the most value in return. Instead of a 2028 fifth-round pick, they now have a 2027 fourth-round pick.
Tuesday's moves have cleared over $17.7 million in salary cap space and added three draft picks.
The 49ers' time to win is now, which means all chips are in. The Niners are one of the NFC's and the NFL's best teams at 6-1. Despite an abundance of injuries, they've managed to put on solid performances.
Adding some security on the defensive line gives the team that added assurance, along with a veteran presence, someone with postseason experience and someone they know.
Defensive tackles C.J. West and Alfred Collins are on IR, so the Niners were already in the market to cushion that position. Buckner has already spent multiple seasons with the team, so he not only knows the front office and schemes and has played with some of these guys before, but he will also have that extra fire that comes from a reunion with a former team.
Not to mention, his new/former teammates are happy:
DEFOOOOO THE BOYS ARE BACK @DeForestBuckner @JuiceCheck44 @49ers pic.twitter.com/jUoMNJ96Dx
This season, Buckner has 31 combined tackles, four sacks and three pass breakups in seven starts. In 158 games, including 153 starts, he has 683 combined tackles, including 101 for a loss, 75.5 sacks, 31 pass deflections, nine forced fumbles, 11 fumble recoveries, nine forced fumbles and two touchdowns.
When the Niners do make that playoff push, if they do as they are expected and make it to the postseason, Buckner will know that song and dance. He was there when the 49ers made a Super Bowl run, losing to the Kansas City Chiefs to end the 2019 season. He started all three playoff games that season, finishing with 12 combined tackles, four quarterback hits, 2.5 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery,
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: DeForest Buckner trade: Colts send DT to 49ers in exchange for 2027 fourth-round pick
summary: Buckner began his NFL career with the Niners as a first round pick in 2016
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts announced they are trading defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick, according to ESPN . Buckner will now reunite with the team that drafted him at No. 7 overall in 2016.
Buckner played for the Niners through the 2019 season, before joining the Colts ahead of the 2020 season. The three-time Pro Bowler will now head back to Levi's Stadium to help the Niners' defensive line.
This season, he has 31 combined tackles, four sacks and three pass breakups.
The 32-year-old has 683 combined tackles, including 101 for a loss, 75.5 sacks, 31 pass deflections, nine forced fumbles, 11 fumble recoveries, nine forced fumbles and two touchdowns in his 11-year career. Of the 158 games he's played in, he's started 153, including all seven so far this year.
49ers star tight end George Kittle celebrated the news on social media:
DEFOOOOO THE BOYS ARE BACK @DeForestBuckner @JuiceCheck44 @49ers pic.twitter.com/jUoMNJ96Dx
Buckner joins a defense with DT Osa Odighizuwa , DE Mykel Williams , LB Fred Warner and DE Nick Bosa , who has missed multiple games with a calf injury. The Niners defense has allowed 299.3 total yards per game, fourth-best in the league. Their run defense is their strongest area, with just 89.0 yards allowed per game, fifth-best in the league and their three rushing touchdowns allowed are tied for best.
The Colts currently sit at 2-5 and second in the AFC South. They fired their general manager, Chris Ballard, and, with the changes, rumors surfaced that they would be part of a major trade as they turn to new management.
It was a busy day for Indy as it also dealt Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks . With the two big moves on Tuesday, the Colts added three draft picks (two in 2027 and one in 2028) and cleared over $17.7 million in salary cap space.
Running back Jonathan Taylor and wide receiver Josh Downs are two more Colts players who could be involved in a trade soon.
The 49ers are in a much different spot than what Buckner is coming from at 6-1 and in first place in the NFC West. Their next game is against the Las Vegas Raiders , who are currently on a four-game losing streak, on Nov. 8.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: NFL trade deadline: Four Eagles, a star Colt and two starting QBs included among top 25 candidates
summary: Saquon Barkley, Jonathan Taylor, Kirk Cousins and more could fetch returns at the trade deadline
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is exactly two weeks away. That means the hot stove will heat up considerably fairly soon. We've already seen multiple high-profile deals this season, with Joey Porter Jr . heading to the Cowboys , Marvin Harrison Jr . heading to the Texans and Quenton Nelson heading to the Seahawks , and we could see several more over the next 14 days, given how wide open the league appears to be at the moment.
With that in mind, we wanted to take a look at some of the top targets who could be on the move. We ranked the top 10 situations that bear the most watching, but with a twist. Some of them are team-wide, meaning there are multiple targets that interested teams could pursue over the next two weeks. There are 25 targets in all.
So without further ado, here's the list...
Saquon Barkley's contract, with all the various option bonuses included, makes dealing with him somewhat financially complicated, but given the Eagles ' struggles, his age, and the fact that teams are looking for explosiveness at running back these days, he makes sense as a target for needy teams. His current injury situation muddies the picture a bit, but that could be cleared up in the coming days and weeks as he gets further away from the hamstring pull.
Moro Ojomo is in the final year of his rookie contract. The Eagles just paid big money to two defensive tackles ( Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis ), so they probably can't afford to keep Ojomo around. He's 25 years old and has shown production upside with 6 sacks last season.
If the Eagles want to get aggressive, they can consider dealing both him and Nolan Smith , whose fifth-year option they picked up for next season but who they probably can't afford to keep in the longer term. Smith is more of a force in the run game than as a pass rusher, but that could still be valuable for teams that need help on the edge.
Dallas Goedert , meanwhile, signed a renegotiated contract with the Eagles this past offseason and is carrying only a $1.3 million base salary. He's not the most dynamic tight end these days, but he's a reliable pass-catcher and blocker, and any team that needs an additional tight end (teams love multi-tight end sets these days) could get interested for a small price.
Nelson is already on the move, traded to the Seahawks for a pair of draft picks. Jonathan Taylor is one of the best running backs in the NFL and has been able to remain productive even while the Colts ' offense has fallen apart around him. (He's only at 4.2 yards per carry, but he's carrying a 55% rushing success rate, per Pro-Football-Reference.) He's the type of explosive back who can change an offense in the way Kenneth Walker III did for the Chiefs . The contract isn't prohibitive for trade purposes, as the Colts would incur only $10 million in dead money next year if they move him. DeForest Buckner has also been traded away .
It would be pretty surprising if Jeffery Simmons were dealt away, considering he recently signed a three-year, $105.8 million contract extension that made him the highest-paid defensive tackle in the NFL. But the Titans are going nowhere fast, and Simmons is by far their best asset if they want to kick-start yet another rebuild, which seems to be in the offing. Tennessee would take on a bunch of dead money by dealing him, but it might be worth it if they can get as much draft capital as he's worth.
Amani Hooker is a very good, very versatile safety (he's played 232 snaps in the box, 127 as a deep safety and 56 as a slot corner so far this year), and those are valuable around the NFL. He still has three years left on his contract, including 2026, so there is a team-control aspect that would be valuable to a potentially acquiring team.
Tony Pollard is in the final year of his deal with only a $6.7 million base salary. He's 29 years old, but if you look under the hood, the numbers show he's actually running pretty well so far this season. He's 10th in yards after contact per attempt among the 39 running backs with 50-plus carries, for example, according to Tru Media. He's also 12th in explosive run rate. He can still play, and help a team in need of a committee back.
Calvin Ridley has completely fallen out of favor in Tennessee and could potentially help a team in need of depth-chart wide receiver help.
Khalil Mack is on a one-year deal with an $8 million base salary. He's got three sacks in six games and has played 71% of the Chargers ' defensive snaps. He's not going to be the player he once was, but any team in need of a rotational pass rusher should give the Chargers a call to see if they can get him for a late pick.
Tuli Tuipulotu only has two sacks in the Chargers' six games, but a deeper look at the numbers reveals a player playing better than that. He's 23rd in pressure rate among 148 players with 100 or more pass-rush snaps, according to Tru Media, and 18th in havoc play rate. He's still just 24 years old and you can get out ahead of his free agency by acquiring him now.
Derwin James , like Jeffery Simmons, recently signed a contract extension, so it would be somewhat surprising to see him get dealt. But he's 31 years old, the Chargers are terrible, and he's one of their most valuable assets. His base salaries for the next three years are also pretty high ($17.5 million, $24.6 million and $21.5 million), so the return might not be as much as the Chargers would be looking for.
Johnston only has 8 catches for 165 scoreless yards this season, and he's seemingly been surpassed in the target pecking order. He also has an $18 million salary for next season after the Chargers picked up his fifth-year option. So the return is likely to be low, but it's hard to imagine that L.A. wants to keep him around.
Budda Baker has base salaries of $14.4 million and $16.1 million this year and next, but he's a valuable enough player to make those price tags worth it. He's extremely versatile and can play both the run and the pass, whether lined up deep or in the box. He's 30 years old and still likely has several quality seasons left under his belt. The Cardinals aren't going to contend for the postseason, and Baker is their best asset for future value.
Josh Sweat is having a down year, both sack-wise (2 in 7 games) and in terms of his pressure rate (7.9%). And his contract doesn't exactly make that type of production attractive. But his track record over the long term, up to and including last year, is much more impressive, and teams could bet that he has a bounce-back in a more favorable environment. He probably wants a new contract, but that could be worked out once you see him play for your team.
Jacoby Brissett is clearly not the long-term answer under center for the Cardinals, and they might turn to Carson Beck sooner rather than later so they can see what they have in the third-round pick before making a decision on whether to select a quarterback in next year's draft. That makes Brissett expendable, and some team looking for a quality backup or fill-in for an injured starter could be interested in his services.
Win over the Jets notwithstanding, the Dolphins look like arguably the worst team in the league this season. Zach Sieler , though, remains a quality player. He hasn't been at his best this season (nobody on the Dolphins has), but we've seen high upside as both a run defender and a pass rusher from the defensive interior. If you can tap back into that, his base salaries over the next few years are very affordable ($44.5 million from 2027 through 2029, none of which is guaranteed).
Jordyn Brooks , like Jeffery Simmons and Derwin James, recently signed an extension. But his deal actually made him easier to trade and gave the Dolphins the benefit of selling to an acquiring team, knowing they'd have Brooks under team control for multiple years. With the emergence of rookie Jacob Rodriguez and Brooks having recently turned 29 years old, they could look to deal him for a pretty sizable return.
