title: Quenton Nelson trade grades: Seahawks add eight-time Pro Bowler, while Colts look to sell pieces
summary: Seattle shores up protection for Sam Darnold with an eight-time Pro Bowler, while Indianapolis opens the door to sell more
full_text:
The reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks made a splashy move ahead of the trade deadline, as they acquired former Indianapolis Colts eight-time Pro Bowl offensive guard Quenton Nelson for a third-round pick and a future fifth-round pick.
The 2-5 Colts were thought to be sellers ahead of the trade deadline, having already fired general manager Chris Ballard. Interim general manager Ed Dodds has a relationship with Seahawks general manager John Schneider, as he worked in Seattle from 2007-2016 as a scout and senior personnel executive. The Colts have a couple of intriguing trade pieces on expiring deals, including Nelson, who now finds himself on a contender. According to The Ringer , Seattle will pay the remaining $9.78 million on Nelson's deal.
The former No. 6 overall pick in the 2018 NFL Draft out of Notre Dame has long been regarded as one of the best offensive guards in the NFL , having earned eight straight Pro Bowl nods and three First Team All-Pro selections from 2018-2020. Not only is Nelson effective at protecting quarterbacks from interior pass rushers, but he's also incredibly durable, having not missed a game since the 2021 season.
Let's attempt to grade this massive trade.
In seven games played this season, Nelson has allowed six pressures and zero sacks from his left guard spot, according to TruMedia. The Seahawks' offensive line has struggled in 2026, especially on the interior, where they've allowed the highest pressure rate in the NFL, per CBS Sports Research. While Sam Darnold was kept clean on Sunday night against the Kansas City Chiefs , he was hit 17 times and sacked five times in the Week 6 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos .
PFF ranked Seattle's offensive line as the No. 9 unit entering Week 7, pointing out that the right side was a weak spot. With the addition of Nelson, the Seahawks will likely move former first-round pick Grey Zabel to right guard, per ESPN .
It's true that Nelson could be playing for another team in 2027, but the Seahawks have traded for expiring deals before and re-signed those players. It happened just last year with wide receiver/returner Rashid Shaheed .
Plus, the compensation Seattle gave up for a top offensive guard makes this an "A" grade.
Adam Schefter points out that the Seahawks should have five compensatory picks in this upcoming draft after losing Kenneth Walker III , Tariq Woolen , Coby Bryant and Boye Mafe in free agency. They also get a third-round pick after former assistant general manager Nolan Teasley was hired to be the new GM of the Minnesota Vikings . Seattle has capital to utilize, and this looks like a wise investment.
It's hard for the Colts to "win" this kind of trade. Not only are they selling off elite talent at a discount, but a move like this also signals that the Colts' 2026 season is over. They aren't the sleeper in the AFC South fans hoped they would be, and it just opens the door for other players like Jonathan Taylor or DeForest Buckner to be moved. Remember, the Colts do not own their 2027 first-round pick after sending it to the New York Jets for Sauce Gardner last year.
One question I have is if the Colts waited two more weeks to trade Nelson, could they have fetched a better package? We'll never know. ESPN reports the Green Bay Packers , Chicago Bears and Philadelphia Eagles all showed interest in Nelson prior to Tuesday.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: 2027 Super Bowl halftime show: Jay-Z picks himself to perform for Super Bowl LXI
summary: This is a public service announcement sponsored by Roc Nation
full_text:
The moment we've all been waiting for is here: the NFL halftime show performer announcement. Jay-Z and his company, Roc Nation, are in charge of selecting the performer, and the rapper has chosen himself.
Jay-Z, a New York native, is bringing East Coast hip-hop to the West Coast.
The 56-year-old will take the Super Bowl LXI halftime stage on February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. The stadium is home to the Los Angeles Rams and Los Angeles Chargers.
The announcement was made across social media with a video. The video was playing "Public Service Announcement" with Jay-Z himself sitting on a stage.
Jay-Z it is! Perfect. pic.twitter.com/L6xnBfedeX
"From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl Halftime stage, this has been a journey," Jay-Z said, via press release. "Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world's biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true."
This marks the first time the rap mogul will perform during the halftime show in any capacity and according to NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell, it's been years in the making.
"For several years, we've had the privilege of working closely with Jay-Z and Roc Nation, and I've seen the extraordinary impact he has had on the Super Bowl Halftime Show," Goodell said. "When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him. I couldn't be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring to the Super Bowl stage."
Roc Nation partnered with the NFL in 2019 to produce the halftime show, and since then the 89-time Grammy nominee has been a key decision-maker on who will perform on the biggest stage in football.
The "99 Problems" singer has not announced if he will have any special guests, but since the NFL typically throws in a few surprises for these performances, there is a good chance that pattern will continue. One name that could show up at the Valentine's Day game is Jay-Z's Valentine, Beyoncé.
The superstar singer previously performed in two halftime shows. She headlined the 2013 halftime show and performed with Coldplay and Bruno Mars at halftime in 2016. She also sang the national anthem at Super Bowl XXXVIII in 2001, in her hometown of Houston. On Christmas Day 2024, she took the stage during halftime once again in her home city, for what is commonly referred to as the "Beyonce Bowl.
Beyoncé is no stranger to NFL performances, and considering the two have toured together and have numerous songs, it would make sense.
HOV is currently on the JAŸ-Z30 Tour, celebrating the 30th anniversary of his debut studio album "Reasonable Doubt" and the 25th anniversary of "Blueprint."
The last time a rapper headlined the halftime show was two years ago when Kendrick Lamar performed and brought out special guest SZA. Other rappers to take the Super Bowl halftime show this decade include Eminem, Snoop Dogg, Dr. Dre and Lil Jon.
The Super Bowl is historically the most-watched game of the year and the halftime show is historically the most-watched performance of the year. Last year, Bad Bunny was the halftime performer. For a look at every Super Bowl performer in NFL history, click here .
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Quenton Nelson trade: Seahawks acquire All-Pro guard from Colts for two draft picks, per report
summary: Indianapolis has begun selling off pieces prior to the Nov. 10 trade deadline
full_text:
One of the biggest dominoes of the trade deadline has already fallen. The defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks are acquiring All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts , according to ESPN . As for the compensation that Indy is getting in return for Nelson, The Ringer reports that the Seahawks are sending over a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick.
Nelson, 30, is in the final year of his contract, so this currently should be viewed as a half-season rental for Seattle. That said, they could always deploy the franchise tag or extend Nelson to keep him for the long haul, which is something the franchise has done before. For instance, they extended both Leonard Williams and Rasheed Shahid after acquiring them on expiring deals in the past. According to The Ringer , Seattle will pay the remaining $9.777 million on Nelson's deal.
By acquiring Nelson, who has long been viewed as one of the best interior linemen in the league, it gives their offensive line some flexibility. With Nelson, he can come in and assume his typical left guard position, which would allow 2025 first-round pick Grey Zabel to move to right guard, which he played at North Dakota State.
In seven games played this season, Nelson has allowed just six pressures and no sacks, according to TruMedia. He's allowed just five sacks over the last five seasons, which will be a welcome sight for Sam Darnold . The six-time All-Pro (three first-team) will also help Seattle's ground game, which is getting healthier with the looming returns of backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price .
After beating the Chiefs on Sunday night, the Seahawks enter Week 8 with a 4-3 record that has them in second place in the NFC West and positioned as the No. 8 seed in the NFC.
As for the Colts, they have been eyed as a seller ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline following their 2-5 start to the season and the recent firing of general manager Chris Ballard. Nelson, who has been with the organization since being the No. 6 overall pick at the 2018 NFL Draft out of Notre Dame, was one of the key players rumored to be on the block. He is the first to be dealt as they fill the cupboard back up with draft capital before embarking on what most view as a full rebuild.
As a reminder, the Colts do not own their 2027 first-round pick, shipping that selection away last deadline to acquire cornerback Sauce Gardner.
Outside of Nelson, running back Jonathan Taylor and pass rusher DeForest Buckner are other possible trade chips Indy may ship out before the deadline.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Tank, Eagles tank? Reeling Philadelphia on verge of entering Jeremiah Smith sweepstakes
summary: A five-game slide and mounting injuries have Philadelphia spiraling toward the top of the draft, where Ohio State's generational wide receiver awaits
full_text:
With their 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys , the Philadelphia Eagles have now fallen to 2-5. This is the Eagles' worst seven-game start to a season in five years, while Philly has now lost five straight games for the first time since 2016.
Monday night felt like a turning point in more ways than one. Quarterback Tanner McKee didn't exactly impress in his second start of the season; the Eagles' defensive front got pushed around by the Cowboys, Dak Prescott threw for three touchdowns and wasn't sacked once, while Javonte Williams had the best performance by a Cowboys running back in years, rushing for 155 yards and a touchdown. However, the Cowboys have a losing record for a reason. If that squad can drop 38 points on you in front of your fans in prime time, what does it say about your team?
It doesn't look like Jalen Hurts is going to return this season due to his blood clot situation, and your other top offensive players, Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith, are currently battling hamstring issues. Is this season already over for Philadelphia? Could the Eagles become legitimate sellers at the Nov. 10 trade deadline? Here's another question to consider: Are the Eagles about to enter the Jeremiah Smith sweepstakes?
CBS Sports NFL analyst Bryant McFadden thinks that if the Eagles lose to the 1-4-1 Washington Commanders next Sunday night, it's a conversation we'll have to entertain.
"If the Eagles lose to the Commanders, get ready for the Jeremiah Smith sweepstakes." 😳 @BMac_SportsTalk thinks the Eagles' season is soon coming to an end if they don't turn it around. #Scoreboard #final pic.twitter.com/JR1z9dzwsg
If you were unaware, Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith is viewed as the top prospect in this upcoming draft. Through Week 8, he ranks second in the FBS with 984 yards receiving and 12 touchdowns on 52 receptions, and is listed as the favorite to win the Heisman Trophy over at DraftKings Sportsbook (+122).
Smith has caught 39 touchdowns in his collegiate career, which is tied for most in the Big Ten all-time with Braylon Edwards . While he's in the midst of his third season, Smith already ranks first in Ohio State history in career receptions (215), receiving yards (3,542) and receiving touchdowns (39).
The stats are impressive, but so is the physical makeup. Smith is 6-foot-4, 222 pounds, and looks like he runs a pretty impressive 40 time. The rare combination of size, speed and production makes him one of the best wide receiver prospects we've ever seen. Who can you even compare Smith to? Maybe Julio Jones or Calvin Johnson .
You may say that the Eagles' top positional need is not wide receiver, which is completely fair. But that's how good of a prospect Smith is. DraftKings has him listed at +200 to be the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft . This class was supposed to be a generational quarterback draft, but that simply hasn't been the case. Arch Manning has struggled, and Dante Moore disappointed before he was unfortunately sidelined for the season with a concussion. Miami signal-caller Darian Mensah may be the only quarterback who has lived up to expectations, with Drew Mestemaker as the surprise dark horse.
The Eagles could potentially trade the No. 1 overall pick if they "win" that selection, but it's fun to speculate what an Eagles wide receiver room would look like with Smith in the fold. It could feature three Biletnikoff Award winners in Jeremiah Smith, Makai Lemon and DeVonta Smith!
Sure, the Eagles appear to be out of the running for a Super Bowl this year, but what are their odds of being the worst team in the NFL ? There are three one-win teams in the Commanders, Tennessee Titans and Miami Dolphins , and a winless team in the 0-6 Los Angeles Chargers . According to Tankathon , the Eagles' remaining schedule is middle-of-the-road (No. 15 overall).
Thanks to DraftKings Sportsbook, we actually have odds for the NFL team that will register the fewest regular season wins. As of now, there are five teams with better odds than the Eagles to secure the top pick in the draft.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Jerry Jones on a possible role for Troy Aikman with the Cowboys: 'Don't rule it out'
summary: Aikman won three Super Bowls with the Cowboys in the 1990s
full_text:
Jerry Jones is the owner and general manager of the Dallas Cowboys . That much is not going to change, no matter what. We know that not only from years of watching him operate, but also from his direct quotes over the nearly 40 years that he's owned the team.
But that doesn't mean there can't or won't be changes and/or additions to the Cowboys' front office. And apparently, we shouldn't close the door on something like that happening with a prominent former Cowboys quarterback: Troy Aikman.
Jones was asked during a Tuesday morning radio appearance on 105.3 The Fan about the possibility of Aikman joining the Cowboys in a major role, and he didn't rule it out.
"The answer is not that necessarily we're going to do something more direct with the team at this time, but don't rule it out," Jones said, via The Athletic . "It's very possible."
Aikman is currently employed as the lead analyst on ESPN's "Monday Night Football" broadcast, and has spent the last 26 years calling games for either ESPN or FOX. But he was also recently hired as a consultant for the Miami Dolphins , whom he helped during their search for a new general manager, which ultimately resulted in their hiring former Packers executive Jon-Eric Sullivan.
Of course, Aikman is better known for having won three Super Bowls with the Cowboys in the 1990s, so he has extensive ties to the organization. However, he's also been openly critical of the team -- up to and including Jerry Jones himself -- in the past.
"I think that teams and organizations, whether it's sports, business, I think it all does start at the top, good or bad," Aikman said this offseason when discussing the Cowboys' Super Bowl drought. "I think it starts at the top. I don't think Jerry would shy away from that. I think Jerry would certainly take responsibility. He'll take accountability if and when they win, and I think then you have to take responsibility when it hasn't worked out. And it hasn't worked out."
It's interesting that Jones would still consider potentially bringing Aikman into the organization in the wake of those and other comments that he's made over the years in his capacity as a broadcaster and analyst. But ultimately, Jones will do whatever it takes to bring attention to the Cowboys, and hiring Aikman in some capacity would certainly do that. Whether it would result in their actually getting back to and winning the Super Bowl is, obviously, another story.
This year's Cowboys team fancied itself a Super Bowl contender coming into the season, for example, but has instead been up and down at best. The Cowboys did snap their two-game losing skid with a win over the Eagles on Monday night, but Aikman himself remained unconvinced that their latest win was a sign that they're contenders again.
"Eh, not really. Not really. And I don't mean that as a negative," Aikman said when asked that very question during an appearance on the postgame edition of SportsCenter with Scott Van Pelt. "This is a beat-up Philadelphia team. To come in here and win tonight, I mean, let's not get carried away. They kind of did what you would expect them to do."
Dallas is just 3-4 after the victory, sitting behind the New York Giants in the NFC East standings. The Cowboys do have a somewhat favorable schedule coming up, with games against the Arizona Cardinals , Indianapolis Colts , Tennessee Titans and the Eagles again over the next five weeks, but we've seen them stumble even with a favorable schedule before. (They also have a game against the San Francisco 49ers during that stretch.)
We likely won't get a better idea of their contender status until the stretch surrounding their bye week, when they play the Seattle Seahawks , Los Angeles Rams , Jacksonville Jaguars and Giants in succession. If yet another year goes by where they don't accomplish what Jones wants to accomplish, perhaps a significant change like hiring Aikman for a front-office or consultant role is something that comes to fruition next offseason.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Raiders have 'no controversy' at QB as Klint Kubiak commits to Kirk Cousins over Fernando Mendoza
summary: Kubiak said Mendoza will play this season, but with Cousins locked into the lineup, when will his opportunity arise?
full_text:
In the immediate aftermath of the Las Vegas Raiders ' fourth consecutive loss, a 35-21 trouncing at home against the Los Angeles Rams , coach Klint Kubiak said he would consider "everything" including a quarterback change in the search for improvement. A day later, though, the first-year coach announced that Kirk Cousins will remain the starter indefinitely while Fernando Mendoza continues to watch from the sidelines.
The goal remains to win now even as the Raiders slip below .500 at 3-4 on the year. And Kubiak said Cousins gives them the best chance to do so, especially in the Week 8 road game against the New York Jets .
"Kirk is our starting quarterback," Kubiak said . "There is no controversy there. He is playing at a very high level. He's gotta continue to do that for us to win, and we've gotta keep helping all the areas around him. Excited for him to go play here against the Jets."
It would be unfair to pin the four-game losing streak primarily on Cousins. He has been one of the Raiders' top individual performers even in defeat. His 1,877 passing yards on the year rank third among all quarterbacks, and he is a top-12 signal-caller by passer rating. This has been a renaissance year of sorts for the veteran, who clearly fits well in Kubiak's system.
At some point, though, the Raiders will need to see what they have in Mendoza. They did not draft him with the No. 1 overall pick in April to keep him on the bench. There may reach a point in the not-so-distant future when Las Vegas slips out of contention for the postseason and turns its attention to next year and beyond with what it hopes is its long-term answer at quarterback. But until that time comes, Cousins continues to make it clear that he is capable of winning games.
Although Kubiak committed to Cousins as the No. 1 quarterback for the foreseeable future, he did note that Mendoza "is going to play football" at some point this season.
"We have a plan," Kubiak said. "We don't have a timeline for that. Kirk's playing really well. We're in the hunt. It's really important that we keep playing really well behind him and continue to develop Fernando. But Fernando's going to play at some point. It's not going to be this week."
One logical juncture at which the Raiders could make a change is during their bye week, which does not arrive until Week 13. That would allow for at least another month of attempting to compete for position in the AFC West and conference Wild Card race while also guaranteeing that Mendoza would have some runway at the end of the season to stack important rookie-year starts. If the Raiders continue on their present trajectory, they should be out of the playoff mix when they hit the bye.
Should they make the move during the bye, Mendoza would have an additional week to mesh with the other starters on the practice field. He would then receive a comfortable landing spot for his first career start at home against the winless Chargers. That is a far more favorable setup than anything else that comes before the bye.
Mendoza already has one appearance under his belt. He entered late in the Raiders' 45-17 loss to the New England Patriots and completed six of his eight passes for 48 yards once it became clear Las Vegas would not mount a comeback against last year's Super Bowl runners-up.
author: Carter Bahns

title: Why Giants coach John Harbaugh is backing Cam Skattebo's plan to defy the NFL rulebook
summary: New York's running back refuses to change his hard-nosed approach and his coach wants clarity from the league
full_text:
After becoming the first offensive player all season to get flagged for lowering his helmet into a defender, Giants running back Cam Skattebo said he's not going to change his running style, even if it leads to more penalties. Normally, a head coach probably wouldn't be on board if his player was planning to defy the NFL rulebook, but John Harbaugh is backing Skattebo here.
During an interview on Monday, the Giants head coach was asked about Skattebo's penalty, which came in the first quarter of New York's 27-21 win over the Houston Texans . On the play, Skattebo got called for unnecessary roughness after running over Texans safety M.J. Stewart .
Cam Skattebo with one of the most violent TRUCK STICKS you’ll ever see. The Giants sophomore RB is arguably the SCARIEST runner in the entire NFL 😳🤯 pic.twitter.com/Jj6TRvIOgI
Harbaugh definitely didn't agree with the penalty flag and he vehemently defended Skattebo's running style during a press conference on Monday.
"Skatt runs low. You have to run low. You have to run low to protect the football," Harbaugh said. "You have to run low to protect your body. You can't run in there and give tacklers your chest. When you run low, your head's down there, too. You can't move your head off your shoulders. It's a physical impossibility."
Skattebo has already said that he's going to keep running low even if it leads to more penalties and Harbaugh has no problem with that, because he doesn't think his running back is doing anything illegal.
"I'm quite sure Skatt's not trying to use his helmet as a weapon, as a battering ram," Harbaugh said. "It's not the way he's thinking. He's leading with his shoulder. That's what he's trying to do. He's trying to keep his head in a good, strong, upright position. But his pads are down there low. He runs low to the ground. That's a good thing, that's football. That's the way you're supposed to run. That's how you protect yourself and the football."
If Skattebo starts running more straight up, that could mean that he'll take bigger hits, and as Harbaugh noted, it makes it tougher to protect the football. Skattebo's running style might be illegal by NFL standards, but Harbaugh isn't going to ask him to change a thing.
"I didn't have a problem with the technique personally at all, but we haven't heard from the league," the Giants head coach said.
Harbaugh has been an NFL head coach since 2008, so he knows the rule book inside and out, but he's just not sure what his player is supposed to do in this situation, so he'd like the NFL to fill him in.
"Maybe they'll be able to enlighten us a little bit on it in terms of what they want us to teach, and that would be great," Harbaugh said of the NFL.
This is certainly an interesting situation. You have a long-time head coach calling out the league over a subjective rule that almost never gets enforced. Although plenty of players have been fined this year for lowering their head, Skattebo was just the fourth player -- and first offensive player -- to actually be hit with a penalty. As Harbaugh noted, running low to the ground is something he likes to see from his running backs, and it seems bizarre for the NFL to penalize that.
The league obviously doesn't want defenders lowering their helmet on a tackle, but penalizing an offensive player is a little more dicey. The NFL does fine players for lowering their helmet, and for now, that might be the fairest way to punish players like Skattebo.

title: Lessons from NFL Week 7: Jaxon Smith-Njigba could make WR history, Seahawks look like champs again
summary: Seattle delivered a championship-caliber performance, while Cincinnati discovered that its best offensive formula may also be its simplest
full_text:
There was plenty of consternation about the Seahawks ' 3-3 start to the season. The offense couldn't stop turning the ball over. The running game had no juice. The defense wasn't quite back to last year's elite level. These guys were really the reigning champions? With Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III coming to town, all those issues would be on display under the bright "Sunday Night Football" lights.
The Seahawks answered them and then some in a 20-3 shellacking. The Chiefs didn't reach the red zone once, the first time that's ever happened in a Patrick Mahomes start. Walker, the league's leading rusher, had just been 36 yards on the ground. Seattle looked very much like the dominant unit it was at the end of last year, and no one was more dominant than Jaxon Smith-Njigba .
He leads off our six lessons learned from Week 7.
On a field full of stars, and with Walker's return taking up most of the spotlight pregame, Jaxon Smith-Njigba took the spotlight back: nine catches, 150 yards, one touchdown. He roasted anyone lined up against him.
pic.twitter.com/CErI1Vg5Hb
Smith-Njigba is too quick to jam at the line and an absurdly smooth route runner. Once he's past you, he's gone. And once he has the ball in his hands, he's hard to bring down, with a mix of jukes, vision, craftiness and strength to get past the defender guarding him.
And Smith-Njigba is doing it while carrying an immense load. He has 50.2% of Seattle's receiving yards this year. Only one player-- Ken Burrough in 1975 -- has had more than half of his team's receiving yards since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger.
We already knew Smith-Njigba was excellent. But Sunday night, he truly went to another level. This was a defense that hadn't allowed more than 72 yards to an opposing wide receiver. Smith-Njigba more than doubled that.
He's now up to +450 odds to win Offensive Player of the Year, according to DraftKings , only behind Jahmyr Gibbs (+250) and Kenneth Walker III (+280). No wide receiver has ever gone back-to-back for the award, but as Nick Emmanwori said after the game, "He's one of one."
Sticking with the champs, Emmanwori is now fully back to wreaking havoc. Sunday night, he played defensive snaps at 11 different positions, including at least five snaps at ...
The Seahawks didn't play a single snap of base personnel, according to Sumer Sports , and Emmanwori is the key that unlocks that versatility.
Nick Emmanwori is a special talent 🔥 @seahawks (via @GridIronically ) pic.twitter.com/rRCPxe9v7T
He also provided the pressure on Mahomes' interception while playing right linebacker. But he's not just an absurd athlete; he's also a really high-IQ player. Look at him somehow defend three players at once here: He occupies Noah Gray as blocker on the edge and, when he sees Mahomes rolling out and getting pressured, turns and finds Walker for a pass breakup.
Nick Emmanwori é um atleta especial. QUE JOGADA! 😤 📺: #KCvsSEA ao vivo no sportv2 pic.twitter.com/4v31xagAR5
The numbers with Emmanwori on the field this season are absurd.
Seahawks with Emmanwori on field this season
The Bengals trailed the Ravens 13-0 at halftime.
The Bengals beat the Ravens 35-13.
It was the third-largest win ever by a team trailing by 13+ at halftime, and my goodness did it serve as a great reminder of how much firepower the trio of Joe Burrow , Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins has. In the second half alone ...
The highlights from Higgins are as good as it gets.
Tee Higgins went from zero catches in the first half to completely taking over after halftime. 6 REC, 148 REC YDS, 1 TD vs Ravens pic.twitter.com/DtN0SUwyNW
Higgins has gotten so, so much better in one crucial area: the middle of the field. He has always been an exquisite talent on the perimeter, but this year, he has 24 catches between the numbers. That's 11 shy of his career high ... and it's only been six games!
Oh yeah, and then there's Chase, who can do this:
There goes Ja'Marr 👀 CINvsBAL on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/EYx5NhdcCT
The Bengals entered this season wanting to do more under center and play action, an attempt to expand the playbook, make things harder on the defense and give Burrow more easy answers. It was a worthwhile attempt, but it just wasn't a fit; Burrow has never liked turning his back to the defense.
In the second half, Burrow was out of the shotgun on 17 of his 18 pass attempts. Sometimes, it can be as easy as "our players are better than yours."
The Rams got back on track with a 35-21 win over the Raiders , a much-needed victory after a rough Week 6 loss to the Cardinals, followed by even rougher injury news .
With no Davante Adams , Los Angeles ran the ball 38 times, or on 55.9% of its offensive plays -- its highest rate of any game in the past two seasons. Yes, playing from the lead helps, but the Rams' 44% rushing rate in the first half was their highest since Week 1 and powered the Rams to a 28-3 halftime lead.
Not only did the Rams run a lot, but they did so with a season-high 63.2% success rate. Kyren Williams ran 16 times for 99 yards, and Blake Corum ran 17 times for 93 times. Both scored a touchdown.
From an outside perspective, it always made sense for this to be a run-first game for Los Angeles, and without Adams for the foreseeable future, it could stay that way. The Rams ran 13 personnel (one running back, three tight ends) on half of their snaps, their highest rate since Week 2, when Puka Nacua was out.
They had a 68% rushing success rate with 13 personnel, and for the year, they have a 57.4% rushing success rate out of 13 personnel. In fact, they have a 55.4% rushing success rate overall, second only to the 49ers .
All of this is to say the Rams finally leaned on the run. Williams gives them down-to-down consistency, while Corum gives them some explosiveness. The Rams have a manageable stretch of game -- Chargers , at Commanders , at Cardinals -- to continue to lean into it, especially with heavy personnel. It will do lots of good with Adams out and add a weapon to the repertoire if/when he returns.
The Texans ' 27-21 loss to the Giants was disappointing for a variety of reasons. It undid all the good work they had done over the previous two weeks, when they went from 0-4 to 2-4. The offense had all-too-familiar struggles with short yardage and penalties.
But nothing was more disappointing than the defense. J.J. McCarthy threw for 252 yards, and the Giants ran for 188 yards -- their most in any game in the last three seasons. New York had four explosive runs, including two in a row to end the game: Cam Skattebo's 42-yarder followed by Devin Singletary's 30-yard walkoff touchdown. Neither runner was touched until they were well into the secondary.
This has happened far too often this year. The Texans are 25th in defensive rushing success rate this year. They were seventh last year. This has become a major issue not just because stopping the run is important (duh), but also because it limits Houston's chances to attack the quarterback when opponents get behind the sticks. Last year, the Texans had the second-highest rate of opponent plays that went for 0 or negative yards. This year, they are 22nd.
And then there's the secondary, which has completely fallen off. No one epitomizes that more than Kamari Lassiter -- the cornerback opposite Derek Stingley Jr . -- who was so good last year.
Kamari Lassiter as Primary Defender
There have just been far, far too many explosive plays. The Texans are tied with the Lions for most passes of 20+ yards allowed (29). They only allowed 47 all of last year. They're on pace for 70 this year. Yes, big plays are part of the deal when you play as aggressively as Houston's secondary does, but they can't be this big a deal.
DeMeco Ryans took over defensive play calling from Matt Burke after the 0-4 start, and though it helped against the Titans , it hasn't helped against the Jaguars or the Giants. There are too many missed tackles and too many missed assignments.

author: Zachary Pereles

title: NFL hot-seat rankings: Nick Sirianni's seat getting warmer? Shane Steichen running out of time
summary: These coaches are feeling the most heat entering Week 8
full_text:
Several NFL coaches are feeling the heat as the regular season nears its halfway point. A whopping 10 coaching jobs opened up last offseason, and it's safe to say that several coaches will receive their pink slips soon. Here's a look at the hottest seats with Week 8 of the regular season upon us.
Sirianni's situation is odd. It's hard to blame him for the Eagles ' struggles on the injury front. Along with Jalen Hurts , the Eagles were missing DeVonta Smith , Dontayvion Wicks and Nolan Smith during Monday night's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys . Saquon Barkley played but was a non-factor in the second half, as his hamstring is clearly still an issue.
The issue is that the Eagles were already in free fall before Hurts' medical situation. Philadelphia started the season with two unimpressive wins before being blown out in Week 3 by a Bears team that didn't have Caleb Williams . Shortly after that, they lost two-fifths of their starting offensive line when Lane Johnson retired and Cam Jurgens was traded to Baltimore.
This is the second straight season in which the Eagles have fallen well short of expectations. Philadelphia's struggles since its Super Bowl-winning season have put Sirianni's status beyond this season in jeopardy.
Quinn's heat has been intense since Washington's inexplicable lack of clock management at the end of their eventual tie against the Giants in Week 5. That game was sandwiched between two losses that put the Commanders at 1-4-1 entering their Week 7 bye.
The shine from Quinn's first season in Washington is gone. The Commanders are just 6-16-1 since their 2024 NFC Championship game run, and it appears that things may get worse before they get better. The Commanders recently lost their best skill player -- Terry McLaurin -- for the season after he injured his knee during the team's Week 6 loss to the 49ers .
If there are any positives for Washington, it's that Jayden Daniels is healthy and looking more like the 2024 version of himself. The Commanders also appear to have a budding star in rookie linebacker Sonny Styles . Additionally, Washington plays in the winnable NFC East, where every team has a losing record.
Like Greg Roman before him, new Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is the current scapegoat in Los Angeles. Barring a miraculous turnaround, the Chargers' merry-go-round at offensive coordinator will continue. The question is whether or not Chargers' ownership will be looking for a new coach, as well.
This season has been an unmitigated disaster. The Chargers are now the NFL's only winless team after the Dolphins defeated the Jets on Sunday. More than the losing, though, is how the Chargers are losing.
The offense is dead last in the NFL in points scored. Justin Herbert , a former Pro Bowler who set an NFL rookie record with 31 touchdown passes in 2020, looks like a shell of himself. Herbert's shocking regression is the biggest argument for moving on from Harbaugh, who was brought to Los Angeles to help elevate Herbert's career trajectory.
Instead, Herbert is floundering, the team is in disarray, and the Chargers' drought of playoff wins will undoubtedly reach eight years by season's end. Ironically, all of this is happening exactly 20 years after Chargers owner Dean Spanos fired Marty Schottenheimer following a 14-2 regular season.
It's not easy being green, especially for Glenn, who has been taking heat for his clock management (he let the Dolphins run out most of the clock at the end of the first half as they increased their lead to 14 points) during the Jets' loss to previously winless Miami.
That debacle magnified how bad Glenn's Jets have been in the final two minutes of the first half. New York has been outscored 107-6 in those situations since the start of last season. Really, the Jets can't be any worse at the end of halves than they've been under Glenn.
A similarly ugly stat is Glenn's record against divisional foes. The Jets are 0-8 in such games since the start of the 2025 season.
Prior to hiring Glenn, Jets owner Woody Johnson said he wanted to show more patience after firing Saleh and former general manager Joe Douglas during the 2024 season. Johnson might have a change of heart, however, if the Jets' current struggles continue.
Steichen's situation couldn't be much worse. Following Chris Ballard's dismissal, it'll take nothing short of a miracle for Steichen to save his job. The issue (among others) is that the Colts could make that impossible if they decide to trade away some of their best players before the trade deadline (a process that began with Tuesday's trade of Pro Bowl G Qenton Nelson to the Seahawks).
The 41-year-old Steichen hasn't been the main issue during his tenure in Indianapolis. Ballard deserves much more blame for the Colts' recent struggles, starting with his decision to select Anthony Richardson with the No. 4 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft . Steichen, fairly or not, also owns some of Richardson's lack of development.
Looking back, Steichen's tenure in Indianapolis changed forever when Daniel Jones sustained his season-ending injury last season. The Colts started the 2025 season with an 8-2 record but finished 8-9 after 44-year-old Philip Rivers was unable to save their sinking ship. They're 2-5 this season and have continued to receive subpar play from the quarterback position.
Steichen's time with the Colts is a cautionary tale of what happens when there is instability at the most important position in sports. Unfortunately for him, there will probably be another coach in his seat when the Colts finally find their next franchise quarterback.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Should the Giants trade for Saquon Barkley? Making the case for and against potential blockbuster deal
summary: A look at the pros and cons of acquiring Barkley
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles ' season keeps taking hits, and their long line of injuries isn't helping their other struggles. Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is reportedly out for the season with blood clots . The other injuries they've dealt with this season include WR DeVonta Smith , TE Dallas Goedert , G Landon Dickerson and RB Saquon Barkley , and to add insult to injury, longtime tackle Lane Johnson retired at the beginning of October.
In total, they had 25 players on the injury report heading into their Monday night loss to the Dallas Cowboys . Even when they were healthier, the offense looked uninspired, and they made costly mistakes across all three phases of the game.
This offseason, the Eagles lost star WR A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots , and as the trade deadline looms, there are rumors that they could lose another key member of the offense. Barkley could find himself in a new zip code -- or, we should say, a familiar one -- soon. But where exactly would be the best fit? The Giants are one team that could make sense. Barkley returned Monday after missing two games and briefly looked explosive. He ran for 62 yards and a touchdown but appeared to aggravate his hamstring in the first half.
Here's the case for and against trading for Barkley and creating a reunion with the Giants:
Adding a former first-round pick, Super Bowl champion and three-time Pro Bowler has some obvious positives.
Barkley hit 1,000-plus yards rushing five times in the seven full seasons he played, excluding 2020 due to injury. He hit the mark three times as a member of the Football Giants and twice with the Birds, including the record-setting 2,504 yards during the 2024 regular season and playoffs.
The offense needs a spark and a veteran presence who can deliver, and Saquon can be that guy. Barkley earned Offensive Rookie of the Year honors as a member of the Giants. The team looks very different now, but he does have a history of success at MetLife Stadium.
The Giants just cut running back Najee Harris after his criticisms about the running back rotation, so they are in the market for another RB. In Week 6, it was quarterback J.J. McCarthy who led the team in rushing with just 26 yards, and he didn't even play the entire game. They need someone other than Cam Skattebo who can put up solid numbers.
Head coach John Harbaugh said it would be "great" to be in a "Saquon Barkley circumstance" where there were no questions about who the strongest ball carrier is. That Saquon circumstance may be closer than it seems.
New York is already in a position to add another running back, so why not make it fun and add someone your fans already know? It would be about more than just making it fun, however, given Barkley's resume.
Now, let's look at the Giants' season. It may look over when you watch their individual games, but they are actually sitting atop the NFC East for the first time since 2015. If the season ended today, they would be the No. 3 seed. The Eagles are 2-5 after losing five straight, while the Cowboys improved to 3-4 with last night's victory. The Commanders have only one victory, leaving the NFC well within New York's reach.
The NFC East is theirs for the taking. The Giants may be able to make it to the playoffs and start building an offense that can finally show some consistency, and Barkley can help with that.
The Giants already tried a notable reunion this season, bringing wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr . on and eventually elevating him to the active roster. The nostalgia wore off quickly, however, and he was cut after three games with no receptions over just 20 total snaps.
Just because it may seem fun and entertaining to watch doesn't mean it's a good idea. The Giants already tried the Saquon experiment once, and going back doesn't seem like the most sensible move. Not to mention that Barkley is 29, which is getting up there in the running-back world.
The Giants didn't want to pay for Barkley in 2024 when he ended up joining the Eagles in free agency, and while Barkley is older, he is still among the top running backs in the league. Big names come with a big price tag.
If the Giants get rid of Skattebo for Barkley, which is one option CBS Sports' Carter Barns could see as the value of this trade , New York continues to be stuck in the hamster wheel of mediocrity. Not because Barkley is mediocre, but because he doesn't provide a long-term answer.
The Giants have struggled to find the perfect combination on offense and keep catching players at the wrong time. If they trade Skattebo for Barkley, yes, they will have someone with a stronger track record as a top RB, but they will also be closer to having to replace him with another RB1 as his career window closes.
Things seemed to be working between quarterback Jaxson Dart and Skattebo in the last one-plus years, the limited time they were healthy together, and that's what the Giants should build around. Skattebo has 129 carries for 530 yards and has scored eight touchdowns in nine games with Dart in his career.
The Eagles got the rare inter-divisional big signing when they landed Barkley, and I don't think they want to let their NFC East rival in on that fun.
If the Giants do get Barkley, they will end up overpaying for him.
The Giants are still early in their Dart Era and are finding their new identity. They need to start fresh with their up-and-coming RB rather than go back to their former player. They have a potential solid RB1 in Skattebo, and they should see where he develops. He's had ball-security issues this season, but he had a major redemption game in Week 7 after his benching.
Barkley provides more value on the Eagles than he does on the Giants in terms of impact off the field as well. I don't think it makes sense for either side right now, and Philly losing another consistent offensive playmaker will only hurt its already rough season.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Why Cowboys' offensive revival could launch an NFC East run
summary: The Cowboys still have work to do, but their offensive ceiling and favorable upcoming schedule give them a chance
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys (3-4) were down in the dumps after consecutive primetime losses against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Green Bay Packers . Their offense had become stale while  Brian Schottenheimer and George Pickens traded barbs during the week . Panic levels were at a fever pitch after Dallas scored below 20 points in consecutive starts for the first time in seven years with Dak Prescott .
All of that is now washed away after the Cowboys' 38-21 road victory at the Philadelphia Eagles (2-5) on "Monday Night Football" that all but buried their hated rival this season and put Dallas back on track in their pursuit for their first NFC East division title since 2023.
The Cowboys got everything they could have hoped for on Monday in a get-right game against the two-time defending division champs, albeit a battered version of them, quarterbacked by backup Tanner McKee and led by Saquon Barkley on one leg with a hamstring injury. Prescott threw for 212 yards and three touchdowns. Javonte Williams totaled a career-high 150 yards rushing and a touchdown on 25 carries for a 6.2 yards per carry average. CeeDee Lamb led the way with 74 yards receiving and two receiving touchdowns on five catches while Pickens caught a 21-yard diving touchdown. For as beat up as the Eagles were, most of those injuries were on their offense. With Williams rolling, the Eagles had no answer for Prescott, Lamb, Pickens and Dallas' passing game.
* Dallas' most rushing yards against the Eagles since 2000
Edge rusher Nolan Smith (concussion) was the only Philadelphia defensive starter out on Monday, but a limited Barkley, no Jalen Hurts and no DeVonta Smith led to an environment where an outmatched Eagles squad couldn't keep pace with Dallas' high-flying, locked-in attack. The Cowboys should feel good about their ability to put Philadelphia out of their misery at Lincoln Financial Field. Oft-injured linebacker DeMarvion Overshown overcame a hamstring that had him sidelined since Week 1 to return Monday night in Week 7 to tally his first interception since 2024. Everything the Cowboys could have hoped for came to fruition while they were able to avoid an avalanche from Barkley, who finished with 62 yards and a touchdown on seven carries. Barkley pulled up after an apparent hamstring reaggravation at the tail end of his 29-yard run on the Eagles' opening drive.
DEMARVION OVERSHOWN INT DALvsPHI on ESPN⁰Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SH5FW4gwC0
Dallas' schedule now parts like the Red Sea as they take aim at overtaking the first-place New York Giants (4-2-1) for the NFC East lead. The Cowboys' next five opponents have a combined 13-22 record, with their only game against a team with a winning record from Weeks 8-12 coming in the friendly confines of AT&T Stadium against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 10.
Plus, Prescott rediscovered his connection with both Lamb and Pickens. He had no touchdowns and two interceptions when targeting his dynamic wide receiver duo in Week 6 against the Packers, but against Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio's unit on Monday night, he threw three touchdowns to no interceptions when targeting Lamb and Pickens. Dallas' face-of-the-franchise quarterback now has 39 victories in his first 40 starts against the NFC East with 98 touchdown passes to 24 interceptions. That's tied for the most wins in a quarterback's first 50 divisional starts since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger with Tom Brady and Patrick Mahomes .
After all the handwringing about Pickens' offensive involvement, he's now up to 260 yards receiving and 2 touchdowns across the last three games after just 225 yards and no touchdowns in Dallas' first four games. Prescott, Schottenheimer and the rest of the Cowboys' offense waved a magic wand and seemingly fixed all their offensive issues in a week. As long as Prescott is upright, the J.J. McCarthy-led Giants shouldn't get too comfy atop the NFC East because no team in the division can rival the ceiling Dallas' offense provides the Cowboys.
author: Garrett Podell

title: NFL Week 8 picks and score predictions: Bills survive Baltimore, Browns end 38-year drought
summary: Week 8 brings Halloween scares for several contenders, including the Bills, Vikings, Chiefs and Seahawks
full_text:
In honor of Halloween weekend, the NFL is giving us a horrifying Sunday night game this week: the Eagles (2-5) at the Commanders (1-4-1).
Roger Goodell, if you're reading, there's still time to flex this game out. I say move it to 2 a.m. and put it on Telemundo, because at this point the only thing that might make the game better is listening to it in Spanish.
Anyway, since Halloween is coming up on Saturday, this seems like the perfect time to hand out costume ideas, so that's exactly what we're going to do before we get to the picks this week.
If you're a Commanders fan, you could go as a clock since your team doesn't understand time management. If you're an Eagles fan, you could go as a couch since that's where the team will be sitting once the playoffs start. If you're a Titans fan, you could go as a bench, since that's where Cam Ward should probably be at this point. And if you're a Chargers fan, you could go as nothing since that's what your team has done this season.
Will I pick any of these teams to win in Week 8? Let's get to the picks and find out.
Actually, before we get to the Week 8 picks, here's a quick reminder that you can check out the weekly picks from every CBSSports.com NFL expert by clicking here . Also, as you probably know by now -- because I point it out every week -- I'm in charge of the NFL newsletter here at CBSSports.com. If you want to subscribe, all you have to do is click here and enter your email address .
Through the first seven weeks, the Bills look like one of the best teams in the AFC, but my biggest issue with them is that they have one major flaw and it's their entire defense. Having a major flaw isn't necessarily a bad thing. My major flaw is that I watch "Hot Tub Time Machine" whenever it's on TV. To fix that flaw, I could either stop watching TV or I could destroy all the TVs in my house. Either one of those would work. Unfortunately for the Bills, there's no easy fix for their problem.
Heading into Week 8, the Bills are surrendering 28.5 points per game, which is the third-most in the NFL. Only the Cardinals and Commanders are worse. When you're mentioned in the same conversation as those two teams, that's definitely a red flag.
One reason the Bills are giving up so many points is that they can't stop the pass. Through their first six games, the Bills are surrendering an average of 285.8 yards per game, which is the second-highest number in the NFL.
Since I've started things off here by ripping the Bills' defense, you might be thinking that I'm about to pick the Bills to lose, but there are two reasons why I'm hesitant to do that. For one, Josh Allen exists. For the Bills, it doesn't matter how bad their defense plays because Allen always manages to save the day.
The Bills defense has given up at least 30 points in four different games this season, but thanks to Allen, the Bills have gone 4-0 in those games. To put that in perspective, the other 31 teams are a combined 8-47 this year when they surrender at least 30 points.
The other reason I'm hesitant to pick against the Bills is that I have no idea whether Lamar Jackson will play. Jackson injured his ankle in Week 4 and hasn't played since. The Ravens have been saying he's "Day-to-day" for the past three weeks and all I have to say is that someone needs to explain to them how a calendar works. You can't be "day-to-day" for THREE WEEKS.
Although Jackson didn't play in Week 7, he returned to practice last week, suggesting there's at least a chance he could play in this game. If anyone can take advantage of the Bills' defense, it's definitely Jackson. For that reason, I'm going to make two picks here, one for if Lamar plays and one for if he doesn't. Actually, you know what, I really don't even need to make two picks because I'm taking the Bills either way.
PICK (Lamar plays): Bills 34-31 over Ravens PICK (No Lamar): Bills 34-24 over Ravens
The Vikings have done it. They're officially the final undefeated team left in the NFL. This is the greatest accomplishment by any Viking since Erik the Red and Leif Erikson roamed the planet.  Despite having no offense, the Vikings have somehow run the table through the first seven weeks.
So how bad is their offense? Glad you asked.
The Vikings are winning because of their defense, and if I were defensive coordinator Brian Flores, I would ask the organization to triple my salary and then double it again on top of that. One reason the Vikings' defense has been so good this year is that Flores has come up with a brilliant new strategy called, "We're going to blitz you on every play and see what happens." I won seven straight Super Bowls in Madden while using that strategy in college and it seems to be working out well for the Vikings.
In their win over the Colts , they blitzed at an 85.2% rate. THEY BLITZED ON ALMOST EVERY PLAY. And this was not a one-time thing: For the entire season, the Vikings have a blitz rate above 70%.
First, let me say that I love this strategy, but over the past three weeks, the Vikings have beaten Malik Willis , Tyler Shough and Daniel Jones . That's the NFL equivalent of winning a hamburger-eating contest against three vegans. What I need to know is if the Vikings defensive strategy is sustainable.
The Vikings have played the third-easiest strength of schedule through the first seven weeks, but things are going to get a lot more difficult starting this week. As a matter of fact, from Week 8 through Week 11, the Vikings have the most difficult strength of schedule in the NFL (.731) with games against the Lions , Bills, Packers and 49ers .
It's one thing to blitz Daniel Jones into oblivion, but that might not work against Jared Goff , Josh Allen, Jordan Love or Brock Purdy . I'm not sure what Flores will end up doing against the Lions, but I feel like he's going to have a special surprise in store for them. The Vikings swept the Lions last year, and a big reason was that Flores' defense held Detroit to 34 total points in the two games combined.
Flores has been the defensive coordinator in Minnesota since 2023, so he knows this Lions offense inside and out. If defense wins championships, then there's no way I can pick against the Vikings in this game.
PICK: Vikings 19-16 over Lions
The Browns have already beaten the Steelers once this season, and if they win this game, that would give them their first season sweep of Pittsburgh since 1988. That's right, it has somehow been 38 years since the Browns have swept the Steelers. The NFL should have flexed this game to Sunday night and asked everyone at the stadium to dress up like their favorite character from 1988. I would have definitely been John McClane from Die Hard, or maybe AC Slater. You know what? I'm not sure and we don't have time to talk about this.
This game is not an easy one to pick and that's mostly because both teams still feel like a mystery to me. I do love a good mystery -- That's why I read all 200 "Encyclopedia Brown" books as a kid -- but I can't quite figure out either team.
On Cleveland's end, the Browns are 5-2, but I still have no idea how good they are. The Browns seem to be flying by the seat of their pants every week. Their last three wins have all come on a field goal in the final 10 seconds, which I'm only pointing out, because they are the FIRST TEAM in NFL history to have three straight wins come by a field goal in the final 10 seconds.
Also, all five of their wins have come by four points or less. There have only been three other teams in NFL history to pick up their first five wins in games they won by four points or less and none of those teams made the playoffs. That being said, the Browns do have a great defense, Deshaun Watson has been absolutely clutch this year, and their rookie receivers have been impressive.
Maybe we should have seen all of this coming. Oh wait, I DID! Back in June, I predicted Cleveland's entire season and had them finishing 10-7. HERE'S THE VIDEO PROOF.
I actually had every AFC North team…

title: Prisco's NFL Week 8 Power Rankings: Lone unbeaten Vikings take over top spot
summary: Pete Prisco shares his Week 8 Power Rankings for the 2026 NFL season, including some big risers and fallers
full_text:
Legit question: How good are the undefeated Minnesota Vikings ?
That isn't to demean the Vikings, the league's last undefeated team, but rather to ask an honest football question. Can a team that is so limited on offense be considered good?
The Vikings are 6-0 after beating the Indianapolis Colts , 16-10, on Sunday, but they are winning games without a real semblance of an offense that scores or scares.
They have scored 125 points in their six games, which means 10 touchdowns on the season. That is historically bad. They are a tough watch on the eyes, even if they showed a little more life on offense against the Colts.
We will learn a lot more about the Vikings over the next four weeks. They play at the Lions , home against the Bills , at the Packers and the 49ers in Mexico. That's quite the string of games.
They will need to be better on offense for sure. But the defense is the gold standard right now in the league, thanks to the uber-aggressive coordinator Brian Flores.
Minnesota takes over the top spot in my Power Rankings this week after the 49ers and Kansas City Chiefs both lost, leaving the Vikings as the only team without a blemish.
The Minnesota offense was a little better in the victory over the Colts, but Indianapolis isn't very good on defense. The Vikings are ranked first in scoring defense and 23rd in scoring offense. That is a heck of a disparity for an unbeaten team.
Quarterback Kyler Murray has to be better. The passing game has to improve from its 29th-ranked yards-per-game mark. If not, the next four games could be a big problem for the Vikings, and their stay at the top won't last long.
The bottom of my rankings has a new team this week. The Miami Dolphins , fresh off their first victory of the season over the New York Jets , have moved above the Los Angeles Chargers .
The Chargers are the only team without a victory this season, and they couldn't lose this past week because they were on a bye. At 0-6, they play their city rival, the Los Angeles Rams , this week. It might mean a stay at the bottom for the Chargers as the heat intensifies for all in that building.
author: Pete Prisco

title: Who will Jay-Z bring out for the 2027 Super Bowl halftime show? Four possible guests
summary: Will Jay Z bring out any guests? If he does, here are some guesses of who they could be
full_text:
It's official: Jay-Z will take the stage for the Super Bowl halftime show on February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium. Jay-Z and his company, Roc Nation, are partners with the NFL on the halftime show, having produced the event since 2019. The rapper is a key decision-maker in who performs, and this year he chose himself.
While we know who the performer will be during the biggest game in American sports, we do not know who will be playing in the Super Bowl. We'll have to wait until the last day of January for that one.
Another mystery that remains is who, if anyone, will be his special guest(s). Many halftime show performers bring out additional artists, and while Jay-Z has not announced any yet, there is a good chance he will.
Here is a look at artists that he could bring out, based on their past history and collaborations:
Queen Bey is first on the list for obvious reasons. The superstar singer has been married to Jay-Z since 2008 and shares three children together.
The two have worked together numerous times, including their first collaboration before they were dating, "'03 Bonnie and Clyde." Their most popular song together is arguably "Crazy in Love," released in 2003. Other collaborations include "Drunk in Love," "Part II (On the Run)," "Deja Vu" and "Lift Off." They toured together, so they are used to sharing the same stage.
She also has a history of performing on the NFL stage. She headlined the 2013 halftime show and performed with Coldplay and Bruno Mars at halftime in 2016. She also sang the national anthem at Super Bowl XXXVIII in 2001, in her hometown of Houston. On Christmas Day 2024, she took the stage during halftime in Houston for what is commonly referred to as the "Beyoncé Bowl."
Jay-Z was pivotal in Rihanna's early success. In 2005, as CEO of Def Jam Records, Jay-Z had Rihanna audition for him and others, and the rest is history. She eventually left Def Jam for Roc Nation in 2010.
The two have multiple songs together, including "Umbrella," "Run This Town," and "FourFiveSeconds."
Earlier this year, she was a surprise guest at his tour, joining him on stage at Yankee Stadium, a main character in many of Jay-Z's songs.
Rihanna is another potential special guest, who is no stranger to the NFL. She was the Super Bowl headliner in 2023 and had one of the most memorable performances in recent history, announcing her pregnancy during the event.
Blu Ivy Carter is the oldest child of Jay-Z and Beyoncé. She performed as a dancer during Beyonce's 2024 Christmas Day halftime show in Houston. Blu Ivy also joined her mom for the Cowboy Carter tour, once again as a dancer. For being so young, she already has a huge fanbase, with concertgoers holding signs for her, yelling her name at shows and tweeting about her talents.
Not only has Ms. Carter performed on an NFL stage before, but she is also often seen attending NFL games with her dad. The Super Bowl halftime show could turn into a family affair.
Slim Shady joined Jay Z on stage during his current tour, and the two could have another reunion at the Super Bowl. The two collaborated on the song "Renegade" on Jay-Z's album The Blueprint.
Like the others on the list, Eminem has experience as an NFL performer. His comes via the 2022 Super Bowl, where he was a special guest on an iconic hip-hop lineup.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: NFL trade deadline matchmaker: Vikings add Jonathan Taylor to boost offense, Chiefs nab WR
summary: Moves for several contenders who could look to buy
full_text:
For much of October, reports will tell of teams that could be willing to buy or sell waiting to see how the next few weeks will go. A potential seller wins a few games, and all of a sudden, maybe that team wants to keep more key players than originally thought. A couple of losses from a potential buyer could mean that team isn't so keen on making a win-now move. A lot can and does change in the NFL every week.
But now the end of October has arrived, and the trade deadline is two weeks away. Phone lines are buzzing, and Week 7 revealed some more notable concerns for potential buyers. Does that mean sellers will take advantage sooner rather than later? With big names such as Jonathan Taylor and Saquon Barkley being floated as potential trade targets this trade season, we play matchmaker for several top teams looking to patch up their rosters for the stretch run of the regular season and beyond.
The need: Help on offense The solution: RB Jonathan Taylor
The NFL's only undefeated team, Minnesota, moved to 6-0 with a 16-10 win over the Colts . That sort of score has been the norm. The Vikings have 10 touchdowns this season, the fewest by any 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions . 1934!
The Kyler Murray experience has been a rough one. He'll produce a big play or two with his legs or his arm, but the down-to-down consistency hasn't been close to good enough. He is 27th in sack rate, 29th in passing success rate and 31st in touchdown rate.
Surprisingly, the Vikings score on 41.5% of their drives, 12th in the NFL, but that's been a lot of Will Reichard field goals. Taylor, meanwhile, is a scoring machine, and he'd provide explosiveness to the running game, too. The Vikings saw it up close and personal Sunday, with Taylor totaling 110 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown. Aaron Jones has been playing through a knee injury, which he aggravated Sunday. The Vikings can't risk wasting their Super Bowl-caliber defense. Taylor is the solution.
The need: Running back The solution: RB Saquon Barkley
The Bengals are up to 4-2 on the young season after a beatdown of the Ravens . Joe Burrow and co. don't particularly like running the ball, and perhaps the reason why is that the offense only averages 3.6 yards per carry.
It's been a disappointing year for Chase Brown . His -0.6 yards per attempt over expected is among the worst in the NFL, and it seemingly isn't clicking for him. Enter Barkley, who is actually producing 1.15 yards per rush over expected despite pretty much everything around him falling apart. Only four players -- Kenneth Walker III , Jaylen Warren , Bijan Robinson and Kyle Monangai -- have a higher rate. The Bengals made a blockbuster move for Dexter Lawrence this year despite concerns about his age and productivity, and it has been hugely successful so far. Barkley could be a similar spark, especially with defenses devoting so much attention to Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins .
The need: Another disruptor up front The solution: DL Jeffery Simmons
Even with big leaps from defensive tackle Deone Walker and EDGE Greg Rousseau , the Bills are 24th in defensive rushing success rate, and with Ed Oliver's injury issues, Buffalo has been iffy up front outside of Walker. Buffalo has long maintained the status quo at the deadline, but this is the year to change that in a big way.
Simmons is a superstar -- one of the best defenders on the planet, regardless of position. Could you imagine combining him with Walker? Legitimately terrifying. It would also help a leaky secondary. When opposing quarterbacks aren't pressured, the Bills are getting shredded: 30th in defensive EPA per play and dead last in defensive success rate. That has to change.
The need: Downfield passing The solution: WR Adonai Mitchell
The Chiefs fell from the ranks of the undefeated with a humbling 20-3 loss to the Seahawks that exposed multiple issues. One of the biggest was the complete lack of a downfield passing attack. Patrick Mahomes attempted three passes 20+ yards downfield and connected on zero of them. It was his most such attempts without a completion since Week 16 of 2024.
Kansas City's downfield passing game has gone out the window ever since Tyquan Thornton's injury. Mahomes didn't even attempt a pass 20+ yards downfield last week against the Chargers , just the second time that's happened in his entire career. Thornton still has more than half of Mahomes' completions 20+ yards downfield this year (4) despite not having played since Week 4. No other Chiefs pass catcher has more than one.
As fun as it would be to send George Pickens to Kansas City, the Cowboys seem dead set on trying to win this year. Mitchell was actually off to a strong start this season before a finger injury. Omar Cooper Jr . has shined the past two weeks, and when Mitchell returned in Week 7, he only played 44% of the offensive snaps.
The need: Interior defensive linemen The solution: DL DeForest Buckner
Buckner made it clear last week he wants to play for a winner, and the Colts don't look like a winner any time soon. The Packers , meanwhile, are 4-3 and look like they could be a legitimate contender, especially when Micah Parsons returns. The defense has rounded into shape without him, and that's even with significant injuries on the interior of the line. Buckner has been a very good -- and at times dominant -- player this year. The Packers are down some draft capital after the Parsons trade last year, but Buckner, at 32 and in the last year of his contract, wouldn't be prohibitively expensive.
The need: Secondary help The solution: CB Tariq Woolen
Woolen came to Philadelphia on a one-year deal to fill the hole at outside cornerback opposite Quinyon Mitchell , and he has done a decent job. Opponents are completing under half of their passes and averaging just 6.2 yards per attempt when Woolen is the primary defender this season. The Lions were in on Joey Porter Jr . before he ultimately ended up on the Cowboys. This could be another solid option for much, much cheaper. The Eagles figure to be sellers given the disastrous run of injuries on the offensive side of the ball.
The need: Help up front The solution: EDGE Khalil Mack
Not all reunions make sense. This one does. The Bears actually rank seventh in pressure rate and third in sack rate this season, but they could still use some pass rush juice on the edge. Chicago is 18th in pressure rate when not bringing a blitzer from pass coverage. The Chargers are obvious sellers, and Mack is still effective: three sacks and seven quick pressures, which is more than any current Bears EDGE.
The need: More push up front The solution: DL Daron Payne
The 49ers rank 29th in percentage of opponent plays that go for zero or negative yards. Enter the stout Payne, who not only remains a solid player himself, but would free things up for offseason acquisition Osa Odighizuwa on the interior. Payne's counting numbers aren't anything special, but he ranks 21st in PFF's run defense grade among 136 interior defensive linemen. Payne is in the final year of his deal, and Commanders GM Adam Peters used to be in San Francisco's front office. There's a deal to be made here.
The need: Offensive line reinforcements The solution: OL Kevin Zeitler
A longtime stalwart who was playing solidly as recently as last year, Zeitler signed with the Packers less than a month ago amid major offensive line issues in Green Bay. But he is yet to play an offensive snap and was a healthy scratch in Week 7. It just might not be working out, and if that's the case, Green Bay could be eager to recoup any draft capital for him.
New England, with injuries up and down the offensive line, could make sense as a buy-low candidate. Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) is on IR, and Ben Brown (knee) missed Week 7. Mike Onwenu (ankle) is out for most, if not all, of the rest of the season. Onwenu's replacement, Greg Van Roten (thigh), is also on IR.

Branch continues to be dynamic with the ball in his hands, even if his opportunities are limited, while Blair is a superb blocking option at wide receiver when called upon. The story of this game, though, was a story of tight ends. Seeking more blocking against San Francisco’s ferocious front, the Falcons leaned on all four of their tight ends and got all four involved in the passing game, with Muse and Pitts each catching a touchdown, Woerner making a nice grab and getting a sneak for a first down, and Hooper making his presence known as well. The Falcons are at their best when they can utilize their tight ends in a way defenses don’t expect, and Tommy Rees and company certainly did that Sunday. Beyond the bedrock guys, the Falcons have shown they’re willing to mix things up, and I expect that to continue. Whether Branch has overtaken Zaccheaus as the third receiver is anyone’s guess at the moment, though. Defense ILB Kendal Daniels: 66 CB A.J. Terrell: 65 S Jessie Bates: 64 S Xavier Watts: 63 CB C.J. He made a couple of big plays today in his reduced role and was good overall after drawing the start, which was nice to see, but it looks like Sydney Brown and Avieon Terrell may split nickel reps while A.J. Terrell and C.J. Henderson play outside once Terrell the Younger is back, which clouds Hughes’ future. The Falcons could mix and match based on matchup, too, but after the first six weeks it’s a justified move that might stick. Hughes being able to rotate in on early downs when the Falcons need a boost against the run either outside or inside makes him a very valuable reserve. In his first action as a Falcon, Snowden got two pressures, and he and Jackson (recently promoted to the 53 man roster) had larger roles than I would have expected. We’re nearing a return for James Pearce Jr., which will cost one or both their roster spots, but it’s good to have more options to keep everyone in the EDGE group as fresh as possible. Except for Cameron Thomas, of course, because he’s going to play an outlandish number of snaps every single game, apparently. Daniels leading the team in snaps after being carted off the field last week and playing that well blows my mind. Truly special Sunday for him. Even if he’s just on the practice squad, we likely haven’t seen the last of him in 2026. Three more missed tackles on special teams this week, with one from DeMarcco Hellams—easy to forgive when he had two good tackles and an assist—and both Chris Blair and Christian Harris. The latter is still young and experienced enough to be a factor down the line, but with Divine Deablo on the team, Kendal Daniels and Harold Perkins Jr. thriving, and Josh Woods ahead of him and Asamoah lurking, Harris can’t afford any special teams miscues.

title: Ravens survey and discussion: predicting Baltimore’s 2026 win total
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Ravens fans and fans across the country. The Baltimore Ravens entered the 2026 season with Super Bowl expectations and an 11.5-win over/under. But Jesse Minter is 4-3 through his first seven games and […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - OCTOBER 25: Head Coach Jesse Minter of the Baltimore Ravens looks on from the sidelines during the first quarter against the Cincinnati Bengals at M&T Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Todd Olszewski/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Ravens fans and fans across the country. The Baltimore Ravens entered the 2026 season with Super Bowl expectations and an 11.5-win over/under. But Jesse Minter is 4-3 through his first seven games and sitting in last place in the AFC North with the NFL’s toughest schedule for the rest of the season. Can he bounce back and bring the Ravens to double-digit wins, or is Baltimore headed for another disappointing finish? Here are Beatdown’s thoughts: Nikhil Mehta I only see one clear win on the Ravens’ remaining schedule – Week 10 against the Chargers – and four more games in which I would favor Baltimore. That’s five at worst, nine as expected, and 10 or more at best if this team can stay healthy and field something resembling a second-half defense. But I have little reason to believe either of those things will happen, so I will land in the eight- to nine-win band. Frank Platko While the vibes around the Ravens are bleak right now, and for good reason, I still believe better days are on the horizon. That is, of course, assuming Lamar Jackson can return within the next couple of weeks without a dropoff in his performance. The Ravens have a tough schedule ahead but with Jackson under center, every game is winnable. I think the team can rally enough to roughly split the remainder of their divisional matchups, beat both NFC North teams (Panthers and Buccaneers), and earn at least one win against another non-divisional opponent (Bills, Jaguars, Texans, Chargers). Even if not exact, this ballpark projection would give the Ravens 10 total wins — meaning they’d have to go 6-4 the remainder of the season. Even amidst continuing injuries and inconsistencies in all three phases, this seems doable. 10-7 will most likely not be enough to win the division anymore but a wild-card playoff berth is still within striking distance. Stephen Bopst The Ravens, while in stress, aren’t nearly in as bad of a spot as they were at this time last year. Their record ultimately hinges on the health of Lamar Jackson, but that’s currently a big if. They should win 2/3 against the Browns and Steelers, that puts them at 6. From there, I expect them to win four out of the remaining seven against the Chargers, Bills, Bucs, Texans, Panthers, Bengals, and Jaguars. It they really want some breathing room, they’ll have to take one of these next two games against Jacksonville or Buffalo. If not, it could be tough to sneak into the playoffs and they’ll need a really hot finish. Regardless, I see this as a 10-7 team that should be in contention for a wildcard. Dustin Cox Even though it may feel like the Ravens’ season is imploding after consecutive divisional losses, this team can still make a run with a healthy Lamar Jackson. Any hopes of the top seed in the AFC are probably out the window at this point, and winning the division will be much harder now, but I still expect Baltimore to find their footing over the next month or so and become a dangerous team in the conference. I think 11-6 is a realistic record if Jackson can return this week and remain healthy for the remainder of the season. I expect them to split the next two games against the Bills and Jaguars while losing to the Steelers once and another loss coming to either the Texans or Bengals again. Just getting into the playoffs is all that matters at this point, and I think the Ravens still have the team and coaching staff to make some noise if they get there. Now, it’s your turn!
