title: Bengals Tuesday Trenches: A Tale of Two Halves
summary: “It was the best of times, it was the worst of times……” Actually, no. Reverse that. “It was the worst of times, then it was the best of times.” I have zero understanding of how the Cincinnati Bengals went into the locker room down 13-0 to the Ravens in Baltimore, looking about as bad as […]
full_text: “It was the best of times, it was the worst of times……” Actually, no. Reverse that. “It was the worst of times, then it was the best of times.” I have zero understanding of how the Cincinnati Bengals went into the locker room down 13-0 to the Ravens in Baltimore, looking about as bad as I’ve ever seen them, and definitely worse than they’ve ever looked in the Joe-Burrow era, only to turn around and outscore the Ravens 35-0 in the second half. They looked like pod people in the first half—like they were all still on their bye week and sleepwalking through the game. The offense gained a pitiful 59 yards in the first half. They only had three first downs. Then, in the second half, they gained 298 yards, picked up 19 first downs, and scored five touchdowns on five possessions. I know the Ravens have struggled in the second half of games, but this was so far beyond that. They made me think of the movie Seabiscuit . To make a long story short, it’s a true story about a racehorse that could only win once it got behind and made eye contact with another, less-talented horse (it came out in 2003, and I saw it only once, so forgive me if I’m leaving a lot out). Basically, Seabiscuit had to have his back against the wall to tap into some deep reserve of potential. It’s a neat little story about the competitive spirit and how it can transcend species. It’s NOT a neat story for my football team! Could the Bengals have pulled off a 35-0 run in the second half if Lamar Jackson had been in the game? Can they afford to play only one half of football against the Steelers or Browns (I can’t believe I’m writing this)? They have a winning record, but teams can’t play only two quarters of winning football and expect to win very often. Here are some random thoughts on Sunday’s game: The Bengals, once again, really tried to force the under-center offense in the first half. They really, really want to get that run game established. They just couldn’t do it. They have the third-fewest rushing yards in the NFL so far this season (487) and are on pace for just over 80 rushing yards per game. It’s not easy to win in the postseason when you can’t run the ball. Having said that, the offense flowing through Joe Burrow to his star wide receivers is a sight to behold. When the engine is running clean, it’s a beautiful thing. When it’s not, though, it’s incredibly frustrating. Ja’Marr Chase reportedly gave a fiery halftime speech that got everyone pumped up for the second half. They shouldn’t need a Tony D’Amato speech at halftime to get ready to play. They’re way too talented for that. Once again, Dexter Lawrence has been worth every single bit of the No. 10 overall pick. He has completely reshaped the defensive front. Al Golden’s defense is not perfect—not even close—but Lawrence makes up for so much. Tee Higgins is proving, once again, that he’s a WR1 who just happens to play on the same team as the best wide receiver in the NFL. Double Chase and leave Higgins in single coverage at your own peril. Mike Gesicki is the Bengals’ WR3. He’s a tight end in name only. It was hard seeing Erick All leave the field looking as upset as he was. He’s had a long history of injuries to his right knee dating back to college, and it’s the same knee he injured in November of the 2024 season, which kept him out for the entirety of the 2025 season. Drew Sample is the next man up. While he’s not capable of stretching the field the way All can when he’s healthy, he’s a capable blocker, and I love seeing a Sample touchdown because it’s as close as we’re going to get to a big-man TD, which is one of the greatest moments the sport has to offer fans—like the NFL’s version of a no-hitter. Shemar Stewart was a healthy scratch, and if that’s not a damning indictment of the Bengals’ scouting department, I don’t know what is. The No. 17 overall selection in the 2025 draft is fully healthy, and the Bengals decided they had a better chance to win with him not on the field. He’s been passed on the depth chart by rookie second-round pick Cashius Howell (who recorded his first sack on Sunday) and 2024 sixth-round pick Cedric Johnson. Teams are reportedly interested in a potential trade for Stewart in hopes they can develop him in a way the Bengals haven’t or can’t. I doubt he goes anywhere other than the bench, though. The Bengals return home in Week 8 to host the 1-6 Tennessee Titans, who are dealing with a ton of issues. The best way to beat them is for the Bengals to play a complete four quarters of football the way they played in the second half in Baltimore. More specifically, if they can get out to an early lead, force the ball into Cam Ward’s hands, and make the Titans one-dimensional, they will win. They’re the much better team—on paper and on the field—but they have to play like it. The best thing that could come out of Week 8 (I hate that we’re already at Week 8) is a blowout win over an outmatched and struggling team. Would I be surprised if they won 35-0? No. Would I be surprised if they won 17-14? Also no, but I’ll be mad. Who Dey! Relative Song Lyrics: An angels smile is what you sell You promised me heaven, then put me through hell Chains of love got a hold on me When passion’s a prison, you can’t break free

full_text: Late last week, there appeared to be some optimism that the Baltimore Ravens quarterback would suit up against the Cincinnati Bengals. Jackson hasn’t played since October 4th, and as he eased back into practice before Week 7, the Ravens changed his “week-to-week” status to “day-to-day.” Jackson spoke to the media on Friday, and while he said the injury was still painful, he did not rule out taking the field while the internet speculated on his status. The speculation didn’t last too long, as the Ravens would rule Jackson out for the game on Saturday afternoon. During Sunday’s game, the CBS broadcast crew mentioned that Baltimore was surprised that Jackson didn’t play, so Jackson may have informed the staff on Saturday that he wouldn’t be able to play, leading to even more speculation about the disconnect between Jackson and the team. When asked if he was surprised, first-year head coach Jesse Minter said it was a mischaracterization. Jesse Minter on Lamar Jackson: "Lamar is working his butt off to be back and be out there. … I think he'll be in a decent spot, but we'll know more Wednesday." He was asked about CBS broadcast reporting about his ankle having swelling after practicing, but Jesse said he… pic.twitter.com/Ev8PSrN3u4 — Sarah Ellison (@sgellison) October 26, 2026 Minter was pretty quiet on the subject after saying that “shocked” wasn’t the right word. In the end, Tyler Huntley got the start, and the Bengals left with a 35-13 victory, but it sounds like there may be more questions than answers in Baltimore when it comes to their starting player. The Bengals and Ravens will meet again on Thursday Night Football in Cincinnati on New Year’s Eve.

title: Cleveland Browns news: Breaking the Three Rivers Jinx
summary: The Cleveland Browns head to Pittsburgh on Sunday looking to break a decades-long losing streak. The Browns have not won a regular-season game against the Steelers in Pittsburgh since 2003 – a span of 23 seasons! Sadly, this is not the first extensive losing streak for the Browns in the Steel City, as older fans […]
full_text: (Photo by George Gojkovich/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns head to Pittsburgh on Sunday looking to break a decades-long losing streak. The Browns have not won a regular-season game against the Steelers in Pittsburgh since 2003 – a span of 23 seasons! Sadly, this is not the first extensive losing streak for the Browns in the Steel City, as older fans will remember the infamous “Three Rivers Jinx.” Beginning with the opening of that concrete dump in 1970, the Browns made the annual trip 16 times, and 16 times they came home on the losing end. Sometimes it looked like the Browns would break the jinx as they suffered four-point losses in 1974 and 1977; three-point losses in 1979, 1980, and 1984; and a one-point loss in 1985. The franchise tried everything to change its luck, from taking a bus instead of flying and switching hotels, but nothing could break the jinx. Until the afternoon of October 5, 1986. The most memorable play of the day came when Gerald McNeil returned a kickoff 100 yards for a touchdown in the second quarter, Cleveland’s first touchdown return in 12 seasons. After the Steelers retook the lead in the third quarter, the Browns moved to within one point heading into the fourth quarter after a field goal from Matt Bahr. The deficit grew to four points after a Gary Anderson field goal, but Cleveland retook the least on Earnest Byner’s four-yard touchdown run. Pittsburgh had one final chance after Bahr’s second missed field goal of the day, but Cleveland’s defense held and the jinx was finally over. title: Browns WR up for a league honor after big game in Week 7
summary: Cleveland Browns wide receiver KC Concepcion had the type of day on Sunday that he and the Browns have been waiting for since he was selected in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft. Concepcion finished the game against the Tennessee Titans with eight receptions for 129 yards and 23 rushing yards, including an […]
full_text: (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) Cleveland Browns wide receiver KC Concepcion had the type of day on Sunday that he and the Browns have been waiting for since he was selected in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft. Concepcion finished the game against the Tennessee Titans with eight receptions for 129 yards and 23 rushing yards, including an 18-yard scamper in the fourth quarter that helped set up a touchdown. The 129 receiving yards are the eighth-most by a rookie in a single game in franchise history , placing Concepcion in the company of notable players like Paul Warfield, Kevin Johnson, and Webster Slaughter. While pleased with his stats in Cleveland’s latest comeback victory, after the game Concepcion said he believes this should be the norm rather than the exception : “I enter every week expecting to have a game like this. This week was my breakout game. I just can’t wait to keep stacking weeks. I’ve been this way all my life. I play this game with so much heart, so much effort. I’m finally glad that Browns fans and the Browns community were finally able to see what I can bring to this team.” The Titans were not the only ones who took notice of Concepcion’s big day, but the NFL did as well as Concepcion has been nominated for Rookie of the Week honors for Week 7. Who should be the @pepsi Rookie of the Week for Week 7? Vote in the poll below! ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/RiClxCg3W2 — NFL (@NFL) October 27, 2026 Concepcion leads the Browns in receptions (30), is second in receiving yards (315) to fellow rookie Denzel Boston, and is one of eight Cleveland players averaging more than 10 yards per reception. The other players nominated for the award are: New York Jets wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr., who had five receptions for 115 yards and one touchdown Miami Dolphins wide receiver Caleb Douglas, who had two receptions for 70 yards and two touchdowns Atlanta Falcons linebacker Kendal Daniels, who has 11 tackles, one interception, and one fumble recovery Fan voting takes place on Instagram or X (@NFL) through Thursday at 11 a.m. EST. As of now, as reported previously, Cleveland plans on running with four quarterbacks on their active roster, […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns continue to keep things moving on their roster, as NFL trade rumors and deals start to heat up. On Monday, the Browns activated QB Dillon Gabriel from injured reserve and waived seventh-round TE Carsen Ryan . As of now, as reported previously, Cleveland plans on running with four quarterbacks on their active roster , which can create some needs in other areas. GM Andrew Berry and HC Todd Monken could help offset those needs by how they use the practice squad, including for game-day elevations. On Tuesday, the Browns made three practice squad-related moves, which leaves an open spot on that part of the roster: Signed DE Nadame Tucker Released RB Jaret Patterson Released S John Saunders Tucker was released from Cleveland’s practice squad last week to make room for DT Eric Johnson II . It is possible that the currently open practice squad spot will go to Ryan if he clears waivers. While Gabriel was activated from injured reserve, the Browns did not do the same with DT Kalia Davis which now sidelines him on IR for the rest of the season: The Browns will not be activating DT Kalia Davis (quad) off IR, so he will miss the remainder of the season. Cleveland signed Davis to a one-year deal in the offseason, but he only practiced a few times as he dealt with the injury. https://t.co/yTgMsiCGyq — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) October 26, 2026 It is possible that Davis’ inability to return spurs trade action from Berry before the November 10th deadline. Davis was expected to play a role at nose tackle for the Cleveland defensive line.

full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - OCTOBER 25: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns celebrates a touchdown with Quinshon Judkins #10 of the Cleveland Browns during the first quarter against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Browns fans and fans across the country. The Cleveland Browns are 5-2 after having beaten the Tennessee Titans, and they remain atop the AFC North. However, they cannot take their foot off the gas, because the rest of the teams in the division have competitive records as well. That includes this week’s game in Pittsburgh, a city that Cleveland has not won a regular season game in since 2003. The stakes are that the division lead is on the line. With that in mind, the second question in our Reacts survey below asks for your confidence in the direction of the team. It was at 85% last week, can it possibly get higher? Our other question focuses on the Browns’ offense this past Sunday against the Titans. It was their best collective effort of the season, as they put up nearly 500 yards of offense and tied a season high with 27 points. Perhaps most impressive is the fact that despite being down 14-0 early, they maintained a good mix of effective runs and passes to get right back in it. It was also the best that the running game has looked all season, and rookie WR KC Concepcion had a breakout performance. The poll is trying to gauge whether you attribute the offensive success to the Titans just being bad, or the offense starting to find a groove. What did you think of the Browns offense? title: Week 8 Browns NFL Power Rankings: Cleveland moves into the upper half of NFL
summary: It is Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns put together a game-winning drive for the fifth time this season to improve to 5-2 and remain atop the AFC North. Overall, the Browns went up by 1.8 spots from week-to-week to have an overall ranking of 14.3. That is now good […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 18: Todd Monken of the Cleveland Browns tips his cap prior to a game against the Baltimore Ravens at Huntington Bank Field on October 18, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns put together a game-winning drive for the fifth time this season to improve to 5-2 and remain atop the AFC North. Overall, the Browns went up by 1.8 spots from week-to-week to have an overall ranking of 14.3 . That is now good for third in the division, just ahead of the Ravens, while Pittsburgh and Cincinnati are ranked higher. Here is a summary of how the Cleveland Browns are viewed across mainstream media outlets in NFL Power Rankings heading into Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season. CBS Sports – No. 14 (up 2 spots) Beating the Titans in a close one might not be impressive, but they are 5-2. That is impressive. Deshaun Watson is playing well. ESPN – No. 16 (up 3 spots) Best offseason addition: HC Todd Monken The first-year coach has the Browns at 5-2 for the second time since the franchise returned to Cleveland in 1999. Quarterback Deshaun Watson is playing his best football with the Browns, and the NFL’s second-youngest team has taken on Monken’s ethos as a tough, resilient bunch with a league-high five winning drives. “Coach Monk has put us in these situations in practice time after time … so whenever we get into the game and whenever we get into these situations, we already have the confidence to go down there and set up a game-winning drive,” rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion said. NFL.com – No. 12 (up 4 spots) I feel like I write this every week, yet it remains true: They can’t keep getting away with this! The Browns recorded yet another victory by completing a game-winning drive, with Andre Szmyt drilling his second walk-off field goal in as many weeks. Now, a narrow win over the lowly Titans isn’t exactly inspiring on it’s own, but with Cleveland at 5-2, I can’t continue arguing against the Browns’ method of success. They earned bonus points from me for overcoming an early 14-0 deficit. That type of hole would have buried past Cleveland teams, but not Todd Monken’s squad. Sporting News – No. 15 (up 1 spot) Deshaun Watson has led game-winning fourth-quarter drives in all of their five wins. Give them a close game late and they can turn a trick into a treat with a gritty defense and experienced quarterback. Todd Monken needs more attention for coach of the year. Yahoo Sports – No. 16 (up 3 spots) The Browns are on the kind of exciting run in close games that has rarely been seen in NFL history. Cleveland got another last-second win when it responded to a game-tying touchdown by Tennessee with 58 seconds left by putting together a quick drive for the game-winning field goal as time expired. Pulling out close wins every week is unsustainable (“We’re gonna have to figure out how to start faster. That’s for damn sure,” head coach Todd Monken said), but a 5-2 record will keep the Browns in playoff contention. Odds are skeptical. DVOA has the Browns with just a 30% chance to make the playoffs. That’s not stopping the good vibes. “There’s something about this group,” Monken said, via the team’s site. “There’s something about those guys that play the next play and continue to fight for each other.” Bleacher Report – No. 12 (up 1 spot) Under first-time head coach Todd Monken, the Cleveland Browns have found ways to win one-score games. They won a last-second nail-biter in Tennessee, keeping them atop the AFC North. At this point, we have to give the Browns more respect in the power rankings, even if questions remain about their quarterback and limited offense. Cleveland is 5-1 in one-score games decided by five points or fewer. Monken has a battle-tested squad. USA Today – No. 15 (down 1 spot) Say what you want about QB Deshaun Watson − and I generally do − but he’s led a game-winning drive in all five of this first-place team’s wins. He had one in his first four seasons in Cleveland … combined. title: Former Browns QB Seneca Wallace checks in with DBN: Cleveland, cold weather, and so much more
summary: The New Cleveland Browns were reborn in 1999 and struggled to gain any footing in the league. A lot of head coaches, GMs, and players came and went. Mike Holmgren had been a successful head coach while at the helm of the Green Bay Packers, including winning Super Bowl XXXI. He then became the head […]
full_text: The New Cleveland Browns were reborn in 1999 and struggled to gain any footing in the league. A lot of head coaches, GMs, and players came and went. Mike Holmgren had been a successful head coach while at the helm of the Green Bay Packers, including winning Super Bowl XXXI. He then became the head coach of the Seattle Seahawks beginning in 1999. RELATED: QB PAUL MCDONALD INTERVIEW In the 2003 NFL Draft, Holmgren selected QB Seneca Wallace out of Iowa State in the fourth round. This was the draft in which QB Carson Palmer of USC was selected first overall. At the time, the Seahawks had Matt Hasselbeck entrenched at quarterback with Trent Dilfer as his backup. Wallace filled in nicely as QB3, slated for development behind two seasoned veterans. In his five seasons in Seattle, Wallace played in 48 games with just 14 starts under center. However, because he was such a gifted athlete, Holmgren would insert Wallace at receiver at times, or as a Wildcat option. In the 2005 NFC Championship Game between the Seahawks and the Carolina Panthers, a convincing 34-14 Seahawks win, Wallace made a pivotal reception that became the game’s longest pass completion. The victory placed Seattle in Super Bowl XL against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Holmgren stepped down as head coach of the Seahawks in order to take off for a year. He was an analyst for NBC plus served as an analyst for Seattle Sports station KJR 950AM. The following season, he accepted the job of President of the Cleveland Browns. One of his first orders of business was to work out a trade with his former team to obtain Wallace. Wallace played two seasons in Cleveland. He suffered a high-ankle sprain, which derailed his time with the Browns, and only played in 14 games with seven starts. Wallace played eight seasons in the NFL. His career stats: 64 games played, 22 starts, threw 788 attempts with 468 completions for 4,947 yards, a 59.4% completion ratio, converted 237 first downs, tossed 31 touchdowns with 19 interceptions, and had a 64.4 QB rating. He also rushed 68 times for 293 yards with another score, and had six receptions for 106 yards. A California kid, Wallace grew up in Rancho Cordova, just a stone’s throw east of Sacramento, which is two hours from San Francisco. He was a standout athlete playing for Cordova High School on their basketball and football squads. As good as he was in football, he was a standout in basketball despite being 5’-11” and 190 pounds. He was named All- Sierra Conference and All-Sacramento Honorable Mention in basketball and recognized as one of the top basketball talents in his region. He also lettered in football, where he won multiple football honors. But because of his size, he did not see a future in basketball past the college level. He accepted a scholarship with Sacramento City College to play football because he did not have enough credits. At Sac City, he absolutely shined. He set the school record by amassing 513 passing yards in a single game, a record that stands today. He was a standout QB who had great legs and made lots of damage as a runner. He ran a 4.56 in the 40, which added to his elusiveness. Wallace then made the decision to transfer to Iowa State for the 2001 college football season. He had bonded with their head coach, Dan McCarney, and the campus just felt like home. He won the starting QB position for his junior and senior campaigns, and started 25 games with 411 completions on 712 attempts for 5,289 yards, a 57.7% completion ratio, threw 26 touchdowns and 27 picks, with a QB rating of 124.6. He rushed 237 times for 912 yards and added another 15 touchdowns. In his junior year, he was named the “Big 12 Newcomer of the Year, and as a senior, he was voted Second Team All-Big 12. Wallace was taken by the Seahawks in the fourth round of the 2003 NFL Draft. He played a wide variety of positions in order to get himself on the field, including quarterback, receiver, and as a Wildcat option. In 2010, the Browns traded a seventh-round draft pick for him. Later, he signed with the New Orleans Saints, San Francisco 49ers, and the Green Bay Packers, where he played in two games with one start. After he hung up his cleats, he was a coaching assistant with the Dallas Cowboys, coached high school football, and recently was the QB coach with the St. Louis Battlehawks of the UFL. Wallace has been inducted into several Hall of Fames: Sacramento City College Hall of Fame (2013) Rancho Cordova High School Hall of Fame inaugural class (2015) Iowa State Athletics Hall of Fame (2019) Today, Wallace resides in Prosper, Texas. His wife, Abbie, and their three children are Christians. He has a foundation called Joyce’s Angels , which is in honor of his mother, who passed away from Multiple Myeloma. Dawgs by Nature staff writer Barry Shuck had a great conversation with Wallace about his playing career, including his time with the Browns. Shuck: You played basketball and football at Cordova High School. You were named All-Conference in basketball. At some point, did you think that basketball was going to be your path? Wallace: I did a little bit and enjoyed playing the game of basketball. Growing up in Sacramento, California, you were playing basketball on the streets, and it was easy to play with or without anybody else. All you needed was a ball and a hoop. But with football, you could play catch with one other person, but that was it. You don’t play it by yourself. So, naturally, I gravitated to basketball. But my first love was soccer. I played soccer for about six years around some clubs, and I just remember my buddies growing up in California; they would always drive by when I was at soccer practice, and they were on their way to football practice. I played my eighth-grade year of Pop Warner and then in the ninth grade in football all the way through high school. But I played soccer through the seventh grade. I played basketball and football through high school. I always loved basketball. I have a goal in my backyard. But football took me to another level. I was able to go and play in college, but I didn’t put all my resources into basketball. Once I started playing football in high school, it was over after that. Shuck: At what point did you decide to pursue football over basketball? Wallace: Probably my junior year. I was All-City and All-District for basketball and played all the way through high school, but unless you are 6’-6” and go on to score 30 a night, it’s hard to make it. Football gave me more opportunities, and I got a lot of scholarship offers. And that’s at the point where I decided, like, you know what, football’s going to take me to a different level and give me an opportunity to play in college. Shuck: How did you end up at Sacramento City College? Wallace: The short version is I wasn’t qualified coming out of high school. I didn’t have enough qualifications to transfer coming out of high school. You have to have four years of transferable English, four years of some other transferable subjects, and they just put some basic communications to get you to graduate high school. They put a lot of people in those classes who they don’t really consider going to college. It was unfortunate, but in my senior year, going to my junior and senior counselors, you have to have XYZ classes in order to get offered. In my junior and senior years, I ended up taking three years of English, geometry, and all these classes to get above a 750 SAT. Those are hard courses. I did all this and got 1110 on my SAT. I got a scholarship offer from Oregon State, accepted the offer, and was there for about two months. They had to petition for the last class. They said if you get your three years of geometry, Spanish I and II, they said they could petition for the last English class and should be able to get me through. We did all that; I went to school, and the petition didn’t go through. We had letters from principals and counselors, and they denied it. So, I ended up having to go…

title: Browns victory in review: Offense unlocked, Jared Verse questions, and celebrating 5-2
summary: Spread the news: the Cleveland Browns are 5-2. After overcoming an early 14-0 deficit against the Tennessee Titans, the Browns responded by scoring 17 unanswered points in the 2nd quarter. It wasn’t necessarily a back-and-forth affair, but Cleveland was able to find a way to come out with a victory. 1st Down: Offense has best […]
full_text: Spread the news: the Cleveland Browns are 5-2 . After overcoming an early 14-0 deficit against the Tennessee Titans, the Browns responded by scoring 17 unanswered points in the 2nd quarter . It wasn’t necessarily a back-and-forth affair, but Cleveland was able to find a way to come out with a victory . 1st Down: Offense has best game as a unit If there was any chance for the Cleveland Browns offense to have a confidence-building game, Sunday against the Titans was the perfect opportunity. Overall, the unit had one of its better performances of the season. In terms of the quarterback play, another good performance for Deshaun Watson. Despite the interception that wasn’t necessarily his fault (but it’s not worth rehashing), he was getting the ball out quickly, going through his progressions and using his legs when necessary. The offensive line also deserves their flowers as well. In terms of pass protection, the group was stout in that department, but the main thing that was impressive was the run blocking. The running game was able to materialize to some degree, as the running lanes were being opened, which allowed the running backs to find open space and gain positive yards. However, there will be a play when the defender breaks through the line of scrimmage or meets directly at the line of scrimmage. It isn’t to say that the running game is completely fixed, but Sunday was a positive development. Overall, a good day at the office for the offense. 2nd Down: Defense struggles, let’s talk about Jared Verse From a defensive standpoint, the Browns didn’t play their best, but it wasn’t an abysmal performance. It just wasn’t a good performance by their standards. Running back Tony Pollard must have a vendetta against Cleveland because every time he plays against them, he has a monster game. Pollard was an issue last time these teams played, and he was an issue on Sunday. Defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg continues to show why the defense is in good hands with him leading the show. However, Rutenberg will tend to play more zone coverage than I like. In the 4th quarter specifically, quarterback Cam Ward was able to find the soft spot in the zone, which allowed the Titans to drive down the field. Tennessee’s offense has talent, make no mistake, but at times the defense made the Titans’ job easier. When the Browns traded away Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams for Jared Verse as well as draft capital, we all had some thoughts, including me: I know what an elite pass rusher looks like, and Jared Verse is not elite. He’s very good. https://t.co/jhnqtIDqjk — Curt (@curtiss_brown21) June 3, 2026 Jared Verse ain’t bad but I’ve seen him have more disappearing acts when it matters the most. — Curt (@curtiss_brown21) June 1, 2026 I’ve seen my share of Rams games, and oftentimes Verse was nonexistent. Verse is very good; however, he’s not great. His pass rush skill set is limited, and he’s not going to beat you with speed. When his bull rush isn’t working, he has nothing to counter with. The Browns were never going to get 3 firsts for Garrett; it was impossible. Expecting Verse to replicate what Myles did was impossible as well. However, he can’t have games in which he’s not getting multiple pressures and/or turning those into sacks or forcing a turnover, as he did on Sunday. Verse would benefit from a star edge rusher across from him rather than being the main guy. 3rd Down: KC, Judkins and Fannin Jr made an impact It makes sense to focus on wide receiver KC Concepcion, tight end Harold Fannin Jr and running back Quinshon Judkins for this section. Starting with Concepcion: Browns rookie WR KC Concepcion: 8 catches, 129 yards with another 23 yards on 3 carries. Star performance for a breakout young player — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) October 25, 2026 K.C. Concepcion had a career-high 129 yards receiving. Concepcion gained 55 yards after contact, the most by any @NFL wide receiver in any game this season. (via @NFLPlus research) — Andrew Siciliano (@AndrewSiciliano) October 25, 2026 When the ball is in his hands, he’s likely going to make something happen. The one thing that the Browns lacked in the passing game was generating explosive plays, and Concepcion does that. Aside from the performance, the rookie receiver is someone that you want to root for. From his work ethic to his overall demeanor, you can see why Cleveland took him so early: #Browns WR KC Concepcion: "I play this game with so much heart, so much effort. I'm finally glad that Browns fans and the Browns community was finally able to see what I can bring to this team." pic.twitter.com/4a0ERfzN41 — Camryn Justice (@camijustice) October 25, 2026 Running back Quinshon Judkins had a bounce-back game, and he looked confident when he was running the ball. Tight end Harold Fannin was a topic of discussion due to his lack of targets this season, but like Concepcion, it changed for him on Sunday. Fannin has been asked to do more than expected, mainly due to the lack of depth in the tight end room, but when his name is called upon, he makes a play. He benefitted from the team moving him around and utilizing him in different ways, but this specific play was the reason why the Browns came out with a win: Harold Fannin Jr. with the big catch and run to put the Browns into field goal range! CLEvsTEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/x27nZZqjK0 — NFL (@NFL) October 25, 2026 4th Down: 5-2 is 5-2, so enjoy it and ignore any detractors Personally, as long as you are winning, I don’t care how it’s supposed to look. Sunday’s game wasn’t any different. Despite their record, the Titans have talent on their team, so the idea that the Browns should’ve steamrolled them is a little too far-fetched. Both squads are rebuilding teams, with Cleveland ahead of schedule, and this game had the potential to be close. Why? It’s the NFL. As far as the Browns go, I’ve seen people try to discredit their 5-2 record, and I won’t allow it. Going into the season, many experts had this team finishing with the worst record in the league. Instead, the team has eclipsed their win total from last season, and they are finding ways to win. That’s all that matters. Whether the team is a playoff team is another topic for another day, but for now, enjoy this because it doesn’t happen as much as it should. Extra Points: The Browns getting the referee group that has thrown the most penalty flags this season wasn’t a coincidence at all. The officiating in the NFL has been egregious this season. Yes, RT Dawand Jones should’ve been called for a false start during the Browns last possession late in the 4th, but the Titans should’ve been called for a delay of game on their drive when they tied the game in the 4th, so it doesn’t really matter. Not a great game from WR Denzel Boston, but it’s the NFL; he’ll bounce back Expect the Browns to be buyers at the trade deadline considering how the AFC playoff picture is wide open What are your thoughts now that you’ve had a day to digest the Browns most recent win? title: 2026 NFL Week 8: Dallas Cowboys vs. Arizona Cardinals
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are coming off of a win for the first time in a while. It feels pretty nice. Last time that was the case much was made about how they have only had one winning streak under head coach Brian Schottenheimer. That remains true, but Sunday’s tilt against the Arizona Cardinals offers the […]
full_text: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are coming off of a win for the first time in a while. It feels pretty nice. Last time that was the case much was made about how they have only had one winning streak under head coach Brian Schottenheimer. That remains true, but Sunday’s tilt against the Arizona Cardinals offers the next opportunity for the Cowboys to do it. While the Cowboys are coming off of a much-needed win on Monday night against the Philadelphia Eagles, the Cardinals have seen better days. Arizona just lost to the Denver Broncos and much was made about how poor attendance was in their home building, especially since it was a celebration for Larry Fitzgerald entering the Pro Football Hall of Fame this past summer. This game is at AT&T Stadium though, and quite frankly the Cardinals have owned the Cowboys in it and everywhere for that matter. The old school NFC East rivals have squared off a bit over the last decade, and the extreme majority have gone to the Cardinals. Dallas is 1-8 against Arizona since 2008. Brian Schottenheimer, Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, and Javonte Williams will be charged with scoring points to not let another loss happen. Defensively it goes without saying that we need to see more from Christian Parker, but even the likes of Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark need to raise their games another level. Joey Porter Jr. has been excellent since Dallas acquired him. Something else to monitor in this game is the fact that Dallas has been linked to Cardinals pass rusher Josh Sweat. Perhaps a Cowboys win pushes Arizona closer to selling off assets like Sweat. Bring it on. title: Complementary football gets Cowboys back on the horse in primetime
summary: For the first time in eight games, the Dallas Cowboys had more rushing attempts than passing attempts in a game, and the result was the same on Monday night as it was in Week 17 last season – a win against a division rival. The Cowboys won at the Philadelphia Eagles for the first time […]
full_text: Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images | Getty Images For the first time in eight games, the Dallas Cowboys had more rushing attempts than passing attempts in a game, and the result was the same on Monday night as it was in Week 17 last season – a win against a division rival. The Cowboys won at the Philadelphia Eagles for the first time in five tries, avoiding a three-game losing streak while handing the Eagles a fifth straight loss, sending Philly to 2-5 and improving their own record to 3-4. The Cowboys won’t return to division play until they see the Eagles again on Thanksgiving, but also will only play one team currently with a winning record until then, and three of those four at home. For a fanbase as starved for a win as this one, it’s super easy to get carried away with talking about what elements can carry over from this Eagles win and make it something more than it is, but in this case the opportunity really is right out in front of Brian Schottenheimer’s team. For now, let’s start with how they capitalized on the opportunity to play a depleted Eagles team, and came away with a win, 38-21 in primetime, while holding their third straight opponent under 25 points. Taking Back Control The Eagles started the second half with the ball and possessed it for 9:16 over a 17-play drive, converting a trio of third downs along the way, one fourth down, and then ultimately scoring on third-and-goal with Makai Lemon’s first NFL touchdown. A Quinnen Williams tackle for loss on 1st-and-goal couldn’t save the possession from giving the lead back to the Eagles, their third touchdown drive of the night. The only reason there wasn’t panic at this point for the Cowboys, despite seeing the nightmare script of their past two losses starting to unfold again, was because they had already scored on four of five of their own drives. As wild as it is to say, if this game needed to be a Dak Prescott versus Tanner McKee shootout, the Cowboys were ready for it. The Cowboys targeted CeeDee Lamb four times on the ensuing drive and finally got him in the endzone from 16 yards out to go up 28-21. They stayed in control of the game from here on out. The Eagles remaining four drives from this point on totaled 7:19 of possession, four first downs, and zero points with a Demarvion Overshown interception thrown in. It’s amazing just how many things a strong running game can unlock within a game, but by way of the Cowboys running the ball uber-efficiently, they could trust the defense more as the game wore on. They continued to hit timely passes, kicked field goals that actually felt like wins and not defeats, and leave the city of brotherly love feeling good. Overcoming Hyperbole is commonplace when it comes to NFL fans, especially those of America’s Team. The Cowboys did earn plenty of criticism during their two-game losing streak though, and at the center of it was how easily the team seemingly folded when things weren’t going their way. The fact the Cowboys had to overcome as many things as they did to beat this injury-riddled Eagles team will certainly come up this week, but for now the improved signs of fight from Schotty’s squad with their backs against the wall can be complimented. The Cowboys offense had not been starting games strong, with opening drives often stalling out around midfield. The same thing happened on Monday night, but getting more burst from Javonte Williams from the start at least got them in field goal range for Brandon Aubrey to make it 3-0. The Eagles needed just four plays to score with Saquon Barkley after this, and go up 7-3. Dallas committed a penalty on the ensuing kickoff and started their next drive backed up, but overcame this to get a slot-fade touchdown to Lamb and a 10-7 lead. The Dallas defense had a Quinnen Williams offsides on fourth and short, they gave up a first down on a screen on third and long, had an LT Overton roughing the passer call, and gave up another touchdown to see the home team go back up 14-10. The Cowboys started backed up yet again in response to this, after Tyler Goodson’s kickoff return touchdown was called back by a Justin Barron holding penalty. Still, they overcame and scored a touchdown, this time unleashing George Pickens behind the defense. The offense also overcame a sequence on this drive that could have doomed them, after throwing a 1st-and-10 double-move deep ball to Jonathan Mingo that really didn’t have a chance. Followed by a second down run, this drive looked destined to stall out, but Pickens getting enough on third down to allow Javonte Williams to move the chains on fourth down gave it life again. The touchdown followed. When the defense finally did get a stop, it led to the offense being pinned at their own two-yard line and going three and out. DeMarvion Overshown and Joey Porter Jr. had the back-to-back pass deflections to get the Eagles off the field, with Overshown getting the vast majority of the run at middle linebacker in his return to action. The defense stepped up again and got their first three and out of the game right after this, getting the ball back in time for the offense to get three more points and lead 20-14 at halftime. The early goings of this game felt like the pressure on the offense was building, and one Prescott mistake could have seen the house of cards come falling all down again. The way the Cowboys turned this around, which in turn helped Prescott settle into a groove, was well done. The Cowboys had 25 first downs, gaining 12 of them through the air and 11 on the ground. Complementary football was on display in Philadelphia. Whether or not the Cowboys can consistently play like this, we have no idea. What we do know is they’ll get to spend the week seeing a game film that showed highly-paid and highly-anticipated players stepping up all over the place to prove they can collectively make a winning difference, and for now that’s a whole lot better than anything that came out of the Tampa Bay or Green Bay losses. Glimpses of What it Could Be To go a bit further on this and put a bow on the first primetime win of the season, the Cowboys offense showed it’s most legitimate glimpses of the season of how good they really could be. We’ve been harping on for weeks about playing to the strength of the offensive line and letting them go downhill, and it was so good at the Eagles that All-Pro Tyler Smith was flat out looking for defenders to block and not finding them while Williams broke off a big run anyway. The drive before halftime to get a field goal will lead to Monday Tuesday morning quarterback discussions on how Schottenheimer managed the timeouts, but it also saw one of the best examples of the offense taking something that should be easy to do, making it exactly that, and executing at a high level because of it. The Philly defense was sitting on the slant routes from Lamb and Pickens all night, and in hurry-up mode the Cowboys took advantage and got Lamb behind the defense with a slant and double move down the field. Lamb’s first touchdown was also a crystal clear example of what this offense could be at it’s best, and it was a thing of beauty. The Eagles had clear safety help to the side of Pickens on this play, and Prescott recognized it right away. Ryan Flournoy ran a crisp vertical route to create space in the seam area for Lamb to work out of the slot, and Lamb got the touchdown. Between these passing plays and the trio of Lamb, Pickens, and Williams on the ground having big nights, fans can only hope this is the game that teaches Schottenheimer and Klayton Adams alike that getting the ball to the team’s best players doesn’t have to be hard. Frankly, with the defensive performance still leaving quite a bit to be desired, the simplest thing to learn from this win is that the Cowboys continue to be a team that will go as Dak Prescott goes, but hoping for more repeat performances of the Dak we saw on Monday night is a bit easier to do now being back in the win column.

title: Cowboys run game paves the way in bounce-back win over Eagles
summary: The Dallas Cowboys needed a win on Monday night in the worst way. Coming off two straight losses and facing off against a Philadelphia Eagles team that was missing key pieces on both sides of the ball, Dallas needed to walk out of Philly with a win to avoid a complete freefall. While they were […]
full_text: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys needed a win on Monday night in the worst way. Coming off two straight losses and facing off against a Philadelphia Eagles team that was missing key pieces on both sides of the ball, Dallas needed to walk out of Philly with a win to avoid a complete freefall. While they were far from perfect, the Cowboys avoided that third straight loss as their offense led them to a 38-21 win over the beaten-down Eagles. Multiple players on Dallas’ offense had notable performances, but it was their running attack that stole the show, earning them this week’s game ball award. Against the Buccaneers and Packers, the Cowboys couldn’t sustain success in the run game. Dallas totaled 98 rushing yards in the two matchups, and their one-dimensional attack played a role in their losses. On Monday night, for what felt like the first time this season, the Cowboys’ rushing attack set the stage for their offense. Dallas totaled a season-high 204 rushing yards on 38 attempts, averaging 5.4 Y/R as a team. The Cowboys finished with the third-best offensive rush EPA of any team in Week 7 (0.199) while also finishing in the top eight in rush success rate (48.6%). Javonte Williams had a notably impressive performance, recording a career-high 155 rushing yards to go with 82 yards after contact and five missed tackles forced. Williams’ impressive physicality in the run game set the tone for Dallas’ offense from the first snap. Javonte Williams on MNF: 25 carries 155 yards (career high) 1 TD First Cowboy with 150+ rushing yards in a game since Ezekiel Elliott in 2018. pic.twitter.com/xOqz51Kdqq — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) October 27, 2026 If the Cowboys can continue to have a complementary, balanced attack on the offensive side of the ball like they did on Monday night, they are going to be very hard to slow down.

title: Cowboys at Eagles: The good, the bad, and ugly from Week 7
summary: In what was a must-win game, it was good to see the Dallas Cowboys take care of business in prime time on Monday Night Football to secure the 38-21 victory over their division rival, the Philadelphia Eagles. They now have a chance to string some wins together over the next few weeks and hopefully continue […]
full_text: Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images In what was a must-win game, it was good to see the Dallas Cowboys take care of business in prime time on Monday Night Football to secure the 38-21 victory over their division rival, the Philadelphia Eagles. They now have a chance to string some wins together over the next few weeks and hopefully continue to get better. While it was good to see the Cowboys secure the win in the first of two matchups with the Eagles this year, it was also obvious this team still has a lot to work on. There seemed to be more positives than negatives this week, which is a good sign things could be heading in the right direction. Hopefully that continues. THE GOOD – RB Javonte Williams For the first time this season the Cowboys leaned heavily on the running game and it paid off in a big way. Dallas rushed for over 200 yards, but it was Javonte Williams who led the way, rushing for 155 yards and one touchdown on 25 carries. This is the first time this season No. 33 rushed for 100+ yards, averaging an impressive 6.2 yards per carry. If this continues Dallas’ offense can get back on track and become lethal once again. THE BAD – Cowboys’ defense The Cowboys defense is still a major concern. They faced a shorthanded Eagles offense without their starting QB and their top two receivers and still allowed Philadelphia to put up 21 points on them. And, had Saquon Barkley been a 100%, the outcome of this game may have been different. He alone managed to rush for 62 yards and a TD on just seven carries. Christian Parker still is a lot of work on before his defense isn’t considered such a liability. THE UGLY – Eagles’ defensive line The Cowboys offensive line has been criticized in the first six weeks of the season. Considering the talent they have across the board, they had been underperforming and it has negatively impacted the offensive production. On Monday night against the Eagles they looked much improved. They provided a clean pocket for Dak Prescott to throw from the and opened up huge holes for Javonte Williams to run through. The Cowboys gave up zero sacks and zero tackles for loss in the game. Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis were non-factors. The offensive line made Philadelphia’s defensive line look ugly.
author: Brian Martin

title: 4 key plays from the Dallas win over the Eagles
summary: Boy, does it feel good to be back in the win column again. After falling to 2-4, the Dallas Cowboys were able to pull away late to secure the 38-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles. Dallas set the tone on the ground and ran the ball down the Eagles’ throats in a physical performance more […]
full_text: Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images | Getty Images Boy, does it feel good to be back in the win column again. After falling to 2-4, the Dallas Cowboys were able to pull away late to secure the 38-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles. Dallas set the tone on the ground and ran the ball down the Eagles’ throats in a physical performance more akin to what we should expect from an offensive line of their caliber. The defense still needs to perform better overall, but there were signs of progress, albeit against a depleted opponent offensively who featured a less-than-full-strength Saquon Barkley. Dak Prescott threw multiple scores, and maybe all isn’t lost this season as some might have feared. The Cowboys are one game back in the win column of the division-leading New York Giants in the NFC East. The team might be buying their chances of winning the division title and is ready to build the roster further versus dismantling it. So what were the pivotal moments in Monday night’s big win? Here are the four key plays that earned the Cowboys the victory. Javonte Williams untouched for 15 yards, 1 QTR, 13:44, 1st & 10 The Cowboys have come under a lot of fire lately, primarily for getting bullied on both sides of the ball in the trenches. You got the sense that if the Eagles felt like they could push Dallas around in front of their home crowd, it would ignite their belief that they could beat up on the Cowboys like many teams have done this season. Instead, the Cowboys turned the tables on the Eagles and their harshest critics. Javonte Williams found his footing early with a couple of big gains during the team’s first drive. On one play, Williams ran off to the left side of the offensive line and ran through a gaping hole for 15 yards that set up the Cowboys’ first points of the game. Upon looking at the replay, the play was blocked so well that Tyler Smith had no one to hit. From early on, the offensive line established themselves with that run and created big lanes all night for Williams, who set a career-high in rushing yards. Cowboys RB Javonte Williams’ rushing chart from his 25 carry, 155 yard performance vs. the Eagles via @NextGenStats Williams was not tackled for a loss on Monday night, and tied a career-high forced missed tackles with 8. pic.twitter.com/2HrQEvmyNW — Tommy Yarrish (@tommy_yarrish) October 27, 2026 This run was indicative of the team needing to play angry, and it certainly showed how they mauled the Eagles interior defensive line. If you needed any further indication of how dominant the offensive line was, the graphic above is pretty telling. That first series and that first big run let the Eagles know they were going to be in for a long night. Javonte Williams 4th-down conversion , 2nd QTR, 9:10, 4th & 1 Without a key time out called, this play likely doesn’t happen. On 4th and 1 from the Philadelphia 48-yard line, the Cowboys lined up in an attempt to draw the Eagles offsides with a hard count, and it appeared that the Cowboys had no intention of going for it on fourth down. However, after Nick Sirianni called a timeout, it gave Brian Schottenheimer more time to reassess his decision, opting to trust his offense. Javonte Williams easily picked up the fourth down, and the team capitalized thanks to George Pickens. ELITE throw and catch from Dak Prescott and George Pickens. pic.twitter.com/8oYulQ9ztK — RJ Ochoa (@rjochoa) October 27, 2026 Although you’d prefer not to be in a shootout against the Eagles’ backup quarterback, it definitely helps having the caliber of weapons the Cowboys have at their disposal. George Pickens has been under the microscope this week after some not-so-veiled comments by his head coach regarding his effort in the running game. Let’s call it a call to action, because Pickens made one of his best plays of the season. The throw from Prescott is excellent, but the effort by Pickens to catch the ball cleanly off first contact with his hands is top-notch. To have the wherewithal to get both of his feet in bounds to complete the process of the catch was elite. That touchdown was the result of Schottenheimer making the key decision to go for it on fourth down. Riq Woolen keeps drive alive, 3rd QTR, 4:53, 3rd & 9 After the defense was strung out on the field for yet another extensive drive that has become all too familiar this season, the Cowboys had to answer with points. Having surrendered a nine-minute drive, you felt that familiar dread start to sink in, and started to think this would be the moment it would begin to slip away. Except the Eagles threw the Cowboys a gift when they committed one of their five penalties on the night. While working back to the outside on a route, Riq Woolen grabbed CeeDee Lamb, drawing the flag for defensive holding. It was a pivotal sequence because Lamb dropped the pass thrown to him on this play. With the penalty, the Cowboys avoided giving the ball back to Philadelphia and proceed to end the drive with Lamb’s second score of the night and a two-point conversion to pull ahead 28-21. DeMarvion Overshown shuts it down, 4th QTR, 7:55, 1st & 10 DEMARVION OVERSHOWN INT DALvsPHI on ESPN⁰Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SH5FW4gwC0 — NFL (@NFL) October 27, 2026 DeMarvion Overshown has teased the Cowboys with his talent for the last few seasons. Injuries have kept him from him fully reaching his potential, and prevented him from being a full contributor to the defense. Overshown hadn’t played since the season opener when he was injured and sidelined with a hamstring issue. His interception of Tanner McKee was a long time coming. Overshown did a great job of reading the eyes of the quarterback to break on the ball, undercutting the out route and making the timely interception. If the Eagles had an outside chance, that was the moment that removed all doubt. The defense has a lot more work to do, but they did show flashes in the second half. They got pressure on the passer and broke up passes in the secondary. Overshown’s interception stopped the Eagles’ last best chance, and sent Dallas on their way to the win.

The win moved the Cowboys to 3-4 and kept them within striking range of the New York Giants in the NFC East. Season not over just yet. The Cowboys are also getting the aid of a soft schedule coming up. They face the Arizona Cardinals (2-5), Indianapolis Colts (2-5), San Francisco 49ers (6-1), Tennessee Titans (1-6), and the Philadelphia Eagles (2-5). Only one out of their next five games is against a good football team. Whether the Cowboys can take advantage of that schedule is still in doubt. For one thing, they are still a work in progress as a football team. They can lose to anybody at any time. Another thing is the Cardinals. The Cowboys have lost eight out of the last nine times these two teams have played each other, and the Cardinals have run out plenty of bad teams over that stretch. So what is your call BTB? title: 2026 NFL Week 8 Power Rankings: Cowboys move up after Monday night win
summary: We are right around the corner from the halfway point of the 2026 NFL season. Where did the time go? Wherever it went, the Dallas Cowboys spent part of it driving us mad and now are on the verge of (hopefully) turning things around. We have to see as always, obviously. The first step in […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect We are right around the corner from the halfway point of the 2026 NFL season. Where did the time go? Wherever it went, the Dallas Cowboys spent part of it driving us mad and now are on the verge of (hopefully) turning things around. We have to see as always, obviously. The first step in that process was winning on Monday night against the Philadelphia Eagles. Given the state of Philly though, that isn’t obviously saying much. What exactly is the state of everyone involved here? Let’s discuss in our weekly power rankings. 1 – Buffalo Bills (LW: 2) Back from the bye. Let’s see how it goes. 2 – San Francisco 49ers (LW: 1) The stumbled for the first time, but it is a long season and we know better than to doubt them. 3 – Detroit Lions (LW: 5) I’ve said that I really doubted them entering this season. It is only Halloween week, but I’ve got plenty of crow to share if anybody wants some. 4 – Chicago Bears (LW: 9) They look very much like a contender with Caleb Williams back. Watch out. 5 – Jacksonville Jaguars (LW: 6) Also back from the break. 6 – Seattle Seahawks (LW: 11) It is clear that things are not fully perfect, but finding a way really matters. 7 – New England Patriots (LW: 4) There is not a ton of shame in losing on the road against a top-tier team on a short week, but it still doesn’t feel great. 8 – Minnesota Vikings (LW: 12) Every now and then the final undefeated team is one that nobody really finds to be all that intimidating. Minnesota’s defense is clearly very special. But they are hardly a juggernaut overall. 9 – Cincinnati Bengals (LW: 13) They appear to be very much the real deal right now. Future winners of the AFC North, perhaps? 10 – Baltimore Ravens (LW: 7) Huge analysis here, but Lamar Jackson is needed. 11 – Atlanta Falcons (LW: 20) Maybe it is time to start taking the Falcons seriously. It is hard to gauge their overall ceiling, or floor for that matter, but they are clearly a team to monitor. 12 – Kansas City Chiefs (LW: 3) People have written off Kansas City many times in their overall run. Maybe that’s what’s happening here, but it doesn’t quite feel that way. It feels like they are still pretty good, just not as good as they have been before. They are hardly bottoming out. At least not yet. 13 – Green Bay Packers (LW: 8) It is strange how they looked mortal a week after dominating the Cowboys. 14 – Los Angeles Rams (LW: 18) A game against the Raiders will get things right on track. 15 – New York Giants (LW: 23) They might truly and actually be the best team in the NFC East. It is very impressive how John Harbaugh has turned that ship around. 16 – Denver Broncos (LW: 15) Winning at Arizona is fine, but we need to see more. Also we know the Cowboys are hardly one to talk about the Cardinals. 17 – Cleveland Browns (LW: 16) Can they really sustain this? It is hard to believe so. Maybe, though. 18 – Pittsburgh Steelers (LW: 17) Mike McCarthy keeps finding a way. 19 – Tampa Bay Buccaneers (LW: 27) Baker Mayfield is back and so might be the Buccaneers. 20 – Dallas Cowboys (LW: 24) Monday was nice. Now do it again. 21 – Carolina Panthers (LW: 10) And it all came at their expense. 22 – Houston Texans (LW: 14) Losses like theirs are why 0-4 starts are so devastating. You lose all room for error so when you drop another game, particularly in overtime, it hurts all the more because of how consequential it is. 23 – Las Vegas Raiders (LW: 19) Fernando Mendoza time? 24 – New Orleans Saints (LW: 22) They have spunk. That’s about it, though. 25 – Arizona Cardinals (LW: 21) They are definitely beating the Cowboys, right? 26 – Philadelphia Eagles (LW: 25) This team is pretty lifeless these days. Oh well. 27 – Indianapolis Colts (LW: 26) This team is so boring. 28 – New York Jets (LW: 28) They have always been boring. 29 – Washington Commanders (LW: 29) It has been over a full year since they won a game with Jayden Daniels. 30 – Miami Dolphins (LW: 32) At least they won a game! 31 – Tennessee Titans (LW: 30) Sigh. 32 – Los Angeles Chargers (LW: 31) The only winless team in the NFL. Hype them up more, though. Please. ESPN : 20 (LW: 20) An interesting “best offseason addition” choice. Best offseason addition: DT Otito Ogbonnia It wasn’t supposed to be this way when the Cowboys put together their roster in the offseason. Their biggest free agent signing in a decade, safety Jalen Thompson, has missed the past four games because of a hamstring injury and hasn’t made game-changing plays. First-round pick Caleb Downs has been OK at safety. The other first-round pick, edge rusher Malachi Lawrence, moved into the starting lineup in Week 6. Ogbonnia, who signed a modest one-year, $2.75 million deal, has been the Cowboys’ best run defender up front over Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark. — Todd Archer NFL.com : 22 (LW: 26) A little up, but at least some movement. While it’s certainly not perfect, it appears the Cowboys’ offense is back. Dallas racked up 400 yards of offense against the Eagles’ defense — which is supposed to be Philadelphia’s strength — on Monday night, and received some welcome contributions from its defense in the second half, capped by DeMarvion Overshown’s diving interception. Javonte Williams cleared 130 yards on the ground, the CeeDee Lamb/George Pickens connections with Dak Prescott were reestablished, and Dallas proved itself as the better team in this NFC East rivalry. Does that mean the Cowboys are back on track? No, but it’s encouraging progress. USA Today : 23 (LW: 26) A little bump up. Perhaps the most encouraging component of Monday night’s win at Philadelphia was the full reawakening of RB Javonte Williams. Yahoo : 20 (LW: 21) As small a bump as possible here. There are still defensive problems. The Eagles, without several key starters on offense, including Jalen Hurts, moved the ball with ease on their first two drives that ended in touchdowns. But Dallas deserves credit for pitching a fourth-quarter shutout in a win it had to have. And the Cowboys’ offense seems to be over whatever slump it was in. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer challenged the offense to find balance, and it responded with 204 rushing yards on 5.4 yards per attempt on Monday night. If the Cowboys can run the ball like that, they’ll have a few more 38-point games. And they might need those types of games, unless the defense’s fourth-quarter performance is a sign of improvement. CBS Sports : 20 (LW: 19) Actually a drop here. Against the Eagles, that was the offense we expected to see from the Cowboys this season. If they can run it like that, they will be tough to beat. The Athletic : 18 (LW: 22) A little bit more of a climb. Something spooky: The NFC East Even with the Giants’ surprising record, the Cowboys, after the way they played in Philadelphia, might be the favorites to win the division. Javonte Williams (155 yards rushing and a touchdown) was incredible, and Dak Prescott threw three touchdown passes. ProFootballTalk : 21 (LW: 23) And there it is. The best solution for a bad defense is an offense that stays on the field for as long as it can. Week To Week Movement Full Power Rankings

title: Cowboys at Eagles Stock Report: Javonte Williams has a day
summary: A win is a win. To be clear Monday night was not that type for the Dallas Cowboys, but things have been so down as of late that even one road win against a hated division rival is likely not enough to bring some all the way back. That is fair. But a win is […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images A win is a win. To be clear Monday night was not that type for the Dallas Cowboys, but things have been so down as of late that even one road win against a hated division rival is likely not enough to bring some all the way back. That is fair. But a win is a win as noted, and the Cowboys took a serious step forward by getting one on Monday night in Philly. Now awaits the true test in the Arizona Cardinals. If you know you know. It was hardly a perfect effort from the Cowboys, but several key figures on the team really shined. Let’s get to them in our stock report. Stock Up: Brian Schottenheimer There was really only one direction for Schotty to go. Public approval was about as low as it had ever been for the Cowboys head coach, and while he still had some decisions on Monday that left us scratching our heads, he had the team ready for the challenge and everyone involved executed it. We are talking step by step, once more. In all seriousness, Schotty did have the Cowboys ready to go from a head coach perspective and also was a man of his word as an offensive play-caller. He leaned on the ground game and saw a lot of success in that area. That shows a willingness to change and he deserves credit for that. Stock Up: Javonte Williams Speaking of! Javonte Williams established a new career high in rushing with 155 yards, the most that any Cowboys player has had in a game since Ezkeiel Elliott back in 2016. What a throwback. It is one thing for the head coach to commit to running the ball more. It is another thing for the running back to be ready for the challenge. Williams clearly was. Stock Up: CeeDee Lamb Over training camp, as people were fawning (rightfully so!) over George Pickens, it felt like CeeDee Lamb was getting a bit forgotten. He is so incredibly special. Lamb is one of the most dynamic players in the entire NFL and sometimes it seems that he wills things into existence. This felt like the case during Monday night’s win. Thankfully the Cowboys have both of their star receivers. Stock Up: George Pickens GP3 did not have the full statistical day that his counterpart did, but he had several incredible catches that were critical to the overall team succeeding. That is commendable. What’s more, Pickens answered the call from his head coach to be more involved and help everything out. A rising tide and all that jazz. Stock Up: Dak Prescott Everything was moving and grooving for the Cowboys on offense and that certainly starts with the quarterback. Like his head coach and play-caller, Prescott had struggled over the last two weeks. He put that behind him, thankfully. Of note, this was Prescott’s 80th career game with multiple passing touchdowns. He now has the most in franchise history as he broke a tie he had with Tony Romo at 79. Stock Up: Tyler Goodson While Javonte Williams rightfully got all of the headlines, Tyler Goodson is seriously earning a larger role on this team. Or at least he should be. Goodson had the kickoff return touchdown called back due to penalty, but it seems like every time he touches the ball (however that is) he is doing so with extreme tenacity. He is making the most of those touches and you love to see that. Obviously KaVontae Turpin was out for this game due to injury, but maybe the Cowboys should look to Goodson as an alternative option. Stock Up: Shemar James The Cowboys put a lot of responsibility on Shemar James’ shoulders and it sort of felt like a surprise that they did so. To be clear, his stock up is relative to that context because obviously there isn’t much to write home about for the defense at large. Still, James kept things together in an overall sense. Given that the defense is really struggling to find any kind of stability out there that is a huge plus in his favor. So good for him. Static Stock: Quinnen Williams I’d like the record to show that I believe that Quinnen Williams rebounded a bit in the second half, but the first half was absolutely dreadful for him. Williams committed two penalties early on in this game that cannot happen. These penalties cannot happen for anyone on your team, one was an encroachment that gave the Eagles new life after Dallas stopped them on fourth down, let alone from your defensive leader who you traded serious capital for and gave a massive extension to. In the second half Williams was much more himself. He got a sack, and had three TFLs. That’s a pretty decent comeback for your star on the defense. He evened out his first-half mistakes. Stock Down: Christian Parker How is the defense still so consistently bad? And how are they committing so many penalties? Pre-snap penalties at that? I recognize that Christian Parker’s stock cannot go down any further. But what is his “get right” game? It wasn’t Jalon Daniels. It wasn’t Tanner McKee. What circumstances does it take for his group to look proper or dare I say even good? Stock Down: DaRon Bland Like with a lot of things on defense, there isn’t a whole lot to say that hasn’t already been offered. It is a little bit easier to see Bland’s struggles now that Joey Porter Jr. is a part of the fold, but this is such a serious point of weakness for the Cowboys. It might be their highest level priority in the offseason. Sigh.

title: Broncos News: Why are we talking about the Broncos making a trade?
summary: With the NFL trade deadline looming, all the talk is about your team making a trade for a good player from a bad team in order to help improve their roster. The buzzphrase is that your team is in “win now mode.” Yes, the Broncos are absolutely taking a big swing at making a run […]
full_text: With the NFL trade deadline looming, all the talk is about your team making a trade for a good player from a bad team in order to help improve their roster. The buzzphrase is that your team is in “win now mode.” Yes, the Broncos are absolutely taking a big swing at making a run for a Super Bowl. Yes, it is fun to think about making a trade for a Jonathon Taylor or Saquon Barkley. Yes, either of these players, or some of the other names thrown around like new Seahawk Quenton Nelson, would look great in a Broncos uniform. I’m just curious why anyone is getting their undies in a twist about the Broncos making a trade. “They need a guard like Quenton Nelson!” Why? They have a very solid group of linemen that are veterans. Their problem so far this year has more to do with execution, not a lack of ability. They also have guys like Alex Palczewski and Kage Casey in the wings ready to step in next year if we lose a guard. And let’s not forget that with Coleman running the ball, the line sure did look pretty decent. “The one thing the Broncos need is a better running back” I’m very much not sure on this one. They need a better back than 2026’s version of JK Dobbins. With Jonah Coleman healthy and looking like a stud so far in his one game back, I think they already have an answer. They also get Tyler Badie back somewhere around week 12 or later. The big problem is the cap space The Broncos currently have less than $5M in cap space available. Many of these players that people are talking about trading for have contracts far north of that this year, with possible considerable impact on the next couple of years. That’s not to say that the Broncos front office can work some numbers magic to make room, but they are already poised to lose some key players next season like Riley Moss, Ben Powers, and Evan Engram. Bringing in an expensive free agent may not be tenable with a team that is building a long-term winning culture. A five-game stretch beginning with three-straight road games. All five games are against legitimate playoff contenders. The Broncos would need to pull away just a bit during that stretch and put up a big enough cushion to take the division crown for the second straight year. title: NFL Power Rankings for Week 8: Denver Broncos somewhere up there
summary: It’s been a few weeks since I’ve run a power rankings update, but after a three-game win streak it felt like a good barometer check for how the national media feels about these Denver Broncos. The answer was that there is no consensus and they have Denver all over the map in these rankings. From […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - OCTOBER 25: RJ Harvey #12 of the Denver Broncos celebrates with Jaylen Waddle #17 after scoring a touchdown against the Arizona Cardinals during the third quarter at State Farm Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s been a few weeks since I’ve run a power rankings update, but after a three-game win streak it felt like a good barometer check for how the national media feels about these Denver Broncos. The answer was that there is no consensus and they have Denver all over the map in these rankings. From the best spot at third in the NFL to the worst at twelfth. The consensus seems to be around the sixth or seventh spot if you take out the extremes. That could all change this week is the Broncos take care of business at home against the Kansas City Chiefs. They will move into first place in the AFC West and put the Chiefs into ‘catch-up’ mode after being one of the only unbeaten teams in the NFL just two days ago. Here’s how the Broncos are doing in this week’s power rankings around the web: CBS Sports – 7th The offense showed signs of life against the Cardinals. That’s progress. Maybe it took a long touchdown run for Bo Nix to get him going this season. NBC Sports – 6th Take that, Ryan Fitzpatrick. ESPN – 8th Rookie running back Jonah Coleman has played in only three games because of an ankle injury , and he might win the impact-per-snap-played quotient, but Waddle leads the Broncos in receptions (26) and receiving yards (276). His numbers would likely look better if he had not been caught up in the swirl of Denver’s passing struggles. Waddle left Sunday’s game because of an apparent shoulder injury, but if it’s not serious and the Broncos can simply get him the ball more, his output will improve along with their offense. Yahoo Sports – 12th It’s unfair to just eliminate three long plays for a team and judge it on the rest of its production. Those explosive plays are earned. And the Broncos got a 62-yard touchdown run from Bo Nix, a 52-yard touchdown on a short pass to RJ Harvey and a 47-yard catch to Marvin Mims Jr. that set up a touchdown. On the Broncos’ other 53 plays, they gained only 216 yards. That’s a middling 4 yards per play. Still, Sunday was another win. The Broncos are 5-2 and the Chiefs’ loss on Sunday sets up a game that should frame the rest of the AFC West race as the Chiefs visit Denver in Week 8. The Broncos will have to find some consistency on offense and they have a few key injuries to track: receiver Jaylen Waddle has a chest injury, defensive lineman Zach Allen hurt his hamstring and cornerback Pat Surtain II has missed three straight games with an ankle injury. USA Today – 3rd Bo Nix looked like a functional quarterback Sunday in the team’s best offensive showing of the season. Next, he gets the opportunity to make up for Week 1’s disappearing act in Kansas City. Fox Sports – 4th The Broncos may have scored 30 points against the Cardinals, but this team still has a Bo Nix problem. He scored on a 62-yard run of his own and threw a short pass that RB R.J. Harvey turned into a 52-yard score. But other than that, the Broncos quarterback was once again unimpressive and downright shaky. Maybe this is just the way it’s going to be. The Broncos are just going to keep finding a way to win. But Nix is probably going to have to get it together at some point — like, perhaps, next Sunday against the Chiefs. Bleacher Report – 6th Finally, the Denver Broncos got a little juice instead of being held back by the quarterback position. Bo Nix opened up the Broncos offense with a 62-yard touchdown run. More importantly, the third-year quarterback began to push the ball downfield more against the Arizona Cardinals than he did during Denver’s previous six games. As a result, the Broncos built a halftime lead and continued to score on their first three second-half drives. The performance was a welcome change of pace after Denver struggled to get anything going during the first half of previous contests, which makes the Broncos a more complete team as the season progresses. What do you think of these power rankings? Share in the comments section below!
