title: Would any of these rookies have helped Rams this season?
summary: Los Angeles Rams first-round pick Ty Simpson hasn’t played a snap yet this season. Would a different first-rounder have contributed much more? The debate over whether or not it was smart of the Rams to take their hopeful quarterback of the future with the 13th-overall pick in a win now year was debated in the […]
full_text: (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Los Angeles Rams first-round pick Ty Simpson hasn’t played a snap yet this season. Would a different first-rounder have contributed much more? The debate over whether or not it was smart of the Rams to take their hopeful quarterback of the future with the 13 th -overall pick in a win now year was debated in the heat of the moment and will be debated for years to come, in all likelihood. But if the Rams had gone in a different direction, would they be getting more bang for their buck right now? It’s not a sure thing they would be. Wide receivers Wide receiver was an obvious position of need for L.A. heading into this year’s draft. The Rams waited until the sixth round to take one, selecting C.J. Daniels out of Miami . But with the benefit of hindsight and in the wake of Davante Adams’s injury , it’s even more obvious how badly Los Angeles needed help in that room this offseason. The Rams didn’t get a shot at the player who’s been the best rookie receiver so far, Carnell Tate, since he went fourth overall to the Tennessee Titans. There were several others who went later in the first round, however. Makai Lemon was a popular mock draft selection for the Rams, but he’s been less than impressive with the Philadelphia Eagles after being taken with the 20th-overall pick. So far, Lemon has 18 receptions for 127 yards with no touchdowns. That’s just 7.1 yards per reception. Then there’s Omar Cooper Jr., now with the New York Jets, who went 30 th overall and, while he’s only played three games, already has 12 catches for 248 yards and two scores. The best non-Tate receiver in the first round this year, when you factor in production and availability, has been KC Concepcion with the Cleveland Browns, who has 30 receptions for 315 yards so far. 186 receiving yards entering today for Browns rookie WR KC Concepcion Anddddd here’s the breakout game: 8 catches for 129 yards in the first half vs the Titans pic.twitter.com/hpu5xswODW — Clint Goss (@NFLDraftDome) October 25, 2026 In fact, Concepcion is third in Rookie of the Year odds, according to FanDuel, only trailing Tate and his own teammate, second-round pick Denzel Boston. First rounders making an impact Along the offensive line, Vega Ioane of the Baltimore Ravens has been as impactful as nearly any rookie so far this season, though he won’t get the same accolades as skill-position players for obvious reasons. At tackle, four players were drafted after Simpson: Blake Miller to the Detroit Lions (five starts, coming off a strong Week 7 win), Monroe Freeling to the Carolina Panthers (increased playing time due to injuries), Max Iheanachor to the Pittsburgh Steelers (praised heavily by his head coach on Monday) and Caleb Lomu to the New England Patriots (one start on a poor offensive line). The Rams haven’t needed a ton of additional help along the line this year. In fact, they’re allowing one of the lowest pressure rates in the NFL, and they’re eighth and fifth, respectively, in ESPN’s pass block and run block win rate stats. 2026 Pressure Rate Allowed (PFR) Shows how often each team's offensive line allowed its QB to be pressured. The Rams have allowed it the least at 16.5%, while Carolina has allowed it the most at 31.8%. pic.twitter.com/nWv3Bgnxff — Gridiron Stats and Info (@GridironInfo_) October 24, 2026 Wide receiver and offensive line help were arguably the two most commonly mocked positions for the Rams in the leadup to the draft. Based on early returns, it’s still reasonably easy to make the argument Los Angeles would be better off right now with one of those aforementioned players than with Simpson sitting and learning. Of course, the Rams could have gone in a different direction entirely. Tight end Kenyon Sadiq has been decent for the Jets, and taking him early would mean no Max Klare pick in the third round (four games played, zero receptions). Jacob Rodriguez didn’t go until the second round, but the Rams need linebacker help badly and he’s been excellent to start his career with the Miami Dolphins. We knew Ty Simpson’s presence on the Rams’ roster would be a hot-button topic all year. The performance of a few late first-round rookies isn’t helping the optics of that pick any more as things currently stand.
author: Brendan Dzwierzynski

title: Don’t call Blake Corum Rams’ RB1 just yet
summary: Blake Corum had a fine game for the Los Angeles Rams in Week 6, and fumble aside, so did Kyren Williams. There is the notion that Corum will get more work for the Rams, and he could take over as the RB1, but before Corum is anointed, he has to actually become the RB1. Corum […]
full_text: Blake Corum had a fine game for the Los Angeles Rams in Week 6, and fumble aside, so did Kyren Williams. There is the notion that Corum will get more work for the Rams, and he could take over as the RB1, but before Corum is anointed, he has to actually become the RB1. Corum seems to have the talent, he appears to be learning Sean McVay’s playbook and Corum has shown a willingness to block as hard as he’ll run. But, to be the Rams RB1, you have to be consistent. Can Corum handle the true workload as the featured running back for L.A.? Can Corum stay healthy? Can Corum stay productive? We don’t know that, yet. We know Williams can handle it. Fumbles aside, he’s been amazing for the Rams as a fifth-round pick who plays like one of the best running backs in the league, and has been one of the most productive. The future for Corum looks bright, but for now, he’s not the RB1. That’s seems like it’s Williams’ job to keep, or lose. Rams Week 7 snap counts: Corum’s role grows, WR2 still unclear (ramswire) “Kyren Williams still played more snaps than Corum, but just barely. He had 37 plays compared to 32 for Corum, and five of those snaps were on the final drive when the Rams were just milking the clock. Corum’s 32 snaps were a season-high and his 44% snap share was his second-highest.” Rams Top PFF Performers in Week 7 Victory Over the Raiders (sports.yahoo) “Here are the top five players on offense and defense via Pro Football Focus (PFF). Offense RB Blake Corum: 87.4 WR Puka Nacua: 86.8 RT Warren McClendon Jr.: 75.2 RB Kyren Williams: 72.3 QB Matthew Stafford: 70.5 The Rams returned to a split-carry situation with both Kyren Williams and Blake Corum having strong days.“ Rams Player Grades: Running Game Leads the Way in Week 7 Win Over Raiders (si.com) “Running Backs: A- The engine of the Rams’ offense on Sunday against the Raiders was the running game . They rushed 33 times for 192 yards and had a touchdown. Blake Corum and Kyren Williams became the first Rams running back duo since Marshall Faulk and Trung Candidate in 2001 to each have 90 rushing yards in the same game. Williams did have a fumble, which continues to be an issue. However, outside of the fumble, Williams and Corum were fantastic. Blake Corum PFF Grade: 83.6 Kyren Williams PFF Grade: 70.4 Wide Receivers: B There continues to be a significant drop-off at wide receiver behind Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. With Adams out, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell rotated as the second wide receiver. Mumpfield had one catch for 15 yards while Atwell had nothing. If the Rams make a trade at the deadline, it needs to be for a wide receiver. “ Rams RB duo passes legend Marshall Faulk’s 25-year-old record (sports.yahoo) “Williams, 26, led the way as the starter, recording 99 rushing yards and a touchdown on 16 carries. Corum, 25, complemented him with an equally impressive performance, finishing with 93 yards and a touchdown on 17 carries. Their combined production gave the Rams a balanced rushing attack that helped them pull away from Las Vegas and secure an important victory. The achievement recalls the days when Faulk was one of the NFL’s most dynamic offensive weapons. During his time with the Rams, Faulk established himself as a central figure in the franchise’s success, making the comparison particularly notable for the current backfield duo.“ Puka Nacua cracks top 10 of Rams’ all-time receiving list in just 49 games (ramswire) “If Nacua adds another 722 yards this season, he will finish the year ranked seventh all-time, eclipsing Hall of Famer Tom Fears for the spot. Despite his incredible output, Nacua has only played in 49 games for the Rams so far, but his averages of 7.3 receptions per game and 95.4 yards per game lead the franchise by a significant margin. Cooper Kupp is ranked second for receptions per game with 6.1, while Torry Holt averaged 80.1 yards per contest.“ Rams Captain Quentin Lake Says Your Body Is Your Résumé (sports.yahoo) “”Your body is your résumé, and your best ability is availability,” Lake says. He admits he did not fully understand that principle when he entered the league. Now he treats recovery as an investment in his career. His routine can include massage, chiropractic work, acupuncture, compression boots, and individualized strength work designed to address differences in mobility and strength between each side of his body. “You have to reinvest the money that you make into yourself so that you can put your best product out there,” Lake says.“ Davis Allen showed he can do more than block in Rams’ win over Raiders (ramblinfan) “There seems to be another consistent theme running throughout the Rams roster. LA has accumulated talented players whose greatest challenge is getting enough work in to make a difference. Allen is one such example. Now in Year 4, Allen has been targeted a mere 71 times, catching 50 passes for 425 yards and six touchdowns. That’s a catch rate of over 70 percent. And yet, he has only been targeted 14 times this season. Over the course of his career, he has only cracked 100 receiving yards once in a season. with his two-score performance in Week 7, he now has two seasons with multiple touchdowns.“ Sean McVay & Colby Parkinson discuss Week 7 win over the Raiders, tight end depth, playing resilient & more (nfl.com) “Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay and tight end Colby Parkinson recap the Rams’ Week 7 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Watch them discuss standout performances, tight end depth, playing with resiliency & toughness, and more.” Rams Deliver Myles Garrett Update as Roster Decision Looms (heavy.com) “The Los Angeles Rams are uncertain about Myles Garrett’s immediate future. The same is true of second-year tight end Terrance Ferguson, according to Rams head coach Sean McVay during his day-after press conference. “I’m not sure yet. Have not decided on those things,” McVay told reporters on October 26 when asked about opening their 21-day practice windows from IR, per the LA Times’ Gary Klein.“ Comment of the day: “Yes, he had a pretty good, not great, rookie season. However, in 2025, Thomas missed three regular season games, he was targeted 91 times, caught 48 for 707 yards and two touchdowns. That’s a 52.7% reception rate, no bueno, to say the least. So far, in 2026, he has caught 9 passes out of 19 targets, less than 50%, he has 105 yards, and 1 touchdown. Trevor Lawrence is just not throwing him the ball any longer, and we can see the reason why. Hard pass for me, and no way is he worth a 2nd round pick. If we could get him for a 5th or 6th I might, and I do mean might, consider it.” -BradleyS Feed post of the day:

title: How Las Vegas Raiders’ defense had no answer for Los Angeles Rams’ 13 personnel in Week 7 loss
summary: The Los Angeles Rams entered Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders with several key injuries, including wide receiver Davante Adams. Additionally, Los Angeles hadn’t logged 100 or more rushing yards as a team in its previous two contests. However, none of that mattered with the Rams cruising to a 35-21 victory while setting a […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams entered Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders with several key injuries, including wide receiver Davante Adams. Additionally, Los Angeles hadn’t logged 100 or more rushing yards as a team in its previous two contests. However, none of that mattered with the Rams cruising to a 35-21 victory while setting a season high with 199 rushing yards and 5.2 ypc, including three kneel-downs from quarterback Matthew Stafford. How did that happen? L.A. leaned heavily on 13 personnel (one running back, three tight ends), and Las Vegas simply had no answer for it. According to Sumer Sports , the Rams were in 13 personnel for 50 percent of their offensive snaps, which is 41.17 percent higher than the NFL average. While Stafford didn’t exactly torch the Raiders through the air with just 195 passing yards, he completed six of nine passes (66.7 percent) for 51 yards, a 0.02 EPA per pass and 66.7 percent success rate with three tight ends on the field. That being said, it was the rushing attack that really did the Raiders’ defense in. Los Angeles had 25 rushes for 111 yards (4.4 ypc), a 64 percent success rate and 0.24 EPA per rush out of 13 personnel. Vegas’ defensive coordinator Rob Leonard tried to counter with more base personnel on 61.8 percent of his play calls, up exactly 40 percent from the season average , but that didn’t matter. Leonard’s crew allowed 0.125 EPA per play (run and pass) on 33 plays with seven front seven defenders against the Rams’ three-tight end looks. But to really answer the question of how it happened, we have to turn on the film to find out. This concept has been killing #Raiders in the last 3 weeks -Vs. 12 or 13 personnel, Leonard puts an extra LB on the LOS with Cover 3 behind it -PA, TE on corner occupies CB, WR runs flat -OLB steps down vs. run fake & can't get to flat, easy 1st down NE & BUF ran it, LAR copied pic.twitter.com/XDCV0FYoz6 — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) October 26, 2026 We’ll start with a few passes because the Rams actually had more success throwing the ball out of 13 personnel earlier in the game and then leaned on the rushing attack to close it out. Also, the Raiders have been getting killed by the play design above, as the New England Patriots and Buffalo Bills had success with it. So Los Angeles copied it, and the result was the same: an easy first down. Pretty much every time the Raiders face 12 or 13 personnel, Leonard has an off-ball linebacker on the line of scrimmage. Typically, it’s Quay Walker, but in this instance, it’s Tommy Eichenberg. Meanwhile, the Rams run a play-action fake where the outside tight end has a corner route to occupy Darien Porter (the corner at the top of the screen), who is responsible for the deep third of the field. That’s another key tendency at play here; Leonard leans heavily on Cover 3 behind this front. So, when Eichenberg steps down to play the run and sees the tight end release upfield, by the time he recognizes it’s a pass, there’s no chance for him to get in the flat with enough time to disrupt the pass to Puka Nacua. On top of that, with Porter pulled out of the play, Nacua is wide open for an easy catch and run to move the sticks and put the ball in the red zone. In other words, Sean McVay was able to manipulate the defense to get the look he wanted by leaning on Leonard’s tendacies and following the blueprint that the Patriots and Bills used. Another 13 personnel pass from the Rams – #Raiders in man coverage -Treydan Stukes sees his TE bluff a block on Jeremy Chinn and shifts his eyes to the backfield -TE is wide open for an easy TD #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/sm9LIqPcVO — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) October 26, 2026 To be honest, there isn’t too much to break down on this one. The Raiders are in man coverage, which gets confirmed by the tight end’s (No. 87, Davis Allen) pre-snap motion, where Treydan Stukes mirrors his movement step for step. Post-snap, it’s play action, and Stukes sees Allen bluff a block on Jeremy Chinn, so the rookie takes his eyes to the backfield. He quickly realizes he’s been duped and it’s a pass, but it’s too late. Allen is wide open in the end zone for an easy pitch-and-catch to put six points on the board. That’s the result of knowing what coverage is coming, allowing a veteran play caller and quarterback to pick on a young defensive back. 3rd & 2 and #Raiders do a decent job of not falling for run fake…However: -Jeremy Chinn bites on head fake from TE -Darien Porter doesn't get enough depth to help -Higbee climbs the latter for a 1st down #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/icToEiuEGd — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) October 26, 2026 This time, it’s third and two, and Las Vegas does a decent job of not falling for the run fake despite the down and distance. However, that doesn’t matter when it comes to the end result. The Raiders are playing Cover 2 where, at the bottom of the screen, Porter is the end man on the line of scrimmage and Eichenberg takes a couple of steps toward the line when the tight end motions across the formation to get into a two-by-two set. Post-snap, the outside tight end (No. 89, Tyler Higbee) has a vertical release to run an intermediate route, and the other tight end works across the formation to help in pass protection. So, Eichenberg gets hands on Higbee to disrupt the timing of the route a bit and pass Higbee off to Jeremy Chinn. With no one threatening his area, Porter starts working for depth but doesn’t get deep enough to tighten the throwing window to Higbee. But the bigger problem is that Chinn gets manipulated by the tight end’s eyes/head fake, anticipating a dig or drag route across the field. So, the safety tries to cheat toward the middle of the field and jump the in-breaking route, leaving his area open while Higbee breaks toward the sideline and climbs the ladder on the out route for a 15-yard gain. Also, it doesn’t help that the pass rush doesn’t come close to getting pressure, giving Stafford a clean pocket to throw from. 13 personnel from the Rams -LBs slide over when TE motions despite all backside gaps being accounted for -Walker is a step late to shoot the gap b/c of the shift -2 TEs to double Nakobe Dean on ISO -Patrick Johnson can't cross RT's face to make the tackle #Raiders pic.twitter.com/NfuxlufHQn — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) October 26, 2026 Moving on to the running game, Los Angeles primarily stayed on or slightly ahead of schedule with a bunch of four- or five-yard runs out of 13 personnel. That on its own isn’t a huge deal, but the problem was the Rams also had a few chunk runs that really broke the Raiders’ backs, like the one above. LA comes out in a three-tight end formation but run iso by motioning the outside tight end into the backfield, where he settles in the B-gap like an offset I-formation fullback. The problem is the linebackers respond to that action by sliding over to the weak side despite the offense not changing the strength and all of the weak side gaps being accounted for. Notice how the weak-side defensive tackle (JJ Pegues in a 3-technique) slants into the A-gap, while Maxx Crosby tries to work across the left tackle’s face (B-gap), and the corner blitzes off the edge (C-gap). The linebackers shifting ends up being very costly for the Raiders. Allen, the motioning tight end/fullback, goes to iso block Dean. Meanwhile, Walker is an unblocked defender and has an opportunity to shoot the B-gap to the inside of Allen’s block, but Walker is a step late because of that shift. To make matters worse, with Hibgee executing a fold block inside of the right tackle, the Rams get a double team on Dean to kick him out of the rushing lane. On top of that, Patrick Johnson can’t cross the right tackle’s face to make the play, and Eric Stokes sees the tight end work inside but doesn’t follow him to get involved in the run fit and clog the lane. So, running back Blake Corum gets nine yards. Duo -Tonka Hemingway gets pushed by the RG/RT…

title: Klint Kubiak bangs head his against the Rams and loses
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders played another team that was heavily hampered by injuries and got the crap kicked out of them again. From the second series, it was obvious to anyone with eyes that the defense had nothing for 13-personnel. Offensively, the flaws of Klint Kubiak’s rookie head coaching campaign were on full display. Kubiak […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders played another team that was heavily hampered by injuries and got the crap kicked out of them again. From the second series, it was obvious to anyone with eyes that the defense had nothing for 13-personnel. Offensively, the flaws of Klint Kubiak’s rookie head coaching campaign were on full display. Kubiak continues to pick interesting times to be aggressive on fourth downs in the red zone with little to no return on his analytical beliefs. Combined with going for two-point conversions twice and failing to convert, his aggressiveness continues to cost the team points. Pressing is natural and to be expected when trying to come from behind, but when down by multiple scores, points in every possession are essential. Trying to win games in one possession is something he will need to calm down on. After seven weeks with the offensive lineup, Kubiak continues to trot out; his offense is entirely predictable. Former first-round draft pick and #6 overall Ashton Jeanty is more Jalen Richard than the generational talent he was billed as. Every time Mike Washington Jr. touches the football and clears the line of scrimmage, it is clear who is the better option at running back. To everyone except Kubiak, who continues to feature an ineffective runner for three plays and a punt. The Rams have run man coverage 53.3% of the time today so far vs. the Raiders, per Sumer Sports. That’s 29.8% higher than the league average of man usage. https://t.co/cvTOzs5aj1 — Jesse Merrick – Silver & Black Sports Network (@JesseSBSN) October 25, 2026 Brock Bowers, as a wide receiver, was a good experiment and can be effective in spurts, but as an every-down wideout, he’s not the answer. Bowers finished the game with six receptions for 73 yards, but despite these numbers, it was still a rather pedestrian game for him. Most of his catches were junk-time plays when the defense had eased off the press coverage. The fact that the Kubiak isn’t able to call plays where his receivers can beat man coverage is an indictment of not only his play calling but also his personnel. Beating man coverage is as elementary as football gets. But, it’s not all on the wide receivers. Cousins, for all the good that he has done and being tied for the league lead in passing touchdowns, hasn’t been hitting wide-open receivers when they have presented themselves. These are the plays that the rookie will let it rip and 9/10 going to be a TD. WAO, wide ass open. Kirk has done well but this can’t keep happening. https://t.co/syQtZSAYMf — Phil Robinson III (@PhilRobinsonIII) October 26, 2026 Finally some offense In the second half, speedy wide receiver Tre Tucker showed why he should be more than an afterthought in this offense. With a pass he could do something with, he showed YAC (yards after the catch) ability, taking a short reception and finishing with a 41-yard catch-and-run. Later, he added a 37-yard catch-and-run for a touchdown after making a man miss. Jeanty, had his lowest average yard per carry total of the season 1.9 yards, and is averaging 2.9 yards per carry on the season. However, he has proved his worth as a pass catcher. Catching a season-high eight passes on eight targets, including both a 22-yard sideline catch and a 15-yard touchdown pass. Ultimately, the offense was unable to overcome the lack of their own running game and Kubiak’s strange fascination with wanting to see Washington’s blocking ability over his 4.9 yards-per-carry average. On a team with a non-existent rushing attack, keeping a runner like Washington on the bench instead of switching Jeanty to a complementary role, which better suits him, is hurting the team. If “just win baby” is the goal, Kubiak needs to get over his own biases and coach to the strengths of his team and players.
author: Philip Robinson

title: Kirk Cousins-Fernando Mendoza chatter leads Las Vegas Raiders discussion in Week 8 NFL Power Rankings
summary: After going undefeated in September, the Las Vegas Raiders managed to go winless in October and are rapidly falling out of playoff contention. So, it’s not surprising that the Raiders are sliding down the Week 8 NFL Power Rankings. The four-game losing streak has also led to a lot of discussion about when Fernando Mendoza […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images After going undefeated in September, the Las Vegas Raiders managed to go winless in October and are rapidly falling out of playoff contention . So, it’s not surprising that the Raiders are sliding down the Week 8 NFL Power Rankings. The four-game losing streak has also led to a lot of discussion about when Fernando Mendoza will make his first start, despite Klint Kubiak confirming on Monday that Kirk Cousins remains QB1 . Sports Illustrated 22. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 19 Assuming the Raiders can beat the woeful Jets this coming weekend, the subplot of Kirk Cousins remaining the starter versus being a legitimately valuable trade chip (he’s leading the league in touchdown passes!) will thicken. Fernando Mendoza will play at some point, but if the Raiders can get a mid-round pick for Cousins with all their needs, wouldn’t that be difficult to turn down? — Conor Orr I understand the line of thinking, but I’d honestly be surprised if Cousins gets traded at the deadline. When teams are winning, most coaches don’t want to disrupt the situation by making a quarterback change, especially with someone from outside the building who will have to learn the playbook. Unless an injury happens in the next two weeks, it would take a team that’s on the bubble but on the outside looking in and has an unstable quarterback situation. The Baltimore Ravens could fall into that category given the uncertainty surrounding Lamar Jackson. But Jackson should be returning soon, and I don’t think John Spytek is looking to do Eric DeCosta any favors for obvious reasons. The Atlanta Falcons are the other team potentially in that spot, but they’ve been winning with Michael Penix Jr. and chose to move on from Cousins this past offseason. ESPN 22. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 18 While the masses are eager to see Fernando Mendoza take over the offense, Cousins has played surprisingly well to the point that the No. 1 pick has had to wait longer than expected to be the starter. Cousins, 38, ranks third in passing yards (1,877) and first in touchdown passes (16). Sure, the limitations at his age, such as arm strength and mobility, have been prevalent. But Las Vegas’ four-game losing streak is not solely on him. Coach Klint Kubiak confirmed that Cousins will start in Week 8 against the Jets. — Ryan McFadden The Raiders’ four-game losing streak isn’t on Cousins, that’s for sure. However, the team isn’t winning with the 38-year-old behind center, and at some point, the focus of this season needs to shift to the future. Facing a lower-quality opponent this Sunday was a good opportunity to give the rookie his first start, but Kubiak referenced the Silver and Black still being “in the hunt” as part of his rationale for continuing to roll with Cousins. Mathematically, yes, Las Vegas still has playoff hopes. But let’s be honest, the last month has proven that the offseason expectations for the rebuilding Raiders were valid, and the team isn’t ready to be a legitimate postseason contender. Bleacher Report 20. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 18 The feel-good start to the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 campaign came screeching to a halt when the calendar flipped to October. The team turned into a pumpkin and lost all four games in the month. At this juncture, the possibility of this year’s No. 1 overall pick, Fernando Mendoza, taking over Las Vegas’ offense on a full-time basis must be under strong consideration. A Week 13 bye may be too late in the process to get the team’s biggest investment onto the field, because he could use all of the snaps he can get. On the flip side of the coin, the Raiders still face four of the league’s top 12 defenses over the next five games, which doesn’t even include the Denver Broncos’ talented unit. So, the Raiders have a significant decision to make. Either the coaching staff and organization feel Mendoza is ready no matter who he faces, or the team will have to wait until December before pulling Kirk Cousins from the starting lineup. — Brent Sobleski This brings up an interesting exercise: looking at the rest of the schedule to determine where the sweet spot for Mendoza’s first start is. Obviously, it isn’t happening this Sunday in New York. Then, in the four weeks before the bye, the options are: at the San Francisco 49ers, vs. the Seattle Seahawks, at the Denver Broncos, and at the Cleveland Browns. Meanwhile, the first game after the bye is at home against the Los Angeles Chargers, and the rest of the schedule is fairly soft: vs. Broncos (tough matchup), vs. Tennessee Titans, at Arizona Cardinals, and at Kansas City Chiefs (who might have nothing to play for in Week 18). NFL.com 25. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 18 It’s official: The Raiders’ 3-0 start was a mirage. Las Vegas has now lost four straight and can no longer rely on Kirk Cousins to simply throw them to victory (or close losses). The calls for Fernando Mendoza are only going to grow louder if this continues, even if the Raiders’ struggles aren’t really a product of Cousins’ performance. The defense certainly didn’t do them any favors Sunday, but perhaps they can bounce back against a Jets team mired in similar struggles. — Nick Shook The Jets have one quality win (Week 5 against the Browns), with the other victory coming against the Titans in the season opener. Also, New York just lost to a previously winless Miami Dolphins team. That’s to say, this Sunday is a very winnable game for the Raiders, putting the record at 4-4 and pretty much confirming that Cousins will start for at least one more game. Additionally, it could buy him two more games since the Raiders would still be “in the hunt” at 4-5 even with a loss in San Francisco. The Athletic 24. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 18 Something spooky: Quarterback questions After a fourth straight loss on Sunday, Kirk Cousins was asked about how and when the team would turn things over to No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza. It’s not happening yet, but even if Cousins wasn’t the biggest problem Sunday (he threw for 295 yards and two touchdowns, but the Raiders still can’t run the ball), the questions about Mendoza will get louder if Las Vegas drops next weekend’s game in New York. — Josh Kendall, Chad Graff This is the other end of the spectrum, where at 3-5 with five straight losses, Kubiak has to look in the mirror and be honest with himself about the team’s outlook for the rest of 2026. Then it becomes a question of what’s more valuable for the rookie quarterback: Getting as many starts and as much experience as possible, or not throwing him to the wolves with four legitimate playoff contenders right off the bat and waiting until the schedule softens up? There’s only a handful of people who can answer that question, and they’re all at Intermountain Health Performance Center in Henderson, Nev.

title: Geno Smith isn’t terrible this year
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders will see a familiar face Sunday when they visit the New York Jets and it won’t bring back good memories. The Jets are quarterbacked by Geno Smith. The Raiders, of course, traded Smith and a seventh-round pick in 2026 for a sixth-round pick this year. The Raiders used that pick as […]
full_text: (Photo by Jordan Bank/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders will see a familiar face Sunday when they visit the New York Jets and it won’t bring back good memories. The Jets are quarterbacked by Geno Smith. The Raiders, of course, traded Smith and a seventh-round pick in 2026 for a sixth-round pick this year. The Raiders used that pick as part of a deal to move up 12 spots to draft running Mike Washington in the fourth round. Las Vegas was going to release Smith before the Jets, who drafted him more than decade ago, came in with the trade deal. Smith’s one season with the Raiders was a disaster. Las Vegas gave Seattle a third-round pick for Smith last year to reunite him with former Seahawks’ head coach Pete Carroll. The 2025 season was brutal for both Smith and Carroll and they both were jettisoned after one season. Smith threw 19 touchdowns and 17 interceptions for the 3-14 Raiders. To his credit, Smith, 36, has rebounded some for the Jets even though they are just 2-5. Smith is completing 70 percent of his passes and has thrown just two interceptions with 10 touchdown passes. title: Mike Washington flashes in limited role again
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 35-21 home loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the New York Jets. Fernando Mendoza:The No. 1 overall pick has only […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 35-21 home loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the New York Jets. Fernando Mendoza: The No. 1 overall pick has only played in Week 5 in a mop-up role. If the losses pile up, he may get a chance to play. Treydan Stukes: The Raiders’ second-round pick played all 72 defensive snaps. He is a core defender. Trey Zuhn: The third-round pick played five snaps on offensive and four on special teams, which has been about the norm for him. Jermod McCoy: The fourth-round pick didn’t play on defense for the fifth time this season. He did play 13 snaps on special teams. Mike Washington: The fourth-round pick played 18 snaps after being a game-day decision with foot and back injuries. He ended up 27 yards on six carries. he did have a nifty 21-yard run and he should continue to get more work this week. Dalton Johnson: The fifth-round pick safety was inactive for the sixth time in seven games. Zeke Masses: The fifth-round pick played 29 snaps, the most since he lost his starting cornerback job three weeks ago. It will be interesting to see how much he plays at the Jets. Malik Benson: The sixth-round pick played a season-low three snaps. He was targeted once with no catches. He did have two punt returns for 26 yards.

title: Miami Dolphins Week 7 quick hits: Tuesday Thoughts With The Earl
summary: SHHH!!!  Hey… you’uns hear that?  That’s the sound of… VICTORY!!! The Miami Dolphins got their first win of the season over the hated New York Jets.  It wasn’t a comfortable win by any means, but we will take any win we can get.  Especially over the Jets.  As The Miami Ute said in the reactions […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 25: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins looks on during warm ups before their game against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on October 25, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Jordan Bank/Getty Images) | Getty Images SHHH!!! Hey… you’uns hear that? That’s the sound of… VICTORY!!! The Miami Dolphins got their first win of the season over the hated New York Jets. It wasn’t a comfortable win by any means, but we will take any win we can get. Especially over the Jets. As The Miami Ute said in the reactions thread: “A victory versus the Jets is worth 10 victories over common opponents.” I looked into it and that is correct; the math on that definitely checks out. So what all went into this DUB? THE OFFENSE CAME TO PLAY But Duke… it’s just the lowly 2-4 Jets. That’s correct. But as Marisa Marino from DolphinsTalk tweeted, the Jets were a top 10 defense in just about every metric . I pointed out some of those as well. The Jets may now be 2-5, but they have only lost one game this season by more than one score, and that was just 11 points. The Jets have held every team they have faced under their average passing yards per game… except the Dolphins. Now, it doesn’t take much to get over Miami’s average, which was 31st entering the game. But they exceeded that average nonetheless. There were some hiccups in the second half, but they did what was necessary to win when it mattered most. They also scored 28 points, which is the 2nd most points the Jets have allowed in a game this season. They are now off the bottom of the scoring average, nearly a full PPG ahead of the Titans and 1.3 PPG ahead of Mike McDaniel and the Captain If Justin Herbert led Chargers. Whether they can maintain it is another question for another day. But if they play like they did for the majority of this game, I don’t see why they can’t maintain it. It’s also impressive that the Dolphins gained 360 total yards. That’s the 4th most the Jets have allowed this season. The teams ahead of the Dolphins are ranked in the top 10 in total yards this season. But the most impressive thing the offense did Sunday: they got the ball with 3:24 left in the game. The Jets had just scored 8 points to bring the game to within 3 points. Outside of the explosive play to Douglas, the Dolphins had been quiet in the 2nd half. This is big boy football time and if we are all being honest, we were all clinched up for this drive. We have seen this FAR too many time, especially in the last regime, where the team just couldn’t put away an opponent. NOT THIS TIME!!! The Dolphins ran for a first down with a 14-yard run. Then 3 runs for 9 total yards. They were at midfield with a 4th-and-1 with 2 minutes left. They went for it using their version of the Tush Push play. And that was it. They converted and entered the victory formation. In the past, we have heard the talk about the Dolphins becoming more physical, but it was always nothing more than talk. In that moment, the Dolphins were the more physical team and it showed up. THE DEFENSE STILL NEEDS WORK The pass defense is what it is. The Dolphins still allow a ridiculously high completion percentage to opponents. I somewhat expected this against the Jets as Geno Smith has been less reluctant to throw downfield this season. Smith actually pushed the ball downfield this game and hit some explosives that resulted in TDs for the Jets. This is stuff they’ll need to clean up from the film room and work on the communication. Two big plays were busted coverages, and the other was a play that looked Dante Trader had a chance to intercept it. Those 3 plays accounted for 153 yards, which is over half of the total passing yards. Of course, we could do the same type of accounting for the Dolphins or any team really. But 3 plays out of 30 passing attempts accounting for over half of the production signals outliers to me. On 27 other attempts, the Dolphins allowed 134 yards, which tracks with the idea of the Jets keeping it short. They still have issues with TEs although I’ll give them credit: both of Taylor’s TDs were contested catches. The issue I’m going to take up is the run defense. The Dolphins were top 10 in YPC allowed and overall yards allowed. They held MVP candidate Kenneth Walker III in check a few games ago. They allowed the Jets to run over them, especially late. Braelon Allen ran for 104 yards on 17 carries, a 6.1 YPC average. Allen has stepped up into lead back role for the Jets in the absence of Breece Hall and he is averaging over 4 YPC in games where he is the primary contributor. But the Dolphins should have held their ground against him. The game plan changed for the Jets in the 2nd half. Of Allen’s 17 carries, 12 of them came in the 2nd half. Allen had 5 carries for 23 yards in the 1st half. The Jets, down 2 TDs, said they didn’t think the Dolphins could stop their rushing attack, and they were right. The Jets are bad in the red zone, and the Dolphins got a goal line stand that resulted in a FG. But the Dolphins will face much better RBs and better rushing attacks in the next few weeks. I don’t know if they can fix the pass defense anytime soon, so the run defense needs to do their part. THIS AND THAT Malik Willis played exceptionally well this game. The difference from what we’ve previously seen and that was night and day. His stat line won’t blow anyone’s mind, but he was decisive, made smart decisions, and protected the ball. As JUK pointed out, 5 bad games of Willis were not enough of a sample size to make a judgment on him, and neither is 1 good game. But this level of play could be the start of an upward trend. Of course, we need to see this next week and then the next and so on. But give credit where credit is due, he played very well. Ollie Gordon continues to be refreshing part of a tough season with his aggressive running and fiery temperament – he’s gonna get a flag thrown on him with the way he’s chirping. But that’s fine, because we need to see that fire from players. Do you think Gordon is gonna be laughing on the sideline after making a mistake that effectively ends your season? No. He’s old school and I’m here for it. He’s currently 19th in rushing yards, which is wild considering he had 3 carries for 7 yards in the 1st 2 games this season. In the 3 games since becoming the primary back, he has averaged 97 yards per game. If he maintains that pace the rest of the way, he’ll finish with over 1400 rushing yards! More importantly, he has scored a TD in all 4 games he has had be a heavy contributor. That pace will be difficult to continue, but he has a chance to finish with double digit TDs. There are too many AFC backs ahead of him and the Dolphins’ eventual record with be a deterrent, but he is on a Pro Bowl pace. Bobby Slowik needs a shout out. He finally listened to me (not really but let me feel important for a minute) and dialed up the short passing game. Here are some interesting tweets about that here and here . But what he was doing was working. My favorite offensive stat: 41 rushing attempts. Look, I grew up in the 80s on hard-nosed rushing attack football that was 3 yards and a cloud of dust. The current NFL is flashy and pass happy and we saw all of that with McDaniel. I’m glad to see the return of “ground and pound”. The Dolphins’ passing game was good against the Jets. It will need to be better in future games. But I’ll never complain about a dominant rushing attack. Now… Willis rushed for 8 attempts. 3 of those were called runs for sure: the 2 kneeldowns and the tush-push. On of the 2 sacks he took was actually a designed QB run play. The others were pass plays, so we can assume 25 total dropbacks to 36 run plays called. But still… if the Dolphins can dominate in the run game, they will be tough for anyone to beat. Welcome back Caleb Douglas. He was not a major factor in terms of volume, but both his catches went for TDs. He is still a rookie and playing in only his third game. He…

title: Miami Dolphins’ Most Valuable Player | Week Seven | Arrival
summary: It took until week seven of the 2026 NFL season, but the Miami Dolphins have earned their first victory of the year by downing the hated New York Jets by a score of 28-25 on Sunday. The win comes after multiple one-score losses in a row. Does this indicate that Jeff Hafley’s squad has turned […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 25: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins runs with the ball during the second quarter against the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium on October 25, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images It took until week seven of the 2026 NFL season, but the Miami Dolphins have earned their first victory of the year by downing the hated New York Jets by a score of 28-25 on Sunday. The win comes after multiple one-score losses in a row. Does this indicate that Jeff Hafley’s squad has turned the corner and are ready to add more tallies to the victory chalkboard — or was this simply a feel-good moment for an organization that is deep in the throngs of yet another rebuild? At this point, it’s too early to tell. Just like how Sunday’s performance from first-year starting quarterback, Malik Willis, was an incredible sight to see — but it doesn’t mean he’ll continue to put up elite numbers as the season rolls on. Miami Dolphins Week Seven MVP – QB Malik Willis The last time Dolphins fans saw Malik Willis in action was in week five against the Cincinnati Bengals… and let’s just say that after his three turnover day, there was some very strong condemnation coming from the team’s fanbase. People were calling for his benching while declaring his signing a massive misstep. “Well, well, well, how the turntables…” On Sunday in New Jersey, Willis completed 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns, while adding 37 yards rushing on eight carries and scoring a third touchdown with his legs. He finished the day with a 130.7 passer rating. According to Kyle Crabbs of A to Z Sports , Willis’ day was even better when you take a deeper look at the numbers. His expected points added (EPA) against the Jets was the fifth best single-game EPA per drop back total out of any quarterback this season. With his strong week seven performance, Willis joined an exclusive list of quarterbacks with at least 1,000 yards passing and 200 yards rushing on the year. QBs with 1,000+ passing yards and 200+ rushing yards so far this season: Josh Allen Drake Maye Deshaun Watson Malik Willis pic.twitter.com/31xXy507zO — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) October 26, 2026 MVP TRACKER Week One – WR Caleb Douglas Week Two – LB Jacob Rodriguez Week Three – OC Aaron Brewer Week Four – EDGE Chop Robinson Week Five – RB Ollie Gordon II Week Six – BYE Week Seven – QB Malik Willis

At 6-0, the Vikings are the only team in the NFL without a loss heading into Week […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - DECEMBER 25: Minnesota Vikings running back Aaron Jones (33) spins into the end zone from 1-yard out for a touchdown and Detroit Lions linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez (44) defends during the first quarter of a NFL game between the Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions on December 25, 2025, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Nick Wosika/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings will try to extend their run as the NFL’s last undefeated team on Sunday afternoon, as they make their annual trip to the Motor City to take on their NFC North rivals, the Detroit Lions. At 6-0, the Vikings are the only team in the NFL without a loss heading into Week 8, and they’ve been getting it done with defense and special teams as the offense continues to have issues putting points on the board. They trailed going into the fourth quarter this past Sunday at home against the Indianapolis Colts, but a 5-yard touchdown pass from Kyler Murray to T.J. Hockenson put the Vikings ahead and helped them to hang on for a 16-10 victory. They head into Detroit looking to remain perfect in the NFC North as well, having already defeated the Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears earlier in the season. The Lions come into this one with a record of 4-2, having escaped in Week 7 with a 20-17 victory over Green Bay at Ford Field. The Lions have put up points in bunches this season, as they’re currently second in the NFL in points per game and should pose a tough test for the Vikings’ NFL-best defense. They’ve also given up points in bunches, as they’re 26th in the league in points allowed per game, but the Vikings have had issues scoring regardless of who they’ve gone against. Will they be able to get out of that funk this Sunday at Ford Field? The Vikings will be looking for their third consecutive win over the Lions, having swept the season series against Detroit last season. Kickoff for this one is slated for noon Central Time, with coverage being provided by the FOX family of networks. title: The McCarthy/Murray Discourse Isn’t Going Away
summary: When the Minnesota Vikings traded quarterback J.J. McCarthy to the New York Football Giants a month ago, a lot of Vikings fans seemed to be relieved because they thought they would likely never have to hear McCarthy’s name again. After all, after McCarthy missed his entire rookie season following a meniscus tear in the team’s […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - AUGUST 15: Kyler Murray #1 and J.J. McCarthy #9 of the Minnesota Vikings warm up before a preseason game against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on August 15, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Mike Coppola/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the Minnesota Vikings traded quarterback J.J. McCarthy to the New York Football Giants a month ago, a lot of Vikings fans seemed to be relieved because they thought they would likely never have to hear McCarthy’s name again. After all, after McCarthy missed his entire rookie season following a meniscus tear in the team’s 2024 preseason opener and then had an up-and-down first season as the full-time while dealing with multiple injuries, a significant portion of the fan base had decided that there was no chance he could possibly be “the guy” in Minnesota. The return the Vikings received for the highest-drafted quarterback in franchise history was a fifth-round selection in the 2027 NFL Draft, and a disturbingly large number of people seemed to be fine with that. The thought was that McCarthy would go to New York, continue to struggle, and likely be out of the league before he got to a second contract, after which everyone would just forget about him. But a funny thing happened on the way to McCarthy’s impending irrelevance, and all of a sudden the people who were so sure that McCarthy was the worst quarterback they’d ever seen just don’t want to talk about him anymore. Why? Because now people have questions. In Week 6, after Jameis Winston put the Giants into a 34-10 hole against the New Orleans Saints, McCarthy entered the game, led the Giants to 17 unanswered points, and had them within 12 yards of a potential tying score before he ran out of time. In Week 7, after being named the starter, he led the Giants into Houston as a double-digit underdog against the Texans and led New York to a 27-21 overtime win. He also seems to have unlocked Giants star wide receiver Malik Nabers, who has 11 catches for 206 yards since McCarthy took over. In the five quarters plus overtime that McCarthy has been running the Giants’ offense, that offense has generated six touchdown drives. The Minnesota Vikings’ offense has generated four touchdown drives. . .since Week 3. There was Jordan Addison’s 41-yard touchdown catch against Tampa Bay, Justin Jefferson’s 15-yard touchdown catch and Aaron Jones’ 8-yard touchdown run against New Orleans, and T.J. Hockenson’s 5-yard touchdown catch against Indianapolis. That’s it. If you want to count the drive where Hockenson slid down at the 1-yard line against Miami, fine, but five touchdown drives in four games really isn’t terribly impressive, either. And let me be clear on something. . .yes, the Vikings are 6-0, and I’m positively thrilled that they’re 6-0. The Vikings are 6-0 because Brian Flores is out here every week turning water into wine and Will Reichard is some sort of kicking robot cyborg machine from another planet. The defense and special teams have dragged this offense, kicking and screaming, to 6-0. For the last few weeks, we’ve heard about how this is going to be the week that the Vikings’ offense was finally going to get itself right. Week 4: “Well, the Dolphins might be the worst team in the league. This is going to be a get-right game for the Vikings’ offense.” Week 5: “Well, the Saints have given up the most points in the league so far. This is going to be a get-right game for the Vikings’ offense.” Week 7: “Well, the Vikings are getting almost all their key players back on offense and the Colts just lost to the Titans at home. This is going to be a get-right game for the Vikings’ offense.” And the Vikings’ offense just continues to. . .not get right. Which brings us to Kyler Murray. The case for bringing in Murray to be the starting quarterback was that he was the sort of veteran who could get the ball to Justin Jefferson and help this offense push the ball down the field in ways that McCarthy, Carson Wentz, and Max Brosmer couldn’t in 2025. Now, because of injuries to both Murray and Jefferson, they’ve only played two full games together, so there’s still time for chemistry to develop, but the early results have not been great. On Sunday, against a Colts defense that has been less than stellar this season, Murray completed 14-of-24 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown. That included four catches for 44 yards for Jefferson. Jefferson did not have a catch in the second half. He was targeted once in the second half. The Colts came into the game with star cornerback Sauce Gardner on the sideline and, by the end of the game, had none of their top three corners on the field due to injuries. I don’t know why this happened, but it’s precisely the sort of thing that people had complaints about last season with this offense. Now, as many people have pointed out, the Vikings’ schedule gets significantly tougher. They head to Detroit this week, then it’s Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills in prime time, then they travel to Green Bay before heading to Mexico City to take on the San Francisco 49ers. As good as the Vikings’ defense has been so far this season, it seems unlikely that point totals in the teens are going to be good enough going forward. This shouldn’t be “training wheels” time for the Minnesota Vikings’ offense. This should be “put the ball into the end zone more than once a game and stop relying on Brian Flores and company to bail you out” time. And now Vikings fans are seeing a 23-year-old quarterback that their team sold for pennies on the dollar and had been dismissed as a complete flop performing at a significantly improved level for a team he’s been with for a month and, if the season ended today, a team that the Vikings could potentially see in the NFL’s postseason party. So, yes, people are going to have questions. And the people who thought they had all the answers a month ago have, suddenly, found a lack of desire to approach the topic. Strange, that. Put simply, the discourse about J.J. McCarthy and Kyler Murray isn’t going anywhere. It’s going to continue until at least one of those two parties puts forth enough compelling evidence to suggest that it shouldn’t continue. To this point, neither of them has. And until one of them does, it’s only going to get louder.

title: Vikings Offense Film: Kyler Murray Close, Run Game the Problem
summary: On the latest episode of The Real Forno Show, Tyler Forness dove deep into the Vikings’ All-22 film against the Colts and delivered a blunt assessment: “This offense was very weird on Sunday, and I mean that from every possible angle. It was both good, it was both bad, and it was also ugly.” The […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 25: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray (1) throws a pass in the fist half of play during a NFL game between the Indianapolis Colts and the Minnesota Vikings on October 25, 2026 at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On the latest episode of The Real Forno Show , Tyler Forness dove deep into the Vikings’ All-22 film against the Colts and delivered a blunt assessment: “This offense was very weird on Sunday, and I mean that from every possible angle. It was both good, it was both bad, and it was also ugly.” The frustration, Forness argues, is amplified by J.J. McCarthy’s success in New York — “the guy was selected 10th overall to be our starting quarterback and he’s not, and the Vikings got rid of him for a fifth and any time he shows any semblance of success, it’s gonna hurt a little bit more.” But the real story is the run game. Forness didn’t mince words: “Vikings’ run game sucks. It’s bad.” He praised Aaron Jones as “an absolute warrior” who “doesn’t have the juice anymore,” and called Jordan Mason “a good 1B, but he’s not a 1A.” The proposed fix? A trade for a home-run threat like Jonathan Taylor — “somebody who can get big chunks, somebody who can be a home run threat, is going to be the simplest way to fix a lot of these offensive issues.” Dave Stefano agreed: “If Taylor can give us a Christian McCaffrey type boost, that would be beneficial.” Meanwhile, Kyler Murray drew a provocative comparison. Forness said: “My biggest hot take with this Vikings team is right now it is being quarterbacked by 2020 Kirk Cousins.” He placed Murray in “purgatory range where he does just enough good stuff to keep you excited and just enough bad stuff where it’s like, ‘I’m going to beat you with a hammer.'” Yet the data shows a path forward — Murray was dead average in EPA per play (.156) and success rate (45.5%), suggesting regression to the mean could help. The defense, however, is otherworldly. “This is trending to be a historic defense,” Forness said. Stefano’s response: “Legendary is the proper term.” Forness went further: “You can win a Super Bowl with this defense paired with this offense.” They’ve allowed just three points in the fourth quarter over six games, and upcoming tests against the Lions, 49ers, and Bills will prove whether that dominance is sustainable. Key Points: Run game is the #1 problem: The Vikings rank 26th in EPA per rush and 26th in success rate (34%). Forness’s blame pie chart: 50% run game, 30% Kyler Murray, 10% Kevin O’Connell, 10% pass blocking. Trade deadline target: Jonathan Taylor is the ideal acquisition — a package similar to the Christian McCaffrey deal (2nd, 3rd, 4th/5th) makes sense. Saquon Barkley is a longer shot. Offensive line reality: Will Fries “is getting cut” per Forness. Blake Brandel hasn’t taken the expected step forward. Joe Huber has been a nice surprise but is still a backup. Brian O’Neill and Christian Darrisaw remain solid but have occasional breakdowns. O’Connell’s “can” system exposed: O’Connell admitted his two-play call system lets defenses dictate outcomes: “We can’t put it so much in the defense’s hands on ultimately what play we end up running.” Forness wants more aggressiveness — “We’re gonna run this, and we’re just gonna jam it down your throat.” Kyler Murray = 2020 Kirk Cousins: flashes of brilliance (deep outs to Justin Jefferson, seam routes to T.J. Hockenson) mixed with uncharacteristic accuracy issues and conservative decision-making. Historic defense: Six games, three fourth-quarter points allowed. Forness believes a Super Bowl is within reach if the offense improves even marginally. 2027 NFL Draft devaluation: With NIL and extended eligibility weakening rounds 3-7, trading mid-to-late picks for impact players hurts less this year than in most. Kevin O’Connell is safe: At 49-25 with an 11-game win streak, Forness shut down hot-seat talk: “The Wilfs aren’t firing him.” If anyone goes, it’d be Josh McCown or Wes Phillips. Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: Forness summed up the vibe perfectly: “It is close, and I hope I can stop saying it because eventually it’s either going to be, hey, they figured it out, or they’re just not hitting them.” For Vikings fans riding the rollercoaster, The Real Forno Show is your weekly compass through the chaos — unfiltered film analysis, trade-deadline speculation, and the kind of honest takes you won’t get from the highlight reels. Whether you’re a believer or a skeptic, Tyler and Dave give you the full picture, All-22 included. Fan with Us!!! Tyler Forness @TheRealForno of Vikings 1st & SKOL @Vikings1stSKOL and A to Z Sports @AtoZSportsNFL , with Dave Stefano @Luft_Krigare producing this Vikings 1st & SKOL production, the @RealFornoShow found at the @BleavNetwork . So here’s the question: Will Nolan Teasley swing big at the deadline, or will Vikings fans be left watching another team land the difference-maker?

title: Examining the roster ties between Patriots, Dolphins ahead of Week 8
summary: There’s a Rolodex to flip through before head coach Mike Vrabel’s New England Patriots visit head coach Jeff Hafley’s Miami Dolphins. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, 11 players in the fold for Sunday’s AFC East matchup have been members of both locker rooms during their NFL journeys. Here’s the list of […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Josh Uche #9 of the Miami Dolphins gets set during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s a Rolodex to flip through before head coach Mike Vrabel’s New England Patriots visit head coach Jeff Hafley’s Miami Dolphins. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, 11 players in the fold for Sunday’s AFC East matchup have been members of both locker rooms during their NFL journeys. Here’s the list of former Patriots and former Dolphins ahead of the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff at Hard Rock Stadium. MIAMI Jalen Reagor, wide receiver — Reagor joined the Dolphins in June and was retained on the practice squad at its formation after being released in August. The 27-year-old wide receiver spent the previous two campaigns with the Los Angeles Chargers. Before then, he appeared in 11 games for Bill Belichick’s former club in 2023 and outlasted the initial 53-man roster deadline in 2024 only to be released, signed to the practice squad and then released from the practice squad. Entering the NFL with the Philadelphia Eagles in the first round of the 2020 draft at No. 21 overall, the TCU product had been traded to the Minnesota Vikings before finding his way to Gillette Stadium. Reagor now stands 64 games and 27 starts into his career. He has caught 86 passes for 1,037 yards and four touchdowns. An additional two visits to the end zone have arrived as a kickoff and punt returner. Caedan Wallace, guard — During training camp in August, the Patriots traded Wallace to the Dolphins in a pick swap involving a 2028 sixth-rounder and a 2029 seventh-rounder. The 26-year-old Penn State product had arrived in Foxborough in the third round of the 2024 draft class at No. 68 overall. He appeared in 10 games during his previous AFC East stop, starting a pair while going between offensive tackle, guard and jumbo tight end. Wallace has since checked into six games during his time in Miami Gardens, reporting as eligible for 14 offensive snaps while also working in protection on field goals and extra points. Joshua Uche, linebacker — Selected in the second round of the 2020 NFL draft at No. 60 overall, Uche’s Patriots tenure spanned 76 tackles and 20.5 sacks. A season featuring 11.5 sacks arrived along the way for an outside linebacker who once lined up across from the red-sleeved Matthew Judon. After 58 games off the edges, the stay reached its end ahead of the trade deadline in 2024. Uche headed to the Kansas City Chiefs as a sixth-rounder in the 2026 class headed back. The 28-year-old Michigan alum moved on to the NFC East on a one-year deal last campaign before returning to the AFC East on a one-year deal in March. He has made five starts this fall and stands 82 games, 134 tackles, 22.5 sacks, three forced fumbles and two recoveries into his career. Amari Gainer, linebacker — Gainer signed to the Dolphins’ initial practice squad after being waived by the Patriots at the 53-man roster deadline. The 26-year-old outside linebacker landed on New England’s practice squad last winter and was retained on a futures contract following Super Bowl LX. Originally entering the NFL with the Las Vegas Raiders as an undrafted free agent in 2024, the former transfer from Florida State to North Carolina appeared in all 17 games during his rookie year in the AFC West and was credited with five tackles through 328 snaps on special teams and 12 snaps on defense. Marcellas Dial Jr., cornerback — Dial was claimed off waivers by Miami after being let go by New England leading up to August’s cutdown deadline. The 25-year-old cornerback by way of Georgia Military and South Carolina had been chosen by the Patriots in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL draft at No. 180 overall. He was the last selection left from that class beyond All-Pro quarterback Drake Maye. Dial would make 17 appearances and one start as a rookie while seeing 60 snaps on defense and 378 snaps on special teams. A dozen tackles and a forced fumble were registered along the way. But a torn ACL saw Dial’s 2025 season end on injured reserve in training camp. He has since appeared in two games on the other side of the division. Tucker Addington, long snapper — Between summers, falls and winters, Addington had three separate stints with the Patriots from 2022 through 2024 as longtime long snapper Joe Cardona dealt with injuries. The 29-year-old specialist’s last came as a standard elevation from the practice squad before reverting and being released. Undrafted out of Sam Houston State, Addington has also been a member of the Houston Gamblers, Dallas Cowboys, Jacksonville Jaguars, Houston Texans and Washington Commanders. He has also been in Miami Gardens on more than one occasion, too. Addington’s NFL journey includes 16 games and a trio of tackles. NEW ENGLAND Ryan Miller, wide receiver — The Patriots signed Miller to the practice squad midway through October after placing wide receiver Romeo Doubs on injured reserve with a shoulder injury. The 26-year-old went undrafted out of Furman in 2023 and spent three seasons between the 53-man roster and practice squad of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before being claimed off waivers by the New York Giants. Miller then became a waiver claim at Hard Rock Stadium amid training camp. He has played in 30 NFL games, including six starts, while totaling 17 receptions for 254 yards and four touchdowns. His most recent TD took place in a Dolphins uniform from 77 yards out in September. Mack Hollins, wide receiver — Placed on injured reserve due to a calf injury in October, Hollins has caught 61 passes for 759 yards and two touchdowns through 19 games and 16 starts with the Patriots. The 2017 fourth-round pick out North Carolina earned a Super Bowl LII ring as a member of the Philadelphia Eagles and was later claimed off waivers by ex-Miami head coach Brian Flores & Co. A Dolphin from 2019 through 2021, Hollins served as a special teams captain before making stops with an additional three teams. The 33-year-old’s NFL career has featured 228 receptions for 2,828 yards and 17 visits to the end zone across 131 appearances. Julian Hill, tight end — The Patriots lost Hill to season-ending injured reserve in June. The 26-year-old inline tight end had agreed to terms on a three-year pact in March after not being tendered by the Dolphins as a restricted free agent. Hill spent the past three campaigns there while appearing in 45 games, including 26 starts, on the way to reeling in 33 receptions for 288 yards. The 2023 undrafted addition out of Campbell recorded 1,298 snaps on offense and 496 snaps on special teams. Tanner Conner, tight end — Conner had been among a group of tight ends in Foxborough for workouts before signing to the practice squad in September. The 28-year-old Idaho State alum entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2022. He made the Miami Dolphins’ initial 53-man roster as rookie and went on to appear in 33 games during his first AFC East stop. Finishing 2025 on the practice squad of the New York Giants before being released in August, Conner’s career includes 12 catches for 107 yards across 251 snaps on offense and 413 snaps on special teams. K.J. Britt, linebacker — The Patriots reached a one-year deal with Britt in March and the veteran linebacker agreed to remain on the practice squad after initially outlasting the 53-man roster deadline. One standard elevation has followed thus far, spanning 14 snaps in the kicking game and a tackle on a kickoff return. Selected in the fifth round of the 2021 NFL draft at No. 176 overall, Britt stands 77 games and 16 starts into a run hat began with Tampa Bay. The 27-year-old Auburn product spent last year with the Miami Dolphins and finished atop the team with 76.9 percent of the workload on special teams. His career stretches 162 tackles, half a sack, four…

title: Patriots Power Rankings Week 8: Streak stops, Pats drop
summary: All good streaks must come to an end, so they say. Many had the Bears matchup marked as a loss for the Patriots as soon as the schedule came out, but I was among the disappointed ones who picked a win. [Editor’s note: I always pick a win.] Injuries, fatigue and sloppy play weighted down […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: Devin Bush #12 of the Chicago Bears tackles Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots during the third quarter of the game at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images All good streaks must come to an end, so they say. Many had the Bears matchup marked as a loss for the Patriots as soon as the schedule came out, but I was among the disappointed ones who picked a win. [Editor’s note: I always pick a win.] Injuries, fatigue and sloppy play weighted down the team, and QB Caleb Williams’ converting on 4th down late in the fourth quarter was the point of no return. One game’s result shouldn’t be an indictment on the season, but how the team responds the next week can be. The experts on average dropped the Pats down 3 spots in the rankings, keeping them hovering around the 10th spot which is fair. Up next the Pats travel to Miami to play the 1-5 Dolphins in Week 8. Miami earned its first win last week, beating the New York Jets (hee hee). It would be better to quash any feistiness in the Fins early on and not let them in the game. With a few days longer rest period, it would also be a boost if New England gets to see some of the walking wounded heal up enough to return to practice this week. Division games are always tricky, but I am picking the Pats to win decisively on Sunday. GO PATS!! AFC East: Buffalo Bills (5-1) vs. Baltimore Ravens (4-3) New England Patriots (4-3) at Miami Dolphins (1-5) New York Jets (2-5) vs. Las Vegas Raiders (3-4) AFC Matchups: Kansas City Chiefs (5-1) at Denver Broncos (5-2) Cleveland Browns (5-2) at Pittsburgh Steelers (5-2) Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) vs. Indianapolis Colts (2-5) Cincinnati Bengals (4-2) vs. Tennessee Titans (1-6) Houston Texans (2-5) – Bye Week Los Angeles Chargers (0-6) at Los Angeles Rams (3-4) 8th – Nate Davis (USA Today): Turnovers continue to be their bugaboo, their 14 giveaways the second most in the league and a minus-7 differential also the second worst. Factor in a rash of injuries, and it’s fairly remarkable that the Pats are 4-3 . [nc] 10th – Vinnie Iyer (Sporting News): Drake Maye isn’t seeing ghosts, but he’s been haunted by turnovers in their losses. He’s up to eight interceptions and the Patriots’ three-game winning streak ended in Chicago. Maye leads the league and has matched his total from all last season . [-5] 10th – NFL Nation (ESPN): Best offseason addition: Edge Gabe Jacas. A second-round pick out of Illinois, Jacas has played 58% of the defensive snaps and provided juice for the pass rush with his high motor. He has totaled 20 tackles, six QB hits and 1.5 sacks while also contributing on the punt protection/punt coverage unit. Jacas has been a quick study, considering he was away from the team in the spring because of a knee procedure and had a contract stalemate that lasted into the early days of training camp . — Mike Reiss [-3] 10th – Nick Shook (NFL): It was good to see the Patriots compete with a legitimate contender on a short week in Chicago, and it was encouraging to watch Drake Maye shake off an ugly interception by throwing a similar pass for a touchdown later in the game. It was also frustrating to watch New England’s defense fail to make the most important plays in a game decided by them. A.J. Brown’s lack of involvement upon return is a concern, too, but overall, the Pats just have issues to correct. None will doom them . [-3] 10th – Ian Glendon (Full Press Coverage): New England’s three-game winning streak ended with a 30-24 loss at Chicago. Drake Maye threw for 321 yards and two scores but also made a costly mistake, and the defense could not contain Caleb Williams. The Patriots have earned respect over the past month, although the road loss puts a temporary cap on their climb . [-5] 11th – Conor Orr (SI): There will come a day when the Mike Vrabel act wears thin in New England, but in the wake of a quarter-million dollar fine for badmouthing the referees, his response shows that day is not today . [-2] 11th – Frank Schwab (Yahoo! Sports): Only two teams are worse than -5 in turnover differential. The Colts are last in the league at -9, and the Patriots are -7. It’s impressive New England is above .500 given that mark. The other five teams at -4 or worse are under .500. The big turnover Thursday night that cost the Patriots dearly was a bad pass by Drake Maye into the end zone that was picked off by linebacker D’Marco Jackson. That was a big difference in a 30-24 loss at the Bears. Maye played well other than that blemish. He had 321 passing yards and two touchdowns with that interception. One mistake swinging the game showed how slight the margins are in the NFL . [-4] 11th – Pete Prisco (CBS Sports): Losing at Chicago on a short week isn’t damning, but the defense wasn’t as good as in weeks past. That’s concernin g. [-2] 11th – Mike Florio (ProFootballTalk): With the Packers and Lions looming, they can’t overlook the Dolphins . [-3] 11th – Ralph Vacchiano (FOX Sports): The Patriots’ narrow loss to the Bears on Thursday night might only be a bump in the road for a team that is clearly back on the right track. Drake Maye continues to play well. The Patriots still don’t run the ball very well, though, and that’s going to be a problem against a schedule that just doesn’t get much easier between now and the playoffs. They’re going to need to hold the ball to slow down some of the high-powered offenses they face. If they keep playing shootouts, it’s not going to end well for them. Stat To Know : Rhamondre Stevenson’s 48-yard touchdown catch as time expired in the first half against the Bears was the Patriots’ longest touchdown to end a half since 2010. Over the past 20 years, 1,006 passes have been thrown in the final 10 seconds of a half from at least 40 yards from the end zone and traveled 10 or fewer air yards. Drake Maye’s throw to Stevenson was the only one to result in a touchdown . [nc] AVG RANK: 10.3 [-2.7]

title: Patriots trade deadline 2026: News and rumors tracker
summary: Even though they have already matched their total losses from last year, the New England Patriots once again look like a legitimate contender for a playoff spot in the AFC. However, in order to get there, they will have to find a way to overcome the injuries that have ravaged their roster over the first […]
full_text: Even though they have already matched their total losses from last year, the New England Patriots once again look like a legitimate contender for a playoff spot in the AFC. However, in order to get there, they will have to find a way to overcome the injuries that have ravaged their roster over the first two months of the regular season. While the expectation is that they will get several players back from injured reserve at some point, they also could go for a more radical approach in hopes of improving their team and gearing up for a stretch run in 2026. Like they have done multiple times in 2026 already, they could look at the trade market. Will there be additions to a list that already includes the likes of A.J. Brown, Jaylen Reed, Corey Kiner and Walter Rouse? Or could they move on from some of their players, like they did in 2025 ? We will know soon: the NFL trade deadline is coming up on Tuesday, November 10, at 4 p.m. ET. Until then, please make sure to bookmark and regularly revisit our Patriots trade deadline tracker for all the latest developments.
