title: Eagles-Cowboys Film Review: Most annoying defensive performance of the Vic Fangio era
summary: I have made plenty of excuses for the Eagles’ defense this year. There have been games when I thought this unit fought hard and received very little help from the other side of the ball. There is absolutely no excuse for this one. Monday Night Football. At home against the Cowboys. Most of the defense’s […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 4: Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on prior to the game against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field on October 4, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Rams defeated the Eagles 24-20. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images I have made plenty of excuses for the Eagles’ defense this year. There have been games when I thought this unit fought hard and received very little help from the other side of the ball. There is absolutely no excuse for this one. Monday Night Football. At home against the Cowboys. Most of the defense’s best players were available, including the expensive “superstars” up front. And this was the performance? I can’t remember coming away from a game this annoyed about a defense since the Super Bowl LVII defeat vs. the Chiefs. The Cowboys scored on seven of nine possessions, rushed for 204 yards, and finished with 416 total yards at 6.4 yards per play. The Eagles recorded zero sacks, zero quarterback hits, and zero rushing tackles for loss. After the offense opened the second half with a 17-play touchdown drive that took 9:16 off the clock, the defense immediately surrendered another touchdown. We cannot blame the offense for that. This defense had a long rest and a lead, and still couldn’t get a stop. As always, the advanced data here comes courtesy of Fantasy Points Data Suite . What really annoyed me was the combination of Dak Prescott’s 13.12-yard average depth of target (!), 2.95-second average time to throw (!!), and the Eagles’ lack of pressure. The Cowboys were giving routes time to develop downfield, and the Eagles still couldn’t affect the quarterback. Vic Fangio deserves criticism, too. The Eagles appeared prepared for the short throws and middle-of-the-field passing that had characterized the Cowboys’ offense, then looked shocked when the Cowboys attacked vertically and leaned on the run. Let’s get into an ugly one. Defense The Cowboys’ use of jumbo personnel was a disaster for the Eagles all game long. The Cowboys brought on a sixth offensive lineman, Broderick Jones, and created some of the biggest gaps you will see in an NFL game multiple times. Look at the space between Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter here. You cannot invest this much in the defensive interior and get this little resistance. Davis and Carter slide in different directions to avoid the double teams, which creates this massive gap. I think Jihaad Campbell has to do significantly better, too. I’ve defended his play this year, so this game was a real letdown. He was way too passive. He must get downhill quicker. Jones played nine offensive snaps. On the eight runs he was on the field, the Cowboys gained 74 yards. That’s 9.3 yards per carry! Remove those eight runs, and you’re left with 30 carries for 130 yards, or 4.3 per carry. That tells you how damaging the Cowboys’ jumbo package was. I hated how often the Eagles maintained a two-high safety look against it, including looks with George Pickens as the only wide receiver. I understand that Fangio wants to keep a split-safety pre-snap look, but I think at times you have to bring a safety into the box if you simply can’t stop the run. Eagles' Defense All22 Thread vs. Cowboys. Buckle up. 1) The Cowboys absolutely destroyed the Eagles with Jumbo (6 OL) personnel. The Eagles had no answers all night. Some of the gaps were as big as you will ever see at this level. No single player or reason made it so bad. But… pic.twitter.com/ulxLxZueEn — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 27, 2026 The Eagles had early success showing six potential rushers on the line of scrimmage before dropping two into coverage. I like creating uncertainty about who is coming, and this was an example of the idea working on the first 3rd down of the game. The problem was what happened as the game developed. The Cowboys became increasingly comfortable because the threat of extra pressure rarely became actual pressure. This kind of look works because linebackers often drop into short hook zones and can take away quick slants. Eventually, the Cowboys just stopped throwing short routes against this look and threw vertically. The Eagles had no answer. The Eagles sent five or more rushers on eight of 28 dropbacks. Those plays allowed 4.1 yards per dropback and minus-0.01 EPA per play, compared with 10.0 yards per dropback and +0.69 EPA when they sent four. The blitzes only generated one pressure, so I’m hardly claiming it was great. But when your four-man rush is this ineffective, you have to find another way to challenge the offense. Showing pressure and then repeatedly dropping bodies into the middle also left the outside corners with some difficult assignments, which we will get into later. Sometimes, I hate to be basic, but you need to blitz. 2) One of the successes on the first drive was the Eagles showing 6 potential rushers on the LOS and then dropping 2 into coverage. It worked here, but eventually the Cowboys realized the Eagles were not actually going to send extra rushers. Fangio didn't blitz enough,… pic.twitter.com/4DI4lVCs06 — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 27, 2026 This is where the individual execution becomes impossible to defend. Davis and Moro Ojomo have one-on-one matchups and do nothing with them. The center barely needs to touch Davis before climbing directly to Jihaad Campbell. Campbell has to do a better job shedding the block, but look at how cleanly that blocker reaches him. At the very least, I expect Davis to make it difficult for the center to leave. That did not happen here. Davis and Carter risk becoming what we call in the UK a “flat-track bully.” For those unsure, a flat-track bully is a player who dominates inferior opponents but struggles against top-tier competition. For too long, both Davis and Carter have dominated bad opposition but get dominated by elite competition. Carter in particular has struggled against the Cowboys multiple times. I’m also unsure where Zack Baun is going while being blocked by a tight end. The Eagles looked confused on multiple snaps about who was setting the edge, and that uncertainty made already poor execution worse. It was rough. 3) A lot of bad. Davis and Ojomo both have one-on-one matchups and do nothing. The C barely touches Davis; he just gets immediately to Campbell, who cannot shed a block. At the very least, you'd expect Davis to command a double team, but he didn't in this game. I'm not quite… pic.twitter.com/uN3XZldHeZ — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 27, 2026 The pass coverage is just off this year. On this snap, the Eagles show six rushers and drop two, but Baun and Campbell end up in essentially the same area. The coverage leaves three defenders against three eligible receivers on the boundary side, and the communication breaks down. I’m pretty sure Cooper DeJean is badly at fault here, sadly. These coverage busts are following him this year. The out route is wide open before Tariq Woolen makes it worse by missing the tackle completely. What should the offense be worried about here? There is no pass rush, and the extra bodies in coverage aren’t closing the available throws. These looks have to create some hesitation or force the quarterback to speed up. Instead, Prescott has time to wait for the coverage to break down. At some point, you have to actually send the pressure you keep threatening. If you read my preview, you will know that Dak has a very low average depth of target this year. This offense normally gets rid of the ball quickly. They changed it up this week, and the Eagles didn’t adjust. 4) The pass coverage this year is just off. It's so weird. The Eagles show 6 rushers, but drop 2. Baun and Campbell drop to the same spot in the field. This style of defense results in single-high coverage, and the Eagles end up 3 vs. 3 on the boundary side. They don't… pic.twitter.com/1gRGrSMwse — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 27, 2026 I thought the Eagles asked too much…

title: Eagles-Cowboys snap counts: Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis play a lot, produce little
summary: The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 7 loss to the Dallas Cowboys are in. Let’s take a look and run through some analysis. OFFENSE DEFENSE SPECIAL TEAMS DID NOT PLAY ACTIVE: Joe Milton, Mac McWilliams INACTIVE: Nolan Smith, DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Cole Payton, Michael Carter II, Lane Johnson, Jake Majors
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - DECEMBER 28: Jalen Carter #98 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates with Jordan Davis #90 after sacking Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills (not pictured) in the second quarter of the game at Highmark Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 7 loss to the Dallas Cowboys are in. Let’s take a look and run through some analysis. OFFENSE Jordan Mailata is the only player on offense who’s played 100% of the Eagles’ offensive snaps this season. He’s also played 11.41% of the Eagles’ special teams snaps. Landon Dickerson and Drew Kendall were able to play the entire game in their first action since returning from injury. Darius Cooper, WR1! In terms of offensive snaps played, at least. Despite this, he ranked fifth in targets with three. With DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks out, Makai Lemon logged career highs in snap count percentage, receptions (7), and yards (67). He tied his career-high for targets (8) and scored his first career touchdown. Good to see him showing some promise. Dallas Goedert, who missed two practices due to injury last week, understandably didn’t take his normal workload. He still ranked second in targets with seven. Dameon Pierce was the Eagles’ top running back in terms of usage since Saquon Barkley clearly wasn’t right. But Pierce also got banged up, which led to Elijah Mitchell seeing some playing time. Hollywood Brown looked pretty awesome, didn’t he?! I’d say any team looking to acquire a wide receiver would be very wise to give some good draft picks to the Eagles in exchange for him! Brown was a healthy scratch last week … with Elijah Moore active ahead of him. But then Brown played more in this game. Moore’s four targets this season have resulted in three receptions for 20 yards. Johnny Mundt played his lowest snap count percentage of the season on offense and his second-highest on special teams. His struggles are seemingly leading to less playing time. Eli Stowers saw some snaps in his NFL debut! With E.J. Jenkins gone, he’s the new TE3. Grant Calcaterra wasn’t far behind as TE4. Kudos to Saquon Barkley for trying to tough it out and play through injury. But it doesn’t seem very smart for the team to allow him to do that. He was ultimately able to produce 71 yards from scrimmage on nine total touches. But it remains to be seen if Monday night’s game set back his recovery timeline. Fred Johnson played one snap with the Eagles going with a six offensive lineman formation in the red zone. DEFENSE Quinyon Mitchell briefly missed some time after getting banged up but quickly returned to the game. Jonathan Jones filled in for him. Jalen Carter played a lot of snaps and logged zero stats outside of two assisted tackles. The Cowboys’ interior offensive line is good. But Carter is the highest paid interior defensive lineman in the NFL. He is expected to be much better than he was on Monday night. With Jalyx Hunt and Jonathan Greenard less than 100% while playing through injuries, Arnold Ebiketie was the Eagles’ top edge defender in terms of playing time. He’s a fine rotational player but that workload just isn’t ideal for him. Ditto for A.J. Epenesa playing the second-most edge rusher snaps. Jordan Davis logged his highest snap count percentage of the season. He logged zero stats outside of four assisted tackles. It’s just not good enough. Kenny Moore continues to be the safety next to Andrew Mukuba in nickel packages. Last week, Jihaad Campbell and Jeremiah Trotter Jr. effectively saw a 60-40 split. This week, it basically went down to 55-35 in favor of Campbell. Moro Ojomo entered this game banged up and got hurt again in the game. Ty Robinson played five snaps and had one assisted tackle and zero other stats. Jalen Carter played 59 snaps and had two assisted tackles and zero other stats. Rookie edge rusher Keyshawn James-Newby played a minor role after being temporarily elevated from the practice squad for the second time this season. Only one elevation remaining. SPECIAL TEAMS Kelee Ringo made a really nice special teams tackle on punt coverage. Marcus Epps continues to be limited to special teams duty after previously being the safety next to Mukuba in nickel defense. Willie Lampkin was limited to special teams duty after being replaced by Landon Dickerson in the starting lineup. Could be nice if they experimented with him as a blocking tight end/fullback. Braden Mann is legitimately one of the most useful players on the team this year, sadly. Britain Covey suffered an injury and was ruled out after his only play of the game. DID NOT PLAY ACTIVE: Joe Milton, Mac McWilliams INACTIVE: Nolan Smith, DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Cole Payton, Michael Carter II, Lane Johnson, Jake Majors In Week 6, Payton was the Eagles’ backup quarterback behind McKee since Milton had only just joined the team. Now Milton is the backup with Payton serving as the emergency third quarterback. Nolan Smith might be able to return in Week 8. It’s currently unclear if DeVonta and/or Wicks can return in Week 8. We’ll find out more from the team’s practices this week. As a reminder, Johnson is set to remain on the Eagles’ roster until June 2027 , even though he retired.

title: Thinking about injuries since the Eagles game ended
summary: The Eagles are 2-5, currently in the longest losing streak of the Nick Sirianni era. There isn’t really a light at the end of this tunnel given the team’s injuries and the pervasive feeling of ineptitude and mistrust in the organization’s leadership from the coach all the way up to ownership. While there’s plenty of […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates a touchdown during the first quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles are 2-5, currently in the longest losing streak of the Nick Sirianni era. There isn’t really a light at the end of this tunnel given the team’s injuries and the pervasive feeling of ineptitude and mistrust in the organization’s leadership from the coach all the way up to ownership. While there’s plenty of negative to talk about, I woke up thinking about injuries, player health, and how the NFLPA needs to step up and do their damn job. It’s almost darkly funny that it took until this year for the 49ers injury bug to become a meme. It was mid-last season that the electrical substation thing broke contain of 49ers fandom and jumped to a league-wide unfortunate joke. Then, this year as the Niners suffered early season injuries, the specter of the substation returned. The substation then moved to Philadelphia, with the injury bug hitting early and then reaching a crescendo with the Jalen Hurts disaster. Since then, the Eagles have been dealing with injuries to star players like Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, Jalen Carter … along with Dontayvion Wicks, Tank Bigsby, Will Shipley … and the list goes on. Against the Cowboys, Saquon Barkley was hobbled with a hamstring injury (and a new back injury that flared up) while the team still trotted him out there. He was limping and riding the bike between plays. Carter was previously playing with a hairline fracture and clearly wasn’t playing to a high level while wearing a cast on his hand. Needless to say, injuries happen in football. It’s a physical, violent game. And in the case of the Eagles, you could make the case that after their Super Bowl win in 2024, it took a physical toll on the team. After all, the Chiefs fell apart from injuries last year after three straight seasons where they played 20 games. Maybe that attrition has hit Philly. That’s reasonable enough, but the Eagles medical staff’s handling of the Jalen Hurts injury raises questions about their entire medical, strength and conditioning operation. How many players’ injuries have they mismanaged to get them on the field, jeopardizing their long term health for winning one week? It was well-documented that Cam Jurgens and Landon Dickerson were not healthy last year ( Dickerson admitted he probably shouldn’t have played in 2025 ) and those injuries seemingly compounded to impact their play this year. Back to the 49ers, whose injury problems have persisted through the Kyle Shanahan era, It is well-documented that Shanahan runs more full contact practice than any other head coach in the league. It’s well-documented that his practices are considered generally more physical. It should be considered no surprise, then, that the Niners seemingly lose a major contributor every few weeks to lower body injuries. The teams theoretically have a responsibility to keep their roster healthy. But they also have a short-term incentive to win. Maybe Shanny’s practices are part of the reason his teams are typically so competitive regardless of who is on the field and that’s the trade off he’s willing to make. This is where the union needs to intervene. There needs to be better standardized expectations for practice structure for players, in addition to strength and conditioning and medical care. There are 32 teams that behave in 32 different ways when it comes to these aspects. It is obvious that team-run medical staff cannot be fuly trusted to serve the players’ best interests when there are games and team interests on the line. Players themselves have more incentive to play in the short-term than not play, and they should be protected from that being the case. The competency of a team’s medical and training staff should not be a competitive advantage. It should be something guided by set regulations. Much like the conversations about standardizing playing surfaces, the league must also contend with doing the same with the people that are supposed to keep players healthy.

title: What on earth happened to this Eagles defense?
summary: We all knew the offense was going to be problematic. Sean Mannion’s new scheme would take time to get on its feet. Jalen Hurts would need to acclimate himself to it, the offensive line’s health was a question mark, and there didn’t appear to be many great answers at wide receiver. The prevailing wisdom was, […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: George Pickens #3 of the Dallas Cowboys catches a touchdown pass against Andrew Mukuba #24 of the Philadelphia Eagles during the second quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images We all knew the offense was going to be problematic. Sean Mannion’s new scheme would take time to get on its feet. Jalen Hurts would need to acclimate himself to it, the offensive line’s health was a question mark, and there didn’t appear to be many great answers at wide receiver. The prevailing wisdom was, if the Eagles were going to survive some early season growing pains from the offense, the defense would have to do a little more. But after so much offensive futility over the first six weeks, Hurts’ season ending blood clots, being forced to spend more time on the field than almost any other defense in the NFL and lugging around a 2-4 record, it appeared as if the effort dam broke for Vic Fangio’s unit in the Eagles’ embarrassing 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday Night Football. Ironically, the offense actually showed a pulse for the first time all season. Tanner McKee is a backup quarterback for a reason, but he played pretty well through three quarters. After a really nice touchdown drive coming out of halftime gave the Eagles a 21-20 lead, the defense offered about as much resistance as single-ply Dollar Store toilet paper. It’s fair to say the defense has been far more disappointing than the offense through seven ugly weeks of football. Worse yet, it sure looked like they gave up on Monday night. Former Cowboys coach Wade Phillips summed it up best on ESPN’s Manning Cast. The numbers are disgusting, especially for a unit with this much high-priced, and soon-to-be high priced, talent on it. They have given up the 6th-most yards per game (371.3), 7th-most passing yards per game (239.9), and 6th-most rushing yards per game (131.4). That they are only 12th-worst in points per game allowed (25.0) is a bit of a miracle, thanks to a couple key goal line stands against Jacksonville and the Rams. They have a mere three interceptions and are the only team in the league without a fumble recovery. Those three total takeaways are tied with the Colts for fewest in the league. The Eagles’ 28.1% pressure rate is 10th-worst, they have the 9th-fewest total pressures, and are 2nd-worst in sacks per game (1.1). What’s worse, there are no injury excuses on the defensive side of the ball, certainly not against Dallas. While they missed Nolan Smith (concussion) on the edge rushing the passer, there was more than enough there to hold down the fort. Jalyx Hunt and Jonathan Greenard returned to the lineup, joining a group of tackles thought to be the best trio in the NFL. Instead, a Dallas running game that ranked 30th in the league coming into the Linc, ran for 204 yards on 38 carries, a 5.37 yard per carry average. Dak Prescott not only wasn’t sacked, he wasn’t even threatened. Bear in mind, this is a defensive line with Greenard ($25.2), Jalen Carter ($24.4) and Jordan Davis ($20.5) making a combined $70.1 million this season. Carter has 3 sacks and 18 tackles in seven games. Greenard has one tackle and one QB hit in four games. Davis has 27 tackles and 0.5 sacks. Remember Jalyx Hunt, the guy everyone swore up and down was due for a monster season and huge contract based off his summer reps? He remains without a sack and has 4 QB hits and 17 tackles. The other up-and-comer, Moro Ojomo, has no sacks, 3 QB hits and 18 tackles. They’re not exactly playing themselves into big money deals. Only Smith has shown up this, leading all team edge rushers with 3 sacks, 3 QB hits and 4 tackles for loss. Zack Baun and Quinyon Mitchell continue to play well, but the middle of the defense is missing safety Reed Blankenship’s steady play and Nakobe Dean’s athleticism and team leadership. Jeremiah Trotter, Jr. is now splitting time with last year’s first round pick, Jihaad Campbell, who has disappointed in a larger role this season. The safeties have been a disaster, and Riq Woolen has been extremely uneven. The decline in play from slot corner Cooper DeJean is particularly startling. He’s likely to get a big money extension at some point, but he’s putting it in jeopardy as he has suddenly begun missing a ton of tackles and finding himself at the center of defensive miscommunications that have led to big plays over the last few weeks. Part of the problem is how much Fangio’s unit has been on the field. Through their first seven games, the Eagles’ defense has been on the field for 67.3 plays per game, 4th-most in the NFL. That’s due to the offense leading the league in 3-and-outs. The defense has been on the field an average time of possession of 32:19. Only the Titans’ defense has been out on the field longer. However, on Monday night, the offense was holding its own. They gave the defense a shot to keep them in the game, but they couldn’t keep up with Prescott and the Dallas offense. It was too much to ask. It shouldn’t have been. The defensive side of the ball is where all the money is. So now, at 2-5, the Eagles’ season is likely over. Even in a weak NFC East, it’s clear they don’t have the horses on offense, and it’s clear something is amiss defensively. Howie Roseman should be a seller at the trade deadline in two weeks. At that time, it’s possible some of these contributors on defense will be playing somewhere else. For now, it’s one of the most disappointing performances by any Eagles unit in recent memory.
author: John Stolnis

title: Quenton Nelson trade rumors: Eagles among teams that showed interest in Colts guard
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles were among teams that showed interest in Quenton Nelson before the Indianapolis Colts traded their All-Pro guard to the Seattle Seahawks on Tuesday morning, according to a report from NFL insider Jeremy Fowler. The Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears were also mentioned to be in the mix. Fowler notes that these […]
full_text: Quenton Nelson Indianapolis Colts offensive guard Quenton Nelson (56) walks off the field following their game at Lucas Oil Stadium on Sept. 9, 2018. The Indianapolis Colts lost to the Cincinnati Bengals 34-23.Indianapolis Colts Play The Cincinnati Bengals In Their 2018 Season Opener | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Philadelphia Eagles were among teams that showed interest in Quenton Nelson before the Indianapolis Colts traded their All-Pro guard to the Seattle Seahawks on Tuesday morning, according to a report from NFL insider Jeremy Fowler . The Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears were also mentioned to be in the mix. Fowler notes that these teams “showed varying levels of interest,” so, it’s unclear just how serious the Eagles were about acquiring Nelson. Or exactly when their interest was expressed. It’s not hard to imagine Howie Roseman calling the Colts about Nelson’s availability because 1) he’s always ready to make a big trade and 2) the Eagles’ offensive line situation hasn’t been very good this season. It was previously reported that Roseman was shopping for a starting caliber blocker . But with the Eagles dropping their fifth straight game to drop to 2-5, it’s much easier to picture the Eagles as sellers instead of buyers ahead of the 2026 NFL trade deadline. This doesn’t mean Roseman can’t acquire a player who could conceivably help the team for years to come. It does seem like the Eagles won’t be interested in high-cost one-year rentals, however, which is what Nelson qualifies as since the 30-year-old is a free agent after this season. A few more Eagles thoughts related to this trade: The Eagles host the Seahawks in Week 15. This move makes Seattle better, which is good if you’re rooting for Philly to lose and maximize their draft positioning. Nelson was acquired in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. The Eagles got more for trading Cam Jurgens (plus a 2027 seventh-round pick) for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick. The Nelson trade might point to more of a buyer’s market than a seller’s market, which isn’t what the Eagles want to see if they’re planning to deal players ahead of the deadline.

But there’s reason to believe the Eagles could land some high-end talent if they’re picking high. They last did so when they had favorable selections in the 2021 NFL Draft after a bad 2020 season. The Eagles still have 10 games left this season, so, much can change … for better or for worse. The latter seems more likely right now. But that doesn’t mean the future can’t be bright.

title: Eagles News: “Is there any part of this team to believe in right now?”
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! To answer the question posed in the headline: No. There isn’t. This team is cooked. Stick a fork in them. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Defense??? – Iggles Blitz The loss dropped the Eagles to 2-5. […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Head coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the second quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! To answer the question posed in the headline: No. There isn’t. This team is cooked. Stick a fork in them. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Defense??? – Iggles Blitz The loss dropped the Eagles to 2-5. The play the Commanders and Giants over the next two weeks. Both teams will be coming off byes so that will make things as challenging as possible, especially this week with the Eagles coming off a Monday night game. It will be tough to get Saquon ready for Sunday night. The season isn’t over because the NFC East is such a mess, but it is perilously close. And the defense disappearing the way they did is really discouraging. Is there any part of this team to believe in right now? Roob’s Observations as hapless Eagles drop fifth straight with loss to Cowboys – NBCSP The Eagles finally got some decent offense going, but the defense flat-out collapsed. That’s the kind of season it’s been. The defense was atrocious Monday night and honestly hasn’t been great for much of the year. Certainly not the elite unit we expected before the season. They began the day 26th in total yards allowed, 21st in rush defense, 27th in passing yards allowed, 31st in sacks, 26th in first downs allowed and 28th in points allowed. That was before kickoff. Then went out and got shredded by Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, Javonte Williams and Company. It got so bad that Williams literally walked into the end zone untouched. This defense was supposed to carry the Eagles while the offense was figuring things out, but that hasn’t what happened. Considering expectations, the defense has been worse than the offense. They don’t get turnovers, they don’t get pressure, they don’t get sacks, they don’t stop the run, they don’t cover. The last few weeks they at least played well in the first half or first three quarters before falling apart in the fourth quarter. On Monday night, they just looked overmatched from the get-go. Eagles-Cowboys final score: Philadelphia’s defense gives Dallas offense a get-right game – BGN But Philadelphia’s defense was a problem throughout the night with the Cowboys scoring 38 points and producing 416 yards with 212 coming on the ground. The Eagles’ highly paid defensive line produced zero TFLs, zero sacks, and zero quarterback hits, allowing Dak Prescott to be entirely too comfortable. This was a get-right game for a Cowboys offense that only managed to muster 29 points combined over the past two weeks. The Eagles have now lost five games in a row for the first time since the 2016 season. Analyzing Nick Sirianni’s job security as the Eagles’ head coach – PhillyVoice Sirianni already cashed in one “I won a Super Bowl so I get to survive a terrible season” token after 2025. Was his Super Bowl season in 2024 worth two of those tokens? My guess… Nope. It’s probably going to take a dramatic turnaround and some postseason success for Sirianni to keep his job. Lurie likes Sirianni, so an in-season firing feels unlikely. Sirianni will at least get a chance at some sort of miraculous recovery. But obviously at the moment, any mention of the postseason would conjure up Jim Mora’s infamous “Playoffs?!” rant. Eagles’ defense goes deafeningly silent during — and after — catastrophic collapse vs. Cowboys | The Early Bird – PHLY Eagles The silence in the postgame locker room was deafening. The aftermath of the Eagles‘ 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys on primetime gave way to the hush of a locker room that’s now lacking familiar voices and familiar goals. It was Saquon Barkley to address the team in the moments that preceded reporters swarming into the locker room, and Barkley who explained just how rare it has been for him to be the one called upon to do so with Jalen Hurts on injured reserve, Lane Johnson retired, and the hopes of this team rounding into form withering away. “I know that I gotta take more of a a role of being vocal, using my voice,” Barkley said. “I’m more of a lead-by-example type of guy, but it happens when you have guys banged up, and a guy like Jalen, who’s really basically the vocal leader. It’s gonna take me and Jordan [Mailata,] all of us to kind of fill that void.” The void was plenty big on Monday night. After turning in arguably the worst defensive performance of Vic Fangio’s three-year tenure, both Jalen Carter and Riq Woolen declined to address their role in the mishap with reporters afterward. “Nah, y’all have a good night,” Carter said. “You get home safe.” Eagles-Cowboys Postgame: Eagles Defense EXPOSED — Brandon Graham & Vinny Curry React – PHLY Sports The Eagles are now 2-5 with the season on the ropes following an ugly loss to the Dallas Cowboys in which the defense were barely able to muster a stop despite all the talent at their disposal. Tanner McKee threw a costly interception, though the running game looked its best of the season, and Makai Lemon scored his first career touchdown. Where do the Birds go from here? Super Bowl champions Brandon Graham and Vinny Curry discuss, along with Brandon Lee Gowton, Bo Wulf, Fran Duffy and EJ Smith. NFL Week 7 Recap: Immediate fantasy football takeaways from Cowboys-Eagles – PFF Unsurprisingly, Cooper was one of the team’s top receivers. It was encouraging to see Lemon emerge as the other primary option, considering how rarely he had played in two-receiver sets before this week. That suggests there’s at least a chance Lemon could become the Eagles‘ second receiver at some point this season. He still primarily lined up in the slot when Philadelphia used 11 personnel. Brown typically lined up as the third receiver in 11 personnel, while Elijah Moore rotated in occasionally and served as the primary wide receiver in 13 personnel. Britain Covey was the only other receiver on the roster, but he suffered a knee injury on a special teams play early in the game. It’s unclear whether he would have had a role on offense had he remained healthy. Lemon delivered the best game of his career, catching seven passes for 67 yards and a touchdown. He probably shouldn’t be a top waiver-wire priority, since several other rookie wide receivers have gotten off to better starts without needing injuries to earn additional playing time. However, if you’re looking for help at wide receiver and miss out on the other top rookie options, Lemon is a solid consolation prize. Eagles’ Saquon Barkley says hamstring ‘great’ in return, not sweating back issue – ESPN Eagles running back Saquon Barkley said his “hamstring came out great” and doesn’t believe his back issue will keep him out after a gutsy and highly efficient performance in Philadelphia’s 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys on Monday night. Barkley was questionable entering the game because of a hamstring injury that sidelined him the previous two weeks. The Eagles tried to limit his carries, and that number dropped further when his back locked up as the game progressed. He played a total of nine snaps and touched the ball every time he was on the field, finishing with seven carries for 62 yards and a touchdown, and two receptions for 9 yards. Barkley is the first NFL starter in the past 20 seasons to play at least nine offensive snaps in a game and get a touch on all of them. The personnel packages. The formation variations. A passing game featuring crossing routes and catch-and-run…

title: Now comes the fall for the Eagles
summary: Across various forms of the internet this season I have seen a common defense of Nick Sirianni, who has no answers to save a sinking ship. This defense comes in two versions of the same flavor: his team doesn’t quit/his players try hard. First of all, so what? Players not quitting on their team is […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Head coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles and Dom DiSandro look on prior to the game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Across various forms of the internet this season I have seen a common defense of Nick Sirianni, who has no answers to save a sinking ship. This defense comes in two versions of the same flavor: his team doesn’t quit/his players try hard. First of all, so what? Players not quitting on their team is less than the bare minimum expected of a coach. The team is poorly coached. The game plan sucks, the play calling sucks, the in-game decisions suck, the post-game retrospect sucks. “They play hard” doesn’t have a lot of sticking power when it’s all you have. Dan Quinn is just down the road if you want a guy who brings nothing to the table other than effort. Secondly, it looks like that ship has sailed. Jordan Mailata sowed seeds of doubts about that last week when he said the team didn’t play with “want to.” He was here for the 2020 season, he knows what a lost cause looks like. Monday night was the same script as all season: hang around in the first half, then crumble in the second. They have the worst scoring offense in the second half, and the 6th worst scoring defense. Even in their two wins the Eagles were outscored by Washington in the second half and tied the Titans in the second half. And over his career, Nick Sirianni is now 0-8 as a home underdog, and the Eagles are the only team to not win as a home underdog since 2021. He’s also never covered. Granted, half of those games the line was 3 points or less, but they usually don’t come close to covering, nor do they muck up the game. title: Nick Sirianni talks about the Eagles’ defensive struggles
summary: The Eagles lost another game in embarrassing fashion, and head coach Nick Sirianni spoke to reporters afterward about the defensive struggles, how they handled Saquon Barkley’s return, and how they were able to get things going offensively early in the game. Sirianni was also asked about his message to the team, and it was about […]
full_text: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images | Getty Images The Eagles lost another game in embarrassing fashion, and head coach Nick Sirianni spoke to reporters afterward about the defensive struggles, how they handled Saquon Barkley’s return, and how they were able to get things going offensively early in the game. Sirianni was also asked about his message to the team, and it was about resilience and being grateful. “We just talked about being the same version of yourself every single day. All that matters is we improve. I think back on the 2021 season, the way we finished that year — and I didn’t say this to them, but I’m thinking about it right now — The way we finished that year propelled us into the future Eagles way that we’ve been the last four years. Growth is important. We talked a lot about being the same version of ourselves regardless of the circumstances and that football is going to deal you some tough hands at times, but can you get up and keep fighting? Life’s going to deal you some tough hands at times. Can you get up and keep fighting? We talked about that. We talked about being the same guy every day. We talked about being grateful.” Here’s what the head coach had to say: On the defensive issues “Obviously, it’s never just one thing when you give up a bunch of yards like that. We’ve got to do a better job coaching. We’ve got to do a better job executing, getting off blocks, tackling. We had a couple missed tackles, but it’s always going to be about block destruction, playing on their side of the line of scrimmage, and then us putting them in positions to succeed. I give them credit. They played a good game. Hats off to them.” Sirianni didn’t want to get much into some of the missed tackling, but noted that they do look at each one, assess what the problem was, and then try to rep those corrections in practice and in drills. He explained that not only do they have to put players in position to succeed, but they also have to give them the tools and practice opportunities to do that. The head coach credited the Cowboys offense for the lack of Eagles’ defensive pressure throughout the game. He said that they were able to stay ahead of the sticks quite a bit and had manageable third down situations – and they were able to keep the defense off-balance with the way they ran it and the play action game in those third downs. “Again, there’s never just one thing. Again, when you’re not getting pressures, you’ve got to try to simulate them in some way. So again, it’s always a version of, how are we executing? How are we putting them in positions to succeed? Because all that matters is that it goes out onto the field and we try to give ourselves the best chance to win. In this game of football, just like anything, I think we always want to pin it on something, but there’s multiple things that contribute to it. We’ll look at that, look at some of the common themes and see what we need to do to get better.” When asked specifically about the production from guys like Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis, Sirianni instead pointed to their contributions throughout the season, saying that everyone will want plays back from Monday night’s game, and with the struggles they had against the run, it’s never just one thing. On Saquon Barkley’s return “Obviously, you saw that [Saquon Barkley] was on a pitch count out there today. There was constant communication to see how he was feeling, see where he was, and obviously, he came out early in the second half. Again, when you go into something like that, you make sure that the player’s health is first and foremost. Is he ready to go? Do they feel ready to go? Do the doctors and trainers feel like they’re ready to go? We felt like that was the case today, but obviously wanted to keep a close eye on him, and he’s tough as heck. He wanted to be out there for his teammates, probably had to slow him [down] as far as — he’d be out there every play because of the person he is and the teammate he is and the player he is and the toughness that he has.” Still, Sirianni went on to say that they tried to be smart with him, but it was good to have him back out on the field. He noted that the RB had a nice game and was very productive when he got the ball. The head coach also acknowledged that Barkley ended up playing less than they had planned for after he hurt his back on the first run of the game . On their offensive success “I think when you’re able to be efficient in the run game and set yourself up on third down, we felt like we were able to kind of run some of the things, what we wanted to do coming into the game and coming into the season where we keep run, play action, stuff like that. We were able to get some tempo calls going into it. I think you just got to see a variety of things that we want to do because we weren’t behind the sticks and we have to keep up with that script. Obviously, we did a good job finishing in the red zone. Sometimes it was because some penalties extended the drives, but also being able to run it in down there was key, was obviously good for us. But I think it was just staying in phase, being able to hit explosives in the run game and being able to convert on third down. I’m not sure what we were throughout third down. I think it was over 40%, but we still even want to do better there. But yeah, we’ve still got a lot of things to correct and work on.“ On having to rely on depth players “That’s life in the NFL. We feel good about our process of giving guys that maybe aren’t starters opportunities for developmental periods and things like that. But I think that’s the league. It is our job to bring depth in and it is our job to develop that depth. With that comes opportunity on my end, the opportunity to give them opportunities to grow with practice time, with how we review film with them, everything. But that’s life in the NFL. I’ll never use that as an excuse because at the end of the day, all that matters is if we won or lost and if we continue to get better, and we didn’t do that. No one’s going to feel sorry for us and our job is to get whoever’s on that field ready to play in the game that’s going to play every Sunday or Monday.” Sirianni said that he is committed to helping players develop as leaders in the locker room, especially after losing several of their captains, and is always thinking about ways to coach them up in that regard.

title: Mike McCarthy hypes up Cleveland ahead of Steelers-Browns matchup
summary: It’s Steelers-Browns week… again. This time, the Steelers are looking for a more favorable result. Pittsburgh and Cleveland will meet for the second time following a 27-24 Thursday Night Football victory for Cleveland on October 1. The rematch comes exactly one month later.  It also comes the day after Halloween, when some fans have dressed […]
full_text: (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s Steelers-Browns week… again. This time, the Steelers are looking for a more favorable result. Pittsburgh and Cleveland will meet for the second time following a 27-24 Thursday Night Football victory for Cleveland on October 1. The rematch comes exactly one month later. It also comes the day after Halloween, when some fans have dressed up as Steelers players or found creative ways to take jabs at Cleveland while trick-or-treating across Pittsburgh. The rivalry between Pittsburgh and Cleveland is one of the best in the country and transcends football, seeping into the fabric of our everyday lives. Growing up in Greenfield during the height of the 1970s Steelers, head coach Mike McCarthy grew up, like most of us from Pittsburgh, thinking the worst of Cleveland. That all changed when McCarthy actually paid a visit. “I was shocked the first time I went to Cleveland because it looked like nothing I was told it looked like,” McCarthy said. “They have nice suburbs; they have a good downtown. The impression of what you think of the Cleveland Browns in Cleveland as a kid is different.” It’s a hilarious, yet potentially relatable response for some people, if you put the sports rivalries aside. “I remember the great rivalries in the old days, the Cardiac Kids (1979 and 1980) and the history of it too, so that’s cool,” McCarthy said. “When I do bring it up, I don’t think some of the guys even know what the hell I’m talking about if I bring up the Cardiac Kids.” Not one player on the Steelers roster was born yet. Not even soon-to-be 43-year-old Aaron Rodgers. The Steelers have won three games in a row. Raking down Cleveland at Acrisure Stadium would put the team in sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Teams that start 6-2 have made the playoffs 89% of the time. The Steelers have begun the year 6-2 on 15 occasions, reaching the postseason all but once (2009). The Steelers haven’t won in Cleveland since Halloween night of 2021, but haven’t lost to Cleveland at home in the regular season since 2003. McCarthy understands the gravity of the matchup for numerous reasons on Sunday. This is a new era,” McCarthy said. “They have a new coach, and we have a new coach. We had our first game together in Cleveland, and it was a tough battle. I’m looking forward to getting it on again.”

full_text: (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have been connected to trade talks by multiple NFL insiders. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler noted that Pittsburgh, along with the Kansas City Chiefs are two teams to keep an eye on as it pertains to a trade for Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. And now, Jason La Canfora has named Los Angels Chargers wide receiver Ladd McConkey as a potential target for Pittsburgh. “After decades of operating as a conservative front office, the Steelers are wheeler-dealers now,” La Canfora writes . “One scout suggested to me that someone like Chargers wideout Ladd McConkey might be the kind of target Rodgers would enjoy throwing to to help sustain drives. Brian Thomas Jr. of the Jaguars is another name to keep an eye on.” McConkey has seen his production take a step back in both 2025, and thus far in 2026, as compared to his terrific rookie season in 2024. In five games this season, he has just 13 receptions on an 0-6 Chargers team. In 2025, his reception total dipped down to 66 catches from 82 receptions in 2024. Considering where the Chargers are right now, it would make sense to see them sell ahead of the trade deadline. McConkey splits time on the perimeter and in the slot. So far in 2026, about 53 percent of his snaps have come o the perimeter with 46 percent of snaps in the slot, and the remaining snaps have him line up inline. Should Pittsburgh want to bring McConkey into their receiving corps, it would give them another player who is boundary and slot versatile, while also adding a 1,000-yard receiver to the group. title: Steelers Week 8 power rankings roundup: Three straight wins earns Pittsburgh respect
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the New Orleans Saints 16-10 in the NFL’s first game in Paris on Sunday. The Steelers looked in control from start to finish. Only three points were scored in the second half, and the Steelers improved to 5-2 as they prepare for a date with the 5-2 Cleveland Browns for sole […]
full_text: (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers defeated the New Orleans Saints 16-10 in the NFL’s first game in Paris on Sunday. The Steelers looked in control from start to finish. Only three points were scored in the second half, and the Steelers improved to 5-2 as they prepare for a date with the 5-2 Cleveland Browns for sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Let’s take a look around the internet and see how the rest of the NFL world views Pittsburgh after three straight wins in this week’s power rankings roundup. FOX Sports: No. 13 (No. 15 Last Week) “It’s probably time I stopped underestimating the Steelers, who have won three straight now and have only been out of one game this season in the final minutes. They win ugly and their 42-year-old QB is a shell of his old self, but give Mike McCarthy credit. Pittsburgh finds ways to win. And the emergence of RB Jaylen Warren as a legitimate two-way weapon has been huge for a team that needs to carry Rodgers more than he can carry them. It would be a big boost for the Steelers if they can beat the Browns at home next Sunday and stay atop the AFC North heading into their bye.” – Ralph Vacchiano The Athletic: No.13 (Last Week No.16) “After a horrendous start, the Steelers rank 10th in EPA per play since Week 3. Rodgers made some impressive throws in the win over the Saints, and the offense converted 10 of 16 third downs. Things are looking up in the Steel City.” – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall CBS Sports: No.14 (Last Week No. 17) “It hasn’t always been pretty, but they find ways to win games. They are tied for first place in the division.” – Pete Prisco Pro Football Talk: No.10 (Last Week No. 13) “Sunday’s home game against Cleveland is the closest thing to a “must” win that any 5-2 team will ever have.“ -Mike Florio NFL.com: No.14 (Last Week No.17) “Like with the Falcons, I’m having a difficult time discounting the Steelers. Yes, they defeated another NFC South team by a slim margin, but the promising developments seen on tape are becoming undeniable. The key difference: Aaron Rodgers’ willingness to accept Mike McCarthy’s in-game adjustments and execute them as intended. In the Week 6 win at Tampa Bay, they shifted to a shorter passing game. In Sunday’s Paris win over New Orleans, they decided it was best to ride with both Darnell Washington and Pat Freiermuth on the field at the same time, eliminating their early predictability. Rodgers even scrambled for a first down late, which made me feel like I had entered a time machine. Instead, it was just another victory for the 2026 Steelers, who have enough to continue winning in this fashion and don’t seem interested in going away.” – Nick Shook Yahoo! Sports: No.14 (Last Week No. 16) “Four of the Steelers’ wins have come against losing teams (combined record: 9-19). They have won only one game by more than seven points, but they also have a victory over the Bengals and at some point it doesn’t matter who the Steelers have beaten. They’re 5-2 and going to be in playoff contention all season. They’re making just enough plays, like they did to beat the 2-5 Saints on Sunday.” “What might keep the Steelers going is the running back combination of Jaylen Warren, who has emerged as one of the best playmakers at the position this season, and Rico Dowdle, one of the best backups in the league. They had 223 of Pittsburgh’s 343 yards on Sunday.” “Anytime we can just line up and give you Jaylen and Rico all day, that’s a good day for us,” “Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said, according to the team’s site.” – Frank Schwab USA Today: No.16 (Last Week No.18) “Sometimes you’ve got to suck it up and make a play for your guys,” “QB Aaron Rodgers said of his 8-yard run for a first down in the final minutes of Sunday’s game, a scramble that pretty much buried the Saints.” “I think because I am so much less athletic than I used to be, it actually fires up the guys even more.” “On that play, the 42-year-old four-time league MVP also outrushed every single New Orleans player Sunday.” – Nate Davis ESPN: No.14 (Last Week No. 17) “Both of the Steelers’ starting cornerbacks, Samuel and Jamel Dean, have made big plays this season. But Samuel has turned a modest one-year, $4 million deal into a solidified role. Part of the reason Pittsburgh was comfortable trading cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to Dallas was because of Samuel, who has parlayed a stellar offseason into seven pass deflections through seven games. He has successfully rebuilt his career after undergoing spinal fusion surgery in April 2025.” – Jeremy Fowler Slowly but surely, the Steelers are climbing up the power rankings after three straight wins. Although Pittsburgh is 5-2, they have beaten the Colts, Buccaneers, and Saints, all of whom are among the bottom 10 in the majority of these rankings. It will be interesting to see how high the Steelers move up in the ranks if they are able to capture sole possession of first place of the AFC North this weekend with a win over Cleveland. title: Week 8 odds: The Steelers open as slight favorites vs. Browns
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have a chance to take over first place in the AFC North with a win over the Cleveland Browns on Sunday. full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have a chance to take over first place in the AFC North with a win over the Cleveland Browns on Sunday. This is the second meeting between the division rivals, with Pittsburgh looking to avenge a loss from the first meeting. The first meeting went down to the wire in Cleveland, and things are different for both teams ahead of the second matchup. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Steelers open up as 3.5 point favorites at home. Vegas believes the game will be a defensive struggle, with the over/under set at 39.5. The Steelers moneyline is set at -198. The Browns have won two straight over Pittsburgh, but both matchups were in Cleveland. Each game was won by one possession. The last regular-season win in Pittsburgh for the Browns happened in 2003. However, the biggest win came in 2020 in the AFC Wild Card round, with Baker Mayfield and the Browns prevailing 48-37. In fact, the 2003 victory is the only regular-season win for Cleveland at Acrisure Stadium. The Steelers have won 12 straight at home against Cleveland, but have dropped five straight in Cleveland. The rivalry is still in Pittsburgh’s favor with an 83-66-1 record over the Browns. The Steelers’ run defense will have to remain stingy as Quinshon Judkins returned from injury last week and went over 100 rushing yards against Tennessee. The run defense is the seventh-best in the NFL, allowing 91 rushing yards per game and four rushing touchdowns on the season. Meanwhile, the Browns run defense is vulnerable with 116.4 rushing yards allowed per game and four touchdowns allowed. Sticking with the hot hand of Jaylen Warren should be the game plan for Pittsburgh. Rico Dowdle has been involved, and it’s clear Mike McCarthy wants to get back to a rotation at running back. With the wide receiver injuries, expect both to be on the field at the same time. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Steelers news: How real is the Steelers’ 5-2 start?
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have won three straight games and, through seven weeks, have a record of 5-2, which is good for a tie for first place, but a second-place spot based on tiebreakers with the Cleveland Browns. The next two games are against AFC North opponents, with Cleveland and Cincinnati on the schedule. The best-case […]
full_text: (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have won three straight games and, through seven weeks, have a record of 5-2, which is good for a tie for first place, but a second-place spot based on tiebreakers with the Cleveland Browns. The next two games are against AFC North opponents, with Cleveland and Cincinnati on the schedule. The best-case scenario is winning both games. The NFL media is whispering about the Steelers’ five-game win start and wondering if this is real and sustainable. The idea that the Steelers have been in tough games with perceived “inferior” opponents signaling weakness is a flawed argument. Wins are wins. This isn’t college football. The Steelers defense is tough. The offense has playmakers and does enough to win games. Playing complementary football shouldn’t be perceived as a weakness. Winning in the NFL is hard, and the league is as parity-driven as it has been in years. Keep winning games and let analysts and pundits doubt. It’s always better to almost lose than to almost win. title: Quenton Nelson trade: How it affects the Seahawks 2027 draft capital
summary: The Seattle Seahawks have pulled off yet another major midseason trade under John Schneider, acquiring perennial Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts. Pending a physical, the Seahawks will give up a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder. Not bad for someone who’s long been at the top of his position and […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks have pulled off yet another major midseason trade under John Schneider, acquiring perennial Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts . Pending a physical, the Seahawks will give up a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder. Not bad for someone who’s long been at the top of his position and still remains among the very best guards in the NFL. You’re probably wondering how this affects Seattle’s 2027 draft capital, as giving up a Round 1 or Day 2 pick is one of those things that can make a fanbase uneasy no matter who the trade is for. Well, I have great news on the draft front. Seahawks current native 2027 draft picks Round 1 Round 2 Round 5 Round 7 They lost their 2027 fourth-rounder to the Cleveland Browns to get Beau Stephens , while their sixth-rounder belongs to the Los Angeles Chargers from the Avery Smith trade . Their native third-round pick is going to the Colts in the Nelson trade. Only four native picks? Boo. But wait! This is where things get fun! Seahawks tentative additional 2027 draft picks Round 3 ( Nolan Teasley comp pick ) Round 4 ( Boye Mafe projected comp pick ) Round 5 ( Kenneth Walker projected comp pick ) Round 5 ( Riq Woolen projected comp pick ) Round 6 ( Coby Bryant projected comp pick ) Round 7 ( conditional pick from Michael Jerrell trade ) There’s actually a small chance the Walker comp pick becomes a fourth-rounder, which we’ll explain at another time. Otherwise, there’s a reason why John Schneider hoarded as many comp picks as possible during free agency. If Seattle wanted to make a trade or two at the deadline, they wouldn’t be put in a situation where they enter a stronger draft class (on paper) with a paucity of picks. Seattle tentatively has 10 draft picks and still have skin in the game in all seven rounds. Perhaps they’re not done making major roster moves with two weeks to go until the deadline, but the Seahawks have the best of both worlds: they are well stocked for April, and they’re stocking up for their latest Super Bowl push.

title: Seahawks roster update: ‘Hard Knocks’ star back on practice squad
summary: After injuries to wide receivers Rashid Shaheed and Velus Jones Jr., the Seattle Seahawks are adding a pair of pass catchers to their practice squad, including “Hard Knocks” star Montorie Foster Jr. The Seahawks announced that wideouts Malick Meiga and Foster joined the team’s practice squad on Tuesday, with fullback Jackson Acker and linebacker Josh […]
full_text: After injuries to wide receivers Rashid Shaheed and Velus Jones Jr., the Seattle Seahawks are adding a pair of pass catchers to their practice squad, including “Hard Knocks” star Montorie Foster Jr. The Seahawks announced that wideouts Malick Meiga and Foster joined the team’s practice squad on Tuesday, with fullback Jackson Acker and linebacker Josh Ross released to make room for the duo. Foster, a fan-favorite who balled out in the preseason, made the Seahawks 53-man roster, but was a healthy scratch in the team’s first six games. The undrafted wide receiver was waived to make room for Anthony Bradford’s return ahead of last week’s game against the Kansas City Chiefs and now returns to the Seahawks to hopefully boost their wide receiver depth. Meiga, a Coastal Carolina product, is an undrafted rookie who spent time with Seattle last month after he spent training camp with the Carolina Panthers. The Montreal native was released by the team on Oct. 19 and returns just over a week later. The practice squad reshuffling comes ahead of the Seahawks’ Monday night contest against the Chicago Bears, who will be keyed into slowing down star Jaxon Smith-Njigba after his monster game against the Chiefs.
author: Jack Freeman

title: Seahawks trade for 6-time All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson in massive move
summary: The Seattle Seahawks have just made a major investment in their offensive line, and they’ve swung big at the trade deadline once again. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that the Seahawks have agreed to send a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder to the Indianapolis Colts for 8x Pro Bowl, 6x All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson. […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks have just made a major investment in their offensive line, and they’ve swung big at the trade deadline once again. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that the Seahawks have agreed to send a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder to the Indianapolis Colts for 8x Pro Bowl, 6x All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson. The headline originally said 8-time All-Pro in an error which we have absolutely no regrets over due to the insanely exciting nature of the story. Compensation update; The Seahawks are sending a 2027 third-round pick and 2028 fifth-round round pick to the Colts in exchange for Quenton Nelson. https://t.co/17B0bR47yV — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 27, 2026 The 30-year-old Nelson is on an expiring contract, so not unlike the Leonard Wiliams trade a few years ago , or the Rashid Shaheed trade last season , John Schneider is using Day 2 and Day 3 draft capital to land a major trade deadline name. We can worry about Nelson’s contract at another time, because the now is that Seattle has upgraded at guard in a humongous deal. Nelson has spent his entire career as an elite pass protector and run blocker at left guard, so this could possibly result in Grey Zabel moving to right guard while Nelson slots in at his most comfortable position. Zabel can play on either side and just hasn’t had the need to switch yet. What this means for starting right guard Anthony Bradford remains to be seen, but by default someone is about to lose their starting job at guard. With the Indianapolis Colts headed for a rebuild, firing general manager Chris Ballard midseason and promoting former Seahawks executive Ed Dodds to interim GM, there’s a natural connection between Schneider and Dodds. This is exactly the type of move that could elevate the Seahawks offense both in the pass and run game.

title: Former Seahawks Boye Mafe, Riq Woolen trending in opposite directions with new teams
summary: The Seattle Seahawks defense is still as fearsome and suffocating as ever, even though they lost three key contributors in free agency. Cornerback Riq Woolen went to the Philadelphia Eagles on a one-year deal, edge rusher Boye Mafe inked a three-year contract with the Cincinnati Bengals, and safety Coby Bryant signed his own three-year deal […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks defense is still as fearsome and suffocating as ever, even though they lost three key contributors in free agency. Cornerback Riq Woolen went to the Philadelphia Eagles on a one-year deal, edge rusher Boye Mafe inked a three-year contract with the Cincinnati Bengals, and safety Coby Bryant signed his own three-year deal with the Chicago Bears. With Bryant shelved for potentially the entire season due to a knee injury, that leaves Mafe and Woolen as the notable ex-Seahawks from the Super Bowl defense who’ve been getting snaps on other rosters. Through the first two months of the regular season, Mafe and Woolen’s teams are trending in opposite directions, and their respective performances match the trends. If Mafe was thought to be a solid pass rusher whose sack productivity was not consistent in Seattle, he’s making his presence felt in a revamped Bengals defense. Here’s a report from Cincy Jungle’s Jason Garrison following the Bengals’ blowout win over the Baltimore Ravens. Boye Mafe In a matchup that was set up as a “Trey Hendrickson Revenge” game, it was Boye Mafe who made all the noise. The Bengals did a good job of keeping Hendrickson away from Burrow, often lending Orlando Brown Jr. help. The Ravens, on the other hand, were incapable of keeping Mafe out of the backfield. He ended up with two sacks, but was chasing Huntley around often. Boye Mafe with the sack to force a punt. We forgive you Trey. pic.twitter.com/cx9CCFXu0Y — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026 Mafe and Cook combining for the sack with the Bengals up 21-13 to force a Ravens punt in the 4th. pic.twitter.com/1Hxi1wn8tM — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 26, 2026 Mafe has 4.5 sacks, six quarterback hits, a forced fumble, a fumble recovery, and (per NextGenStats) a career-best 17.6% pressure rate. His 14 quick QB pressures—these are pressures inside of 2.5 seconds—matches his 2025 total and in almost half the snaps of his final season in Seattle. The Bengals are 4-2 and have a super favorable schedule to return to the playoffs. Cincinnati’s defense may not be elite yet, but it’s no longer a laughing stock, which goes a long way toward helping Joe Burrow and the Bengals offense. Mafe has been a major contributor to the turnaround. The same cannot be said for the Philadelphia Eagles and Riq Woolen. Philadelphia’s once elite defense has sharply fallen, and Monday night’s 38-21 loss against the Dallas Cowboys exemplified the collapse of Vic Fangio’s unit to (at best) mediocre. Philadelphia’s secondary is collectively struggling, and after a strong start to the season, Woolen’s “prove-it” deal is steadily turning south. From Bleeding Green Nation’s Joseph Santoliquito : Riq “Reek” Woolen had himself a game. He completely lost CeeDee Lamb with 12 seconds left in the first half for a 30-yard completion to the Eagles’ nine-yard line. Woolen was fortunate Lamb lost his balance and had to crawl out of bounds. The Cowboys had to settle for an Aubrey 27-yard field goal (3 points thanks to Woolen) . The Cowboys scored on four of five drives in the first half. Woolen ran away from adversity, he declined to speak after the game. Woolen did not have a good game. On a third-and-nine on the Cowboys’ first drive of the second half, he was flagged for holding, giving the Cowboys a new set of downs. He was later burned on the same drive by Ryan Flournoy for a 16-yard completion on a first-and-10 to the Eagles’ 27. On the same drive, Woolen was smoked by Lamb in the corner of the end zone for a 16-yard touchdown and a 28-21 Cowboys’ lead with 1:30 left in the third quarter (11 points thanks to Woolen after Prescott’s two-point conversion). Woolen was “credited” with 111 yards allowed when targeted, one of the worst performances of his career. Big pickup down the sideline for Ryan Flournoy DALvsPHI on ESPN⁰Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/zZLwkf9ZON — NFL (@NFL) October 27, 2026 Hard to get more wide open than CeeDee Lamb here DALvsPHI on ESPN⁰Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/dv18lWu4Hw — NFL (@NFL) October 27, 2026 DAK TO LAMB AGAIN pic.twitter.com/q2XMsj12Mv — Tom Downey (@WhatGoingDowney) October 27, 2026 Riq Woolen declined to speak to reporters in the postgame locker room. “Appreciate you all, as always. Y’all have a good night, get home safely as well.” #Eagles — EJ Smith (@EJSmith94) October 27, 2026 Woolen only allowed five catches for 45 yards in Weeks 1-3. Over his last four games he’s given up 17 catches (on 27 targets) for 296 yards and 2 touchdowns. And lest you think his issues with penalties have subsided, he’s been flagged six times for pass interference, illegal contact, or defensive holding. Woolen leads the Eagles in penalties committed. We’ve discussed to death the impact of Kenneth Walker on the Kansas City Chiefs, but on the defensive side of the ball we’ve seen that the performance of the cornerback room has not dropped off since Woolen’s departure. The edge rushing group probably could use Mafe right now given how much has been put on the plates of Derick Hall, DeMarcus Lawrence, and Uchenna Nwosu this season, but at $20 million/year he was highly unlikely to be retained. While Mafe is prepping for a playoff push in Cincinnati, the Eagles could face a fire sale, and it wouldn’t be surprising at this point if Woolen is a potential trade piece as their disastrous season shows no signs of being recoverable.

title: 49ers News: Welcome back, DeForest Buckner!
summary: This moves me. I especially like the mentorship angle about this move. There’s a lot of young defensive linemen on this team that could really benefit from elite peer wisdom.  Kawakami: Adding DeForest Buckner might be just the start of the 49ers’ trade action (paywall)“They’re almost certainly checking in on the Raiders’ Maxx Crosby and […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - JANUARY 19: DeForest Buckner #99 of the San Francisco 49ers heads to the sideline after recovering a fumble during the game against the Green Bay Packers at Levi's Stadium on January 19, 2020 in Santa Clara, California. The 49ers defeated the Packers 37-20. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images This moves me. I especially like the mentorship angle about this move. There’s a lot of young defensive linemen on this team that could really benefit from elite peer wisdom. Kawakami: Adding DeForest Buckner might be just the start of the 49ers’ trade action (paywall) “They’re almost certainly checking in on the Raiders’ Maxx Crosby and the Chargers’ Khalil Mack, among others; and hey, if you’ve got a good edge rusher you might let go for a third-round pick, give Lynch a call. He’ll pick up the phone. I guarantee it. If he hasn’t already dialed you up 10 or 20 times. Sitting at 6-1 and in great playoff position heading into the bye, in the 10th year of the Shanahan/Lynch reign, the 49ers are moving all-in. You could feel the momentum for this gaining inside team HQ for weeks, and now it’s here.” The 49ers have traded for DeForest Buckner “The move for Buckner allows players like Valdez and Odighizuwa to become role players. It takes some off Gracen Halton’s plate. The pecking order and domino effect should make everybody better. Plus, the Buckner is used to playing against double teams. In the first month of the season, Buckner was double-teamed on 36.4% of his pass rushes. That’s a number that’s actually down from 49.5%. That’s because Buckner has aligned at 5-technique or wider on 13.3% of his snaps, the highest rate since he entered the league. Through the first four weeks of the season, Buckner recorded three sacks, which was tied for the second-most among interior defensive linemen. What sets Buckner apart is his ability to turn pressures into sacks. Per Next Gen Stats, Buckner was converting 30% of his pressures into sacks, which was the highest rate of any season for a defensive lineman since 2018. Theoretically, Buckner should see an increase in production with the number of times the 49ers use a 5-down front, not to mention having Nick Bosa on the field.” Colts trade DT DeForest Buckner to 49ers in another major move “Buckner, 32, is entering the final year of his deal with the Colts and is slated to become an unrestricted free agent after the season. Had Buckner signed this offseason with another team, the highest compensatory draft pick the Colts could have received was a 2028 fifth-round selection since he is an 11-year NFL veteran. With the trade, the Colts netted a 2027 fourth-round pick instead.” 49ers game review: Dre Greenlaw’s yelling points to screaming need for cornerback depth (paywall) “ Before the snap, Greenlaw was animatedly clapping his hands, telling Jones, who was playing left outside cornerback, to protect the left flat. Instead, Jones covered wide receiver Zachariah Branch, who ran a go route. The result: QB Michael Penix flipped a 19-yard completion to the all-alone Robinson. After Greenlaw tackled Robinson on the right sideline, he got up in balled-fist fury and began barking at Jones.” 49ers minutia minute: Brock Purdy didn’t complete a pass to a WR until the third quarter (paywall) “The 49ers had only seven missed tackles, though two of them were by Brown. He leads the team with seven missed tackles, one more than Warner and Greenlaw.” 49ers overreactions: Would trading for star left guard be most helpful? “The defensive line also is an area where the 49ers could look to add. The 49ers deploy a nine-man rotation along the D-line, so they never can have too many good players to cycle through during the course of a game.”

title: Kyle Shanahan details balance 49ers must strike at trade deadline
summary: The 49ers are almost certainly going to be buyers at the trade deadline and, if anything, their first defeat of the season at the hands of the Atlanta Falcons is likely to have increased the desire inside the organization to make a move that significantly boosts San Francisco’s Super Bowl chances. San Francisco sits at […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Head coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers looks on in the second quarter against the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 49ers are almost certainly going to be buyers at the trade deadline and, if anything, their first defeat of the season at the hands of the Atlanta Falcons is likely to have increased the desire inside the organization to make a move that significantly boosts San Francisco’s Super Bowl chances. San Francisco sits at 6-1 heading into its bye following a turnover-strewn performance in a 29-20 loss to the Atlanta Falcons, which illustrated the 49ers’ key areas of need as wide receiver Mike Evans’ absence proved telling and Raheem Morris’ defense struggled to produce pass rush after a couple of weeks excelling at getting after the quarterback. Wideout, interior defensive line and edge rusher could all be on the agenda for the 49ers at the trade deadline. But, having had so many injuries at receiver and on the defensive line, head coach Kyle Shanahan pointed out there is a balance the 49ers have to strike as they ponder what moves to make. Speaking on his Monday conference call, Shanahan said of potential trade activity: “That’s stuff, I know [president of football operations and general manager] John [Lynch] and our whole personnel department, they discuss that seven days a week for a long time right now. Just hearing more about things they’ve been doing on the plane last night, I’ll get to watch some stuff here now that I’m done with our team and we’ll be in contact over this next week. We still have two weeks for it. We still have the week when we get back, but if there’s stuff that makes sense that can improve our team in any spot, we’d love for that to happen. The obvious injury spots to us have been receiver and D-Line. We are getting a number of those guys back at both positions, but that also doesn’t exclude us from looking to something that would make sense to help us.” Asked if they have to consider the potential for future injuries when discussing trade plans, Shananhan replied: “Without a doubt, but that’s also the challenge of IR and how many people can return from IR. We were almost not able to field a 48-man team because we have guys who are hurt who are coming back that aren’t on IR. So that almost got us yesterday. When you trade and add players, that might make sense for one or two weeks, but then other guys come back, now you’ve got to cut people. So it’s got to make sense for all that. We would love to just stockpile some players in case some people get hurt going forward because the odds are people do, but that’s what the rules of this league with how many you can carry on a roster and things like that don’t allow you to stockpile players at the position. So, you’ve got to kind of see where you’re at and try to guess the future.” Striking a balance between protecting the team against further injuries while avoiding a situation where multiple players have to be cut is likely to be more difficult at receiver. Evans and Deebo Samuel will be back after the bye, and the Niners still have Demarcus Robinson and De’Zhaun Stribling to return from injured reserve. It’s difficult to see the 49ers wanting to cut more than one of Jordan Watkins, Christian Kirk or Jacob Cowing — with the later the most likely candidate to be let go — so San Francisco will have to be very calculated as they look at the avenues for receiver help. It should be a little easier on the defensive line. The 49ers have only eight healthy defensive linemen on the active roster and Khalid Kareem is an edge defender who, despite some very strong play against the run, they should be confident of sneaking back onto the practice squad. With C.J. West and Sam Okuayinonu the only candidates to return from injured reserve, there is scope for additions on the interior defensive line and on the edge. The good news is that, as Shanahan articulated, the 49ers have plenty of time before the Nov. 10 deadline. However, the Niners will likely want to get any new additions acclimated as quickly as possible. As the 49ers prepare to attempt to get back to winning ways after the bye, the difficult decisions on those trade calculations will likely be made in the very near future.
