title: Evaluating the 49ers’ defense during the bye week
summary: The San Francisco 49ers will enjoy their bye week with a 6-1 record and leading the NFC West. A loss to Atlanta was frustrating, but all things considered, the 49ers are in a great spot with one loss through seven weeks. The loss itself isn’t the end of the world, but it was frustrating, as […]
full_text: (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers will enjoy their bye week with a 6-1 record and leading the NFC West. A loss to Atlanta was frustrating, but all things considered, the 49ers are in a great spot with one loss through seven weeks. The loss itself isn’t the end of the world, but it was frustrating, as the 49ers had every opportunity to leave Atlanta with a win. Nobody expected the 49ers to go undefeated, and they will lose more games this season. If someone told you the 49ers would be 6-1 heading into their bye week, you would take that 10/10 times. The team will return impact players next week against the Raiders, potentially including Nick Bosa. Let’s take a look at the 49ers defense during the bye week. Overall defense rankings The 49ers rank fourth in the NFL, allowing 299.3 yards per game and 13 touchdowns on the season. Some would attribute the fine start to the opponents, but it’s clear this defense is a step or two above last season. Although Sunday was rough for the defensive line and pass rush, the overall body of work is impressive, with the 49ers on pace to shatter last season’s sack total. Passing defense Defending the pass has the 49ers slipping to number ten with 210.3 yards per game and ten passing touchdowns allowed. Still, a top-ten passing defense is excellent, and the secondary has room for improvement. Sunday saw Atlanta attack underneath more and take advantage of soft cushions and Cover 3 zones. The key to that working is generating pass rush up front. Renardo Green has been very good at times this season, and the safety room has turned into a strength with Malik Mustapha, Marques Sigle, and Ji’Ayir Brown all contributing well. The 49ers need more from Deommodore Lenoir and Upton Stout in coverage, but the opportunity to improve and become stingier is there. Rushing defense With a top-five run defense, the 49ers allow 89 rushing yards per game and just three touchdowns on the ground. Bosa’s return will only boost the run defense. As a run defender, Bosa has been underrated, and with Mykel Williams opposite him, the defense stands to be tougher against the run. Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw help clean up against the run as long as the big boys up front hold their blocks and allow the two linebackers to shoot running lanes and gaps. Scoring defense/third down defense/red zone defense The 49ers allow 19.9 points per game, which is good for the sixth-best defense. As far as third-down defense, the 49ers fall out of the top ten with a 37.9% third-down rate. Getting off the field has been an issue at times. Sometimes it is allowing an offense to convert, or, as we saw on Sunday, committing penalties that allow drives to continue. Red zone defense sees the 49ers return to the top ten at number nine with a 47.8% red zone touchdown rate. The top two defenses in the red zone are Minnesota at 23.1% and Kansas City at 26.7%. The 49ers face both teams in 2026. What do you think about the 49ers’ defense in 2026? Are you concerned about one area or many? Let us know in the comments!

title: John Lynch on the 49ers potentially changing kickers: ‘We have a lot of belief in Eddy’
summary: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan was asked if the team would have kicker tryouts after Eddy Pineiro missed another extra point on Sunday. Shanahan said, “I haven’t discussed it with guys. I haven’t been told that we are. I actually just finished with the team and just finished with the quarterbacks and came […]
full_text: (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan was asked if the team would have kicker tryouts after Eddy Pineiro missed another extra point on Sunday. Shanahan said, “I haven’t discussed it with guys. I haven’t been told that we are. I actually just finished with the team and just finished with the quarterbacks and came in here. As far as I’ve heard, we don’t have any plans on that right now.” On KNBR Tuesday morning, John Lynch said, “We don’t have a kicker tryout,” echoing Shanahan. Lynch continued: “We have a lot of belief in Eddy. He has had a tough run early this year, but we extended Eddy for his body of work with us but then throughout the history of his career. He’s going through a rough patch right now. We have belief in Eddy, and we’re going to ride with him.” A financial factor is part of the decision to keep Pineiro. The 49ers owe him $4 million in guaranteed salary in 2027. That’s the final year of guaranteed money in Pineiro’s contract. So, unless he leaves them with no choice, Pineiro will be the 49ers’ kicker through 2027. Pineiro built equity after a near-perfect 2025 season. He still has a little grace to give, but he’s running out of rope, and the tone could change if he misses a game-deciding kick.

full_text: (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Indianapolis Colts’ fire sale has begun. Unfortunately, they are giving the Seattle Seahawks one of the NFL’s best guards. Eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson is headed to the Seahawks. Nelson, who is on an expiring contract, was traded for a 2027 3rd-round pick and a 2028 5th-round pick. That’s a cheap deal, regardless of whether you feel like you can re-sign Nelson. He’s 30, so you’d think Nelson has at least four more years of high-level play. That’s the same deal the San Francisco 49ers made for Trent Williams. The Seahawks are set to have a handful of compensatory picks in the next draft after losing Boye Mafe, Kenneth Walker, Tariq Woolen, and Coby Bryant. Seattle also gets a third-rounder after executive Nolan Teasley became the Vikings general manager. So, in their minds, this is a no-brainer. It was the kind of move we had briefly discussed the 49ers making. Nelson would have been a massive upgrade from Connor Colby at left guard. You’re never looking to counter a trade for a trade, but it would make even more sense for the Niners to trade for DeForest Buckner, a player they were linked to on Monday. League wide expectation is the #49ers will respond next after the #Seahawks acquisition of Quenton Nelson. The NFC West is about to heat up in a big way. — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) October 27, 2026 Would you have made this trade if you were John Lynch? Will the 49ers answer with a trade of their own? Let us know in the comments below.

title: Kyle Shanahan on the 49ers’ corrections: ‘When you make a dumb mistake, you don’t need much discussion on how to correct it’
summary: Turnovers and self-inflicted mistakes defined the San Francisco 49ers’ Week 7. Their win probability plummeted over 41% with four turnovers in plus territory. Head coach Kyle Shanahan was asked whether the team discussed corrections at halftime or after the game. Shanahan said: “When you make a dumb mistake, you don’t need much discussion on how […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Turnovers and self-inflicted mistakes defined the San Francisco 49ers’ Week 7. Their win probability plummeted over 41% with four turnovers in plus territory. Head coach Kyle Shanahan was asked whether the team discussed corrections at halftime or after the game. Shanahan said: “When you make a dumb mistake, you don’t need much discussion on how to correct it. You try not to do dumb things. At halftime we definitely stated that. We’ve got to protect the ball better, which I don’t necessarily look at that as a dumb mistake. Guys in this league are really good at the peanut punch and knocking that ball out, and they got us in two bad plays on that, and our guys have got to protect the ball. There’s no excuse on that. That’s the challenge of anyone who carries the ball in this league: how hard it is to hold it, and they got us twice on it, which is huge. But, the biggest part was our defense stopped them and held them to fourth down and then we had a dumb jump offsides penalty, which yeah, it was talked about. I think everyone knows it was that way, so it didn’t have to be really overstated. Then the second half, we had those two picks, and we had put ourselves in a hole, and we couldn’t have those. I think our guys know the mistakes we made. Anytime you have four turnovers to zero, it’s really hard to win in this league. I still think we could have overcame it, especially at the end with our defense getting those two stops, but you can’t overcome it when you throw a pick there on third down.” The 49ers had a puncher’s chance in this game despite seemingly everything going wrong. This season, there was no evidence Black would put the ball on the ground. If it were happening in practice, Black probably wouldn’t get more carries in Week 1 than Christian McCaffrey. You don’t expect your All-Pro tight end to cough up the ball, even in a two-possession game with a little more than a minute left. You’re comfortable putting the ball in your quarterback’s hands because he came into Week 7 with a 1.2% interception rate, despite having the fourth-highest yards per attempt in the NFL. Brock Purdy threw as many interceptions against the Falcons as he did in the first six games. There’s little to correct in that regard.

title: Week 8 NFL Power Rankings: Have the 49ers have fallen from the top rank?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are undefeated no more, as they fell 29-20 to the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, dropping to 6-1 heading into the bye week. It was not a pretty game by any means for the 49ers, who dealt with too many penalties and turnovers that took the game out of their hands. Still, […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 25: San Francisco wide receiver Jordan Watkins (17) fumbles the ball on a play that was later ruled as an incomplete pass during the NFL game between the San Francisco 49ers and the Atlanta Falcons on October 25th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are undefeated no more, as they fell 29-20 to the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, dropping to 6-1 heading into the bye week. It was not a pretty game by any means for the 49ers, who dealt with too many penalties and turnovers that took the game out of their hands. Still, it was an outing where San Francisco was quite beaten up, even forcing them to play without the regular number of players on game day. In the weekly power rankings, the 49ers have been mainstays at the top spot for weeks. However, after a loss, they’ve finally fallen from the top rank in some places. Here are the Week 8 NFL Power Rankings and where the 49ers stand among the consensus. ESPN Interestingly enough, ESPN’s power rankings is one of the lone spots that kept the 49ers at No. 1, even after the loss. The Buffalo Bills moved up one spot to No. 2 behind them. So did the Minnesota Vikings to No. 3, while the Kansas City Chiefs fell from No. 2 to No. 4 after losing to the Seattle Seahawks. Seattle, even at 4-3, rounded things out at No. 5. Rounding out the top ten were the Jacksonville Jaguars, Chicago Bears, Denver Broncos, Cincinnati Bengals, and New England Patriots. FOX Sports After being at No. 1, FOX Sports’s Ralph Vacciano dropped San Francisco all the way to No. 5 in his latest power rankings. “I admittedly feel a little bad about dropping the 49ers this far against a Falcons team that has been impressive at times over the past few weeks, especially since I still suspect this is the best team in football — you know, in those rare moments when they’re mostly healthy,” Vacciano wrote. “But there’s no avoiding the reality that they are incredibly banged up, and they added RB Christian McCaffrey to their injury list with a calf injury. Mostly, though, I’m concerned about this: They’ve turned the ball over eight times in the past three games, including four on Sunday. They’re too good to be that careless with the ball.” Ahead of the 49ers are the Denver Broncos (No. 4), Kansas City Chiefs (No. 3), Minnesota Vikings (No. 2), and Buffalo Bills (No. 1). CBS Sports In Pete Prisco’s power rankings, the 49ers dropped, but not too far, as they moved down to No. 3 after the loss. “They lost for the first time this season at Atlanta, and it was four turnovers that did them in Sunday,” Prisco wrote. “They head to their bye in need of key players getting healthy when they return.” Here, only the Minnesota Vikings, who remain undefeated, and the Buffalo Bills were ahead of the 49ers, while the Chiefs and Bengals remained behind San Francisco. Yahoo Sports Here, even with the loss, Yahoo Sports’s Frank Schwab still has the 49ers as the No. 1 team in the NFL. “The bye is coming at a good time for the 49ers. One of the reasons Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel Sr., Nick Bosa and others might have been inactive Sunday was because the bye would give them an extra week of rest before their return. Niners tight end George Kittle was unwilling to use the injuries as an excuse for the loss to the Falcons.” “It’s the NFL, injuries happen,” Kittle told NBC Sports Bay Area. “It’s just how much depth do you have, how many vets do you have that can stay healthy that can like continue to keep the elevation, like the standard of play up, you know, that’s all that really matters.” Overall, the Niners are still considered, at worst, a top-five team with their rough loss on Sunday, and now get the bye week to regroup and regain some key pieces from injury.

Three edge rushers played over 30 snaps: Romello Height (38), Keion White (35), and Mykel Williams (31). The edge group had zero tackles for loss. Mykel missed a pair of tackles. He had one pressure. Keion had two. Romello had zero, but he and Williams both had run stops. They bottled up Bijan Robinson, who had only one 10+ yard run, but they still moved off the ball more than usual. Robinson had 19 yards before contact, and Khalil Herbert had four on two carries.”

title: Should the Buccaneers upgrade at punter?
summary: A year and seven games into his Tampa Bay Buccaneers tenure it is a fair question to ask— Do the Buccaneers have a Riley Dixon problem? Dixon is currently playing out the final year of his two-year, six million dollar contract and despite being in a contract year the Bucs’ punter has done anything but […]
full_text: TAMPA, FL - DECEMBER 11: Riley Dixon #9 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers looks on from the sideline during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game against the Atlanta Falcons at Raymond James Stadium on December 11, 2025 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images A year and seven games into his Tampa Bay Buccaneers tenure it is a fair question to ask— Do the Buccaneers have a Riley Dixon problem? Dixon is currently playing out the final year of his two-year, six million dollar contract and despite being in a contract year the Bucs’ punter has done anything but improve or play to standard. Dixon was, once upon on a time, a promising and exciting punting prospect heralded as a savior for Tampa Bay’s punting woes following a 2024 campaign that cycled punters like a merry-go-round. Dixon has not been the stabilizing force that Jason Licht and co. anticipated he could be. In his first season with the Bucs, he averaged 44.7 yards per punt, the second-lowest of his career to that point. The performance was lacking, however, Dixon was able to escape large quantities of blame because the entire Tampa Bay special teams unit was largely poor (with exception of the group’s shining star, Chase McLaughlin). Inside of the Buccaneers’ sweeping changing to their coaching staff this offseason, the Bucs addressed that the unit had been bad. The fix was bringing in long-time special teams coach Danny Smith. Smith’s 30+ years of coaching experience was supposed to be difference for Tampa Bay. The Buccaneers, as a team, have been mostly bad in 2026, but their special teams has not. Danny Smith’s group has been largely improved. Not only has Chase McLaughlin remained the best individual player on Tampa Bay’s roster (he’s possibly gotten even better this season, 16-16 on the year), but the team’s kick coverage, punt coverage, special teams tackling, and return game have all found more consistency in 2026 than any recent years prior— Dating back to the Bruce Arians era of football. This past week, in Tampa’s blowout win, special teams played a huge part. Not only was Danny Smith’s group responsible for a turnover, recovering a muffed punt, but they also scored points when Tykee Smith’s blocked extra point was taken back to the end zone by Zyon McCollum for the score. The one area Tampa’s special teams has still not shown a consistent level of high-level play in is punting. Riley Dixon’s 44.7 yards per punt from a season ago, has actually dropped to 43.4— The worst of his career. Dixon is currently graded out as the league’s 29th-best punter ( 59.5 on pff ). His stats by individual category are all bottom 10 in the league and it is not based in a small sample size as Dixon has tallied the six most punts in the NFL this season (29). All signs would point to Dixon being unlikely to be brought back for a third season with the team following the 2026, but should a move come sooner than that? The 2026 Bucs are in a very weird position. The team is not good. They have not been good. They actually haven’t been a good team for roughly a full calendar year at this point. Still, they have a very legitimate opportunity to make the playoffs — The ineptitude of NFC South reigns supreme— The team, not only is in the hunt record-wise, but they just ran their division leader off their home field with a level of dominance that has to put the rest of South on notice. Excluding last season when they fell victim to the rare three-way tiebreaker; Tampa Bay has won the NFC South every year since 2021 and while the team’s been poor for about 11 months now, Sunday should serve as a reminder that the Buccaneers can easily win the NFC South if they could only ever consistently play to their own potential— Easier said than done these days in Tampa Bay. Whether it should be or not, if the team’s focus is on winning games down the stretch and pushing to have the best season they can have, then punting is a weak point that should be addressed. Yesterday, the New England Patriots released Bryce Baringer. Baringer is a punter, one who presents far more potential than Dixon. After a preseason injury, Baringer began the season on IR. The team moved on to Mitch Wishnowski who has played well enough in his stead to remain in place. That leaves Baringer, a punter whose average has never dipped below 46.9 yards in any one season, available. Baringer, who obviously has yet to compile stats for 2026, was the NFL’s 11-ranked punter according to PFF in 2025 with a 77.6. A year ago, things weren’t much different for Dixon than they are right now, his 59.5 was actually a good bit lower— 56.4. Punting is often an overlooked portion of the game, but field position, blocked punts, or failure to kick above replacement level can win or lose a team games. Dixon has been an ineffective player since joining the Buccaneers and if the team’s focus is on putting the best product on the field every week, discussions about his future should be prominent at One Buc Place.
author: Will Walsh

title: Who were the Titans’ 5 best players vs. Browns in Week 7?
summary: The Tennessee Titans were defeated 27-24 by the Cleveland Browns in Week 7. It was a disappointing loss in true heartbreak fashion, as the Browns emerged victorious via a walkoff field goal. It was a competitive showing by an improving Titans squad. We’ve identified five+ talented players who performed admirably versus the Browns. Tony Pollard, […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Carnell Tate #14 of the Tennessee Titans warms up prior to the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans were defeated 27-24 by the Cleveland Browns in Week 7 . It was a disappointing loss in true heartbreak fashion, as the Browns emerged victorious via a walkoff field goal. It was a competitive showing by an improving Titans squad. We’ve identified five+ talented players who performed admirably versus the Browns. Tony Pollard, RB Veteran running back Tony Pollard had one of the better days of his career . Pollard rushed for 129 yards and three touchdowns while averaging an effective 5.2 yards per attempt. The experienced ball-carrier consistently exposed creases for impactful gains against a stout Browns front seven. Offensive Line (Collectively) The offensive line deserves appreciation for how they generated those running lanes for Pollard. Furthermore, quarterback Cam Ward was sacked just once in protection. The run-blocking tape is an absolute joy to watch. Guys like JC Latham and Peter Skoronski continue to play high-level ball. Offensive line coach Carmen Bricillo has done a phenomenal job. Cor’Dale Flott, CB Cornerback Cor’Dale Flott is starting to play with confidence in Robert Saleh’s coverage scheme. He registered his second interception in as many games on Sunday. Flott’s interception versus the Colts was a picture-perfect example of playing zone coverage in Saleh’s scheme. The Deshaun Watson pick was a good play in man coverage. Carnell Tate, WR Rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate didn’t have a perfect afternoon. The fourth overall selection dropped a catchable pass from Cam Ward and also lost a keynote fumble on what would have been a sizable gain. Tate still had a strong showing, registering five receptions for 69 yards on a team-high seven targets. Anthony Hill Jr., LB Rookie linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. continues being a total revelation for the defense. The former Texas Longhorns standout finally forced his first turnover, stripping TE Harold Fannin Jr. of the football. Hill had another 12 total tackles versus the Browns, bringing his season-long total to 68.

title: Titans offense may have finally unlocked something with Tony Pollard
summary: The Tennessee Titans suffered a nailbiting loss to the Cleveland Browns, losing 27-24 in Week 7. Both the offense and defense squandered away opportunities to win a contest the Titans once led 14-0. Analyzing the bright side, it was arguably the offense’s best output of the campaign. The 24 points were the most the Titans […]
full_text: Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard (20) carries the ball during the first quarter against the Cleveland Browns at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Tenn., Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Tennessee Titans suffered a nailbiting loss to the Cleveland Browns , losing 27-24 in Week 7. Both the offense and defense squandered away opportunities to win a contest the Titans once led 14-0. Analyzing the bright side, it was arguably the offense’s best output of the campaign. The 24 points were the most the Titans offense has scored this season . They collectively scored 26 versus the Colts last weekend, but that included a blocked punt returned for a touchdown. Perhaps Brian Daboll and the offense unlocked something with Tony Pollard moving forward. The Titans rushed for 141 yards. It was arguably Pollard’s best performance in Tennessee. The veteran back rushed for 129 yards and three touchdowns. Pollard did that while averaging more than 5.0 yards per attempt. Pollard’s production removed some pressure from young quarterback Cam Ward. Ward still made a few mistakes, but he also made several big-time throws throughout the second half. Surely he appreciated leaning on Pollard. Entering Week 7, the Titans hadn’t run the football consistently. It was a breakout performance for Pollard in a game where Tyjae Spears and Nicholas Singleton were inactive. It’s worth remembering Pollard and the Titans’ run-game got things going in similar fashion down the stretch of last season. That offensive line also featured Dan Moore, Peter Skoronski, and JC Latham. Hopefully the offensive line will eventually get Fernando Carmona back. If Daboll’s unit continues running the football effectively, the offense could start scoring 20+ points consistently. They’ve failed to reach that scoring benchmark in four of seven games this season. The Titans absolutely should have defeated the Browns on Sunday. Pollard and the offensive line did enough to carry the offense to victory. Unfortunately, both the passing attack and defense let the Titans down in crucial moments. Hopefully the offense made progress though.

title: NFL trade deadline: Should Commanders have pushed for Quenton Nelson?
summary: The Colts traded superstar guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks on Tuesday for a 2027 third-round pick and a fifth-rounder in 2028, per multiple reports.   That’s a big deal. One of the top players on the trading block was moved well ahead of the NFL trade deadline, with decent compensation going to Indianapolis […]
full_text: The Colts traded superstar guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks on Tuesday for a 2027 third-round pick and a fifth-rounder in 2028, per multiple reports. That’s a big deal. One of the top players on the trading block was moved well ahead of the NFL trade deadline , with decent compensation going to Indianapolis for a player on an expiring contract. Trade! The Colts are sending eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports . pic.twitter.com/O1EN6vHWSF — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) October 27, 2026 Nelson has been an elite guard for his entire career, with eight Pro Bowls and three first-team All Pro honors to his credit. The Colts are in the tank and just fired their general manager , so a fire sale seems to be in the works. Nelson would provide an upgrade to most any team at left guard. It’s safe to count the Commanders in that group. The benefits of Nelson over Chris Paul would be massive and create an excellent interior offensive line alongside center Lucas Patrick and right guard Sam Cosmi. Should Commanders general manager Adam Peters have pushed harder to get Nelson? While Washington is 1-4-1, they’re somehow right in the thick of a sad NFC East title race . That would’ve been an aggressive move for a team with that record, but the schedule gets easier from here on out. Nelson could get this offense going. There’s no doubt about that. Our Mark Tyler made a pitch for the Commanders to make a move for Nelson, citing the guaranteed return in Nelson as compared to the suspect quality of Peters draft picks. Here’s an excerpt from Tyler’s Take (you can read the whole thing here : “It secures left guard (a position Washington has struggled to find consistency and solid play) for the foreseeable future. Nelson and Sam Cosmi give Washington arguably the league’s best guard tandem. With the return of Laremy Tunsil, the Commanders would have THREE Blues along the offensive line. Most importantly, he provides protection for Jayden Daniels and should make life easier in the rushing attack. Since he was drafted No. 2 overall in 2024, fans have literally BEGGED to surround Jayden with pieces, so he won’t have to play Superman every time he takes the field. Currently, through six weeks, Daniels is the most pressured quarterback in the NFL in time to throw. Trading for Nelson could help turn this around.” The Commanders have the cap space to offer an extension to Nelson, which surely would’ve been part of any trade proposal. Would you have made the same deal the Seahawks made? Let us know in the comments below:
author: Scott Bair

title: What impact Trey Amos can make on Washington Commanders secondary
summary: Trey Amos hasn’t played much football in the last calendar year.   The second-year Commanders cornerback fractured his fibula on Nov. 9, 2025, during a Week 10 contest against the Detroit Lions. He was placed on injured reserve and embarked on a long, arduous rehabilitation. It lasted through the offseason and into the summer, keeping […]
full_text: Trey Amos hasn’t played much football in the last calendar year. The second-year Commanders cornerback fractured his fibula on Nov. 9, 2025, during a Week 10 contest against the Detroit Lions. He was placed on injured reserve and embarked on a long, arduous rehabilitation. It lasted through the offseason and into the summer, keeping him away from practice even into training camp. He returned to practice on Aug. 7 , but was put back on the shelf the next day with soreness in the same ankle. He missed the rest of camp and was put on injured reserve on cut-down day, prolonging his absence well into the regular season. The Commanders eventually got him right, opened his practice window, and activated him before a Week 7 contest against the 49ers. Amos was clearly excited by the prospect, as he showed on Twitter. pic.twitter.com/KkpwzDXfh6 — Trenayvian❄️ (@TreyAmos01) October 15, 2026 And, with that single action, the Commanders secondary got a whole lot better. Washington’s most talented cornerback is finally back in the fray. He was on a pitch count against San Francisco, playing 36 snaps while splitting time with Rasul Douglas. He allowed two receptions for 25 yards on three targets , with two tackles to his credit. That was a good start to his second season. Every #Commanders CB Trey Amos coverage snap in his return to the NFL field for the first time in a year #RaiseHail https://t.co/ckFPy20OYj pic.twitter.com/Jx4Egke40R — Full Command (@FullCommandShow) October 21, 2026 “First off, man, was it awesome to have him back playing,” Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said during his Monday press conference . “You got from the time going through the spring, getting himself ready for training camp and then only to be out there for maybe a day or a day and a half or something quick to have a re-injury, that can take a toll on you.” “I’m telling you, one of the coolest things was there was no flinch in this competitor. And it’s easy to drift when you’re gonna be out for an extended period, and there just wasn’t. That’s why he was able to really step in and play quickly, just because he wouldn’t allow that drift to take place. And I’m certainly proud of him for that.” Amos’ return provides a huge boost, especially if he can return to full-time work. That would put him and Amik Robertson as full-time corners, with Rasul Douglas as the top reserve and a worker in the sub packages. That also pushes Mikey Sainristil largely out of the picture, a plus because he’s virtually unplayable at this point. The Commanders secondary has largely struggled, impactful only when the pass rush creates issues up front. Robertson has been a pleasant surprise and Douglas has been solid, but at times vulnerable. The safeties were a mess during Nick Cross’ three-game absence. He also returned in Week 6 and made an immediate impact. If Amos plays to his potential, the Commanders defense improves dramatically. Quinn was quick to point out the defensive backfield doesn’t need a savior. It needs quality play from the entire group. “But no, nobody has to put the cape on,” Quinn said. “We have to play like we’re capable of, for sure. But it definitely is a big deal for him to be back. We were close the week prior, but we knew, man, we want him back from here on. And we took a good first step with that.” What kind of impact can Trey Amos make on the Commanders secondary? Let us know in the comments below:

The NFC East is still a mess with the Giants holding a 1.5 game lead over the Cowboys who are one game ahead of the Eagles who they just beat on Monday Night Football. That leaves the Commanders at the bottom of the division, but they still have better odds of making the playoffs than Philadelphia. Jalen Hurts is out for the season due to blood clots in his lungs, and the reset year for the Eagles is in full effect. The Power Rankers are slightly higher on the Washington Commanders after their bye week, and a lack of head-scratching coaching/player decisions played a big factor in that. Washington’s schedule gets a lot easier after the break, and as long as Jayden Daniels is healthy they’ve got a shot in any game left on their schedule. The Giants are riding an adrenaline high from J.J. McCarthy, and the Cowboys took care of a reeling Eagles team. summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Commanders fans and fans across the country. full_text: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Commanders fans and fans across the country. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys: Now that the season is well underway, we’re continuing to ask the standard confidence question each week; that is, “Are you confident the Commanders are headed in the right direction?” We’ve been asking that question weekly from September to December for many years. With the Commanders’ record standing a 1-4-1 heading into Week 8, there is a bit of a “2020 season” feel to the situation, with a weak NFC East and upcoming winnable games against the 2-5 Eagles (who have lost 5 straight games) and the 3-4 Rams in Landover. The Commanders, if they win both games, could find themselves at 3-4-1 and still positioned to make a run at the NFC East title given the relatively weak remaining schedule and the Week 9 road game against the division-leading Giants, where a victory could see Washington at .500 overall and in the division. Typically, any team with just one win as the season approaches the halfway mark would be considered obvious “sellers” at the trade deadline, which is the Tuesday after the Rams game and before road trip to New York. But with the Eagles unraveling and the Giants & Cowboys looking nearly as vulnerable as the Commanders themselves, many have argued that Washington should use the trade deadline as an opportunity to build around Jayden Daniels — attempting to acquire players, not necessarily for a 2026 playoff run, but for 2026 and beyond. In today’s second question, we ask what you think GM Adam Peters should do as the November 10th trade deadline approaches. Comments & Results Of course, we invite you to answer the survey questions below, but also feel free to expand on your answers and provide nuance in the comments section. While you are certainly free to simply share which choices you made on the survey question, the most interesting comments will explain why you answered the way you did. I rely on those comments when discussing the results of the survey when they are posted in a separate article the next few days. Commanders fans: Make your pick in the SB Nation app! Take Reacts surveys, create Commanders polls, and see how your answers compare with fellow Hogs Haven fans. Then discuss the results with the Burgundy and Gold community. title: Commanders News – It’s time: Rachaad White needs to elevate his game
summary: The Daily Slop – 27 October 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Bullock’s Film Room […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 27: Rachaad White #1 of the Washington Commanders catches the ball during the first half against the Seattle Seahawks at Northwest Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Daily Slop – 27 October 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Commanders Film Review: Under Center Struggles [ Note : the play described in the excerpt below can be viewed in the video embedded in the tweet ] [S]ix games into the season, we’ve yet to really see a huge shift in under center usage. It’s definitely gone up compared to the past two years, but they are still in the bottom three in the NFL for under center usage rates so far this season. Now, part of that is the game situation. The Commanders have been behind in a lot of games this year, which naturally leads to the offense having to pass more and using the shotgun as a result. But part of the reason for the lack of under center usage is also its effectiveness. The Commanders started off the season with some nice looks from under center, but as the season has progressed it’s become less and less effective. So why is that and what can David Blough and the Commanders offense do to remedy that? Well first we need to look at what they were doing that worked at the start of the year. They entered the season with the intent to run the ball more from under center and lean into more of a wide zone run scheme. Early on, that had good results. As they went into their second game of the season against the Cowboys, we started to see Blough use some nice sequencing to set up play-action passes. [On] the run by White on the previous play, the Cowboys [kept] two safeties back deep. Their defensive coordinator comes from the Vic Fangio tree that likes to keep both safeties back deep when possible. However, due to the success of that run from that look earlier, you’ll notice on this play that while the Cowboys show two deep safeties initially, one of those safeties rotates down into the box late to help support the run. Keep that in mind as we dive into the passing concept now. The Commanders spent the whole offseason talking about getting under center more, but through six games they've not been able to get much production from those looks. I broke down their struggles: https://t.co/hNFhuLFXHh pic.twitter.com/5O0PVjeP1M — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) October 27, 2026 The Commanders run a play-action concept that is known as “Rider” in the Shanahan tree. On Rider, you have two main routes. To the left of the formation, Terry McLaurin runs a high cross, working to about 20 yards of depth as he crosses the middle of the field. On the other side, Treylon Burks runs a streak right down the seam. This combination is a great one to attack single-high safety coverages like the one the Cowboys play here. Remember my point earlier about how the Cowboys were forced out of their two deep safety structure with this look. It’s important now because this concept puts the single deep safety in conflict. Should he sink back and stay on top of the go route and risk giving up an easy throw underneath him, or should he attach to the high cross and risk giving up the shot over the top? In most situations, the deep safety sinks back and takes away the deepest route, which is the correct thing to do. However, as Jayden Daniels drops back to pass, he reads the safety and spots him playing shallow and opening his body to McLaurin’s route, indicating he’s looking to take over that route and cut it off. So Daniels immediately knows he has Burks on the go route and pulls the trigger. Unfortunately, Daniels puts just slightly too much on the pass and despite Burks making a full diving effort, the ball grazes his fingertips and falls incomplete. While the result might not have been what the Commanders would have wanted, that’s more down to the execution. If Daniels takes a yard off that throw, Burks has an uncontested 55-yard touchdown. The scheme was a good one from Blough and it was made even better by the set up. That’s what the best play callers do. They sequence their plays so they show a look early in the game, come back to it later to bait the defense into thinking it’s the same play, only to fool them with a twist. Despite that promising start, the effectiveness of the Commanders under center game has dropped off significantly. I believe that is in large part due to its predictability. When the Commanders get under center, they almost exclusively run the ball or use a play-action pass. There’s no pure drop back passing game of any sort from under center. In the offseason, I wrote about lessons Blough could learn from Ben Johnson’s first year in Chicago .One of those lessons was incorporating some drop back passing game from under center, but easing the quarterback into it. 1-on-1 with @kurt13warner : The Hall of Famer sees greatness in Jayden Daniels. That's why he wants the Commanders QB to rediscover the aggressive mentality that made him so dangerous as a rookie. What Warner sees on film — and what needs to change ⬇️ https://t.co/N76VtJvKMT pic.twitter.com/DZo6uXEsSk — Ben Standig (@BenStandig) October 26, 2026 Commanders Roundtable Three underperforming veterans need to deliver immediately RB Rachaad White With running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt placed on Injured Reserve, Rachaad White needs to step up in a major way, and so far, he simply has not. Through five games, White has managed just 145 yards on 36 carries (4.0 yards per carry) with no rushing touchdowns, alongside just 83 receiving yards. The former Tampa Bay Buccaneer was brought to Washington to serve as a reliable dual-threat out of the backfield, but his impact in the passing game has waned over time. After averaging 8.6 yards per reception in 2023 and 7.7 in 2024, his efficiency dropped to just 5.4 yards per catch last season. The offensive backfield struggles have been noticeable enough that the Commanders even brought back Austin Ekeler to help patch up the unit’s depth. While it is fair to acknowledge that White has been toughing it out through a shoulder injury, the expectation for a fifth-year veteran of his talent level remains much higher. Ultimately, White has no choice but to elevate his game: with the depth chart stretched thin, he is currently Washington’s RB1. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) Mailbag with Nicki Jhabvala It’s starting to feel a lot like 2020. The NFC East is a mess (again) and the Washington Commanders sit at the bottom of the division with one win in six games. And yet, they’re still in it — barely . The next few weeks could have a significant impact on Washington’s meager playoff hopes; primetime wins over the Eagles and Giants could keep the Commanders in contention, while more losses could all but end their season and amplify calls for a coaching change. (David) Blough is in over his head as OC. Wouldn’t it be wise to get an experienced offensive coordinator not working this year to help out? Even an out-of-work coach is better than this display of ineptitude. He has no clue in regard to misdirection, quick screens and blitz pickup to help (Daniels) out. Heck, bring back Joe Gibbs to give him some pointers on max protect and outlets for the blitz. — Gerald C. An out-of-work coach would be better? You sure? I’m willing to bet there’s a reason (or multiple reasons) those coaches are out of work. The offense certainly hasn’t blown me away, but I’m not sure I fully agree with your assessment, mainly because it’s impossible for outsiders to separate who or what is really at fault in many of these instances. It’s easy to run with a narrative, or an assumption that fits a…

After defeating Notre Dame and rising to #2 in the AP Poll, BYU lost on the road in overtime to UCF. Ole Miss fell from #7 after they could not pull off a comeback against #19 Texas. The #8 team in the country, Texas Tech, couldn’t keep up with Cincinnati, ultimately suffering a loss. In a ranked-on-ranked matchup, #10 Utah prevailed at home over #14 Houston. After the weekend, the only undefeated teams in the Top 25 are Miami, UCLA, and Utah. Week 9 will see the top four teams in the AP Poll in action. #1 Miami will face Bill Belichick and UNC, #2 Ohio State will go on the road to face USC, #3 Georgia will host #17 Florida, and #4 Indiana will play Minnesota. Now ranked #6, Utah will try to avoid being upset by Cincinnati while #13 Texas Tech will be tested again by #22 Arizona. Here are a few players who had a good week and might be able to help out the Commanders. Let me know. what you think about these prospects and feel free to post players that stood out to you. Keyone Jenkins | QB | Senior | UCF Keyone Jenkins picked a great time to have his best game of the season. Jenkins is a small quarterback at 6’, 200 pounds, but he put quality throws on tape in the Knights’ win over BYU. Jenkins threw with touch and layered throws over defenders. On a few of his passes in the end zone, Jenkins placed the ball where only his receivers could catch it. Generally, the ball came out on time, but he kept his eyes downfield and found receivers when it didn’t. Jenkins is a developmental quarterback prospect who needs to become more consistent with his mechanics in order to stick around at the next level. Against BYU, Jenkins went 25 of 41 for 293 yards and three touchdowns and added a touchdown on the ground. Built for this moment 🌟 Keyone Jenkins Highlights vs. #2 BYU 🎬 @UCF_Football pic.twitter.com/zeexAleJSY — Big 12 Studios (@big12studios) October 25, 2026 Caleb Komolafe | RB | RS Junior | Northwestern Northwestern continued its winning ways against Rutgers, and Caleb Komolafe was a major reason why. He’s 5’11”, 210 pounds, so enough size to play at the next level. Northwestern appears to use more zone-scheme run plays than gap scheme, but Komolafe plays well in both. His best attribute might be his ability to find holes and squeeze the most out of runs when much isn’t there. He can anticipate where holes will open on zone runs, then bursts through them. Komolafe rushed 13 times for 150 yards and a touchdown in the Wildcats victory over the Scarlet Knights. Touchdown Northwestern. On 3rd and 14, RB Caleb Komolafe takes it 33yds for the score. NU: 28 || RU: 3 👉 https://t.co/HbcWhfnFvi pic.twitter.com/PC2JUHvF3Q — Rutgers Scarlet Knights | The Knight Report (@RutgersOn3) October 24, 2026 Ryan Wingo | WR | Junior | Texas Ryan Wingo was busy early against Ole Miss, helping the Longhorns gain a lead that Ole Miss could never overcome. Wingo is 6’2”, 214 pounds, so he has the size of an NFL receiver. Wingo’s best attribute is his speed. He uses it to get past defenders downfield or run by them after short receptions. My biggest concern with Wingo is, while he can rely on that athleticism in college, it might not be enough in the NFL. He needs to improve his route-running and clean up focus drops to have a long career at the next level. He showed improvement in these areas against Ole Miss as he had seven catches for 111 yards and a touchdown. Arch Manning drops a dime to Ryan Wingo 🎯 📺 ABC x @SEC pic.twitter.com/0Nsk5RzcCL — CFP (@CFBPlayoff) October 25, 2026 RYAN WINGO WITH A HUGE GAIN pic.twitter.com/M73TWPvqsV — ClutchWire (@ClutchWireHQ) October 25, 2026 Kari Ashley | TE | Senior | TCU Kari Ashley had a unique path to starting tight end for the Horned Frogs. He’s now their leading receiver thanks to his sheer athleticism which Bruce Feldman noted in his College Football Freaks List 2026 . Ashley is very small for a tight end at 6’4”, 225 pounds. title: NFL trade deadline grades: DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson dealt by Colts, more
summary: Does Buckner make the 49ers Super Bowl hopefuls? Will Quenton Nelson upgrade the Seahawks' O-line? We're grading NFL trades ahead of November's deadline.
full_text:
NFL analysts Ben Solak and Seth Walder are grading deals ahead of the 2026 trade deadline , which is Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET.

 When grading trades, we evaluate them for each team based on on-field impact, cap implications, draft compensation and effects within the context of a team's overall short- and long-term outlooks. How confident are we in knowing if this is a good or bad decision? And how big is the impact of this decision? Both questions play a role in our grades, though a low-impact decision can still receive a strong or poor grade. Even with lower stakes, clear-cut wins or losses still matter.

 Here are our evaluations for the first deals of trading season, including the Colts sending guard Quenton Nelson to Seattle and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to San Francisco. Check back through the deadline for grades on the biggest moves.

 

 
 Jump to a trade: 
 Buckner |  Nelson | Harrison   
 Jurgens  |  Porter | McCarthy 

 
 

 

 Colts trade DT Buckner to 49ers 

 49ers get: DT DeForest Buckner 
 Colts get: 2027 fourth-round pick

 49ers grade: A- 
 Colts grade: B-

 As soon as the Colts emerged as a team that might engage in a trade-deadline teardown, it wasn't hard to see the dots connecting Buckner back to the 49ers. That became a reality Tuesday.

 Though his numbers have dipped, Buckner, 32, can still help the 49ers get after the quarterback. He has four sacks this season, but his pass rush win rate ranked in the 45th percentile among defensive tackles, alongside a 69th percentile pressure rate. That is a drop from last season, when he was in the 90th and 88th percentile in those metrics, respectively. However, that 2025 performance is a positive sign for what he could bring to the 49ers the rest of this season.

 Extra pass-rushing help will be welcome in San Francisco, which ranks 19th in pass rush win rate. The 49ers have been without Nick Bosa , who has been out because of  a calf injury since Week 3 but is expected to return soon. Their pass defense is the only one of their major units (run and pass on offense and defense) that ranks outside the top seven in EPA per play (13th).

 

 I'll admit I'm a little surprised the 49ers made this move considering they already have Osa Odighizuwa as a pass-rush-first defensive tackle. But he can play next to Buckner -- especially on passing downs. Also, San Francisco's rash of defensive line injuries makes any help welcome.

 This type of roster-bolstering move makes sense for San Francisco. The 49ers are the Super Bowl favorites, according to ESPN's Football Power Index . In fact, they are the favorites by a lot , with the FPI giving them a 23% chance to win the Super Bowl (every other team is below 11%). Adding Buckner to reinforce those chances is worthwhile.

 The cost was also quite reasonable. The 49ers are surrendering a fourth-round pick and taking over the prorated remainder of Buckner's $13 million salary, assuming his contract is untouched. While compensatory picks are never a guarantee, there's a decent chance that San Francisco might recoup most of that draft capital back via a comp pick if Buckner signs elsewhere in free agency next offseason, especially given that San Francisco is low on 2027 cap space.

 That also is why I'm a little critical of the Colts' move here. Don't get me wrong, it absolutely makes sense for Indianapolis to trade him. The Colts are rebuilding, and Buckner is a 32-year-old in the final year of his contract -- of course they should have dealt him before the deadline.

 

 Perhaps this was the best offer Indianapolis received for Buckner today , but they also didn't have to trade Buckner right now. There are two weeks left until the Nov. 10 trade deadline. I would have thought they could have at least squeezed another Day 3 pick in addition to the fourth-rounder. -- Walder 

 
 

 Colts trade G Nelson to Seahawks 
 Seahawks get: G Quenton Nelson 
 Colts get: 2027 third-round pick, 2028 fifth-round pick

 Seahawks grade: A- 
 Colts grade: B+

 The reimagination of the Colts is officially underway, with longtime Indianapolis stalwart Nelson heading to the defending Super Bowl champions to bolster the interior of their offensive line.

 Nelson, 30, started his career with three consecutive first-team All-Pro selections. His level of play dropped in 2022 and 2023, but the 2018 first-round pick battled back to elite form in 2024, when he posted pass block and run block win rates that were each in the 90th percentile, along with earning second-team All-Pro honors. He earned a second-team All-Pro spot last season, too, along with a 91st percentile and 74th percentile pass block and run block win rates, respectively.

 His win rates haven't been quite as strong this season (66th and 37th percentile, respectively), but Nelson's reputation is still superb, and having such consistent results the previous two years suggests he probably remains one of the best guards in the league if we're projecting the rest of the season.

 

 The Seahawks presumably will keep Nelson at left guard and move Grey Zabel to right guard. That will push Anthony Bradford , who recently returned from injured reserve and has played two games this season, to the bench. Bradford recorded 30th and 33rd percentile pass block and run block win rates last season, respectively, so Nelson is a substantial upgrade.

 The Seahawks have Super Bowl aspirations but must get better play out of an offense that ranks 26th in EPA per play and 31st in EPA per designed rush. They rank 27th in run block win rate, 28th in yards per designed running back carry (3.6) and 28th in yards before contact on designed run plays. They also rank 21st in pass block win rate. So the team needed some offensive line help and upgrading their right guard or center made sense.

 Nelson is on an expiring contract, so unless his deal was altered, the Seahawks will take on the prorated remainder of his $16 million in salary for this season, which is a bargain for the quality of play he brings. The Seahawks could sign Nelson to an extension or a new deal after the season, but they could also let him walk in free agency and possibly collect a compensatory pick to mitigate the draft capital lost in this trade.

 It makes a lot of sense for the Seahawks to push their chips in on their current team. History tells us how hard it is to sustain elite defensive success, so the Seahawks need to take advantage while they have it.

 This was also an easily logical move for the Colts. The 2026 season is lost, and Nelson is a pending free agent. Whatever value he would bring to the team in the second half of the season pales in comparison to what he brings to the Seahawks, and the draft capital return is more than they would get in compensatory picks (which are never a guarantee, anyway) had Nelson left in free agency. Plus, they save money on the remainder of his 2026 salary.

 

 Ultimately, this is a win-win trade. Considering Seattle's contention window, positional (and overall offensive) need, the draft capital required and Nelson's contract, this is a sound move. -- Walder

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline updates: DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson on the move
summary: The NFL trade deadline is Nov. 10, but deals have already started. We're tracking all moves, including the Colts dealing Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner.
full_text:
The  2026 NFL trade deadline  is Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET. But the deals have already kicked off.

 With quarterback Jaxson Dart undergoing surgery on his left knee, the Giants traded for Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy . Amid contract extension negotiations that went nowhere, the Steelers traded  Joey Porter Jr . to the Cowboys. The Eagles sent center  Cam Jurgens  to the Ravens for draft picks after Week 4. In the middle of Week 5, the Texans acquired wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr . from the Cardinals. Also after Week 7, the Colts traded away guard  Quenton Nelson  and defensive tackle  DeForest Buckner .

 We're tracking all in-season moves and trade-related buzz right through the deadline. The most recent deals will be added at the top.

 
 More coverage: 
 Transactions  |  Depth charts 

 

 
 Oct. 27 
 

 Colts trade DT Buckner to 49ers 
 49ers get:  DT DeForest Buckner 
 Colts get:  2027 fourth-round pick

 The Colts are trading three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner back to the 49ers, the team that made him a 2016 first-round pick before dealing him to Indianapolis in 2020, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

 The Colts will receive a 2027 fourth-round pick from the 49ers, sources said.

 Colts get: 2027 third-round pick, 2028 fifth-round pick

 The Colts have agreed to trade eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Nelson is on an expiring contract, and the Colts are opting to get back draft capital now before they could lose him in free agency.

 The Texans have completed a trade for Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr ., coach DeMeco Ryans told reporters. The Texans sent 2027 second- and sixth-round draft picks to the Cardinals for Harrison and a 2027 seventh-round selection, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.  Oct. 7 
 

 Eagles trade C Jurgens to Ravens

 The Eagles are trading two-time Pro Bowl center Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-round pick to the Ravens in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter on Wednesday.

 The Eagles had moved Jurgens to left guard after Landon Dickerson was placed on injured reserve because of a knee injury. Jurgens self-reported concussion symptoms Monday morning, was evaluated and is now in the concussion protocol, a source told NFL Network's Mike Garafolo on Monday.

 Steelers trade CB Porter to Cowboys

 The Steelers are trading Porter to the Cowboys for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round selection, sources confirmed to NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe and ESPN's Todd Archer. 

 The trade marks the end of a monthslong saga that stretched throughout the Steelers' offseason as Porter, one of the team's 2023 second-round picks, awaited an extension and was sidelined with a back injury.

 Vikings trade QB McCarthy to Giants

 The Giants traded for Vikings quarterback McCarthy on Monday, sending a 2027 fifth-round draft pick to Minnesota for the 2024 first-round pick. McCarthy, taken by the Vikings with the No. 10 pick, was the third-string quarterback in Minnesota behind starter Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz .
