title: NFL Power Rankings: How all 32 teams stack up for Week 8, plus offseason adds
summary: How does every NFL team stack up heading into Week 8? We made our 1-32 list and picked the best offseason addition -- coach or player -- for every team.
full_text:
As is the case in every  NFL season , a handful of offseason additions are making splashes with their new teams. In Week 7 , rookie second-round pick Jacob Rodriguez helped the Dolphins to their first win as the defense's signal-caller. Meanwhile,  Kenneth Walker III , who signed with the Chiefs in free agency, leads all running backs in yards per carry (5.8). Also, coaches Todd Monken and John Harbaugh have the Browns and Giants at the top of their respective divisions.

 So which additions have had the most impact so far? Along with the weekly 1-32 rankings, our NFL Nation reporters picked the best offseason addition from each roster. They chose from 2026 draft picks , free agent signings , trade acquisitions or coach hirings .

 To form the list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another. Here are a few highlights from this week's rankings:

 
 The Bengals-Ravens matchup caused a big stir in our rankings, sending the Ravens down five spots and the Bengals up four. Baltimore led at the halftime despite being without quarterback Lamar Jackson  ( ankle ) but blew a double-digit advantage. It is just the sixth team in NFL history to do that three times in the first seven weeks of a season, per ESPN Research -- and the first since the 2022 Ravens. Cincinnati quarterback  Joe Burrow  was nearly perfect in the second half, completing 16 of 18 passes for 249 yards and four touchdowns. 
 All four AFC North and all four NFC North teams are over .500 through seven weeks. It's the fifth and sixth times under the current division format (since 2002) that all teams in a division are .500 or better at this point of the season, per Elias Sports Bureau. In our rankings, the lowest-ranked NFC North team is the Packers (No. 15) and the lowest-ranked AFC North team is the Browns (No. 16). 
 The Buccaneers are getting back on track after a  dominant win over the Panthers brought them to 2-1 over the past three weeks. Sunday's victory also marked the return of quarterback  Baker Mayfield , who missed the past three games because of a dislocated right thumb . Tampa Bay has been as low as No. 30 in our rankings this season, but the Bucs are now in the top 25 ahead of a divisional matchup against the Falcons . 
 
 Let's get into the full list, starting with the same No. 1 team from last week .

 

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 

 1. San Francisco 49ers (6-1) 
 Week 7 result: Lost to the Falcons 29-20 
 Week 7 ranking: 1 

 Best offseason addition: WR Mike Evans 

 

 The 49ers signed Evans  in free agency to be their primary "X" receiver and produce against man coverage. Through the first six weeks, that's exactly what he did. In a Week 5 win over Seattle , quarterback Brock Purdy had a QBR of 90 when Evans was on the field versus 56 when he wasn't. Achilles tendinitis kept Evans out of San Francisco's only loss, driving home his value to the team. -- Nick Wagoner 

 
 

 2. Buffalo Bills (5-1) 
 Week 7 result: Bye 
 Week 7 ranking: 3 

 Best offseason addition: WR D.J. Moore 

 

 The Bills' offense has survived while Moore rehabs a shoulder injury , but it's clear how much smoother the team's passing attack works when he's involved. Moore's field-stretching talents lead to explosive plays and lighten boxes to create bigger alleys for rushing attempts by running back  James Cook III and QB Josh Allen . No player this season is averaging more yards per route run (2.47) with as deep of an average depth of target (15.9 yards) as Moore. He was acquired from the Bears for a 2026 second-round pick this offseason.  -- Nick Suss 

 
 

 

 3. Minnesota Vikings (6-0) 
 Week 7 result: Beat the Colts 16-10 
 Week 7 ranking: 4 

 Best offseason addition: QB Kyler Murray 

 

 In reality, the Vikings' offseason was more about subtractions than additions. But Murray remains the most significant acquisition they made despite his individual performance being uneven in five games. The Vikings have won all of his starts, and there are some signs that he is settling in. His QBR since Week 5 (75.1) ranks sixth in the NFL, powered in part by nine scrambles that gained 94 yards and converted four third downs. -- Kevin Seifert 

 
 

 4. Kansas City Chiefs (5-1) 
 Week 7 result: Lost to the Seahawks 20-3 
 Week 7 ranking: 2 

 Best offseason addition: RB Kenneth Walker III 

 

 Despite his disappointing return to Seattle on Sunday, Walker has perhaps been the biggest reason the Chiefs are atop the AFC standings. He is second in the league with 701 rushing yards; his production has made life easier for quarterback Patrick Mahomes , who has excelled at play-action passes. At this point last season, the Chiefs realized they didn't have any explosion in their running attack. Now the Chiefs' biggest strength on offense has been when Mahomes hands the ball off to his new teammate.  -- Nate Taylor 

 
 

 5. Seattle Seahawks (4-3) 
 Week 7 result: Beat the Chiefs 20-3 
 Week 7 ranking: 6 

 Best offseason addition: RB Emanuel Wilson 

 

 With the Seahawks reserving all their big offseason deals for in-house extensions, they made a few bargain signings in free agency, including Wilson on a one-year, $1.6 million deal . Their run game has not been a strength, with rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price missing the past four games and Zach Charbonnet having yet to make his 2026 debut , but Wilson has helped keep it afloat. He has rushed for 403 yards (3.6-yard average) and three touchdowns, with another touchdown through the air. Much of that has come in a leading role since Price, who is now eligible to return, went on IR ( chest ).  -- Brady Henderson 

 
 

 6. Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) 
 Week 7 result: Bye 
 Week 7 ranking: 5 

 Best offseason addition: LG Emmanuel Pregnon 

 

 A back injury to right guard Patrick Mekari forced the Jaguars to shuffle the offensive line in training camp. Left guard Ezra Cleveland moved over to right guard, which gave Pregnon the opportunity to earn first-team reps. The third-round rookie has a 71.6% run block win rate (fourth highest among Jaguars starting linemen), but he has helped them be much better in short-yardage runs -- a priority for coach Liam Coen in 2026. The Jaguars averaged 1.3 yards per carry on runs in third-and-short (2 or fewer yards) in 2025, which ranked last in the NFL. They're averaging 3.1 yards in that situation in 2026 (eighth-best mark). -- Michael DiRocco 

 
 

 7. Chicago Bears (5-2) 
 Week 7 result: Beat the Patriots 30-24 
 Week 7 ranking: 9 

 Best offseason addition: S Dillon Thieneman 

 

 Thieneman and fellow rookie DB  Malik Muhammad II  have nearly identical stat lines this season, but the No. 25 pick gets the nod here for how he has handled the highest snap percentage of any Bears defender (97.58%). Thieneman is No. 1 or tied for the team lead in total tackles (47), passes defensed (five) and interceptions (one). He also has 1.5 sacks and three QB hits. Thieneman has had his share of learning moments, but the stability he has provided can't be overstated for a secondary that has dealt with moving parts since the start of training camp. -- Courtney Cronin 

 

 
 

 8. Denver Broncos (5-2) 
 Week 7 result: Beat the Cardinals 30-16 
 Week 7 ranking: 10 

 Best offseason addition: WR Jaylen Waddle 

 

 Rookie running back Jonah Coleman has played in only three games because of an ankle injury , and he might win the impact-per-snap-played quotient, but Waddle leads the Broncos in receptions (26) and receiving yards (276). His numbers would likely look better if he had not been caught up in the swirl of Denver's passing struggles. Waddle left Sunday's game because of an apparent shoulder injury, but if it's not serious and the Broncos can simply get him the ball more, his output will…

title: Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 8: WR trade for Chiefs? Goff for MVP?
summary: Get ready for Week 8 with takes on the Chiefs' trade deadline plan, Jared Goff's sneaky season, Kevin Stefanski's Coach of the Year case and the Ravens' struggling defense.
full_text:
Are you excited for NFL Week 8 ? This is our first loaded slate of the season. Ravens at Bills. Vikings at Lions. Browns at Steelers. Chiefs at Broncos. Bears at Seahawks. Even the not-so-great games (Falcons at Buccaneers and Colts at Jaguars) mean a lot for divisional standings.

 Every Tuesday of the NFL season , I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions. They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out. And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts ... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.

 
 Subscribe: 'ESPN's Leaguewide' 

 
 This week, I'll start with a prediction/plea for the Chiefs to make a trade for a receiver. Then I'll put all my hope and joy on the back of a fourth-round rookie. And finally, I'll admit I can't do my job.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Chiefs will make a WR trade 
 Stefanski will be Coach of the Year 
 Goff is a sleeper MVP candidate 
 Coleman could save Broncos' offense 
 Ravens' D disqualifies them from contention 
 QB3 Leonard starts for Colts by Week 10 
 Young is a complicated study 
 Some extra inklings 

 
 

 

 I think ... the Chiefs' loss to Seattle will bully them into making the trade they need to make 
 Have you ever gotten embarrassed on national television? Me neither.

 The 2026 Chiefs sure have. Kansas City scored three points against the Seahawks on Sunday night, marking only the second time in Patrick Mahomes ' career that his team has been held to three or fewer points. The 11 first downs the Chiefs accumulated were their fewest in 153 Mahomes starts, and this was only his fourth start without a single explosive pass. The offense averaged 4.3 yards per play (148th out of Mahomes' 153 starts), produced minus-0.13 EPA per play (148th) and had a success rate of 34% (152nd).

 It's easy to explain this one. The Seahawks, off a two-game losing streak, were hosting an unbeaten Chiefs team at home -- that defense was amped-up for four quarters. The Chiefs were down both starting tackles ( Josh Simmons and Jaylon Moore ) along with two of three starting receivers ( Tyquan Thornton and Rashee Rice ), and the passing offense played like it. Even the Chiefs' ace in the hole -- their interior offensive line's dominance in the running game -- was beaten in this game, as they ran into the league-best defensive tackle duo of Leonard Williams and Byron Murphy II . I didn't think it would look as bad as it did, but it's not too surprising it fell to such dramatic pieces.

 

 Let's also consider the larger context. Simmons didn't just miss this game -- he has been out all season, and ESPN reported Sunday that Reid and Mahomes had to kick Simmons out of a meeting  Wednesday after frustrations boiled over. He has missed the entire season because of back issues, has recently been placed on injured reserve and missed time last season for personal reasons and a wrist injury. Rice has now missed 27 of the 43 games he could have played since the start of the 2024 season for injury or suspension. It's not just that the Chiefs' star receiver and early-drafted left tackle missed this past week -- it's that they've proven to be consistently unavailable. Meanwhile, 2024 Chiefs first-round receiver Xavier Worthy dropped another pass in Week 7 as he continues to be unusable on most downfield routes.

 This was a one-off in that the Chiefs were dramatically outmanned and should get some of these players back from the medical tent soon. But this was not a one-off in the sense that Rice, Simmons and Worthy are just unreliable players.

 The Chiefs should clearly consider drastic measures. Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson has played well enough in Simmons' absence that there's no need to make a big trade for a left tackle. But the need for a three-down receiver who can endure a large target volume and succeed at all three levels of the field is glaring. Worthy isn't even the best speed receiver on the team when Thornton is healthy, so I think Worthy should be dangled in trade packages as well -- he has more value in theory right now than he does in practice.

 Whether the Chiefs actually will consider a big deadline trade is less clear. General manager Brett Veach has typically been active around the deadline, executing at least one in-season trade in five consecutive seasons from 2020 to 2024 before going quiet in 2025. The biggest such deal was the future third-round pick traded for Kadarius Toney in 2022. The Chiefs had just traded Tyreek Hill in the 2022 offseason and were looking for speed on offense. Toney didn't hit as a receiver, but he provided a big punt return in the Chiefs' Super Bowl victory that season.

 This Chiefs team (5-1) is as well suited for a postseason run as that 2022 Chiefs team (5-2 at the time of the trade). Through seven weeks of the 2026 season, the Chiefs are fifth in offensive EPA per play and fourth in defensive EPA per play. They are ninth in offensive points per drive and third in defensive points per drive. With an actual running game well in hand and a reinvigorated defense, this is as balanced of a Chiefs team as I can remember. They just need some more juice on offense.

 

 ESPN's Adam Schefter has reported as such. From "The Pat McAfee Show" on Monday: "They have been calling around, and I don't think it would be a surprise to see them continue to attempt to add a wide receiver before the trade deadline."

 I have five deadline deals for a receiver in mind. These are not sourced and were first written down on the back of a napkin. It's very likely the other teams in these hypotheticals would not even listen to deals for their wideouts. Do not yell at me on the internet about these trade proposals.

 1. Send Worthy and a 2027 third-round pick to the Jaguars for Brian Thomas Jr . 

 Jacksonville benched Thomas in the second half of its Week 6 game. The only value the Jaguars were getting from him was theoretical field-stretching -- Worthy can do much the same, and Mahomes and the Chiefs can give Thomas a chance to rediscover his 2024 form in a new zip code.

 2. Send a 2027 third-round pick and 2028 conditional fifth-round pick to the Cowboys for George Pickens . 

 The Cowboys have 2025 trade acquisition Pickens and 2026 trade acquisition Joey Porter Jr . playing on contract years, and it's hard to imagine they extend both ex-Steelers at market rates. If Pickens would recoup a third-round compensatory pick in free agency, the Chiefs can sweeten the pot with a future pick conditional on production levels and give the Cowboys their third-round comp pick without having to manipulate the formula this offseason. How the Cowboys play in Weeks 8 and 9 (vs. Cardinals, at Colts) will have a big impact here.

 3. Send a 2027 fourth-round pick to the Eagles for Dontayvion Wicks . 

 If I were the Chiefs, I'd be putting a first and then some on the table for DeVonta Smith . It absolutely would not work -- Eagles GM Howie Roseman isn't going to trade both A.J. Brown and Smith in the same season -- but you have to try as the Eagles stare down the barrel of a rebuild in 2027. In lieu of Smith, Wicks has all the traits of a three-level receiver -- ball tracking, ability to catch away from his frame, burst, size -- without any of the route or hands consistency. Grab him for a Day 3 pick and hope to run hot!

 

 4. Send Worthy and a 2027 seventh-round pick to the Saints for Devaughn Vele and a 2027 sixth-round pick. 

 Before you laugh, that's tied-for-22nd-in-total-receptions Devaughn Vele to you! Vele is an entirely unexciting target, but he is also basically what the Chiefs need. He's a big-bodied receiver who can take a ton of contact and endure 10-plus-target games. He also makes good catches away from his frame and provides…

title: How the Falcons' two biggest stars bond off the field
summary: Bijan Robinson and Drake London are like brothers off the field, and on it, they're among the NFL's best.
full_text:
FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- The first time Bijan Robinson  communicated with Drake London , it was about a number.

 The Atlanta Falcons drafted Robinson with the eighth overall pick in 2023. At Texas, Robinson wore No. 5, which was in use by London, who was selected by the Falcons with the exact same pick a year earlier.

 Robinson got London's cell phone number from then-head coach Arthur Smith and shot the wide receiver a text. He wasn't sure exactly how it would go. Robinson didn't know London and some players can be attached to their numbers. So, Robinson, as is his way, asked in the most polite way possible.

 London, to Robinson's relief, was amenable to giving up No. 5. London had worn No. 15 at Southern California. But when London found out that No. 15 wasn't available -- wide receiver Van Jefferson was going to wear it -- he told Robinson he was going to stay with No. 5. Robinson ended up choosing No. 7.

 "It all worked out," Robinson said.

 

 Robinson and London are now close friends and make up the offensive foundation for the Falcons -- and will for the foreseeable future. Both signed long-term contract extensions in the offseason, which will ostensibly keep them in Atlanta together through the 2030 season.

 The Falcons (3-4) have had uneven results so far this season, as well as in the three previous years Robinson and London have been together. The team has failed to make the playoffs or have a winning season, but it is through no fault of its star duo.

 Robinson has emerged as arguably the best running back in the NFL, leading the league in rushing this season (704 yards) and in scrimmage yards (2,298) last season. London has cemented himself as an elite wideout and is fourth in the NFL with 616 receiving yards. His touchdown Sunday helped the Falcons upset the San Francisco 49ers .

 Individual accomplishments aside, Robinson and London share a collective goal: getting the Falcons back to the promised land. Atlanta has not made the playoffs since 2017, the second-longest drought in the NFL. (The Jets haven't reached the postseason in 15 seasons.) And the Falcons have never won a Super Bowl. Robinson and London want to be part of the core that changes that.

 "[Bijan and I] talk about that before every season," London said. "This is the one where we got to do it. We're still striving for that and not even just together, but for this team, for this city, for the fans.

 "I always say that, and that's exactly why I wanted to stay here. You'll be the first to ever do it. I don't care where you're at [on] the totem pole of this team, you're going to be the first to ever do it. And that means something. I know this city will go up if we do that."

 Why the Robinson-London duo is among the NFL's best 
 Robinson and London sat shoulder to shoulder on the Falcons' bench. It was late in a 34-3 loss to the Carolina Panthers at home in Week 2. Robinson and London could both be seen talking to one another and shaking their heads, almost trying to figure out how the game had come to that.

 "We were just talking about how to fix that situation, that game," Robinson said. "What can we do better? How can we be better? And that was the key to that conversation, man. Just how can we help improve this offense? How can we help improve this team to the best of our ability? And that's really what it was about right there."

 There were some extenuating circumstances. The Falcons were playing third-string quarterback Cooper Rush with both Michael Penix Jr . (ACL) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) injured. Rush was dealing with back spasms himself, but played through them.

 

 The following week, with Penix back, Robinson and London both went off. Robinson had 194 yards on the ground and London, fittingly, had the exact same total receiving in a 35-14 win over the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field.

 It was the third time Robinson and London each went over 150 yards in the same game, an NFL record for a running back-wide receiver duo.

 "I mean, that's cool and all, but sometimes I'll be talking to my friends back home, and I'll be tripping out that Bijan [texts] me and stuff like that," London said after the game. "You know what I'm saying? He's going to be a [gold] jacket wearer. ... So it's really, really cool and just blessed to be a part of something like that."

 Robinson refers to London as his "real-life brother." The pair have been through two coaching changes in Atlanta, from Smith to Raheem Morris to Kevin Stefanski. The front office execs who drafted them are mostly gone. They have had a different starting quarterback to begin the season all four years they have been together.

 "I call him my blood brother because we really are," Robinson said. "We do everything together. We work hard together, we train together, do things off the field.

 "We talk about everything, and just seeing some of the adversity that we got to face throughout our career together and for these kinds of moments to happen is pretty special and I know he's enjoying it. I'm enjoying it, too."

 The stars' families have grown close, too. Robinson's grandparents often meet up with London's parents the night before games and go to dinner together. It is a strong bond.

 "They ended up clicking, and just every now and then we'll go out and eat and share a few words and stuff like that," London said. "My parents really do look up to them just as great people because of the age difference and stuff like that."

 

 The two complement each other on the field, as well. London is one of the best blocking wide receivers in the league. Falcons offensive coordinator Tommy Rees has lauded London for how unselfish he is despite being the team's star wideout.

 "When your best player, best receiver is selfless and willing to do those things and actually enjoys doing those things, I think it creates buy-in across the board," Rees said.

 Without London's blocking, Robinson might not be able to break those long runs like that 55-yard scamper he had against the Packers. And without Robinson's ability, London said, he wouldn't have as much room on the outside because teams are forced to stack the box to contain the threat of the ground game.

 "We got to lean on each other to make this train go," London said.

 Both are great players, but London is the fiery one 
 Robinson said he believes he and London are very similar. They're both homebodies and somewhat introverted off the field. You won't find either of them partaking in Atlanta's nightlife.

 On the field, though, teammates say they are very different. Both are extremely competitive, it just comes out in separate ways.

 In that lopsided loss to the Panthers, London fired back verbally to a fan who was lobbing insults at him. London so badly wants to win that if things don't go that way he can lose his cool at times. Robinson always remains even-keeled, regardless of game results.

 

 "On the field, Drake is more loud, screaming, but Bijan, he's always calm and not really saying [much]," Penix said. "But in the locker room, they're both the same. They talk, they're quiet, humble, humble guys. Just on the field, Drake shows it, expresses it more than Bijan does verbally."

 Has Robinson ever gotten angry and acted out?

 "I've never seen him get upset," Penix said.

 Tight end  Kyle Pitts Sr ., who got to Atlanta the year before London, echoed the sentiment.

 "Definitely game day, Drake's probably the more fiery one," Pitts said. "Bijan's definitely not fiery. He's very competitive, but fiery, I don't know. He's not a super yeller, but he'll show leadership when he needs to for sure."

 Robinson said London's intensity is one of the things he likes about his teammate and friend. It's one of the things, Robinson said, that gives the team the juice that can help it get over the hump, which both he and London are desperate to do.

 

 "He's passionate, man," Robinson said. "And I try not to get in the way of that because that's what builds…

title: NFL Week 8 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips: What we're hearing
summary: Are changes coming for the Jets? Could the Chiefs add at the trade deadline? Will the Colts keep unloading? And what's going on in the AFC North standings?
full_text:
It's Week 8 of the  2026 NFL season , and we're under two weeks away from the trade deadline. Insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been calling sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.

 Which teams are most likely to bring in help before the Nov. 10 deadline? Which players are likeliest to end up in a new city? And will the Colts continue dealing away players? Jeremy and Dan have updates on the trade market. Plus, we look into what's happening with the struggling Jets and what's going on in the chaotic AFC North, where the Browns are in first and the Ravens are in last.

 It's all here, as Jeremy and Dan answer big questions, hand out useful fantasy football nuggets and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 8.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Aggressive teams at the deadline 
 Players likely to move  | Colts dealing 
 Jets changes  | AFC North chaos 
 Fantasy advice 

 
 

 Which team is most likely to be aggressive in acquiring help at the deadline? 
 Fowler: The Chiefs appear poised to do something at wide receiver. Injuries to Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton have created holes in the passing game that running back Kenneth Walker III can't mask alone. The Chiefs have managed to win games despite those injuries, but Sunday night in Seattle was a reminder of how ugly things can look without adequate downfield playmakers.

 Enough receivers will be available in the coming weeks, so the Chiefs can get good value trading for the high-impact players or lower-cost options. The Colts' Josh Downs would be a fit for the Chiefs. The Browns' Jerry Jeudy  would also fit, though Cleveland is not inclined to deal him now barring a significant offer.

 Graziano: The Chiefs always seem to do something at wide receiver at the deadline. Usually it's a smaller move such as  Kadarius Toney or late-career DeAndre Hopkins , but the team has a history of targeted trade-deadline additions at the position. I expect Kansas City to be active in trying to add a player or two to boost the offense, be that another pass catcher, an offensive lineman or both.

 The teams that are most interesting to me are the surprises. Would the first-place Giants believe they're in position to trade a draft pick or two for a win-now player? Would the AFC North-leading Browns feel compelled to reward their current roster for its surprising first-half success by adding a player who can help take them to the next level? We saw the Colts do this last year with the big swing for Sauce Gardner .

 

 Of course, last year's Colts are proof that this approach doesn't always work , but what do you think? Would the Browns veer from their long-term building plans to try to make a 2026 run with Deshaun Watson at QB?

 Fowler: Cleveland is a low-key team to watch at the deadline. The Browns are 5-2 and like to make deals. Defensive line help will be available if they tap into it. And adding a versatile blocker, either at tight end or H-back, would be timely, perhaps providing a player similar to what Todd Monken had in Baltimore with Patrick Ricard .

 Seattle has already made a move with the deal for Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson . Edge rusher and running back are positions Seahawks GM John Schneider could monitor, as well.

 Graziano: Yeah, Tuesday was a big day in the NFC West arms race. It makes me wonder what the Rams are thinking. They obviously made their big moves in the offseason, but things haven't worked, and everyone's favorite superteam has fallen behind the 49ers and Seahawks in the division. I wonder whether there's another move for the Rams to make -- they could use a speedy wide receiver if one is available -- and whether they still have the draft picks and/or desire to add more to a roster that was already supposed to be loaded.

 I'm also very curious to see what the Jaguars do. They see themselves as a top AFC contender. I agree with them, but they could use one more piece up front on defense. Remember, the Jags were kind of a surprise at last year's deadline with  their move for Jakobi Meyers , who helped fuel their second-half run.

 

 
 Which player are you most confident will get traded somewhere before the deadline? 
 Fowler: Let's go with Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr . Several execs I've spoken to believe Thomas' days in Jacksonville are numbered due to his diminished role in Year 3. He has trade value, and the Jaguars would be smart to explore that option. One potential deterrent: Jacksonville is in a winning window and needs all hands on deck for the stretch run. Thomas, at worst, still commands defensive coverage, but he hasn't caught a pass in the past two games and was essentially benched in London in Week 6 .

 None of the top trade options around the league is a slam dunk to happen, but place Thomas in the Marvin Harrison Jr . category of a receiver badly needing a fresh start . The safer bet might end up being Vikings wide receiver Jauan Jennings , who isn't a primary option in that offense and is also a trade candidate.

 Graziano: Thomas is my answer, too. He clearly hasn't been a big part of Jacksonville's offense since coach Liam Coen arrived last season. Thomas would surely prefer to either be a bigger part of the Jaguars' offense or go to a team where he can have a sizable role. And there are plenty of teams around the league that still view him as a high-end talent at a premium position and would give up something of value to get him.

 

 Like you said, this closely mirrors the Harrison situation. Thomas is two months younger than Harrison, was also drafted in the first round in 2024 and showed enough promise as a rookie that there's reason to believe a change of scenery could bring out the best in him. Thomas hasn't made any public noise about wanting out, but neither did Harrison. Still, Harrison and his agents were able to work with the Cardinals behind the scenes to find a solution that made everyone happy. I expect the same thing to happen for Thomas.

 Going back to your Jennings mention, I agree that the most likely guys to be traded are the slightly lower-profile names if simply because they won't cost as much to add. But I also imagine Cardinals edge rusher Josh Sweat will be of interest to teams needing defensive help over the next couple of weeks.

 Fowler: Yeah, Dan, Sweat certainly fits the profile of a prime trade candidate, and some around the league have linked the Cowboys to his services.

 

 
 What about the Colts? Are more moves coming after they dealt Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner ? 
 Graziano: With the Colts tearing things down, veteran wideouts such as Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell might have appeal as depth players on contenders that need help at receiver. Defensive tackle Grover Stewart and wide receiver Josh Downs are also on expiring contracts and didn't get extensions this offseason.

 The guy who did get an extension , running back  Jonathan Taylor , might be the most interesting of the bunch. Even after his recent extension, Taylor has a tradeable contract. The Colts would have to absorb $10 million in dead money next year, and the acquiring team would have to take on whatever prorated portion of Taylor's $8 million salary plus bonus compensation is left for this season. He's scheduled to make $16.02 million next year, and right now that's not guaranteed, though it converts to a full guarantee five days after the Super Bowl.

 So technically, you could acquire Taylor without any commitment beyond this season, but you'd also retain the ability to keep him past 2026 if you are comfortable with that price. I believe Tennessee's Tony Pollard is the more likely running back to be dealt, ahead of Taylor or Saquon Barkley , but if the Colts are in full rebuilding mode, you can't rule anything out.

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline: Ranking the top 25 candidates to move, plus team fits
summary: Could the Colts listen on Jonathan Taylor? Would Josh Sweat help a contender's defense? We stacked the top players who might move before the Nov. 10 deadline.
full_text:
We're less than two weeks away from the 2026 NFL trade deadline  (Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET). Which players could potentially be available? And which trade candidates could make the biggest impact with new teams if they do get moved?

 NFL analyst Matt Bowen and national NFL reporter Jeremy Fowler worked together to build a comprehensive list of the top 25 possible trade candidates. To be clear: Players are ranked here by the potential value they'd provide a new team if traded -- not their likelihood of actually being dealt.

 That said, we did include our estimated percentage chances for each player to move, weaving in what we're hearing. Jeremy shared the latest buzz on each player, while Matt broke down what he sees on the tape. We even included some interesting team fits for each candidate. Some players have better odds of changing cities than others on the list, but all 25 are at the very least being discussed in trade conversations. Let's dive in.

 

 
 Jump to the top-ranked: 
 QB | RB | WR | TE | OL 
 Edge | DT | LB | CB | S 

 
 

 

 1. Jonathan Taylor , RB, Indianapolis Colts 
 What Fowler is hearing: Teams I've talked to aren't totally sold that Indianapolis will trade Taylor despite heavy interest  -- at least not yet. He is signed long term and would be a boon for next year's coaching staff, whether it's the current group or entirely new. But what Kenneth Walker III has done for Kansas City shows how a premier running back can put on new jersey colors and immediately reimagine a team's season. And the tenor of Indy's season is getting ugly, which affects all key players and could spark even more movement.

 Predicted chance of getting traded: 30%

 What Bowen sees on tape: Taylor is averaging 109.3 total yards per game this season, and he's tied for first in rushing TDs with eight. He's a volume runner with home run speed and pass-catching ability on screens and swings. His 17 rushes for 10 or more yards are tied for the fourth most in the league. Taylor would be an immediate upgrade for a team in need of a lead back who is decisive with the ball.

 

 Team fits: Seahawks, Commanders, Saints, Broncos, Vikings

 
 

 2. Brian Thomas Jr ., WR, Jacksonville Jaguars 
 What Fowler is hearing: League execs are sensing the end for BTJ in Jacksonville, as his targets and playing time have dipped. How Jacksonville has struggled to make this relationship work is still a mystery. Thomas is an elite mover with size who draws coverage deep, setting the stage for teammates Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers to eat underneath. But that plan for Thomas hasn't materialized this season. And teams are circling with interest. Kansas City and Pittsburgh are among those exploring receiver help.

 Predicted chance of getting traded: 45%

 What Bowen sees on tape: Thomas' numbers have declined over the past two seasons, but he has the traits to still draw interest. At 6-foot-3 and 209 pounds, Thomas has the profile of an X receiver who can separate at multiple levels of the field. I see legit straight-line speed and ball-tracking ability. He had 87 receptions and 10 touchdowns as a rookie in 2024, but he has been limited to a 9-105-1 line so far this season.

 

 Team fits: Chiefs, Steelers, 49ers

 
 

 3. Josh Sweat , Edge, Arizona Cardinals 
 What Fowler is hearing: Rival teams could see him getting moved. "Sweat to Dallas makes a lot of sense to me," an NFC exec said. "That's a profile fit." Rumblings persist that Sweat would want a new contract -- he's in the second year of a four-year, $76 million deal -- and that could complicate things. But many teams are looking for an edge rusher.

 Predicted chance of getting traded: 40%

 What Bowen sees on tape: A long, angular mover who can win with speed-to-power, Sweat had 12 sacks and 37 pressures in Arizona last season. But his numbers haven't been as solid in 2026, with two sacks and 10 pressures. Still, Sweat's ability to threaten the edges of offensive tackles with his quickness off the ball fits pass-rush fronts across the league.

 Team fits: Cowboys, Bears, 49ers

 

 
 

 4. Yaya Diaby , Edge, Tampa Bay Buccaneers 
 What Fowler is hearing: Tampa Bay beat Carolina handedly in Week 7 , with Diaby exploding for three sacks. A loss would have put the Bucs at 1-6 and closer to dealing mode. Diaby, 27, is still on the radar, though, because Tampa is not poised to pay the 2027 free agent, and the emergence of second-year rusher David Walker (four sacks) gives the Bucs a natural replacement. Diaby needs a new contract, but an acquiring team could get a compensatory pick for him if he signs a substantial deal with another team in free agency.

 Predicted chance of getting traded: 35%

 What Bowen sees on tape:  Diaby is a powerful and physical edge rusher with the temperament to set the edge against the run. He has three sacks and six tackles for loss in 2026, and he had 40 or more pressures in each of his past two seasons (with 11.5 total sacks over that time). He should be viewed as a quality starter.

 Team fits: Browns, Seahawks, Cowboys

 
 

 5. Jerry Jeudy , WR, Cleveland Browns 
 What Fowler is hearing: The Browns are not actively sending out feelers on Jeudy, but they would at least consider a substantial offer. Key word here is "substantial," though. I'm not sure, say, a fourth-round pick would move anyone in Cleveland, for example. Jeudy is part of the Browns' three-receiver sets and the veteran in that room for a good team in the playoff hunt. That dynamic diminishes his chances of being dealt. But as always, teams are looking for receiver help.

 Predicted chance of getting traded: 20%

 What Bowen sees on tape: Jeudy has the route traits and stop-start speed to separate as a multilevel route runner. He's sudden at the break point. However, the inconsistent hands have been an issue as a pro (33 career drops), and Jeudy lacks the frame and physicality to win on 50-50 throws. Jeudy had a career-best 1,229 receiving yards in 2024, yet he has just 16 receptions this season.

 

 Team fits: Chiefs, Raiders, Commanders

 
 

 6. Daron Payne , DT, Washington Commanders 
 What Fowler is hearing: Washington dealt key defensive pieces at the deadline three years ago and could be faced with a similar predicament this time with Payne, who's 29 and still has value. Payne is a 2027 free agent with a $16.4 million base this year. But the NFC East is also winnable, despite Washington's 1-4-1 record, so that could be a point in favor of the Commanders keeping him. Jacksonville is a potential fit, with some in the league noting the Jaguars could use a versatile interior player with pass-rush ability and have looked for that since the offseason.

 Predicted chance of getting traded: 25%

 What Bowen sees on tape:  Payne can still provide an interior presence due to his foot quickness and strength in one-on-one matchups, plus he will impact the run game from multiple alignments. He had a career-best 11.5 sacks in 2022, but he has totaled only 12 over his past four seasons.

 Team fits: Jaguars, Giants, Buccaneers

 
 

 

 7. Khalil Mack , Edge, Los Angeles Chargers 
 What Fowler is hearing:  Mack is productive and affordable. The Chargers gave him a $10 million signing bonus in March, so a new team would inherit the prorated version of his $8 million salary to close out his one-year deal. Returning to the Bears is a natural fit for the equivalent of a quality Day 3 pick. The Chargers have held off trading pieces such as Mack up to this point, though.

 Predicted chance of getting traded: 35%

 What Bowen sees on tape: Mack doesn't display the same level of explosive speed on tape, but he can still disrupt the pocket due to his play strength and advanced counter moves. Mack has 14.5 sacks and 83 pressures over his past three seasons, and he can play as both a pass-rushing linebacker or defensive end with third-down upside.

 

 Team fits: Bears, Browns, Bills, Cowboys

title: Inside the complicated injury history of Ravens' Lamar Jackson
summary: If Jackson's injury history has taught the football world anything, his timeline to return can be complicated.
full_text:
Earlier this month, Lamar Jackson stood on the sideline for most of the second half after his left ankle bent awkwardly in the Baltimore Ravens ' win over the Tennessee Titans . 
 
 The sight of the Ravens quarterback keeping on his shoulder pads and jersey suggested he might have been able to return to that game. Three weeks later, it's still uncertain when Jackson will suit up again from his high ankle sprain. 
 
 If Jackson's injury history has taught the football world anything, his timeline to return can be complicated and an extended absence can derail the Ravens' season. But ultimately, the only one who truly knows when Jackson will return is Jackson himself. 
 
 "Look, if he's able to play, [is] healthy enough to play and play the way that obviously we feel like he needs to play, then he will play," coach Jesse Minter said Monday. 
 
 On the day Jackson was injured, Minter said there were "some talks" about Jackson returning to the game and initially indicated he was "dealing with a little bit of an ankle" injury. Jackson then didn't practice for two weeks and was ruled out of the games against the Atlanta Falcons and Cleveland Browns . 
 
 
 
 Last week, there was a feeling within the team that Jackson was going to be able to play Sunday against the Cincinnati Bengals . He practiced as a limited participant all week, worked with the first-team offense Friday and took part in the television production meetings, which usually signifies he will be the starting quarterback. 
 
 But Jackson was ruled out Saturday after he experienced increased swelling in his injured left ankle, according to a report during the CBS game broadcast. Tracy Wolfson, the sideline reporter for Sunday's game, posted on social media that it "came as a shock to the Ravens that Lamar couldn't go." Minter later said that was "a little bit" of a mischaracterization. 
 
 In his first comments since getting injured, Jackson made it clear last week that the decision to play comes down to pain tolerance. It still hurts for Jackson to plant his foot when running. 
 
 "If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play," Jackson said. "But [if] I'm restricted and I can't  do what I do, [then] I'm not helping [anybody]. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and be hit, that's not helping my team at all." 
 
 Jackson has now missed multiple games because of injury in four of his past six seasons, but it's a flawed narrative to describe him as the NFL's most injured quarterback. Jackson, who has been sidelined for 17 games with injuries (excluding COVID and illness), has missed fewer games than four other starting quarterbacks -- Kyler Murray (31), Dak Prescott (26), Daniel Jones (25) and Joe Burrow (22) -- since 2019. 
 
 "It seems like Lamar's the only quarterback that kind of gets the slander that he gets for anytime anything is going on," Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey said earlier this month. "I feel like you just don't see these same articles, and you don't see these same headlines. I think it's unfair treatment." 
 
 Humphrey added, "I just feel like it goes -- sometimes it seems like it gets away from -- I don't know if it's because of lack of agent or what, that no one can kind of defend him. I do know this: If Lamar Jackson can play, if he's healthy enough to play, he will play." 
 
 When Jackson misses time, it can turn the Ravens from a championship contender to a team struggling to make the postseason. In the three seasons in which he has missed at least four games, Baltimore failed to make the playoffs twice (2021 and 2025). 
 
 This season, Jackson started off strong and looked like an MVP candidate in his first four games. He ranked third in QBR (82.7), throwing six touchdowns and one interception. Jackson also led all quarterbacks with 144 yards rushing. 
 
 After Jackson sprained his ankle, the Ravens went from being atop the AFC North at 3-1 to falling to last place in the division at 4-3. Baltimore next travels to Buffalo to face the Bills (5-1). Minter said Jackson is in a "decent spot" health-wise entering this week. 
 
 "Lamar is one of one, right? [He's a] two-time MVP, obviously a high-caliber player," Minter said. "But I just don't like the built-in excuse of why things are going a certain way. So, while we know the caliber of player Lamar is and the numbers when he's out there versus when he's not, we understand all that. That's why he's who he is and why he's won the awards that he's won, but we can still operate better in those times where we don't have him, for sure." 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 2021: Ankle injury 
 
 
 Five years ago, Jackson suffered the first significant injury of his NFL career when he was carted off the field in Cleveland in December. In trying to escape the pocket on a pass play, Jackson went down to the ground after Browns linebacker Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah dove at Jackson's heels. 
 
 Jackson sustained a bone bruise on his right ankle that wasn't considered serious at first. 
 
 After the season, then-Ravens coach John Harbaugh said, "The first week, he thought he had a chance. The second week, he assured me, he said, 'I'll be back. I'll be back.'" 
 
 Jackson ended up missing the final four games, all of which resulted in losses. Baltimore went from leading the AFC North at 8-5 to failing to earn a playoff berth. 
 
 "Those things are really unpredictable," Harbaugh said. 
 
 
 
 
 
 2022: Sprained knee 
 
 
 In early December, Jackson was hurt on the last play of the first quarter when he was sacked from behind by linebacker Jonathon Cooper . It looked like Jackson's left knee was driven into the ground when Cooper landed on top of his back. 
 
 Jackson sprained his PCL, but Harbaugh announced it wasn't a season-ending injury. 
 
 "We'll see if he can go back this week," Harbaugh said after the game. "If not, it'll be sometime after that shortly." 
 
 
 
 It turned out to be a season-ending injury for Jackson, who missed the final five regular-season games as well as the wild-card game in Cincinnati. 
 
 Ravens officials were confident that Jackson would return for the postseason until Jackson posted on social media three days before the game. He explained his left knee "remains unstable" and that his injury is more serious than originally believed. 
 
 Jackson indicated that he has "suffered a PCL Grade 2 sprain, on the borderline of a strain 3." 
 
 "I wish I could be out there with my guys more than anything, but I can't give a 100% of myself to my guys and fans," Jackson wrote. "I'm still hopeful we have a chance." 
 
 The Ravens lost to the Bengals 24-17 when backup Tyler Huntley 's fumble on a quarterback sneak at the goal line turned into a 98-yard winning touchdown return for Cincinnati. 
 
 

 

 
 
 2025: Hamstring 
 
 
 In late September, Jackson left midway through the third quarter of a loss at the Kansas City Chiefs after being sacked by defensive end George Karlaftis and did not return. He sat on the bench for the remainder of the game, occasionally flexing his injured right leg. 
 
 Jackson was out for the next three games, but not without a misunderstanding. After Jackson's second missed game, Baltimore originally listed Jackson as a full participant in a Friday practice before changing his practice status to limited a day later because he ran only the scout team. The Ravens then ruled out Jackson. 
 
 After returning, Jackson never looked at full strength the rest of the year. He was 8-5 as the starter for the remainder of the season, throwing 17 touchdown passes and seven interceptions. Jackson also chose not to run as much, averaging 25 yards rushing in the final 13 games. 
 
 This month, Jackson expressed regret for coming back too quickly from that hamstring injury. 
 
 "I feel like that was dumb a little bit," Jackson said. 
 
 Almost exactly a year later, the Ravens are in waiting mode again for Jackson.

title: Is Bills' Josh Allen the best goal-line rusher ever?
summary: Out of the 153 players who've carried from the 1- or 2-yard line at least 30 times since 1977, Allen has done it best.
full_text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- Josh Allen is quantifiably the best goal-line rusher in NFL history -- well, at least since 1977.

 There's no hyperbole here. No recency bias. No twisting the numbers to make them say something they don't. It's just a fact, one as plain as Allen wearing No. 17 for the Buffalo Bills .

 Dating back to 1977 (sorry, Jim Brown fans) when play-by-play data for NFL games became available, 153 players have carried from the 1- or 2-yard line at least 30 times. Allen, who's carried 53 times, has converted those carries into 43 touchdowns, a scoring rate of 81.1% to top the list.

 No one is within five percentage points of Allen's scoring rate, and only three players (Hall of Fame running back Earl Campbell, MVP quarterback Cam Newton and mid-aughts battering ram T.J. Duckett) land within 15 percentage points of Allen.

 

 Allen has seven goal-line rushing touchdowns this season -- one of the reasons the Bills are 5-1 -- in just six games. The only quarterbacks who've ever reached seven goal-line TDs over a full season are Newton, Jalen Hurts and Allen himself. Heck, Allen's already halfway toward besting the single-season mark for short-yardage TDs set by any player, which stands at 13 -- set by Jamaal Williams in 2022.

 Ask Allen, his teammates and his coaches and they'll tell you there are nights of intricate, bespoke game-planning required to make these sneak plays work. But there's also an awareness in the locker room that's a tad unnecessary. As one teammate told ESPN, the plays work because Allen's bigger and stronger than just about any other goal-line threat.

 For all the tendency evaluations and pre-snap motions and dummy counts the Bills can throw at opponents, so much of the success can be simplified to Allen being a one-of-one siege weapon.

 "I wish I could tell you that it's just 'Hey, we just put it up' and then move on to the next play," coach Joe Brady says. "But there's a lot that goes into it. Maybe sometimes too much. We just are fortunate that we have a 6-foot-4, 230 or 6-foot-5, whatever he is, guy that usually does a good job going and getting it."

 

 Tush push effect 

 With 87 career rushing touchdowns, Allen has already crossed the goal line more times than any QB in NFL history, and his eight rushing touchdowns this season is tied for the league lead and is on pace to break his and Hurts' single-season rushing touchdowns record for a quarterback (15).

 He was in rarified air to start the season, becoming only the fourth player to rush for multiple touchdowns in the first three games -- matching Priest Holmes (2003), Stephen Davis (1999) and Hall of Famer Jim Brown (1958).

 With 39 rushing yards on Sunday against the  Baltimore Ravens  (1 p.m. ET, CBS), Allen would become the fifth QB in league history to surpass 5,000 for a career, joining Lamar Jackson , Michael Vick, Russell Wilson and Newton. With two more rushing touchdowns, Allen will become the eighth player this century, regardless of position, to run for double-digit touchdowns in four consecutive seasons.

 

 Before getting too much further, let's be honest and address the tush-push-shaped elephant in the room. Campbell didn't have a tight end giving him a boost.

 When Newton sprung up for a Superman celebration, there was never a fullback standing next to him pretending to be his greatest supporter -- à la Jimmy Olsen. Meanwhile, 22 of Allen's 43 short-yardage TDs (51%) have come on traditional push plays.

 Two things, though: First off, changes to rules, strategies and circumstances unseat record holders in all sports. Babe Ruth's short porch home runs still count, as do Michael Phelps' gold medals from before the full-body swimsuit was banned.

 And second, there's the Hurts comparison. If the "Brotherly Shove" was the whole reason for Allen's success, then its poster boy wouldn't be nearly 20% less successful in converting goal-line carries into touchdowns.

 That said, 21 of Allen's 22 tush push scores have come since Brady took over as the Bills' playcaller midway through the 2023 season. Since that point, just six of Allen's 27 short-yardage touchdowns have come on non-push plays. And that list of six still includes two from early this season where the Bills didn't line up in push formation but a back still came to Allen's aid late in the play.

 

 

 Pushing through the pain 
 At the end of the day, it's all circular logic anyway. Push plays are a big reason for Allen's success, and Allen's size and power are a big reason why the Bills are comfortable running so many push plays. Whether the tush push is the chicken or the egg, Allen's still scoring.

 And crucially, those plays don't gain their reputation for being automatic without a whole lot of gritting, grinding effort.

 "It's torture," offensive tackle Dion Dawkins says. "It's torture under there."

 "Those sneaks aren't as glamorous as everyone thinks they are," Allen adds. "You're putting yourself up to getting some nice little hits on you there."

 Therein lies the central conflict of Allen's scoring pace. Brady and Allen are adamant that the plan is to build an offense that allows the quarterback to absorb fewer hits.

 Yet the offense is unambiguously gearing up for more short-yardage scores than ever. From 2019 to 2024, just 14% of the Bills' drives reached the opponent's 5-yard line. In 2025, that number jumped to 19%. This season, it's hovering around 21%.

 So now it's time to play the odds against the protective instincts. As established, Allen scores on 81% of his carries from the 2-yard line and in. Bills running back James Cook III scores at a 50% clip (11-for-22 career).

 The Bills are making their choice clear. This year Cook has three carries in these situations and has scored once. Allen has seven carries in these situations and has scored every time.

 It all but makes sense to go with what's automatic.

title: Fantasy football buzz: Philly no problem for Dak Prescott and Cowboys
summary: The Cowboys went on the road to Philadelphia on Monday night and found their lost offense.
full_text:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values.

 Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

 
 Oct. 27: Cowboys go off, Saquon scores but hurt again 
 By Michael F. Florio 
 The big story of "Monday Night Football" was Jay-Z being announced as the Super Bowl halftime performer. However, outside of that, the  Dallas Cowboys  stole the show by getting their offense back on track.

 
 Dak Prescott  bounced back in a big way, throwing for 212 yards and three touchdowns, He finished with 23.28 fantasy points. It was his second-best fantasy game of the season. Prescott has a great chance to stay hot against the  Arizona Cardinals , who have allowed the most passing TDs in the NFL. 
 Prescott's success translated to his top receivers having big days as well. CeeDee Lamb saw 12 targets, catching five of them for 74 yards and two scores. He finished with 24.4 fantasy points. He's surpassed 20 fantasy points three times and has just one game with less than 15. That's elite, high-end WR1 production. George Pickens caught four out of six targets for 57 yards and a touchdown, good for 15.7 fantasy points. He brings an extremely safe floor, but we have not seen as many big performances like last year. Still, you should start him weekly. 
 Javonte Williams was the other star for the Cowboys in this one. He rushed for a career-high 155 yards and a touchdown on 25 carries. That was good for 21.5 fantasy points. Williams brings an extremely safe floor and sees so much volume that he is also a weekly must-start. 
 Saquon Barkley returned from a hamstring injury -- before exiting last night's action due to a back injury. Before he left, he ran seven times for 62 yards and a touchdown, adding two catches for nine yards. If he's able to suit up next week against the  Washington Commanders , you start him. Dameon Pierce , who turned 15 opportunities into 48 yards and a touchdown, also exited late.  Elijah Mitchell finished the game for Philly. The health of both injured backs needs to be monitored. Pierce, or perhaps Mitchell, would be a streaming option if Barkley misses time. 
 Tanner McKee threw for 211 yards, one touchdown and one interception. He finished with 10.54 fantasy points. McKee played well given the circumstances, but still has not had a big fantasy showing. He remains a streaming option for those diving deep (or in superflex leagues) against the Commanders next week. Washington has allowed the fourth-most passing TDs and the second-most QB fantasy PPG. 
 Makai Lemon   and Dallas Goedert were the top targets for the  Philadelphia Eagles . Lemon saw a team-high eight targets, catching seven for 67 yards and a touchdown. All were career highs, as were his 19.7 fantasy points. Lemon should be added off the waiver wire this week. He'd be in play once again if DeVonta Smith sits again next week. Goedert saw seven targets, catching five of them for 48 yards and scoring 9.8 fantasy points. The volume he sees, paired with his safe floor, keep him as a low-end TE1 -- especially next week against Washington. 
 
 
 Oct. 26: Who got the ball in Week 7? 
 

 By Eric Moody 

 The box score doesn't tell you everything. Here are the roles and usage trends from Sunday that stood out to me.

 Pittsburgh Steelers vs. New Orleans Saints 
 

 Germie Bernard came back down to earth after setting season highs with 12 targets and 25.7 fantasy points against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last week. He finished with just five targets and 5.7 fantasy points against the Saints. However, Bernard and DK Metcalf played nearly the same number of snaps and ran a similar number of routes. Better games should be ahead for Bernard, especially with the Steelers having the 10th-easiest remaining schedule for fantasy wide receivers.

 Jaylen Warren led the Steelers backfield in snaps, routes run, touches (21) and fantasy points (16.7). However, Rico Dowdle was still involved, finishing with 15 touches and 14.6 fantasy points. It's frustrating for fantasy managers, but both backs will continue to be involved moving forward.

 Juwan Johnson 's role continues to shrink as Noah Fant and Oscar Delp take away snaps. His route participation has fallen significantly in each of the past two games, while Fant is now getting more playing time on third downs. Johnson can be dropped in most leagues, especially with Jordyn Tyson possibly returning after the bye.

 Alvin Kamara led the Saints backfield in snaps, routes run, touches (13) and fantasy points (13.2). The Saints struggled to run the football against the Steelers, but Kamara still had a solid fantasy day thanks to seven receptions for 57 yards. Travis Etienne Jr . will be eligible to return from injured reserve after the Saints' bye week, which could complicate things for Kamara and Kendre Miller 's fantasy managers.

 San Francisco 49ers at Atlanta Falcons 
 Christian McCaffrey left in the first quarter with a thigh injury and missed the entire second quarter. He returned after halftime, playing 68.4 snaps. The 49ers have a bye next week, giving McCaffrey extra time to recover. His health will be worth monitoring. It's another reminder that Kaelon Black (rostered in 21.9% of ESPN leagues), who finished with 13 touches and 10.9 fantasy points, could be a difference-maker in the 49ers offense if McCaffrey ever misses time.

 Cleveland Browns at Tennessee Titans 
 

 KC Concepcion had his best game of the season against the Titans, catching eight passes for 129 yards and finishing with 23.2 fantasy points. His playing time hasn't changed much, but his 10 targets were a season high. Denzel Boston led the Browns in snaps and routes run but finished with just 5.7 fantasy points. After scoring at least 12 fantasy points in four of his first five games, Boston has combined for just 8.2 points over the past two weeks.

 Harold Fannin Jr . caught six of nine targets for 91 yards and 13.1 fantasy points, his first game with more than 60 receiving yards this season. Fannin also ran a route on nearly every Cleveland dropback, but lost a fumble in the second quarter. Concepcion is on the flex radar, while Fannin remains a low-end TE1.

 Indianapolis Colts at Minnesota Vikings 

 

 Jordan Mason returned from injured reserve and led the Vikings backfield in snaps, routes run and touches (15), finishing with 6.8 fantasy points. Aaron Jones Sr . had nine touches and 3.6 fantasy points before leaving in the fourth quarter after aggravating his previous left knee injury. Mason was already getting more work before Jones left the game. If Jones misses Week 8 against the Lions, Mason would be a must-start for fantasy managers.

 Miami Dolphins at New York Jets 
 Malik Washington led the Dolphins' pass catchers in snaps, but Washington, Caleb Douglas and Greg Dulcich ran a similar number of routes. Dulcich led the team with five targets and 86 receiving yards, while Douglas scored 21.6 fantasy points thanks to two touchdowns in his return from injury. Douglas is worth adding off waivers and could have a bigger role in the second half of the season. Dulcich has had five targets in each of his last two games and is worth considering as a streaming option at tight end.

 Omar Cooper Jr . continues to impress, finishing with five targets, five receptions and 22.5 fantasy points against the Dolphins. He ranked second among Jets pass catchers in snaps and routes run and has now topped 100 receiving yards in consecutive games. Garrett Wilson led the team in both categories but finished with just three targets and 4.6 fantasy points. Adonai Mitchell returned after missing four games but finished fourth among Jets wide receivers in snaps and routes, scoring zero…

title: Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner trades signal big changes in Indianapolis
summary: Stephen Holder breaks down what the Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner trades mean for the Colts as Indianapolis begins a major rebuild.

title: Buckner, Nelson trades signal Colts' rebuild underway
summary: DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson are headed to contending teams. Could Jonathan Taylor be next?
full_text:
INDIANAPOLIS --  DeForest Buckner had seen enough.

 As the curtains closed Sunday on the Indianapolis Colts ' third straight loss, punctuating a season that began with high hopes and devolved into a road to nowhere, the veteran defensive tackle finally let his emotions show.

 Asked by a reporter how he felt after losing to the  Minnesota Vikings  to fall to 2-5, the three-time Pro Bowl selection was blunt.

 "I don't know, how 'bout you guess," he said. "I'm frustrated. Same thing. We lost."

 The losing wore on Buckner. But he and fellow Colts standout Quenton Nelson , an All-Pro guard, will no longer have to endure the frustration. Both were traded  Tuesday during one of the most consequential days for the franchise since the stunning 2019 retirement of quarterback Andrew Luck.

 

 But this development was much easier to predict than Luck's departure as it follows the firing of general manager Chris Ballard last week.

 Assistant general manager Ed Dodds engineered Tuesday's deals, presumably at the direction of owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon. Buckner is heading back to the San Francisco 49ers , the team that drafted him and traded him to Indianapolis in 2020. Nelson is headed to the Seattle Seahawks , one of the Niners' main NFC West rivals. Both players were in the final year of their contracts and their futures in Indianapolis were uncertain at best.

 Moves such as these appeared likely following Ballard's dismissal in his 10th season on the job. Ballard and the Colts had tried tweaking the roster to varying degrees in recent years. And they have tried every iteration of quarterback acquisition in their efforts to replace Luck.

 In the end, it all amounted to nothing.

 The Colts have not won the AFC South since 2014. They last made the playoffs in 2020. Their last postseason victory came in 2018. They've averaged 7.6 wins over the past five seasons. Even great players such as Buckner and Nelson weren't enough to overcome the club's other shortcomings.

 Tuesday's difficult decisions made it official: The Colts are done with that chapter.

 

 The next phase of franchise history will be a full rebuild. The Colts must embark on that rebuild without a first-round pick in 2027 as that selection is heading to the New York Jets to complete last year's Sauce Gardner trade. So, Tuesday's moves were a step toward rebuilding the draft capital that the team's next top executive will need to begin what will be a difficult job.

 The Colts are expected to entertain additional deals with players such as running back Jonathan Taylor , nose tackle Grover Stewart and receiver Josh Downs attracting interest from other clubs.

 But for now, Indianapolis has a single second-round pick in 2027, two third-round choices and two fourth-round selections among its selections. The Nelson deal garnered a 2027 third-round choice (along with a 2028 fifth-rounder) from Seattle, and Buckner netted a 2027 fourth-round choice from San Francisco.

 In terms of free agency, the Colts are projected to have well north of $60 million in salary cap space next spring. They could create significantly more if they trade Taylor or move on from struggling quarterback Daniel Jones .

 Roster flexibility isn't likely to be an issue for the next regime in Indianapolis. But getting to that point is sure to be painful.

 Kind of like Tuesday.

title: How Chargers 2026 first-round pick Akheem Mesidor is faring so far
summary: Safety Derwin James Jr. says Mesidor will be one of the top edge rushers in the league. Judging by the rookie's performance so far, that prediction may not be far off the mark.
full_text:
Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Akheem Mesidor is far from your average rookie.

 For one, he's 25 years old, a year younger than fellow defensive stalwart Daiyan Henley , whom the Chargers drafted in 2023. Linebacker Tuli Tuipulotu , also part of the 2023 draft class, is a year younger than Mesidor.

 Safety Derwin James Jr . laughed when told that Mesidor is older than Tuipulotu, one of the Chargers' top young defensive talents. James agreed it's weird, but emphasized there's no age limit on playing. When one's number is called, it's about going out there and playing.

 And what he's seen so far from the first-round pick led to a bold declaration.

 

 "[Mesidor's] a beast, bro. He's going to be one of the top edges in this league. I can't wait," James said. "I keep seeing him ascend. Very smart, don't say too many words. Just shows up to work, and I feel like he's a great reason why the defense is one of the top ones for sure."

 Judging by Mesidor's performance through seven weeks, James' prediction may not be far off the mark.

 His 24 tackles are the tied for fifth on the team, while his 2.5 sacks rank second and five quarterback hits are tied for third. That production comes on 191 total snaps, which ranks fifth among the team's linebackers.

 Mesidor's breakout came in Week 5 against the Denver Broncos when he led the team in tackles with eight while forcing a fumble on a sack of quarterback Bo Nix  (the Broncos recovered it). Mesidor forced another fumble while tackling Nix late in the third quarter, and Tuipulotu gobbled it up.

 The common adjective to describe Mesidor's play is a simple one that travels throughout the locker room: violent. Whether it's on a bull rush or the way he slides or cross chops, Mesidor exudes enough energy for quarterbacks to feel his cleats flying off the turf.

 Another common description of Mesidor: a player with a high motor, and the type of work ethic the Ottawa product needed to become one of the few NFL players from that region.

 

 Combine those two qualities, and it has resulted in what coach Jim Harbaugh said is "consistently good" and "high-level football." It's not just flashes.

 "The first couple games you feel like maybe he was feeling it out a little bit," said defensive coordinator Chris O'Leary. "But this is a guy that's now playing the way we expect him to play, which is fast and violent, and then letting his tools and his traits show up."

 Mesidor entered a linebacker room already full of talent. Khalil Mack is bound for Canton, Tuipulotu had a team-high 13 sacks last season, and Henley led the team in tackles last season with 103.

 Still, Mesidor is who O'Leary declared as "the standard as far as our effort goes." James said Mesidor is always one of the first on the practice field and last to leave.

 

 Tuipulotu told ESPN that the 6-foot-3, 280-pound rookie is "just a pro" and understands what he needs to do to be the best version of himself. He goes to players like Mack, Tuipulotu and veteran linebacker Bud Dupree for advice, asks questions in meetings and stays well prepared. It has helped him overcome some of the common obstacles rookies face.

 "Obviously, he's been bringing the pass rush, man. He's pass rushing at a high level and rookies ... that's what I mean as a rookie: When I came in, I had trouble rushing my rookie year." Tuipulotu said. "But he's been rushing very well, and I'm happy about that."

 The presence of Mack has also had a big impact. Mesidor is his own player, but after seeing how Mack operates, the rookie has tried to apply those same principles to his game. He'll ask questions and pick the brain of a three-time All-Pro with 116 career sacks.

 

 Mack likes what he sees so far from Mesidor.

 "The different intangibles you need on the edge. Speed. Obviously, the explosiveness. His ability to get off blocks and make tackles. I feel like his tackling was underrated," Mack said. "He's a great tackler and yeah, his ability to get to the ball. His hustle up on the back side of plays, he's chasing stuff down on screens. Yeah, it's just impressive."

title: 'You can overcome this': Students of Jalen Hurts' mom wrote get-well cards for QB
summary: Pamela Hurts, a schoolteacher, was clearly touched by the cards from her students on "Jalen Hurts Day."
full_text:
Some special well-wishers are aiding Jalen Hurts in his recovery.

 On Monday, Hurts' mother Pamela, who is a schoolteacher, posted a video on TikTok of get-well cards from her students for Jalen. Pamela said the Channelview School District had declared Monday "Jalen Hurts Day" in support of her son, who is expected to miss the season due to blood clots in his lungs .

 

 "I'm going to read every last one of them," Pamela said. "Oh, my goodness."

 

 Pamela read one card on the video, from an eighth-grade student named Linda.

 "You can overcome this and Jalen Hurts will overcome this as well," the letter read in part.

 Jalen Hurts was sidelined after the Philadelphia Eagles played the Washington Commanders in London in Week 5. He was initially diagnosed with what was described as superficial blood clots in his leg and played the whole game. Hurts is not allowed to participate in football activities while on anticoagulation medication. The NFL and NFL Players Association are working together to review the handling of his diagnosis .

title: Why did Seahawks trade for Quenton Nelson? Are the Colts just getting started?
summary: The Seahawks acquired an All-Pro guard two weeks before the deadline. What does this mean for them and the Colts?
full_text:
With the NFL trade deadline two weeks away , the Seattle Seahawks acquired All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick.

 The 4-3 Seahawks are getting an All-Pro offensive lineman to add to a potent offense. Nelson is one of four offensive players since the 1970 merger to be selected to the Pro Bowl in each of their first eight seasons. The others are Pro Football Hall of Famers -- running back Franco Harris, running back Barry Sanders and offensive tackle Joe Thomas, according to Elias Sports Bureau.

 The 2-5 Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard last week, which promptly thrust key players into trade speculation. Nelson was the first one to be dealt, but hours later Indianapolis sent DT  DeForest Buckner  to the  San Francisco 49ers  for a 2027 fourth-round draft pick .

 We asked ESPN NFL Nation Seahawks reporter Brady Henderson and Colts reporter Stephen Holder, plus NFL draft analyst Jordan Reid, how this trade impacts the Seahawks and the Colts.

 

 Why did the Seahawks trade for Nelson? 
 Seattle's offensive line has not been a glaring weakness this season, but it hasn't been the strength that it was projected to be after the reigning Super Bowl champions returned all five starters from last season. The Seahawks are gladly sacrificing some of that continuity to add a Hall of Fame-caliber player in Nelson, who will be an upgrade in their starting lineup over Anthony Bradford .

 

 Between Nelson and the impending returns of running backs Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet , there's no reason Seattle's run game shouldn't improve after an underwhelming start to the season, which includes a 3.9 yards-per-carry average that ranks 23rd through seven games.

 General manager John Schneider also has a long-standing relationship with interim Colts GM Ed Dodds -- who was previously in Seattle's front office -- and a long history of big swings at the trade deadline for players like Marshawn Lynch, Duane Brown,  Quandre Diggs , Carlos Dunlap , Leonard Williams , Ernest Jones IV and Rashid Shaheed . He also has a projected five compensatory picks coming his way in 2027. So with a chance to improve a 4-3 team that's two games behind the 49ers in the NFC West standings , there was no way Schneider was going to bask in the glow of the Lombardi Trophy and sit this trade deadline out. -- Henderson 

 

 How will adding Nelson to the mix shuffle the offensive line around? 
 It will require some shuffling, because Nelson has played only left guard in the NFL since the Colts drafted him sixth overall in 2018. Grey Zabel , the team's 2025 first-round pick, is the Seahawks' left guard. The most logical option might be to move Zabel to right guard, which would relegate Bradford -- Seattle's starter at right guard since 2023 -- into a backup role.

 It wouldn't be an easy task for Zabel to switch positions midseason. He did play some right guard in college, but it was only three starts back in 2020. Bradford, meanwhile, could become attractive to other teams as a starting-caliber guard making $3.7 million in the final season of his rookie contract. But the Seahawks aren't hurting for 2027 draft capital even after the Nelson trade, and their O-line depth already took a big hit when Mason Richman tore his ACL in the preseason.

 Something else to consider is that left tackle Charles Cross is expected to miss some time after injuring his ankle Sunday night, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. The Seahawks could in theory move Zabel to left tackle -- where he started his final college season -- then move him to right guard once Cross returns. But they like their swing tackle, Josh Jones , and it might make more sense to move Zabel to right guard now and give him as much time as possible to adjust. -- Henderson 

 

 Does this signal the beginning of an overhaul for the Colts, and could that include moving Jonathan Taylor ? 
 The Colts are widely expected to undergo a roster overhaul this offseason, and it appears to have begun early. Indianapolis fired GM Ballard last week, then proceeded to fall to 2-5 with a loss at Minnesota on Sunday.

 That has made Indianapolis' top players the targets of other clubs' trade overtures, with several veterans in the final years of their contracts now of interest to other teams. The biggest remaining name on the roster is running back Jonathan Taylor , who is already the subject of internal conversations for multiple teams. The Colts signed Taylor to an extension through the 2028 season during training camp, but it's unclear whether the 27-year-old running back meshes with the Colts' rebuild timeline.

 

 Defensive tackle DeForest Buckner  was dealt hours after Nelson to the 49ers -- the 32-year-old is in the final year of his deal and was seemingly frustrated with the Colts' current situation. The Colts acquired a fourth-round pick for Buckner.

 The Colts do not possess a first-round pick in the 2027 draft, making the idea of accumulating picks for veterans at the trade deadline appealing. -- Holder 

 

 Are the Seahawks looking to make more trades before the deadline? 
 As Schneider likes to say, they're in on everything -- and the extra draft picks give them the flexibility to continue looking. But even if a team has the draft capital and cap space to make an acquisition work, cash is another consideration, and the Seahawks doled out a lot of that with massive offseason extensions for Jaxon Smith-Njigba , Devon Witherspoon and  Leonard Williams . They're also inheriting the prorated amount of Nelson's $16 million base salary for 2026, so they might not be able to take on another significant contract.

 

 That's notable with Taylor, a player who has been linked to Seattle, given the issues it has had at running back, but one who just signed a two-year, $44 million extension. The Seahawks have yet to see what their backfield looks like with its top two options in Price and Charbonnet both healthy. That could happen soon , as both have a chance to play Monday night against the Bears. -- Henderson 

 

 The Colts add two picks here, including a Day 2 selection in 2027. What do they need in the draft? 
 Defensive tackle and wide receiver are the two obvious areas of need. Losing Buckner makes their need along the interior defensive front even greater. Justin Scott (Miami), Tavion Gadson (Kentucky) and Bear Alexander (Oregon) all make sense for the Colts to look at on Day 2. And in a deep receiver class, Indianapolis could benefit from someone like Ryan Coleman-Williams (Alabama), Reed Harris (Arizona State) or Ryan Wingo (Texas), potentially with its own second-round pick. -- Reid
